children.text: // om namo buddhāya //
children.translated_text: // Oṃ, homage to the <s>Buddha</s> //

children.text: Saundaranandaṃ Mahākāvyam
children.translated_text: <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>Mahākāvya</s> (The Great Poem of Handsome <s>Nanda</s>)

children.text:
prathamaḥ sargaḥ
kapilavastu varṇana
children.translated_text: First Canto: Description of <s>Kapilavastu</s>

children.text: gautamaḥ kapilo nāma munirdharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Gautama</s>, called <s>Kapila</s>, foremost among upholders of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: babhūva tapasi śrāntaḥ kākṣīvāniva gautamaḥ // Saund_1.1 //
children.translated_text: was wearied in <s>tapas</s> (austerity), like <s>Gautama</s> [who was] the son of <s>Kakṣīvat</s>. // Saund_1.1 //

children.text: aśiśriyadyaḥ satataṃ dīptaṃ kāśyapavattapaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who constantly tended the blazing <s>tapas</s> like <s>Kāśyapa</s>,

children.text: āśiśrāya ca tadvṛddhau siddhiṃ kāśyapavat parām // Saund_1.2 //
children.translated_text: and who, through the growth of that [<s>tapas</s>], attained supreme perfection like <s>Kāśyapa</s>. // Saund_1.2 //

children.text: haviḥṣu yaśca svātmārthaṃ gāmadhukṣad vasiṣṭhavat /
children.translated_text: He who, for his own spiritual purpose, milked the cow into the sacrificial oblations like <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,

children.text: tapaḥśiṣṭeṣu ca śiṣyeṣu gāmadhukṣad vasiṣṭhavat // Saund_1.3 //
children.translated_text: and who milked the cow [of knowledge] into his disciples, purified by <s>tapas</s>, like <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. // Saund_1.3 //

children.text: māhātmyāddīrghatapaso yo dvitīya ivābhavat /
children.translated_text: He who, by his greatness, became as it were a second of the long-austere one [<s>Atri</s>],

children.text: tṛtīya iva yaścābhūt kāvyāṅgirasayordhiyā // Saund_1.4 //
children.translated_text: and who was as if a third of <s>Kāvya</s> [<s>Śukra</s>] and <s>Aṅgiras</s> in wisdom. // Saund_1.4 //

children.text: tasya vistīrṇatapasaḥ pārśve himavataḥ śubhe /
children.translated_text: On the auspicious slope of the <s>Himavat</s>, his hermitage became

children.text: kṣetraṃ cāyatanaṃ caiva tapasāmāśramo 'bhavat // Saund_1.5 //
children.translated_text: both the field and the abode of his extensive <s>tapas</s>. // Saund_1.5 //

children.text: cāruvīruttaruvanaḥ prasnigdhamṛduśādvalaḥ /
children.translated_text: With beautiful creepers, trees, and groves, with smooth, soft, green grass,

children.text: havirdhūmavitānena yaḥ sadābhra ivābabhau // Saund_1.6 //
children.translated_text: it appeared always clouded, as it were, by the canopy of smoke from the sacrificial oblations. // Saund_1.6 //

children.text: mṛdubhiḥ saikataiḥ snigdhaiḥ kesarāstarapāṇḍubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With soft, smooth sandy patches, pale as beds of saffron,

children.text: bhūmibhāgairasaṃkīrṇaiḥ sāṅgarāga ivābhavat // Saund_1.7 //
children.translated_text: with ground-surfaces uncluttered, it was as though adorned with body-paint. // Saund_1.7 //

children.text: śucibhistīrthasaṃkhyātaiḥ pāvanairbhāvanairapi /
children.translated_text: With pure bathing-places, counted as <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred fords), both purifying and elevating,

children.text: bandhumāniva yastasthau sarobhiḥ sasaroruhaiḥ // Saund_1.8 //
children.translated_text: it stood as though surrounded by kinsmen, with its pools bearing lotuses. // Saund_1.8 //

children.text: paryāptaphalapuṣpābhiḥ sarvato vanarājibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With rows of trees on all sides, abundant in fruit and flower,

children.text: śuśubhe vavṛdhe caiva naraḥ sādhanavāniva // Saund_1.9 //
children.translated_text: it shone and flourished like a person possessed of means. // Saund_1.9 //

children.text: nīvāraphalasantuṣṭaiḥ svasthaiḥ śāntairanutsukaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Though filled with ascetics rich in <s>tapas</s>, content with wild rice and fruits, self-controlled, tranquil, and free from anxiety,

children.text: ākīrṇo 'pi tapobhṛddhiḥ śūnyaśūnya ivābhavat // Saund_1.10 //
children.translated_text: it appeared as though empty. // Saund_1.10 //

children.text: agnīnāṃ hūyamānānāṃ śikhināṃ kūjatāmapi /
children.translated_text: Of fires being offered into, of peacocks calling,

children.text: tīrthānāṃ cābhiṣekeṣu śuśruve yatra niḥsvanaḥ // Saund_1.11 //
children.translated_text: and of the ablutions at the sacred fords, there was heard the sound. // Saund_1.11 //

children.text: virejurhariṇā yatra suptā medhyāsu vediṣu /
children.translated_text: There, deer shone sleeping on the pure sacrificial altars,

children.text: salājairmādhavīpuṣpairupahārāḥ kṛtā iva // Saund_1.12 //
children.translated_text: as though offerings had been made with parched grain and <s>mādhavī</s> flowers. // Saund_1.12 //

children.text: api kṣudramṛgā yatra śāntāśceruḥ samaṃ mṛgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: There, even small animals moved about peacefully alongside the deer,

children.text: śaraṇyebhyastapasvibhyo vinayaṃ śikṣitā iva // Saund_1.13 //
children.translated_text: as though they had learned discipline from the ascetics, who were worthy of refuge. // Saund_1.13 //

children.text: saṃdigdhe 'pyapunarbhāve viruddheṣvāgameṣvapi /
children.translated_text: Even though non-return [to rebirth] was uncertain, and even though the scriptures disagreed [on the matter],

children.text: pratyakṣiṇa ivākurvaṃstapo yatra tapodhanāḥ // Saund_1.14 //
children.translated_text: the ascetics there, rich in <s>tapas</s>, practiced austerity as though witnessing [the results] directly. // Saund_1.14 //

children.text: yatra sma mīyate brahma kaiścit kaiścinna mīyate /
children.translated_text: There, <s>Brahman</s> was celebrated by some and was not celebrated by others;

children.text: kāle nimīyate somo na cākāle pramīyate // Saund_1.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> was pressed at the proper time and was not wasted at the wrong time. // Saund_1.15 //

children.text: nirapekṣāḥ śarīreṣu dharme yatra svabuddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, the ascetics, indifferent to their bodies, with their own understanding directed toward <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: saṃhṛṣṭā iva yatnena tāpasāstepire tapaḥ // Saund_1.16 //
children.translated_text: performed <s>tapas</s> with effort, as though rejoicing. // Saund_1.16 //

children.text: śrāmyanto munayo yatra svargāyodyuktacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, the sages, laboring with minds intent upon heaven,

children.text: taporāgeṇa dharmasya vilopamiva cakrire // Saund_1.17 //
children.translated_text: through their passion for <s>tapas</s>, seemed to be, as it were, plundering <s>dharma</s>. // Saund_1.17 //

children.text: atha tejasvisadanaṃ tapaḥkṣetraṃ tamāśramam /
children.translated_text: Then, to that hermitage — the field of <s>tapas</s>, the abode of the radiant —

children.text: kecidikṣvākavo jagmū rājaputrā vivatsavaḥ // Saund_1.18 //
children.translated_text: certain <s>Ikṣvāku</s> princes came, wishing to dwell there. // Saund_1.18 //

children.text: suvarṇastambhavarṣmāṇaḥ siṃhoreskā mahābhujāḥ /
children.translated_text: Of stature like golden pillars, lion-chested, mighty-armed,

children.text: pātraṃ śabdasya mahataḥ śriyāṃ ca vinayasya ca // Saund_1.19 //
children.translated_text: they were worthy vessels for great renown, for glory, and for discipline. // Saund_1.19 //

children.text: arharūpā hyanarhasya mahātmānaścalātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Worthy in form yet [sons] of one unworthy, great-souled yet [sons] of one of wavering mind,

children.text: prājñāḥ prajñāvimuktasya bhrātṛvyasya yavīyasaḥ // Saund_1.20 //
children.translated_text: wise yet [sons] of one devoid of wisdom — they were [the younger brothers] of their eldest brother. // Saund_1.20 //

children.text: mātṛśulkādupagatāṃ te śriyaṃ [ca] viṣehire /
children.translated_text: They endured the fortune that had come to them as the bride-price of their mother,

children.text: rarakṣuśca pituḥ satyaṃ yasmācchiśiyire vanam // Saund_1.21 //
children.translated_text: and they kept their father's word, on account of which they had to take up residence in the forest. // Saund_1.21 //

children.text: teṣāṃ munirupādhyāyo gautamaḥ kapilo 'bhavat /
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Gautama Kapila</s> became their preceptor;

children.text: gurugotrādataḥ kautsāste bhavanti sma gautamāḥ // Saund_1.22 //
children.translated_text: from the teacher's <s>gotra</s> (lineage), they became <s>Gautamas</s> from the <s>Kautsa</s> [lineage]. // Saund_1.22 //

children.text: ekapitroryathā bhrātroḥ pṛthagguruparigrahāt /
children.translated_text: Just as, of two brothers born of one father, through the adoption of different teachers,

children.text: rāma evābhavad gārgyo vāsubhadro 'pi gautamaḥ // Saund_1.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> became a <s>Gārgya</s> while <s>Vāsubhadra</s> became a <s>Gautama</s>, // Saund_1.23 //

children.text: śākavṛkṣapraticchannaṃ vāsaṃ yasmācca cakrire /
children.translated_text: and since they took up their dwelling concealed by <s>śāka</s> trees,

children.text: tasmādikṣvākuvaṃśyāste bhuvi śākyā iti smṛtāḥ // Saund_1.24 //
children.translated_text: therefore those descendants of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage are known on earth as the <s>Śākyas</s>. // Saund_1.24 //

children.text: sa teṣāṃ gautamaścakre svavaṃśasadṛśīḥ kriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Gautama</s> [sage] performed rites befitting their lineage for them,

children.text: munirūrdhvaṃ kumārasya sagarasyeva bhārgavaḥ // Saund_1.25 //
children.translated_text: as the sage <s>Bhārgava</s> [did] for the young prince <s>Sagara</s> thereafter. // Saund_1.25 //

children.text: kaṇvaḥ śākuntalasyeva bharatasya tarasvinaḥ /
children.translated_text: As <s>Kaṇva</s> [did] for the valiant <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Śakuntalā</s>,

children.text: vālmikiriva dhīmāṃśca dhīmatormaithileyayoḥ // Saund_1.26 //
children.translated_text: and as the wise <s>Vālmīki</s> [did] for the wise sons of <s>Maithilī</s> [<s>Sītā</s>]. // Saund_1.26 //

children.text: tadvanaṃ muninā tena taiśca kṣatriyapuṅgavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: That forest, through that sage and those bulls among warriors,

children.text: śāntāṃ guptāṃ ca yugapad brahmakṣatraśriyaṃ dadhe // Saund_1.27 //
children.translated_text: simultaneously bore the glory of <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Kṣatra</s>, tranquil and protected. // Saund_1.27 //

children.text: athodakalaśaṃ gṛhya teṣāṃ vṛddhicikīrṣayā /
children.translated_text: Then, taking a water-vessel, desiring their prosperity,

children.text: muniḥ sa viyadutpatya tānuvāca nṛpātmajān // Saund_1.28 //
children.translated_text: that sage, rising into the sky, spoke thus to those princes: // Saund_1.28 //

children.text: yā patet kalaśādasmādakṣayyasalilānmahīm /
children.translated_text: 'The stream that falls from this vessel of inexhaustible water onto the earth —

children.text: dhārā tāmanatikramya māmanveta yathākramam // Saund_1.29 //
children.translated_text: follow me in due order, without crossing beyond it.' // Saund_1.29 //

children.text: tataḥ paramamityuktvā śirobhiḥ praṇipatya ca /
children.translated_text: Then, saying 'Very well,' and bowing with their heads,

children.text: rathānāruruhuḥ sarve śīghravāhānalaṃkṛtān // Saund_1.30 //
children.translated_text: they all mounted their chariots, swift-coursing and well-adorned. // Saund_1.30 //

children.text: tataḥ sa tairanugataḥ syandanasthairnabhogataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, followed by them in their chariots, he, going through the sky,

children.text: tadāśramamahīprāntaṃ paricikṣepa vāriṇā // Saund_1.31 //
children.translated_text: encircled the border of that hermitage-land with water. // Saund_1.31 //

children.text: aṣṭāpadamivālikhya nimittaiḥ surabhīkṛtam /
children.translated_text: Having traced out, as it were, a [sacred] chessboard, made auspicious with [ritual] signs,

children.text: tānuvāca muniḥ sthitvā bhūmipālasutānidam // Saund_1.32 //
children.translated_text: the sage, having alighted, spoke this to the sons of kings: // Saund_1.32 //

children.text: asmin dhārāparikṣipte nemicinhitalakṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: 'In this [area] encircled by the stream, marked by the rim of the [chariot-]wheel,

children.text: nirmimīdhvaṃ puraṃ yūyaṃ mayi yāte triviṣṭapam // Saund_1.33 //
children.translated_text: build a city, you [all], after I have departed to heaven.' // Saund_1.33 //

children.text: tataḥ kadācitte vīrāstasmin pratigate munau /
children.translated_text: Then, at a certain time, when that sage had departed,

children.text: babhramuyauṃvanoddāmā gajā iva niraṅkuśā // Saund_1.34 //
children.translated_text: those heroes, unchecked by youth, roamed about like elephants without a goad. // Saund_1.34 //

children.text: baddhagodhāṅgulītrāṇā hastaviṣṭhitakārmukāḥ /
children.translated_text: With arm-guards and finger-guards fastened, with bows held in hand,

children.text: śarādhmātamahātūṇā vyāyatābaddhavāsasaḥ // Saund_1.35 //
children.translated_text: with great quivers swollen with arrows, wearing loose garments, // Saund_1.35 //

children.text: jijñāsamānā nāgeṣu kauśalaṃ śvāpadeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: wishing to test their skill among elephants and wild beasts,

children.text: anucakrurvanasthasya dauṣyanterdevakarmaṇaḥ // Saund_1.36 //
children.translated_text: they emulated the divine deeds of <s>Dauṣyanti</s> [<s>Bharata</s>], who dwelt in the forest. // Saund_1.36 //

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā prakṛtiṃ yātān vṛddhānvyāghraśiśūniva /
children.translated_text: Seeing them reverted to their [wild] nature, like tiger cubs grown old,

children.text: tāpasāstadvanaṃ hitvā himavantaṃ siṣevire // Saund_1.37 //
children.translated_text: the ascetics, abandoning that forest, resorted to the <s>Himavat</s>. // Saund_1.37 //

children.text: tatastadāśramasthānaṃ śūnyaṃ taiḥ śūnyacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that hermitage-ground emptied by those [ascetics], those empty-minded [princes],

children.text: paśyanto manyunā taptā vyālā iva niśaśvasuḥ // Saund_1.38 //
children.translated_text: burning with anger, heaved sighs like serpents. // Saund_1.38 //

children.text: atha te puṇyakarmāṇaḥ pratyupasthitavṛddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, those of meritorious deeds, their prosperity having arrived,

children.text: tatra tajjñairupākhyātānavāpurmahato nidhīn // Saund_1.39 //
children.translated_text: obtained great treasures there, pointed out by those who knew [where they lay]. // Saund_1.39 //

children.text: alaṃ dharmārthakāmānāṃ nikhilānāmavāptaye /
children.translated_text: Sufficient for the complete attainment of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>,

children.text: nidhayo naikavidhayo bhūrayaste gatārayaḥ // Saund_1.40 //
children.translated_text: those treasures, of manifold kinds and abundant, were for those whose enemies had departed. // Saund_1.40 //

children.text: tatastatpratilambhācca pariṇāmācca karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, through the acquisition of those [treasures] and through the maturation of their <s>karma</s>,

children.text: tasmin vāstuni vāstujñāḥ puraṃ śrīmannyaveśayan // Saund_1.41 //
children.translated_text: those skilled in architecture established a glorious city on that site. // Saund_1.41 //

children.text: saridvistīrṇaparikhaṃ spaṣṭāñcitamahāpatham /
children.translated_text: With broad moats [formed by] rivers, with wide, clearly-laid-out main roads,

children.text: śailakalpamahāvapraṃ girivrajamivāparam // Saund_1.42 //
children.translated_text: with great ramparts like mountains — another <s>Girivraja</s>, as it were. // Saund_1.42 //

children.text: pāṇḍurāṭṭālasumukhaṃ suvibhaktāntarāpaṇam /
children.translated_text: With white watchtowers at its entrances, with well-arranged inner marketplaces,

children.text: harmyamālāparikṣiptaṃ kukṣiṃ himagireriva // Saund_1.43 //
children.translated_text: encircled by rows of mansions — like the lap of the snow-mountain. // Saund_1.43 //

children.text: vedavedāṅgaviduṣastasthuṣaḥ ṣaṭsu karmasu /
children.translated_text: There, they employed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — learned in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, established in the six duties —

children.text: śāntaye vṛddhaye caiva yatra viprānajījapan // Saund_1.44 //
children.translated_text: for peace and for prosperity. // Saund_1.44 //

children.text: tadbhūmerabhiyoktṛṇāṃ prayuktān vinivṛttaye /
children.translated_text: There, to repel assailants of that land,

children.text: yatra svena prabhāvena bhṛtyadaṇḍānajījapan // Saund_1.45 //
children.translated_text: they employed the forces of their servants through their own might. // Saund_1.45 //

children.text: caritradhanasampannān salajjān dīrghadarśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those endowed with the wealth of character, modest, far-sighted,

children.text: arhato 'tiṣṭhipan yatra śūrān dakṣān kuṭumbinaḥ // Saund_1.46 //
children.translated_text: worthy, brave, capable householders — they appointed there. // Saund_1.46 //

children.text: vyastaistaistairguṇaiyuktān mativāgvikramādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those endowed with various qualities — intellect, eloquence, valor, and the like —

children.text: karmasu pratirupeṣu sacivāṃstānnyayūyujan // Saund_1.47 //
children.translated_text: they appointed as ministers in their respective appropriate offices. // Saund_1.47 //

children.text: vasumadbhiravibhrāntairalaṃvidyairavismitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Teeming with men who were prosperous yet unconfused, learned yet not arrogant,

children.text: yad babhāse naraiḥ kīrṇaṃ mandaraḥ kinnarairiva // Saund_1.48 //
children.translated_text: it shone like <s>Mandara</s> [mountain] with <s>Kinnaras</s>. // Saund_1.48 //

children.text: yatra te hṛṣṭamanasaḥ pauraprīticikīrṣayā /
children.translated_text: There, with joyful minds, wishing to please the citizens,

children.text: śrīmantyudyānasaṃjñāni yaśodhāmānyacikaran // Saund_1.49 //
children.translated_text: they created glorious places called parks — abodes of fame. // Saund_1.49 //

children.text: śivāḥ puṣkariṇīścaiva paramāgryaguṇāmbhasaḥ /
children.translated_text: And auspicious lotus-ponds, with water of the finest and highest quality —

children.text: nājñayā cetanotkarṣāddikṣu sarvāsvacīkhanan // Saund_1.50 //
children.translated_text: not by command but from the excellence of their intention — they dug in all directions. // Saund_1.50 //

children.text: manojñāḥ śrīmatīḥ praṣṭhīḥ pathiṣūpavaneṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Delightful, splendid rest-houses along the roads and in the groves,

children.text: sabhāḥ kūpavatīścaiva samantāt pratyatiṣṭhipan // Saund_1.51 //
children.translated_text: and assembly halls with wells, they established all around. // Saund_1.51 //

children.text: hastyaśvarathasaṃkīrṇamasaṃkīrṇamanākulam /
children.translated_text: Crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots, yet uncluttered and orderly,

children.text: anigūḍhārthivibhavaṃ nigūḍhajñānapauruṣam // Saund_1.52 //
children.translated_text: with the wealth of the needy unconcealed, but with [its] knowledge and prowess hidden, // Saund_1.52 //

children.text: sanidhānamivārthānāmādhānamiva tejasām /
children.translated_text: it was as if a repository of riches, a receptacle of brilliance,

children.text: niketamiva vidyānāṃ saṃketamiva saṃpadām // Saund_1.53 //
children.translated_text: a dwelling-place of learning, a meeting-point of prosperity. // Saund_1.53 //

children.text: vāsavṛkṣaṃ guṇavatāmāśrayaṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: A wish-fulfilling tree for the virtuous, a refuge for those seeking shelter,

children.text: ānartaṃ kṛtaśāstrāṇāmālānaṃ bāhuśālinām // Saund_1.54 //
children.translated_text: a stage for those learned in the arts, a tethering-post for the mighty-armed. // Saund_1.54 //

children.text: samājairutsavairdāyaiḥ kriyāvidhibhireva ca /
children.translated_text: With assemblies, festivals, gifts, and ritual observances,

children.text: alaṃcakruralaṃvīryāste jagaddhāma tatpuram // Saund_1.55 //
children.translated_text: those of abundant valor adorned that city, the ornament of the world. // Saund_1.55 //

children.text: yasmādanyāyataste ca kaṃcinnācīkaran karam /
children.translated_text: And since they did not levy any unjust tax,

children.text: tasmādalpena kālena tattadāpūpuran puram // Saund_1.56 //
children.translated_text: therefore, in a short time, they filled that city to the utmost. // Saund_1.56 //

children.text: kapilasya ca tasyarṣestasminnāśramavāstuni /
children.translated_text: And because they built that city on the hermitage-site of that sage <s>Kapila</s>,

children.text: yasmātte tatpuraṃ cakrustasmāt kapilavāstu tat // Saund_1.57 //
children.translated_text: therefore it is [called] <s>Kapilavastu</s>. // Saund_1.57 //

children.text: kakandasya makandasya kuśāmbasyeva cāśrame /
children.translated_text: Just as cities are heard of [being named] after the hermitages of <s>Kakanda</s>, <s>Makanda</s>, and <s>Kuśāmba</s>,

children.text: puryo yathā hi śrūyante tathaiva kapilasya tat // Saund_1.58 //
children.translated_text: so too is this [city named] after <s>Kapila</s>. // Saund_1.58 //

children.text: āpuḥ puraṃ tatpuruhūtakalpāste tejasāryeṇa na vismayena /
children.translated_text: Those [princes], equal to <s>Puruhūta</s> [<s>Indra</s>], attained that city through noble brilliance, not through vainglory;

children.text: āpuryaśogandhamataśca śaśvat sutā yayāteriva kīrtimantaḥ // Saund_1.59 //
children.translated_text: and they ever attained renown and fragrance and prosperity, like the illustrious sons of <s>Yayāti</s>. // Saund_1.59 //

children.text: tannāthavṛttairapi rājaputrairarājakaṃ naiva rarāja rāṣṭram /
children.translated_text: That kingdom, though [governed] by princes who conducted themselves as lords, yet without a [consecrated] king, did not truly shine —

children.text: tārāsahastrairapi dīpyamānairanutthite candra ivāntarīkṣam // Saund_1.60 //
children.translated_text: like the sky, even when blazing with thousands of stars, when the moon has not risen. // Saund_1.60 //

children.text: yo jyāyānatha vayasā guṇaiśca teṣāṃ bhātṝṇāṃ vṛṣabha ivaujasā vṛṣāṇām /
children.translated_text: He who was eldest among those brothers in age and in virtues, like a bull in strength among bulls —

children.text: te tatra priyaguravastamabhyaṣicannādityā daśaśatalocanaṃ divīva // Saund_1.61 //
children.translated_text: they, revering their elder, consecrated him there, as the <s>Ādityas</s> [consecrated] the thousand-eyed one [<s>Indra</s>] in heaven. // Saund_1.61 //

children.text: ācāravānvinayavānnayavānkriyāvān dharmāya nendriyasukhāya dhṛtātapatraḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with good conduct, discipline, statecraft, and action, bearing the royal parasol for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, not for sensual pleasure,

children.text: tadbhrātṛbhiḥ parivṛtaḥ sa jugopa rāṣṭram saṃkrandano divamivānusṛto marudbhiḥ // Saund_1.62 //
children.translated_text: he, surrounded by those brothers, protected the kingdom, as <s>Saṃkrandana</s> [<s>Indra</s>] [protects] heaven, followed by the <s>Maruts</s>. // Saund_1.62 //

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvya meṃ "kapilavastu varṇana" nāmaka prathama sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>Mahākāvya</s>, the first canto, called 'Description of <s>Kapilavastu</s>,' is complete.

children.text:
dvitīyaḥ sargaḥ
rājā śuddhodana
children.translated_text: Second Canto: King <s>Śuddhodana</s>

children.text: tataḥ kadācitkālena tadavāpa kulakramāt /
children.translated_text: Then, in the course of time, by the succession of the dynasty, there came

children.text: rājā śuddhodano nāma śuddhakarmā jitendriyaḥ // Saund_2.1 //
children.translated_text: a king named <s>Śuddhodana</s>, of pure deeds and conquered senses. // Saund_2.1 //

children.text: yaḥ sasañje na kāmeṣu śrīprāptau na visismiye /
children.translated_text: He who did not become attached to pleasures upon gaining prosperity, nor was amazed [by it],

children.text: nāvamene parānṛddhyā parebhyo nāpi vivyathe // Saund_2.2 //
children.translated_text: who did not scorn others out of pride, nor trembled before others. // Saund_2.2 //

children.text: balīyān sattvasaṃpannaḥ śrutavān buddhimānapi /
children.translated_text: Mighty, endowed with <s>sattva</s> (virtue), learned, and also intelligent,

children.text: vikrānto nayavāṃścaiva dhīraḥ sumukha eva ca // Saund_2.3 //
children.translated_text: valorous, possessed of statecraft, steadfast, and fair of countenance. // Saund_2.3 //

children.text: vapuṣmāṃśca na ca stabdho dakṣiṇo na ca nārjavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Handsome yet not haughty, courteous yet not lacking in straightforwardness,

children.text: tejasvī na ca na kṣāntaḥ kartā ca na ca vismitaḥ // Saund_2.4 //
children.translated_text: brilliant yet not without patience, a doer yet not vainglorious. // Saund_2.4 //

children.text: ākṣiptaḥ śatrubhiḥ saṃkhye suhṛdbhiśca vyapāśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Challenged by enemies in battle and relied upon by allies,

children.text: abhavad yo na vimukhastejasā ditsayaiva ca // Saund_2.5 //
children.translated_text: he was one who never turned his back — through his brilliance and his generosity alike. // Saund_2.5 //

children.text: yaḥ pūrvaiḥ rājabhiryātāṃ yiyāsurdharmapaddhatim /
children.translated_text: He who, wishing to follow the path of <s>dharma</s> traversed by former kings,

children.text: rājyaṃ dīkṣāmiva vahan vṛttenānvagamat pitṝn // Saund_2.6 //
children.translated_text: bearing the kingship as though it were a [sacred] consecration, followed his ancestors through [righteous] conduct. // Saund_2.6 //

children.text: yasya suvyavahārācca rakṣaṇācca sukhaṃ prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Through whose just governance and protection, the subjects

children.text: śiśyire vigatodvegāḥ pituraṅkagatā iva // Saund_2.7 //
children.translated_text: rested free from anxiety, as though nestled in a father's lap. // Saund_2.7 //

children.text: kṛtaśāstraḥ kṛtāstro vā jāto vā vipule kule /
children.translated_text: Whether learned in the scriptures, or skilled in arms, or born in a great family —

children.text: akṛtārtho na dadṛśe yasya darśanameyivān // Saund_2.8 //
children.translated_text: no one who came into his presence was seen to depart without having attained his purpose. // Saund_2.8 //

children.text: hitaṃ vipriyamapyukto yaḥ suśrāva na cukṣubhe /
children.translated_text: He who, when told what was beneficial though unpleasant, listened well and was not disturbed;

children.text: duṣkṛtaṃ bahvapi tyaktvā sasmāra kṛtamaṇvapi // Saund_2.9 //
children.translated_text: who, having set aside even much wrongdoing, remembered even a little service. // Saund_2.9 //

children.text: praṇatānanujagrāha vijagrāha kuladviṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: He favored the submissive, seized the enemies of his clan,

children.text: āpannān parijagrāha nijagrāhāsthitān pathi // Saund_2.10 //
children.translated_text: protected the distressed, and restrained those who strayed from the path. // Saund_2.10 //

children.text: prāyeṇa viṣaye yasya tacchīlamanuvartinaḥ /
children.translated_text: In his realm, for the most part, [the people], following his character,

children.text: arjayanto dadṛśire dhanānīva guṇānapi // Saund_2.11 //
children.translated_text: Were seen to acquire virtues as well as wealth. // 2.11 //

children.text: adhyaiṣṭa yaḥ paraṃ brahma na vyaiṣṭa satataṃ dhṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: He who studied the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, never wavered from steadfastness,

children.text: dānānyadita pātrebhyaḥ pāpaṃ nākṛta kiṃcana // Saund_2.12 //
children.translated_text: Gave gifts to worthy recipients, and never committed any sin. // 2.12 //

children.text: dhṛtyāvākṣīt pratijñāṃ sa sadvājīvodyatāṃ dhuram /
children.translated_text: With fortitude he fulfilled his pledge, like a fine horse that has taken up the yoke;

children.text: na hyavāñchīccyutaḥ satyānmuhūrtamapi jīvitam // Saund_2.13 //
children.translated_text: For he did not wish to live even a moment, having fallen from truth. // 2.13 //

children.text: viduṣaḥ paryupāsiṣṭa vyakāśiṣṭātmavattayā /
children.translated_text: He attended upon the learned, shone forth through self-mastery,

children.text: vyarociṣṭa ca śiṣṭebhyo māsīṣe candramā iva // Saund_2.14 //
children.translated_text: And was resplendent among the virtuous, like the moon in its fullness. // 2.14 //

children.text: avedīd buddhiśāstrābhyāmiha cāmutra ca kṣamam /
children.translated_text: He knew, through intellect and <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), what was fitting in this world and the next;

children.text: arakṣīddhairyavīryābhyāmindriyāṇyapi ca prajāḥ // Saund_2.15 //
children.translated_text: He guarded both his senses and his subjects through firmness and valor. // 2.15 //

children.text: ahārṣīd duḥkhamārtānāṃ dviṣatāṃ corjitaṃ yaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: He took away the suffering of the afflicted and the accumulated glory of enemies,

children.text: acaiṣīcca nayairbhūmiṃ bhūyasā yaśasaiva ca // Saund_2.16 //
children.translated_text: And he governed the earth by wise policies and by ever-increasing fame. // 2.16 //

children.text: apyāsīd duḥkhitān paśyan prakṛtyā karuṇātmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Compassionate by nature, he was moved seeing the suffering of others;

children.text: nādhauṣīcca yaśo lobhādanyāyādhigatairdhanaiḥ // Saund_2.17 //
children.translated_text: Nor did he tarnish his fame through greed, with wealth obtained by unjust means. // 2.17 //

children.text: sauhārdadṛḍhabhaktitvānmaitreṣu viguṇeṣvapi /
children.translated_text: Due to the firmness of his affection and devotion, [he did not reject] even friends who had faults;

children.text: nādidāsīdaditsīttu saumukhyāt svaṃ svamarthavat // Saund_2.18 //
children.translated_text: Out of graciousness he wished to give away his own [possessions] to those deserving, as though they were theirs. // 2.18 //

children.text: anivedyāgramarhadbhyo nālikṣat kiṃcidaplutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Without first offering the best portion to those worthy of honor, he never tasted anything, being ungreedy;

children.text: gāmadharmeṇa nādhukṣat kṣīratarṣeṇa gāmiva // Saund_2.19 //
children.translated_text: He did not milk the earth unjustly, like a cow [milked] out of mere thirst for milk. // 2.19 //

children.text: nāsṛkṣad balimaprāptaṃ nārukṣanmānamaiśvaram /
children.translated_text: He did not levy taxes that were not due, nor did he mount royal pride;

children.text: āgamairbuddhimādhikṣaddharmāya na tu kīrtaye // Saund_2.20 //
children.translated_text: He enriched his intellect through the <s>Āgamas</s> (scriptures), for the sake of <s>Dharma</s>, not for fame. // 2.20 //

children.text: kleśārhānapi kāṃścittu nākliṣṭa kliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even those who deserved punishment, if they had done wrong deeds, he did not torment;

children.text: āryabhāvācca nādhukṣad dviṣato 'pi sato guṇān // Saund_2.21 //
children.translated_text: And out of noble character, he did not suppress the virtues of even those who were enemies. // 2.21 //

children.text: ākṛkṣad vapuṣā dṛṣṭīḥ prajānāṃ candramā iva /
children.translated_text: He attracted the gazes of the people with his person, like the moon;

children.text: parasvaṃ bhuvi nāmṛkṣanmahāviṣamivoragam // Saund_2.22 //
children.translated_text: He did not touch the property of others on earth, as if it were a great serpent's venom. // 2.22 //

children.text: nākrukṣad viṣaye tasya kaścitkaiścit kvacit kṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: In his domain, no one was injured by anyone anywhere;

children.text: ādikṣattasya hastasthamārtebhyo hyabhayaṃ dhanuḥ // Saund_2.23 //
children.translated_text: For the bow in his hand bestowed fearlessness upon the distressed. // 2.23 //

children.text: kṛtāgaso 'pi praṇatān prāgeva priyakāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even those who had committed offenses, if they bowed down — how much more those who acted kindly —

children.text: adarśatsnigdhayā dṛṣṭyā ślakṣṇena vacasāsicat // Saund_2.24 //
children.translated_text: He regarded with an affectionate gaze and sprinkled with gentle words. // 2.24 //

children.text: bavhīradhyagamad vidyā viṣayeṣvakutūhalaḥ /
children.translated_text: He mastered many branches of learning, without curiosity for sense pleasures;

children.text: sthitaḥ kārtayuge dharme dharmāt kṛcchre 'pi nāsrasat // Saund_2.25 //
children.translated_text: Established in the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (Golden Age), he did not deviate from <s>Dharma</s> even in adversity. // 2.25 //

children.text: avardhiṣṭa guṇaiḥ śaśvadavṛdhanmitrasaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: He ever grew in virtues and prospered in the wealth of friends;

children.text: avartiṣṭa ca vṛddheṣu nāvṛtad garhite pathi // Saund_2.26 //
children.translated_text: He conducted himself among the elders and did not tread the path of the blameworthy. // 2.26 //

children.text: śarairaśīśamacchatrūn guṇairbandhūnarīramat /
children.translated_text: With arrows he quelled his enemies, with virtues he delighted his kinsmen;

children.text: randhrairnācūcudad bhṛtyān karairnāpīpiḍat prajāḥ // Saund_2.27 //
children.translated_text: He did not goad his servants through their weaknesses, nor did he oppress the people with taxes. // 2.27 //

children.text: rakṣaṇāccaiva śauryācca nikhilāṃ gāmavīvapat /
children.translated_text: Through protection and through valor, he safeguarded the entire earth;

children.text: spaṣṭayā daṇḍanītyā ca rātrisatrānavīvapat // Saund_2.28 //
children.translated_text: And through a clear policy of justice, he kept night-vigils [against crime]. // 2.28 //

children.text: kulaṃ rājarṣivṛttena yaśogandhamavīvapat /
children.translated_text: He suffused his lineage with the fragrance of fame through the conduct of a royal sage;

children.text: dīptyā tama ivādityastejasārīnavīvapat // Saund_2.29 //
children.translated_text: Like the sun dispelling darkness with its radiance, he overpowered enemies with his splendor. // 2.29 //

children.text: apaprathat pitṝṃścaiva satputrasadṛśairguṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: He glorified his ancestors with virtues worthy of a true son;

children.text: salileneva cāmbhodo vṛttenājihṇadat prajāḥ // Saund_2.30 //
children.translated_text: Like a rain cloud with water, he nourished the people with righteous conduct. // 2.30 //

children.text: dānairajasravipulaiḥ somaṃ viprānasūṣavat /
children.translated_text: With generous and abundant gifts he gladdened the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> like <s>Soma</s>;

children.text: rājadharmasthitatvācca kāle sasyamasūṣavat // Saund_2.31 //
children.translated_text: And by his firm adherence to kingly duty, he caused the crops to flourish in their season. // 2.31 //

children.text: adharmiṣṭhāmacakathanna kathāmakathaṃkathaḥ /
children.translated_text: Free from doubt, he never spoke of what was unrighteous;

children.text: cakravartīva ca parān dharmāyābhyudasīṣahat // Saund_2.32 //
children.translated_text: Like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), he urged others toward <s>Dharma</s>. // 2.32 //

children.text: rāṣṭramanyatra ca balerna sa kiṃcidadīdapat /
children.translated_text: He made nothing in the kingdom tremble except through [the display of] military strength;

children.text: bhṛtyaireva ca sodyogaṃ dviṣaddarpamadīdapat // Saund_2.33 //
children.translated_text: And with his servants alone, he quenched the pride of enemies with effort. // 2.33 //

children.text: svairevādīdapaccāpi bhūyo bhūyo guṇaiḥ kulam /
children.translated_text: He himself illuminated his lineage ever more with virtues;

children.text: prajā nādīdapaccaiva sarvadharmavyavasthayā // Saund_2.34 //
children.translated_text: But he never oppressed the people, through the establishment of all righteous practices. // 2.34 //

children.text: aśrāntaḥ samaye yajvā yajñabhūmimamīmapat /
children.translated_text: Tireless, a performer of sacrifices at the proper time, he consecrated the sacrificial ground;

children.text: pālanācca dvijān brahma nirudvignānamīmapat // Saund_2.35 //
children.translated_text: And through protecting the twice-born, he enabled the undisturbed study of <s>Brahman</s> (the Vedas). // 2.35 //

children.text: gurubhirvidhivat kāle saumyaḥ somamamīmapat /
children.translated_text: Gentle in disposition, he pressed the <s>Soma</s> with his elders according to rite and at the proper time;

children.text: tapasā tejasā caiṣa dviṣatsainyamamīmapat // Saund_2.36 //
children.translated_text: And through his <s>tapas</s> (austerity) and splendor, he crushed the armies of enemies. // 2.36 //

children.text: prajāḥ paramadharmajñaḥ sūkṣmaṃ dharmamavīvasat /
children.translated_text: A supreme knower of <s>Dharma</s>, he taught the people the subtle <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: darśanāccaiva dharmasya kāle svargamavīvasat // Saund_2.37 //
children.translated_text: And through the vision of <s>Dharma</s>, he attained heaven when his time came. // 2.37 //

children.text: vyaktamapyarthakṛcchreṣu nādharmiṣṭhamatiṣṭhipat /
children.translated_text: Even in financial difficulties, he never resorted to what was unrighteous;

children.text: priya ityeva cāśaktaṃ na saṃrāgādavīvṛdhat // Saund_2.38 //
children.translated_text: Nor did he advance an incompetent person out of mere partiality, thinking 'he is dear.' // 2.38 //

children.text: tejasā ca tviṣā caiva ripūn dṛptānabībhasat /
children.translated_text: With his energy and brilliance he terrified his haughty enemies;

children.text: yaśodīpena dīptena pṛthivīṃ ca vyabībhasat // Saund_2.39 //
children.translated_text: And with the blazing lamp of fame he illuminated the earth. // 2.39 //

children.text: ānuśaṃsyānna yaśase tenādāyi sadārthine /
children.translated_text: Out of compassion, not for fame, he gave to those in need;

children.text: dravyaṃ mahadapi tyaktvā na caivākīrti kiñcana // Saund_2.40 //
children.translated_text: Even having relinquished great wealth, he never earned any disgrace. // 2.40 //

children.text: tenārirapi duḥkhārto nātyāji śaraṇāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: By him, even an enemy in distress was not abandoned when he sought refuge;

children.text: jitvā dṛptānapi ripūnna tenākāri vismayaḥ // Saund_2.41 //
children.translated_text: Having conquered even haughty enemies, he showed no arrogance. // 2.41 //

children.text: na tenābhedi maryādā kāmādveṣādbhayādapi /
children.translated_text: By him no boundary was transgressed, whether from desire, hatred, or fear;

children.text: tena satsvapi bhogeṣu nāsevīndriyavṛttitā // Saund_2.42 //
children.translated_text: Even though pleasures were available to him, he did not pursue the ways of the senses. // 2.42 //

children.text: na tenādarśi viṣamaṃ kāryaṃ kvacana kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: He never saw anything in his duties as uneven or unjust;

children.text: vipriyapriyayoḥ kṛtye na tenāgāmi nikriyāḥ // Saund_2.43 //
children.translated_text: In matters both unpleasant and pleasant, he never acted with impropriety. // 2.43 //

children.text: tenāpāyi yathākalpaṃ somaśca yaśa eva ca /
children.translated_text: By him, <s>Soma</s> was drunk according to the prescribed ritual, and fame likewise;

children.text: vedaścāmnāyi satataṃ vedokto dharma eva ca // Saund_2.44 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s> were constantly recited, and the <s>Dharma</s> declared in the <s>Vedas</s> was [practiced] as well. // 2.44 //

children.text: evamādibhiratyakto babhūvāsulabhairguṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with such and other rare virtues,

children.text: aśakyaḥ śakyasāmantaḥ śākyarājaḥ sa śakravat // Saund_2.45 //
children.translated_text: That <s>Śākya</s> king, lord of <s>Śākya</s> neighbors, was invincible, like <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>). // 2.45 //

children.text: atha tasmin tathā kāle dharmakāmā divaukasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now at that time, the celestial beings, devoted to <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: vicerurdiśi lokasya dharmacaryāṃ didṛkṣavaḥ // Saund_2.46 //
children.translated_text: Roamed through the regions of the world, wishing to see the practice of <s>Dharma</s>. // 2.46 //

children.text: dharmātmānaścarantaste dharmajijñāsayā jagat /
children.translated_text: Those righteous ones, traversing the world in their quest for <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: dadṛśustaṃ viśeṣeṇa dharmātmānaṃ narādhipam // Saund_2.47 //
children.translated_text: Beheld that king of men to be especially righteous. // 2.47 //

children.text: devebhyastuṣitebhyo 'tha bodhisattvaḥ kṣitiṃ vrajan /
children.translated_text: Then from the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, descending to earth,

children.text: upapattiṃ praṇidadhe kule tasya mahīpateḥ // Saund_2.48 //
children.translated_text: Resolved upon his birth in the family of that ruler. // 2.48 //

children.text: tasyā devī nṛdevasya māyā nāma tadābhavat /
children.translated_text: The queen of that god-among-men was named <s>Māyā</s> —

children.text: vītakrodhatamomāyā māyeva divi devatā // Saund_2.49 //
children.translated_text: Free from anger, darkness, and illusion, like a divine <s>Māyā</s> in heaven. // 2.49 //

children.text: svapne 'tha samaye garbhamāviśantaṃ dadarśa sā /
children.translated_text: In a dream, at the proper time, she beheld entering her womb

children.text: ṣaḍdantaṃ vāraṇaṃ śvetamairāvatamivaujasā // Saund_2.50 //
children.translated_text: A white elephant with six tusks, mighty like <s>Airāvata</s>. // 2.50 //

children.text: taṃ vinidiśiśuḥ śrutvā svapnaṃ svapnavido dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing that dream, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> learned in the interpretation of dreams foretold

children.text: tasya janma kumārasya lakṣmīdharmayaśobhṛtaḥ // Saund_2.51 //
children.translated_text: The birth of a prince who would bear fortune, <s>Dharma</s>, and fame. // 2.51 //

children.text: tasya sattvaviśeṣasya jātau jātikṣayaiṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the birth of that extraordinary being, who sought the destruction of birth,

children.text: sācalā pracacālorvī taraṅgābhihateva nauḥ // Saund_2.52 //
children.translated_text: The immovable earth trembled, like a ship struck by waves. // 2.52 //

children.text: sūryaraśmibhirakliṣṭaṃ puṣpavarṣaṃ papāta khāt /
children.translated_text: A shower of flowers, untouched by sunbeams, fell from the sky,

children.text: digvāraṇakarādhūtād vanāccaitrarathādiva // Saund_2.53 //
children.translated_text: As if from the <s>Caitraratha</s> forest shaken by the trunks of the elephants of the quarters. // 2.53 //

children.text: divi dundubhayo nedurdīvyatāṃ marutāmiva /
children.translated_text: Divine drums sounded in the sky, as if the <s>Maruts</s> (storm gods) were sporting;

children.text: didīpe 'bhyadhikaṃ sūryaḥ śivaśca pavano vavau // Saund_2.54 //
children.translated_text: The sun shone with extraordinary brilliance, and an auspicious wind blew. // 2.54 //

children.text: tutuṣustuṣitāścaiva śuddhāvāsāśca devatāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Tuṣita</s> gods and the deities of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) rejoiced,

children.text: saddharmabahumānena sattvānāṃ cānukampayā // Saund_2.55 //
children.translated_text: Out of reverence for the true <s>Dharma</s> and out of compassion for beings. // 2.55 //

children.text: samāyayau yaśaḥketuṃ śreyaḥketukaraḥ paraḥ /
children.translated_text: He, the supreme one, a banner of glory bringing about the banner of the highest good, arrived;

children.text: babhrāje śāntayā lakṣmyā dharmo vigrahavāniva // Saund_2.56 //
children.translated_text: He shone with tranquil beauty, like <s>Dharma</s> incarnate. // 2.56 //

children.text: devyāmapi yavīyasyāmaraṇyāmiva pāvakaḥ /
children.translated_text: And from the younger queen, like fire from the fire-altar,

children.text: nando nāma suto jajñe nityānandakaraḥ kule // Saund_2.57 //
children.translated_text: A son named <s>Nanda</s> was born, bringing perpetual joy to the family. // 2.57 //

children.text: dīrghabāhurmahāvakṣāḥ siṃhāṃso vṛṣabhekṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Long-armed, broad-chested, lion-shouldered, bull-eyed,

children.text: vapuṣāgryeṇa yo nāma sundaropapadaṃ dadhe // Saund_2.58 //
children.translated_text: He, by his supreme physical form, bore a name befitting — '<s>Sundara</s>' (the Beautiful). // 2.58 //

children.text: madhumāsa iva prāptaścandro nava ivoditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like the arrival of the month of spring, like a new moon risen,

children.text: aṅgavāniva cānaṅgaḥ sa babhau kāntayā śriyā // Saund_2.59 //
children.translated_text: He, though bodiless [like <s>Kāma</s>] yet possessing limbs, shone with lovely beauty. // 2.59 //

children.text: sa tau saṃvardhayāmāsa narendraḥ parayā mudā /
children.translated_text: The king raised those two with supreme delight,

children.text: arthaḥ sajjanahastastho dharmakāmau mahāniva // Saund_2.60 //
children.translated_text: Like a great wealth in the hands of a good man [that nurtures] both <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Kāma</s> (love). // 2.60 //

children.text: tasya kālena satputrau vavṛdhāte bhavāya tau /
children.translated_text: In time, those two good sons grew up for the prosperity [of the family],

children.text: āryasyārambhamahato dharmārthāviva bhūtaye // Saund_2.61 //
children.translated_text: Like <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Artha</s> (wealth) of a noble one with great undertakings, for [worldly] benefit. // 2.61 //

children.text: tayoḥ satputrayormadhye śākyarājo rarāja saḥ /
children.translated_text: Between those two good sons, the <s>Śākya</s> king shone resplendent,

children.text: madhyadeśa iva vyakto himavatpāriyātrayoḥ // Saund_2.62 //
children.translated_text: Like the clearly visible <s>Madhyadeśa</s> (central region) between the <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Pāriyātra</s> mountains. // 2.62 //

children.text: tatastayoḥ saṃskṛtayoḥ krameṇa narendrasūnvoḥ kṛtavidyayośca /
children.translated_text: Then, when those two sons of the king had been duly consecrated and had completed their education,

children.text: kāmeṣvajasraṃ pramamāda nandaḥ sarvārthasiddhastu na saṃrarañja // Saund_2.63 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> indulged ceaselessly in pleasures, while <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> (the one whose every aim is fulfilled) was not attracted [to them]. // 2.63 //

children.text: sa prekṣyaiva hi jīrṇamāturaṃ ca mṛtaṃ ca vimṛśan jagadanabhijñamārtacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: For, having seen the aged, the sick, and the dead, reflecting upon the ignorant world, he was distressed in heart;

children.text: hṛdayagataparaghṛṇo na viṣayaratimagamajjananamaraṇabhayamabhito vijighāṃsuḥ // Saund_2.64 //
children.translated_text: With compassion for others arising in his heart, he did not pursue the enjoyment of sense-objects, wishing to overcome the fear of birth and death everywhere. // 2.64 //

children.text: udvegādapunarbhave manaḥ praṇidhāya sa yayau śayitavarāṅganādanāsthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Out of alarm, setting his mind on non-return [to rebirth], he departed, indifferent to the sleeping beauties,

children.text: niśi nṛpatinilayanād vanagamanakṛtamanāḥ sarasa iva mathitanalināt kalahaṃsaḥ // Saund_2.65 //
children.translated_text: From the royal palace at night, resolved upon going to the forest, like a royal swan from a lake whose lotuses have been churned. // 2.65 //

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "rājavarṇana" nāma dvitīyaḥ sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda Mahākāvya</s>, the Second Canto, named 'The Description of the King,' is completed.

children.text:
tṛtīyaḥ sargaḥ
tathāgata varṇana
children.translated_text:
Third Canto:
The Description of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tapase tataḥ kapilavāstu hayagajarathaughasaṃkulam /
children.translated_text: Then, for the sake of austerity, [leaving] <s>Kapilavastu</s>, teeming with throngs of horses, elephants, and chariots,

children.text: śrīmadabhayapranuraktajanaṃ sa vihāya niścitamanā vanaṃ yayau // Saund_3.1 //
children.translated_text: Prosperous, fearless, with devoted people — he departed with resolute mind to the forest. // 3.1 //

children.text: vividhāgamāṃstapasi tāṃśca vividhaniyamāśrayān munīn /
children.translated_text: Having observed the sages practicing various <s>Āgamas</s> (traditions) in their austerities and resorting to various restraints,

children.text: prekṣya sa viṣayatṛṣākṛpaṇānanavasthitaṃ tapa iti nyavartata // Saund_3.2 //
children.translated_text: He turned away, seeing them as pitiable in their thirst for sense-objects and [concluding that their] austerity was unstable. // 3.2 //

children.text: atha mokṣavādinamarāḍamupaśamamatiṃ tathodrakam /
children.translated_text: Then, having attended upon <s>Arāḍa</s>, a teacher of liberation and a proponent of tranquility, and likewise <s>Udraka</s>,

children.text: tattvakṛtamatirupāsya jahāvayamapyamārga iti mārgakovidaḥ // Saund_3.3 //
children.translated_text: With his mind set on the truth, he abandoned [them too, thinking] 'this too is not the path' — being one skilled in discerning the path. // 3.3 //

children.text: sa vicārayan jagati kiṃ nu paramamiti taṃ tamāgamam /
children.translated_text: He, inquiring 'what is the supreme in the world?' and examining this and that tradition,

children.text: niścayamanadhigataḥ parataḥ paramaṃ cacāra tapa eva duṣkaram // Saund_3.4 //
children.translated_text: Not having reached a conclusion from others, practiced the most severe austerity himself. // 3.4 //

children.text: atha naiṣa mārga iti vīkṣya tadapi vipulaṃ jahau tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing 'this is not the path,' he abandoned even that extensive austerity;

children.text: dhyānaviṣayamavagamya paraṃ bubhuje varānnamamṛtattvabuddhaye // Saund_3.5 //
children.translated_text: Comprehending the higher domain of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), he took excellent food for the realization of the immortal truth. // 3.5 //

children.text: sa suvarṇapīnayugabāhurṛṣabhagatirāyatekṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, with golden, full, and yoked arms, with the gait of a bull, with long eyes,

children.text: plakṣamavaniruhamabhyagamat paramasya niścayavidherbubhutsayā // Saund_3.6 //
children.translated_text: Approached a <s>plakṣa</s> (fig) tree, an earthly tree, with the desire to discover the method of supreme determination. // 3.6 //

children.text: upaviśya tatra kṛtabuddhiracaladhṛtiradrirājavat /
children.translated_text: Sitting there with determined mind, with immovable firmness like the king of mountains,

children.text: mārabalamajayadugramatho bubudhe padaṃ śivamahāryamavyayam // Saund_3.7 //
children.translated_text: He conquered the fierce army of <s>Māra</s>, and then realized the auspicious, noble, and imperishable state. // 3.7 //

children.text: avagamya taṃ ca kṛtakāryamamṛtamanaso divaukasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Realizing that he had accomplished his purpose and [attained] the immortal, the celestial beings, joyful in mind,

children.text: harṣatulamagaman muditā vimukhī tu mārapariṣat pracukṣubhe // Saund_3.8 //
children.translated_text: Were transported to the summit of delight, while the host of <s>Māra</s>, dismayed, was thrown into turmoil. // 3.8 //

children.text: sanagā ca bhūḥ pravicacāla hutabahasakhaḥ śivo vavau /
children.translated_text: The earth together with its mountains trembled, an auspicious wind blew with [the warmth of] a companion of fire,

children.text: nedurapi ca suradundubhayaḥ pravavarṣa cāmbudharavarjitaṃ nabhaḥ // Saund_3.9 //
children.translated_text: The divine drums sounded, and the sky rained though free of clouds. // 3.9 //

children.text: avabudhya caiva paramārthamajaramanukampayā vibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Having realized the supreme truth — ageless — the omnipresent one, out of compassion,

children.text: nityamamṛtamupadarśayituṃ sa varāṇasīparikarāmayāt purīm // Saund_3.10 //
children.translated_text: Proceeded to the city surrounded by <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in order to reveal the eternal immortal [truth]. // 3.10 //

children.text: atha dharmacakramṛtanābhi dhṛtimatisamādhinemimat /
children.translated_text: Then, the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Law) — with truth as its nave, with resolution, insight, and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) as its rim —

children.text: tatra vinayaniyamāramṛṣirjagato hitāya pariṣadyavartayat // Saund_3.11 //
children.translated_text: That sage of discipline and restraint, for the benefit of the world, set in motion in the assembly. // 3.11 //

children.text: iti duḥkhametadiyamasya samudayalatā pravartikā /
children.translated_text: 'This is suffering, this is the creeping vine of its origin that sets it in motion,

children.text: śāntiriyamayamupāya iti pravibhāgaśaḥ paramidaṃ catuṣṭayam // Saund_3.12 //
children.translated_text: This is cessation, this is the means' — thus, distinctly, [he proclaimed] this supreme fourfold [truth]. // 3.12 //

children.text: abhidhāya ca triparivartamatulamanivartyamuttamam /
children.translated_text: And having declared the three turnings — incomparable, irreversible, and supreme —

children.text: dvādaśaniyatavikalpaṃ ṛṣirvinināya kauṇḍinasagotramāditaḥ // Saund_3.13 //
children.translated_text: With twelve fixed divisions, the sage first guided [to liberation] <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> and his companions. // 3.13 //

children.text: sa hi doṣasāgaramagādhamupadhijalamādhijantukam /
children.translated_text: For he himself crossed the fathomless ocean of faults — with the waters of conditions (<s>upadhi</s>), teeming with creatures of affliction,

children.text: krodhamadabhayataraṅgacalaṃ pratatāra lokamapi ca vyatārayat // Saund_3.14 //
children.translated_text: Turbulent with waves of anger, intoxication, and fear — and he also ferried the world across. // 3.14 //

children.text: sa vinīya kāśiṣu gayeṣu bahujanamatho girivraje /
children.translated_text: Having guided many people among the <s>Kāśis</s>, at <s>Gayā</s>, and then at <s>Girivraja</s> (Rājagṛha),

children.text: pitryamapi paramakāruṇiko nagaraṃ yayāvanujighṛkṣayā tadā // Saund_3.15 //
children.translated_text: The supremely compassionate one then went to his ancestral city, out of the wish to show kindness. // 3.15 //

children.text: viṣayātmakasya hi janasya bahuvividhamārgasevinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For to people devoted to sense-objects, who follow many and varied paths —

children.text: sūryasadṛśavapurabhyudito vijahāra sūrya iva gautamastamaḥ // Saund_3.16 //
children.translated_text: Risen with a radiance rivaling the sun, <s>Gautama</s> dispelled darkness like the sun itself. // Saund_3.16 //

children.text: abhitastataḥ kapilavāstu paramaśubhavāstusaṃstutam /
children.translated_text: All around <s>Kapilavastu</s>, praised for its supremely auspicious dwellings,

children.text: vastumatiśuci śivopavanaṃ sa dadarśa niḥspṛhatayā yathā vanam // Saund_3.17 //
children.translated_text: he beheld the exceedingly pure, auspicious park as though it were merely a forest, with detachment. // Saund_3.17 //

children.text: aparigrahaḥ sa hi babhūva niyatamatirātmanīśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: For he was free from possessions, of resolute mind, and master of himself;

children.text: naikavidhabhayakareṣu kimu svajanasvadeśajanamitravastuṣu // Saund_3.18 //
children.translated_text: how much less [would he be attached] to kinsmen, fellow citizens, friends, or property — things that cause manifold fears? // Saund_3.18 //

children.text: pratipūjayā na sa jaharṣa na ca śucamavajñayāgamat /
children.translated_text: He did not rejoice at honor, nor did he come to grief at disrespect;

children.text: niścitamatirasicandanayorna jagāma duḥkhasukhayośca vikriyām // Saund_3.19 //
children.translated_text: of settled mind, like sandalwood mixed [with other substances], he underwent no alteration from pleasure or pain. // Saund_3.19 //

children.text: atha pārthivaḥ samupalabhya sutamupagataṃ tathāgatam /
children.translated_text: Then the king, learning that his son had come — the <s>Tathāgata</s> had arrived —

children.text: tūrṇamabahuturagānugataḥ sutadarśanotsukatayābhiniryayau // Saund_3.20 //
children.translated_text: hastily went forth, attended by few horses, eager to see his son. // Saund_3.20 //

children.text: sugatastathāgatamavekṣya narapatimadhīramāśayā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Sugata</s>, seeing the king thus arrived, with unsteady disposition,

children.text: śeṣamapi ca janamaśrumukhaṃ vininīṣayā gaganamutpapāta ha // Saund_3.21 //
children.translated_text: and the rest of the people too with tear-stained faces, wishing to lead them [to the truth], rose up into the sky. // Saund_3.21 //

children.text: sa vicakrame divi bhuvīva punarupaviveśa tasthivān /
children.translated_text: He strode through the sky as if on earth, then descended and stood still,

children.text: niścalamatiraśayiṣṭa punarbahudhābhavat punarabhūttathaikadhā // Saund_3.22 //
children.translated_text: then, with motionless mind, reclined, then became manifold, and then became one again. // Saund_3.22 //

children.text: salile kṣitāviva cacāra jalamiva viveśa medinīm /
children.translated_text: He walked on water as if on ground, and entered the earth as if into water;

children.text: megha iva divi vavarṣa punaḥ punarajvalannava ivodito raviḥ // Saund_3.23 //
children.translated_text: like a cloud he rained in the sky, and again blazed forth like the newly risen sun. // Saund_3.23 //

children.text: yugapajjvalan jvalanavacca jalamavasṛjaṃśca meghavat /
children.translated_text: Simultaneously blazing like fire and releasing water like a cloud,

children.text: taptakanakasadṛśaprabhayā sa babhau pradīpta iva sandhyayā ghanaḥ // Saund_3.24 //
children.translated_text: he shone with a radiance like molten gold, like a cloud illumined by the sunset. // Saund_3.24 //

children.text: tamudīkṣya hemamaṇijālavalayinamivotthitaṃ dhvajam /
children.translated_text: Beholding him, like a banner risen aloft encircled with nets of gold and jewels,

children.text: prītimagamadatulāṃ nṛpatirjanatā natāśca bahumānamabhyayuḥ // Saund_3.25 //
children.translated_text: the king attained incomparable joy, and the people bowed down and approached with great reverence. // Saund_3.25 //

children.text: atha bhājanīkṛtamavekṣya manujapatimṛddhisaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that the lord of men had been made a fitting vessel by [this display of] supernatural attainments,

children.text: paurajanamapi ca tatpravaṇaṃ nijagāda dharmavinayaṃ vināyakaḥ // Saund_3.26 //
children.translated_text: and that the townspeople too were inclined [toward the teaching], the Guide proclaimed the <s>Dharma</s> and the discipline (<s>Vinaya</s>). // Saund_3.26 //

children.text: nṛpatistataḥ prathamamāpa phalamamṛtadharmasiddhaye /
children.translated_text: The king thereupon first obtained the fruit for the attainment of the deathless <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: dharmamatulamadhigamya munermuṃnaye nanāma sa yato gurāviva // Saund_3.27 //
children.translated_text: having realized the incomparable <s>Dharma</s> of the sage, he bowed to the sage as to a teacher indeed. // Saund_3.27 //

children.text: bahavaḥ prasannamanaso 'tha jananamaraṇārtibhīravaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then many, with minds made clear, fearful of the terrors of birth and death,

children.text: śākyatanayavṛṣabhāḥ kṛtino vṛṣabhā ivānalabhayāt pravavrajuḥ // Saund_3.28 //
children.translated_text: bulls among the sons of the <s>Śākyas</s>, accomplished ones, went forth [into homelessness] like bulls fleeing from a fire. // Saund_3.28 //

children.text: vijahustu ye 'pi na gṛhāṇi tanayapitṛmātrapekṣayā /
children.translated_text: But even those who did not leave their homes, out of regard for sons, fathers, and mothers,

children.text: te 'pi niyamavidhimāmaraṇājjagṛhuśca yuktamanasaśca dadhrire // Saund_3.29 //
children.translated_text: undertook the rules of restraint until death, and, with yoked minds, held fast [to them]. // Saund_3.29 //

children.text: na jihiṃsa sūkṣmamapi jantumapi paravadhopajīvinaḥ /
children.translated_text: No one harmed even the tiniest creature, not even those who lived by killing others;

children.text: kiṃ bata vipulaguṇaḥ kulajaḥ sadayaḥ sadā kimu munerupāsayā // Saund_3.30 //
children.translated_text: how much less [would they do so], being of abundant virtue, well-born, always compassionate — especially under the influence of the sage? // Saund_3.30 //

children.text: akṛśodyamaḥ kṛśadhano 'pi paraparibhavāsaho 'pi san /
children.translated_text: Even one of undiminished effort, though poor in wealth and intolerant of another's contempt,

children.text: nānyadhanamapahāra tathā bhujagādivānyavibhavāddhi vivyathe // Saund_3.31 //
children.translated_text: did not steal another's property, for he shrank from another's possessions as from a serpent. // Saund_3.31 //

children.text: vibhavānvito 'pi taruṇo 'pi viṣayacapalendriyo 'pi san /
children.translated_text: Even one endowed with wealth, young, and with senses restless for pleasures,

children.text: naiva ca parayuvatīragamat paramaṃ hi tā dahanato 'pyamanyata // Saund_3.32 //
children.translated_text: did not approach another's wife, for he regarded her as [more dangerous] than fire itself. // Saund_3.32 //

children.text: anṛtaṃ jagāda na ca kaścidṛtamapi jajalpa nāpriyam /
children.translated_text: No one spoke an untruth, and though anyone might speak what is true, none said what was disagreeable;

children.text: ślakṣṇamapi ca na jagāvahitaṃ hitamapyuvāca na ca paiśunāca yat // Saund_3.33 //
children.translated_text: even what was smooth he did not speak if harmful, and he spoke what was beneficial without malice. // Saund_3.33 //

children.text: manasā lulobha na ca jātu paravasuṣu gṛddhamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: No one ever coveted in mind the possessions of others, though of acquisitive disposition;

children.text: kāmasukhamasukhato vimṛśan vijahāra tṛpta iva tatra sajjanaḥ // Saund_3.34 //
children.translated_text: reflecting on the pleasure of desires as painful, the good people there lived as though content. // Saund_3.34 //

children.text: na parasya kaścidapaghātamapi ca saghṛṇo vyacintayat /
children.translated_text: No one, even compassionate, so much as contemplated the harm of another;

children.text: mātṛpitṛsutasuhṛtsadṛśaṃ sa dadarśa tatra hi parasparaṃ janaḥ // Saund_3.35 //
children.translated_text: for the people there regarded each other as mothers, fathers, sons, and friends. // Saund_3.35 //

children.text: niyataṃ bhaviṣyati paratra bhavadapi ca bhūtamapyatho /
children.translated_text: 'What will surely be in the next life was also in the past;

children.text: karmaphalamapi ca lokagatirniyateti darśanamavāpa sādhu ca // Saund_3.36 //
children.translated_text: and the fruit of action and the course of the world are certain' — such was the right view they attained. // Saund_3.36 //

children.text: iti karmaṇā daśavidhena paramakuśalena bhūriṇā /
children.translated_text: Thus, through the tenfold wholesome action, supreme and abundant,

children.text: bhraṃśini śithilaguṇo 'pi yuge vijahāra tatra munisaṃśrayājjanaḥ // Saund_3.37 //
children.translated_text: the people there lived under the sage's shelter, though of relaxed qualities in a declining age. // Saund_3.37 //

children.text: na ca tatra kaścidupapattisukhamabhilalāṣa tairguṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: No one there, through those virtues, longed for the pleasure of [heavenly] rebirth;

children.text: sarvamaśivamavagamya bhavaṃ bhavasaṃkṣayāya vavṛte na janmane // Saund_3.38 //
children.translated_text: understanding all existence to be inauspicious, they turned toward the extinction of existence, not toward [further] birth. // Saund_3.38 //

children.text: akathaṃkathā gṛhiṇa eva paramapariśuddhadṛṣṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Free from doubt, even the householders themselves, of supremely purified vision,

children.text: strotasi hi vavṛtire bahavo rajasaṃstanutvamapi cakrire pare // Saund_3.39 //
children.translated_text: many entered the stream [of the path], and others further attenuated their impurities (<s>rajas</s>). // Saund_3.39 //

children.text: vavṛte 'tra yo 'pi viṣayeṣu vibhavasadṛśeṣu kaścana /
children.translated_text: And whoever among them still engaged in sense-pleasures resembling [worldly] prosperity,

children.text: tyāgāvinayaniyamābhirato vijahāra so 'pi na cacāla satpathāt // Saund_3.40 //
children.translated_text: even he, delighting in generosity, discipline, and restraint, did not deviate from the true path. // Saund_3.40 //

children.text: api ca svato 'pi parato 'pi na bhayamabhavanna daivataḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, there was no fear from oneself, from others, or from the divine;

children.text: tatra ca susukhasubhikṣaguṇairjahṛṣuḥ prajāḥ kṛtayuge manoriva // Saund_3.41 //
children.translated_text: and there the people rejoiced in happiness, abundance, and virtue, as if their minds were in the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (Golden Age). // Saund_3.41 //

children.text: iti muditamanāmayaṃ nirāpat kururaghupūrupuropamaṃ puraṃ tat /
children.translated_text: Thus that city, joyful, free from illness, free from calamity, comparable to the cities of the <s>Kurus</s>, <s>Raghus</s>, and <s>Pūrus</s>,

children.text: abhavadabhayadaiśike maharṣau viharati tatra śivāya vītarāge // Saund_3.42 //
children.translated_text: flourished for the welfare [of all], while the great sage, the guide who gives fearlessness, the passionless one, dwelt there. // Saund_3.42 //

children.text: saundaranande mahākāvye "tathāgatavarṇana" nāma tṛtīya sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third canto, named 'The Description of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,' in the <s>Saundarānanda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.

children.text:
caturthaḥ sargaḥ
bhāryāyācitaka
children.translated_text: Fourth Canto: 'The Wife's Entreaty'

children.text: munau bruvāṇe 'pi tu tatra dharmaṃ dharmaṃ prati jñātiṣu cādṛteṣu /
children.translated_text: But while the sage was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> there, and while his kinsmen were respectful toward the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: prāsādasaṃstho madanaikakāryaḥ priyāsahāyo vijahāra nandaḥ // Saund_4.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, dwelling in his palace, occupied solely with love, sported with his beloved. // Saund_4.1 //

children.text: sa cakravākyeva hi cakravākastayā sametaḥ priyayā priyārhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a <s>Cakravāka</s> drake with its mate, he, worthy of love, together with his beloved,

children.text: nācintayad vaiśramaṇaṃ na śakraṃ tatsthānahetoḥ kuta eva dharmam // Saund_4.2 //
children.translated_text: thought neither of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (<s>Kubera</s>) nor of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), nor of their positions — how much less then of <s>Dharma</s>! // Saund_4.2 //

children.text: lakṣmyā ca rūpeṇa ca sundarīti stambhena garveṇa ca māninīti /
children.translated_text: '<s>Sundarī</s>' she was called for her beauty and form; '<s>Māninī</s>' for her stateliness and pride;

children.text: dīptyā ca mānena ca bhāminīti yāto babhāṣe trividhena nāmnā // Saund_4.3 //
children.translated_text: and '<s>Bhāminī</s>' for her radiance and dignity — thus she bore a threefold name. // Saund_4.3 //

children.text: sā hāsahaṃsā nayanadvirephā pīnastanātyunnatapadmakośā /
children.translated_text: She whose laughter was [like] geese, whose eyes [like] bees, whose full breasts [like] exceedingly high lotus buds —

children.text: bhūyo babhāse svakuloditena strīpadminī nandadivākareṇa // Saund_4.4 //
children.translated_text: that woman-lotus shone forth even more through <s>Nanda</s>, the sun risen from her own family. // Saund_4.4 //

children.text: rūpeṇa cātyantamanohareṇa rūpānurūpeṇa ca ceṣṭitena /
children.translated_text: With her exceedingly captivating form and conduct befitting that form,

children.text: manuṣyaloke hi tadā babhūva sā sundarī strīṣu nareṣu nandaḥ // Saund_4.5 //
children.translated_text: at that time in the human world, she, <s>Sundarī</s>, among women, and <s>Nanda</s> among men, [were preeminent]. // Saund_4.5 //

children.text: sā devatā nandanacāriṇīva kulasya nandījananaśca nandaḥ /
children.translated_text: She, like a goddess roaming in <s>Nandana</s> [garden], and <s>Nanda</s>, the joy-bringer of his family —

children.text: atītya martyānanupetya devān sṛṣṭāvabhūtāmiva bhūtadhātrā // Saund_4.6 //
children.translated_text: surpassing mortals yet not attaining divinity, they seemed as though specially created by the Creator. // Saund_4.6 //

children.text: tāṃ sundarī cenna labheta nandaḥ sā vā niṣeveta na taṃ natabhrūḥ /
children.translated_text: If <s>Nanda</s> had not obtained <s>Sundarī</s>, or if she, the arched-browed one, had not devoted herself to him,

children.text: dvandvaṃ dhruvaṃ tadvikalaṃ na śobhetānyonyahīnāviva rātricandrau // Saund_4.7 //
children.translated_text: that pair, incomplete, would surely not have shone — like night and moon deprived of each other. // Saund_4.7 //

children.text: kandarparatyoriva lakṣyabhūtaṃ pramodanāndyoriva nīḍabhūtam /
children.translated_text: As though the target of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love) and <s>Rati</s>, as though the nest of delight and bliss,

children.text: praharṣatuṣṭyoriva pātrabhūtaṃ dvandvaṃ sahāraṃsta madāndhabhūtam // Saund_4.8 //
children.translated_text: as though the vessel of rapture and contentment — that pair, blinded by passion, sported together. // Saund_4.8 //

children.text: parasparodvīkṣaṇatatparākṣaṃ parasparavyāhṛtasaktacittam /
children.translated_text: With eyes intent on gazing at each other, with minds absorbed in each other's words,

children.text: parasparāśleṣahṛtāṅgarāgaṃ parasparaṃ tanmithunaṃ jahāra // Saund_4.9 //
children.translated_text: with body-paint smeared by each other's embraces — that pair delighted in each other. // Saund_4.9 //

children.text: bhāvānuraktau girinirjharasthau tau kinnarīkiṃpuruṣāvivobhau /
children.translated_text: Passionately devoted to each other, like a <s>Kinnarī</s> and a <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s> by a mountain stream,

children.text: cikrīḍatuścābhivirejatuśca rūpaśriyānyonyamivākṣipantau // Saund_4.10 //
children.translated_text: they both played and shone, as though rivaling each other in the beauty of their forms. // Saund_4.10 //

children.text: anyonyasaṃrāgavivardhanena taddvandvamanyonyamarīramacca /
children.translated_text: Enhancing each other's mutual passion, that pair also delighted each other;

children.text: klamāntare 'nyonyavinodanena salīlamanyonyamamīmadacca // Saund_4.11 //
children.translated_text: and in intervals of fatigue, entertaining each other, they playfully intoxicated one another. // Saund_4.11 //

children.text: vibhūṣayāmāsa tataḥ priyāṃ sa siṣeviṣustāṃ na mṛjāvahārtham /
children.translated_text: Then he adorned his beloved, not for the purpose of cleansing but wishing to attend upon her;

children.text: svenaiva rūpeṇa vibhūṣitā hi vibhūṣaṇānāmapi bhūṣaṇaṃ sā // Saund_4.12 //
children.translated_text: for she, adorned by her own beauty alone, was the ornament even of ornaments. // Saund_4.12 //

children.text: dattvātha sā darpaṇamasya haste mamāgrato dhāraya tāvadenam /
children.translated_text: Then, placing a mirror in his hand, she said: 'Hold this before me for a moment

children.text: viśeṣakaṃ yāvadahaṃ karomītyuvāca kāntaṃ sa ca taṃ babhāra // Saund_4.13 //
children.translated_text: while I apply the <s>viśeṣaka</s> (ornamental mark)' — thus she spoke to her beloved, and he held it. // Saund_4.13 //

children.text: bhartustataḥ śmaśru nirīkṣamāṇā viśeṣakaṃ sāpi cakāra tādṛk /
children.translated_text: Then, gazing at her husband's beard, she too fashioned a similar <s>viśeṣaka</s> [on his face];

children.text: niśvāsavātena ca darpaṇasya cikitsayitvā nijaghāna nandaḥ // Saund_4.14 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Nanda</s>, having fogged the mirror with his breath, playfully struck it. // Saund_4.14 //

children.text: sā tena ceṣṭālalitena bhartuḥ śāṭhyena cāntarmanasā jahāsa /
children.translated_text: At that playful and coy gesture of her husband, she laughed inwardly with hidden mischief,

children.text: bhavecca ruṣṭā kila nāma tasmai lalāṭajihmāṃ bhṛkuṭiṃ cakāra // Saund_4.15 //
children.translated_text: and, pretending to be angry with him, she furrowed her brow across her forehead. // Saund_4.15 //

children.text: cikṣepa karṇotpalamasya cāṃse kareṇa savyena madālasena /
children.translated_text: She tossed the ear-lotus at his shoulder with her languid left hand,

children.text: patrāṅguliṃ cārdhanimīlitākṣe vaktre 'sya tāmeva vinirdudhāva // Saund_4.16 //
children.translated_text: and thrust that same leaf-like finger at his face as he half-closed his eyes. // Saund_4.16 //

children.text: tataścalannūpurayoktritābhyāṃ nakhaprabhodbhāsitarāṅgulibhyām /
children.translated_text: Then, before his beloved's feet — adorned with tinkling anklets, with toenails gleaming bright,

children.text: padbhyāṃ priyāyā nalinopabhābhyāṃ mūrdhnā bhayānnāma nanāma nandaḥ // Saund_4.17 //
children.translated_text: lotus-like in beauty — <s>Nanda</s> bowed his head as if in feigned fear. // Saund_4.17 //

children.text: sa muktapuṣponmiṣitena mūrdhnā tataḥ priyāyāḥ priyakṛd babhāse /
children.translated_text: Then, with his head from which flowers had fallen loose and [new ones] bloomed, the one who brought joy to his beloved shone

children.text: suvarṇavedyāmanilāvabhagnaḥ puṣpātibhārādiva nāgavṛkṣaḥ // Saund_4.18 //
children.translated_text: like a <s>Nāga</s> tree on a golden platform, bent down by the wind under the weight of blossoms. // Saund_4.18 //

children.text: sā taṃ stanodvartitahārayaṣṭirutthāpayāmāsa nipīḍya dorbhyām /
children.translated_text: She, with the string of pearls pushed up by her breasts, raised him up, pressing him with her arms,

children.text: kathaṃ kṛto 'sīti jahāsa coccairmukhena sācīkṛtakuṇḍalena // Saund_4.19 //
children.translated_text: and laughed aloud, saying 'What have you done?' — with her face turned aside, earrings swinging. // Saund_4.19 //

children.text: patyustato darpaṇasaktapāṇermuhurmuhurvaktramavekṣamāṇā /
children.translated_text: Then, again and again gazing at the face of her husband, who held the mirror in his hand,

children.text: tamālapatrārdratale kapole samāpayāmāsa viśeṣakaṃ tat // Saund_4.20 //
children.translated_text: she completed that <s>viśeṣaka</s> on her cheek, with its surface still moist from the <s>tamālapatra</s> (bay-leaf pigment). // Saund_4.20 //

children.text: tasyā mukhaṃ tat satamālapatraṃ tāmrādharauṣṭhaṃ cikurāyatākṣam /
children.translated_text: Her face, with its <s>tamālapatra</s> marks, coppery lower lip, and eyes long as locks of hair,

children.text: raktādhikāgraṃ patitadvirephaṃ saśaivalaṃ padmamivābabhāse // Saund_4.21 //
children.translated_text: with reddish tips where bees had alighted, shone like a lotus with moss. // Saund_4.21 //

children.text: nandastato darpaṇamādareṇa bibhrattadāmaṇḍanasākṣibhūtam /
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> then, holding the mirror with care, serving as witness to her adornment,

children.text: viśeṣakāvekṣaṇakekarākṣo laḍat priyāyā vadanaṃ dadarśa // Saund_4.22 //
children.translated_text: with eyes squinting as he examined the <s>viśeṣaka</s>, beheld his beloved's face with tenderness. // Saund_4.22 //

children.text: tatkuṇḍalādaṣṭaviśeṣakāntaṃ kāraṇḍavakliṣṭamivāravindam /
children.translated_text: Her face, with the <s>viśeṣaka</s> pressed by the earring, like a lotus chafed by a <s>Kāraṇḍava</s> duck —

children.text: nandaḥ priyāyā mukhamīkṣamāṇo bhūyaḥ priyānandakaro babhūva // Saund_4.23 //
children.translated_text: gazing at his beloved's face, <s>Nanda</s> became all the more her joy-giver. // Saund_4.23 //

children.text: vimānakalpe sa vimānagarbhe tatastathā caiva nananda nandaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s> thus delighted in that palace chamber, like an aerial mansion;

children.text: tathāgataścāgatabhaikṣakālo bhaikṣāya tasya praviveśa veśma // Saund_4.24 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the time for alms having come, entered his house for alms. // Saund_4.24 //

children.text: avāṅamukho niṣpraṇāyaśca tasthau bhrāturgṛhe 'nyasya gṛhe yathaiva /
children.translated_text: He stood with downcast face and without greeting, in his brother's house as though in a stranger's;

children.text: tasmādatho preṣyajanapramādād bhikṣāmalabdhvaiva punarjagāma // Saund_4.25 //
children.translated_text: and then, because of the servants' negligence, without even receiving alms, he departed again. // Saund_4.25 //

children.text: kācit pipeṣāṅgavilepanaṃ hi vāso 'ṅganā kācidavāsayacca /
children.translated_text: For one woman was grinding body-ointment, and another was perfuming garments;

children.text: ayojayat snānavidhiṃ tathānyā jagranthuranyāḥ surabhīḥ srajaśca // Saund_4.26 //
children.translated_text: another was preparing the bathing ritual, and others were stringing fragrant garlands. // Saund_4.26 //

children.text: tasmin gṛhe bharturataścarantyaḥ krīḍānurūpaṃ lalitaṃ niyogam /
children.translated_text: As they went about the master's house performing charming duties suited to their play,

children.text: kāścinna buddhaṃ dadṛśuryuvatyo buddhasya vaiṣā niyataṃ manīṣā // Saund_4.27 //
children.translated_text: some young women did not see the <s>Buddha</s> — though this was surely the <s>Buddha</s>'s own intention. // Saund_4.27 //

children.text: kācit sthitā tatra tu harmyapṛṣṭhe gavākṣapakṣe praṇidhāya cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: But a certain woman, standing on the roof terrace, fixing her gaze through the lattice window,

children.text: viniṣpatantaṃ sugataṃ dadarśa payodagarbhādiva dīptamarkam // Saund_4.28 //
children.translated_text: saw the <s>Sugata</s> departing — like the brilliant sun [emerging] from a mass of clouds. // Saund_4.28 //

children.text: sā gauravaṃ tatra vicārya bhartuḥ svayā ca bhaktyārhatayārhataśca /
children.translated_text: Considering both the reverence due to her master and her own devotion and the worthiness of the worthy one,

children.text: nandasya tasthau purato vivakṣustadājñayā ceti tadācacakṣe // Saund_4.29 //
children.translated_text: she stood before <s>Nanda</s> wishing to speak, and with his permission, she reported thus: // Saund_4.29 //

children.text: anugrahāyāsya janasya śaṅke gururgṛhaṃ no bhagavān praviṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Out of grace for this household, I think the teacher, the Blessed One, has entered our home;

children.text: bhikṣāmalabdhvā giramāsanaṃ vā śūnyādaraṇyādiva yāti bhūyaḥ // Saund_4.30 //
children.translated_text: but not receiving alms, nor a word, nor a seat, he departs again, as from an empty forest.' // Saund_4.30 //

children.text: śrutvā maharṣeḥ sa gṛhapraveśaṃ satkārahīnaṃ ca punaḥ prayāṇam /
children.translated_text: Hearing of the great sage's entry into his home, and of his departure without proper reception,

children.text: cacāla citrābharaṇāmbarasrakkalpadrumo dhūta ivānilena // Saund_4.31 //
children.translated_text: he trembled — like a wish-fulfilling tree with resplendent ornaments, garments, and garlands, shaken by the wind. // Saund_4.31 //

children.text: kṛtvāñjaliṃ mūrdhani padmakalpaṃ tataḥ sa kāntāṃ gamanaṃ yayāce /
children.translated_text: Placing his lotus-like palms in <s>añjali</s> at his forehead, he then asked permission of his beloved to go:

children.text: karttu gamiṣyāmi gurau praṇāmaṃ māmabhyanujñātumihārhasīti // Saund_4.32 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall go to pay obeisance to the teacher — please grant me leave here.' // Saund_4.32 //

children.text: sā vepamānā parisasvaje taṃ śālaṃ latā vātasamīriteva /
children.translated_text: She, trembling, embraced him, like a creeper stirred by the wind [clinging to] a <s>Śāla</s> tree.

children.text: dadarśa cāśruplutalolanetrā dīrghe ca niśvasya vaco 'bhyuvāca // Saund_4.33 //
