children.translated_text: She gazed with tear-flooded, trembling eyes, and heaving a long sigh, she spoke these words: [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.33]

children.text: nāhaṃ yiyāsorgurudarśanārthamarhāmi kartuṃ tava dharmapīḍām /
children.translated_text: "I who do not wish to go should not cause you the torment of duty for the sake of seeing your teacher.

children.text: gacchāryaputraihi ca śīghrameva viśeṣako yāvadayaṃ na śuṣkaḥ // Saund_4.34 //
children.translated_text: Go, noble son, and quickly — before this <s>viśeṣaka</s> (ornamental forehead mark) has dried!" [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.34]

children.text: sacedbhavestvaṃ khalu dīrghasūtro daṇḍaṃ mahāntaṃ tvayi pātayeyam /
children.translated_text: "But if you should be long in returning, I would impose a great punishment upon you;

children.text: muhurmuhustvāṃ śayitaṃ kucābhyāṃ vibodhayeyaṃ ca na cālapeyam // Saund_4.35 //
children.translated_text: I would wake you again and again as you lie sleeping, with my breasts, but would not speak to you!" [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.35]

children.text: athāpyanāśyānaviśeṣakāyāṃ mayyeṣyasi tvaṃ tvaritaṃ tatastvām /
children.translated_text: "And if you come quickly to me whose <s>viśeṣaka</s> has not yet dried,

children.text: nipīḍayiṣyāmi bhujadvayena nirbhūṣaṇenārdravilepanena // Saund_4.36 //
children.translated_text: I will press you with both my arms — unadorned and moist with unguent." [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.36]

children.text: ityevamuktaśca nipīḍitaśca tayāsavarṇasvanayā jagāda /
children.translated_text: Thus spoken to and embraced by her whose voice was like his own,

children.text: evaṃ kariṣyāmi vimuñca caṇḍi yāvad gururdūragato na me saḥ // Saund_4.37 //
children.translated_text: he said: 'I shall do so; release me, fierce one, before that teacher of mine has gone far!' [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.37]

children.text: tataḥ stanodvartitatacandanābhyāṃ mukto bhujābhyāṃ na tu mānasena /
children.translated_text: Then, released from her arms — with their sandalwood paste rising from her breasts — but not from his mind,

children.text: vihāya veṣaṃ madanānurūpaṃ satkārayogyaṃ sa vapurbabhāra // Saund_4.38 //
children.translated_text: he put aside his attire suited for love and assumed a form worthy of paying respects. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.38]

children.text: sā taṃ prayāntaṃ ramaṇaṃ pradadhyau pradhyānaśūnyasthitaniścalākṣī /
children.translated_text: She gazed at her departing lover, standing motionless with unblinking eyes, vacant in contemplation,

children.text: sthitoccakarṇā vyapaviddhaśaṣpā bhrāntaṃ mṛgam bhrāntamukhī mṛgīva // Saund_4.39 //
children.translated_text: like a doe with ears raised high, having dropped the grass, watching her wandering mate with a bewildered face. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.39]

children.text: didṛkṣayākṣiptamanā munestu nandaḥ prayāṇaṃ prati tatvare ca /
children.translated_text: But <s>Nanda</s>, his mind drawn forth by the desire to see the sage, hastened toward the departure;

children.text: vivṛttadṛṣṭiśca śanairyayau tāṃ karīva paśyan sa laḍatkareṇum // Saund_4.40 //
children.translated_text: yet he went slowly with his gaze turned back toward her, like an elephant watching a playful she-elephant. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.40]

children.text: chātodarīṃ pīnapayodharoruṃ sa sundarīṃ rukmadarīmivādreḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, gazing sideways at <s>Sundarī</s> — slim-waisted, with full breasts and thighs — as at a golden cave of a mountain,

children.text: kākṣeṇa paśyan na tatarpa nandaḥ pibannivaikena jalaṃ kareṇa // Saund_4.41 //
children.translated_text: was not satisfied, like one drinking water with only one hand. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.41]

children.text: taṃ gauravaṃ buddhagataṃ cakarṣa bhāryānurāgaḥ punarācakarṣa /
children.translated_text: The reverence he felt toward the <s>Buddha</s> drew him forward, while love for his wife drew him back;

children.text: so 'niścayānnāpi yayau na tasthau turaṃstaraṃgeṣviva rājahaṃsaḥ // Saund_4.42 //
children.translated_text: from indecision he neither went nor stood still, like a royal swan on swift-moving waves. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.42]

children.text: adarśanaṃ tūpagataśca tasyā harmyāttataścāvatatāra tūrṇam /
children.translated_text: But when he reached the point where she was out of sight, he quickly descended from the palace;

children.text: śrutvā tato nūpuranisvanaṃ sa punarlalambe hṛdaye gṛhītaḥ // Saund_4.43 //
children.translated_text: then, hearing the sound of her anklets, he was again seized by the heart and lingered. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.43]

children.text: sa kāmarāgeṇa nigṛhyamāṇo dharmānurāgeṇa ca kṛṣyamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, held back by the passion of desire and drawn forward by devotion to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: jagāma duḥkhena vivartyamānaḥ plavaḥ pratistrota ivāpagāyāḥ // Saund_4.44 //
children.translated_text: went on painfully, being tossed about, like a raft against the current of a river. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.44]

children.text: tataḥ kramairdīrghatamaiḥ pracakrame kathaṃ nu yāto na gururbhavediti /
children.translated_text: Then he proceeded with the longest strides, [thinking:] 'How [can I ensure] that the teacher has not yet gone?

children.text: svajeya tāṃ caiva viśeṣakapriyāṃ kathaṃ priyāmārdraviśeṣakāmiti // Saund_4.45 //
children.translated_text: And how [can I go] back to embrace that beloved one, fond of her <s>viśeṣaka</s>, with her moist ornamental mark?' [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.45]

children.text: atha sa pathi dadarśa muktamānaṃ pitṛnagare 'pi tathā gatābhimānam /
children.translated_text: Then on the path he saw the one free from pride, who even in his ancestral city had transcended self-regard —

children.text: daśabalamabhito vilambamānaṃ dhvajamanuyāna ivaindramarcyamānam // Saund_4.46 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten-Powered One), followed on all sides, being honored like the banner of <s>Indra</s> in a procession. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 4.46]

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "bhāryāyācitaka" nāma caturtha sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem), the fourth <s>sarga</s> (canto) named 'The Wife's Entreaty' is complete.

children.text:
pañcamaḥ sargaḥ
nandadīkṣā
children.translated_text: Fifth Canto: The Initiation of <s>Nanda</s>

children.text: athāvatīryāśvarathadvipebhyaḥ śākyā yathāsvarddhigṛhītaveṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Śākyas</s>, having descended from horses, chariots, and elephants, dressed according to their respective ranks,

children.text: mahāpaṇebhyo vyavahāriṇaśca mahāmunau bhaktivaśāt praṇemuḥ // Saund_5.1 //
children.translated_text: and the merchants from the great marketplaces, bowed before the great sage out of devotion. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.1]

children.text: kecit praṇamyānuyayurmuhūrttaṃ kecit praṇamyārthavaśena jagmuḥ /
children.translated_text: Some, after bowing, followed for a moment; some, after bowing, went on their business;

children.text: kecit svakeṣvāvasatheṣu tasthuḥ kṛtvāñjalīn vīkṣaṇatatparākṣāḥ // Saund_5.2 //
children.translated_text: some stood in their own dwellings, joining their palms, with eyes eagerly fixed on gazing. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.2]

children.text: buddhastatastatra narendramārge sroto mahadbhaktimato janasya /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Buddha</s>, on the royal road, entered with difficulty the great stream of devoted people,

children.text: jagāma duḥkhena vigāhamāno jalāgame strota ivāpagāyāḥ // Saund_5.3 //
children.translated_text: wading through as if entering the current of a river in flood. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.3]

children.text: atho mahadbhiḥ pati saṃpatadbhiḥ saṃpūjyamānāya tathāgatāya /
children.translated_text: And as the <s>Tathāgata</s> was being worshipped by great men rushing to meet him,

children.text: karttuṃ praṇāmaṃ na śaśāka nandastenābhireme tu gurormahimnā // Saund_5.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> was unable to make his salutation; yet he rejoiced in the greatness of the teacher. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.4]

children.text: svaṃ cāvasaṅgaṃ pathi nirmumukṣurbhaktiṃ janasyānyamateśva rakṣan /
children.translated_text: Wishing to free himself from attachment on the path, protecting the devotion of the people [and] the opinions of others,

children.text: nandaṃ ca gehābhimukhaṃ jighṛkṣan mārgaṃ tato 'nyaṃ sugataḥ prapede // Saund_5.5 //
children.translated_text: and wishing to take hold of <s>Nanda</s> who was heading homeward, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) took another route. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.5]

children.text: tato viviktaṃ ca viviktacetāḥ sanmārgavin mārgamabhipratasthe /
children.translated_text: Then the one of secluded mind, knower of the right path, set out upon a solitary path;

children.text: gatvāgrataścāgryatamāya tasmai nāndīvimuktāya nanāma nandaḥ // Saund_5.6 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Nanda</s>, going ahead, bowed to that foremost one, who was free from all joy [of worldly pleasure]. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.6]

children.text: śanairvrajanneva sa gauraveṇa paṭāvṛtāṃso vinatārdhakāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Walking slowly out of reverence, with his shoulder covered by a shawl, his upper body bent,

children.text: adhonibaddhāñjalirūrdhvanetraḥ sagadgadaṃ vākyamidaṃ babhāṣe // Saund_5.7 //
children.translated_text: with palms joined below and eyes directed upward, he spoke these words in a choked voice: [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.7]

children.text: prāsādasaṃstho bhagavantamantaḥpraviṣṭamaśrauṣamanugrahāya /
children.translated_text: "Standing in my palace, I heard that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had entered [the city] to bestow grace;

children.text: atastvarāvānahamabhyupeto gṛhasya kakṣyāmahato 'bhyasūyan // Saund_5.8 //
children.translated_text: therefore I have come in haste, aggrieved at the expanse of my great house. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.8]

children.text: tatsādhu sāhupriya mattpriyārtham tatrāstu bhikṣūttama bhaikṣakālaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O good one, lover of the good, for my sake who love you, let the time for alms be there, O best of <s>bhikṣus</s>;

children.text: asau hi madhyaṃ nabhaso yiyāsuḥ kālaṃ pratismārayatīva sūryaḥ // Saund_5.9 //
children.translated_text: for that sun, wishing to reach the zenith of the sky, seems to remind us of the time." [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.9]

children.text: ityevamuktaḥ praṇatena tena snehābhimānonmukhalocanena /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by that bowing one, whose eyes were upturned with affection and pride,

children.text: tādṛṅ nimittaṃ sugataścakāra nāhārakṛtyaṃ sa yathā viveda // Saund_5.10 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Sugata</s> contrived such an occasion that he [<s>Nanda</s>] did not attend to the business of food. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.10]

children.text: tataḥ sa kṛtvā munaye praṇāmaṃ gṛhaprayāṇāya matiṃ cakāra /
children.translated_text: Then, having made salutation to the sage, he [<s>Nanda</s>] resolved to return home;

children.text: anugrahārthaṃ sugatastu tasmai pātraṃ dadau puraṣkarapatranetraḥ // Saund_5.11 //
children.translated_text: but the <s>Sugata</s>, with lotus-like eyes, gave him his alms-bowl for the purpose of guiding him. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.11]

children.text: tataḥ sa loke dadataḥ phalārthaṃ pātrasya tasyāpratimasya pātram /
children.translated_text: Then he, the worthy vessel for that peerless vessel which bestows fruit upon the world's givers,

children.text: jagrāha cāpagrahaṇakṣamābhyāṃ padmopamābhyāṃ prayataḥ karābhyām // Saund_5.12 //
children.translated_text: received it reverently with both lotus-like hands, fit for such a reception. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.12]

children.text: parāṅmukhantvanyamanaskamārād vijñāya nandaḥ sugataṃ gatāstham /
children.translated_text: Perceiving that the <s>Sugata</s> had turned away, his mind elsewhere, and departed from nearby,

children.text: hastasthapātro 'pi gṛhaṃ yiyāsuḥ sasāra mārgānmunimīkṣamāṇaḥ // Saund_5.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, though wishing to go home with the bowl in hand, followed along the road, gazing at the sage. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.13]

children.text: bhāryānurāgeṇa yadā gṛhaṃ sa pātraṃ gṛhītvāpi yiyāsureva /
children.translated_text: When, out of love for his wife, he still wished to go home even after receiving the bowl,

children.text: vimohayāmāsa munistatastaṃ rathyāmukhasyāvaraṇena tasya // Saund_5.14 //
children.translated_text: the sage then bewildered him by blocking his view of the entrance to the street. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.14]

children.text: nirmokṣabījaṃ hi dadarśa tasya jñānaṃ mṛdu kleśarajaśca tīvram /
children.translated_text: For he [the <s>Buddha</s>] saw in him the seed of liberation, knowledge that was soft, and the dust of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) that was thick,

children.text: kleśānukūlaṃ viṣayātmakaṃ ca nandaṃ yatastaṃ munirācakarṣa // Saund_5.15 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Nanda</s> who was inclined toward the <s>kleśas</s> and given to sense-objects — therefore the sage drew him [along]. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.15]

children.text: saṃkleśapakṣo dvividhaśca dṛṣṭastathā dvikalpo vyavadānapakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The side of affliction is seen to be twofold, and likewise the side of purification is of two kinds:

children.text: ātmāśrayo hetubalādhikasya bāhyāśrayaḥ pratyayagauravasya // Saund_5.16 //
children.translated_text: self-dependent for one in whom the causal force predominates, and other-dependent for one in whom the force of conditions prevails. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.16]

children.text: ayatnato hetubalādhikastu nirmucyate ghaṭṭitamātra eva /
children.translated_text: One in whom the causal force predominates is liberated effortlessly, merely by being touched [by the teaching];

children.text: yatnena tu pratyayaneyabuddhirvimokṣamāpnoti parāśrayeṇa // Saund_5.17 //
children.translated_text: but one whose understanding is guided by conditions attains liberation with effort, through external support. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.17]

children.text: nandaḥ sa ca pratyayaneyacetā yaṃ śiśriye tanmayatāmavāpa /
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, whose mind was guided by conditions, attained absorption in that which he had resorted to;

children.text: yasmādimaṃ tatra cakāra yannaṃ taṃ snehapaṅkān munirujjihīrṣan // Saund_5.18 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the sage, wishing to lift him from the mire of attachment, performed that deed [i.e., initiated his ordination]. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.18]

children.text: nandastu duḥkhena viceṣṭamānaḥ śanairagatyā gurumanvagacchat /
children.translated_text: But <s>Nanda</s>, struggling painfully, slowly and reluctantly followed the teacher,

children.text: bhāryāmukhaṃ vīkṣaṇalolanetraṃ vicintayannārdraviśeṣakaṃ tat // Saund_5.19 //
children.translated_text: contemplating the face of his wife — those eyes restless with longing, that moist ornamental mark. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.19]

children.text: tato munistaṃ priyamālyahāraṃ vasantamāsena kṛtābhihāram /
children.translated_text: Then the sage led him — fond of garlands and necklaces, adorned as if by the spring season,

children.text: nināya bhagnapramadāvihāraṃ vidyāvihārābhimataṃ vihāram // Saund_5.20 //
children.translated_text: his dalliance with beautiful women now broken — to the monastery, the abode cherished for the pursuit of learning. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.20]

children.text: dīnaṃ mahākāruṇikastatastaṃ dṛṣṭvā muhūrta karuṇāyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the greatly compassionate one, seeing him dejected, feeling pity for a moment,

children.text: kareṇa cakrāṅkatalena mūrdhni pasparśa caivedamuvāca cainam // Saund_5.21 //
children.translated_text: touched his head with a hand bearing the mark of the wheel on its palm, and spoke thus to him: [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.21]

children.text: yāvanna hiṃsraḥ samupaiti kālaḥ śamāya tāvat kuru saumya buddhim /
children.translated_text: "Before the harmful time of death approaches, O gentle one, set your mind upon peace;

children.text: sarvāsvavasthāsviha vartamānaṃ sarvābhisāreṇa nihanti mṛtyuḥ // Saund_5.22 //
children.translated_text: death strikes down all who exist in every condition, with a full-scale assault. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.22]

children.text: sādhāraṇāt svapnanibhādasārāllolaṃ manaḥ kāmasukhānniyaccha /
children.translated_text: Restrain your mind, which is fickle, from sense-pleasures — which are shared by all, dream-like, and without substance —

children.text: havyairivāgneḥ pavaneritasya lokasya kāmairna hi tṛptirasti // Saund_5.23 //
children.translated_text: for the world is never sated with desires, like a fire with offerings fanned by wind. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.23]

children.text: śraddhādhanaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ dhanebhyaḥ prajñārasasṛptikaro rasebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wealth of faith is the best of all riches; the taste of wisdom is the most delightful of all tastes;

children.text: pradhānamadhyātmasukhaṃ sukhebhyo 'vidyāratirduḥkhatamāratibhyaḥ // Saund_5.24 //
children.translated_text: the inner happiness of meditation is the chief of all pleasures; the cessation of ignorance is the greatest [relief] among all cessations. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.24]

children.text: hitasya vaktā pravaraḥ suhṛdbhyo dharmāya khedo guṇavān śramebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who speaks what is beneficial is the best of friends; exertion for <s>dharma</s> is the most virtuous of efforts;

children.text: jñānāya kṛtyaṃ paramaṃ kriyābhyaḥ kimindriyāṇāmupagamya dāsyam // Saund_5.25 //
children.translated_text: action for the sake of knowledge is the highest of deeds — why submit to the servitude of the senses? [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.25]

children.text: tanniścitaṃ bhīlkamaśugviyuktaṃ pareṣvanāyattamahāryamanyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Choose that which is certain, fearless, free from sorrow, independent of others, and unassailable by any —

children.text: nityaṃ śivaṃ śāntisukhaṃ vṛṇīṣva kimindriyārthārthamanarthamūḍhvā // Saund_5.26 //
children.translated_text: the eternally auspicious bliss of peace; why embrace the calamity of sense-objects? [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.26]

children.text: jarāsamā nāstyamṛjā prajānāṃ vyādheḥ samo nāsti jagatyanarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no impurity equal to old age for people; there is no misfortune in the world equal to disease;

children.text: mṛtyoḥ samaṃ nāsti bhayaṃ pṛthivyāmetattrayaṃ khalvavaśena sevyam // Saund_5.27 //
children.translated_text: there is no fear on earth equal to death — yet this triad must be endured against one's will. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.27]

children.text: snehena kaścinna samo 'sti pāśaḥ sroto na tṛṣṇāsamamasti hāri /
children.translated_text: There is no bond equal to affection; there is no current as sweeping as craving;

children.text: rāgāgninā nāsti samastathāgnistaccet trayaṃ nāsti sukhaṃ ca te 'sti // Saund_5.28 //
children.translated_text: there is no fire equal to the fire of passion — but if you are free from this triad, then happiness is yours. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.28]

children.text: avaśyabhāvī priyaviprayogastasmāñca śoko niyataṃ niṣevyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Separation from the beloved is inevitable; and from that, grief must certainly be experienced;

children.text: śokena conmādamupeyivāṃso rājarṣayo 'nye 'pyavaśā vicelu // Saund_5.29 //
children.translated_text: and driven to madness by grief, royal sages and others too have helplessly wandered. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.29]

children.text: prajñāmayaṃ varma badhāna tasmānno kṣāntinighnasya hi śokabāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, put on the armor of wisdom; for the arrows of grief cannot strike one armed with forbearance;

children.text: mahacca dagdhuṃ bhavakakṣajālaṃ saṃghukṣayālpāgnimivātmatejaḥ // Saund_5.30 //
children.translated_text: and [use it to] kindle the fire of your inner brilliance, as if from a small flame, to burn the great thicket of worldly existence. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.30]

children.text: yathauṣadhairhastagataiḥ savidyo na daśyate kaścana pannagena /
children.translated_text: Just as one who is learned, holding herbs in hand, is not bitten by any serpent,

children.text: tathānapekṣo jitalokamoho na daśyate śokabhujaṃgamena // Saund_5.31 //
children.translated_text: so one who is detached, who has conquered worldly delusion, is not bitten by the serpent of grief. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.31]

children.text: āsthāya yogaṃ parigamya tattvaṃ na trāsamāgacchati mṛtyukāle /
children.translated_text: Having taken up <s>yoga</s> and comprehended reality, one does not feel terror at the time of death,

children.text: ābaddhavarmā sudhanuḥ kṛtāsro jigīṣayā śūra ivāhavasthaḥ // Saund_5.32 //
children.translated_text: like a warrior on the battlefield, armored, with a fine bow, skilled in arrows, intent on conquest. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.32]

children.text: ityevamuktaḥ sa tathāgatena sarveṣu bhūteṣvanukampakena /
children.translated_text: Thus spoken to by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who has compassion for all beings,

children.text: dhṛṣṭaṃ girāntarhṛdayena sīdaṃstatheti nandaḥ sugataṃ babhāṣe // Saund_5.33 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, sinking inwardly in his heart, boldly spoke to the <s>Sugata</s>: 'So be it.' [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.33]

children.text: atha pramādācca tamujjihīrṣan matvāgamasyaiva ca pātrabhūtam /
children.translated_text: Then, wishing to lift him from heedlessness and considering him a worthy vessel for the teaching,

children.text: prabrājayānanda śamāya nandamityabravīnmaitramanā maharṣiḥ // Saund_5.34 //
children.translated_text: the great sage, with a benevolent mind, said: 'Ordain <s>Nanda</s> for the sake of peace, O <s>Ānanda</s>!' [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.34]

children.text: nandaṃ tato 'ntarmanasā rudantamehīti vaidehamunirjagāda /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, weeping inwardly, was addressed by the sage of <s>Vaideha</s>: 'Come!';

children.text: śanaistatastaṃ samupetya nando na pravrajiṣyāmyahamityuvāca // Saund_5.35 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Nanda</s>, slowly approaching him, said: 'I will not go forth [into the monastic life].' [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.35]

children.text: śrutvātha nandasya manīṣitaṃ tad buddhāya vaidehamuniḥ śaśaṃsa /
children.translated_text: Having heard <s>Nanda</s>'s intention, the sage of <s>Vaideha</s> reported it to the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: saṃśrutya tasmādapi tasya bhāvaṃ mahāmunirnandamuvāca bhūyaḥ // Saund_5.36 //
children.translated_text: and having learned his state of mind from him as well, the great sage spoke to <s>Nanda</s> again: [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.36]

children.text: mayyagraje pravrajite 'jitātman bhrātṛṣvanupravrajiteṣu cāsmān /
children.translated_text: "When I, your elder brother, have gone forth, and when our brothers too have gone forth after us,

children.text: jñātīṃśca dṛṣṭvā vratino gṛhasthān saṃvinna kiṃ te 'sti na vāsti cetaḥ // Saund_5.37 //
children.translated_text: O uncontrolled one, seeing kinsmen who are householders observing vows — do you not have, or have you, any stirring of conscience? [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.37]

children.text: rājarṣayaste viditā na nūnaṃ vanāni ye śiśriyire hasantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Surely the royal sages are not known to you — those who laughingly resorted to the forests,

children.text: niṣṭhīvya kāmānupaśāntikāmāḥ kāmeṣu naivaṃ kṛpaṇeṣu saktāḥ // Saund_5.38 //
children.translated_text: having spat out desires, desiring tranquility, not attached to wretched pleasures in this way! [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.38]

children.text: bhūyaḥ samālokya gṛheṣu doṣān niśāmya tattyāgakṛtaṃ ca śarma /
children.translated_text: Having looked again at the faults in household life and having perceived the happiness that comes from its renunciation,

children.text: naivāsti moktuṃ matirālayaṃ te deśaṃ mumūrṣoriva sopasargam // Saund_5.39 //
children.translated_text: you still have no inclination to leave your home — like one about to die [refusing to leave] a plague-stricken region! [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.39]

children.text: saṃsārakāntāraparāyaṇasya śive kathaṃ te pathi nārurukṣā /
children.translated_text: How is it that you, who are headed toward the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, have no desire to ascend the auspicious path,

children.text: āropyamāṇasya tameva mārgaṃ bhraṣṭasya sārthādiva sārthikasya // Saund_5.40 //
children.translated_text: like a caravan-merchant who has fallen from his caravan even as he is being led onto that very road? [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.40]

children.text: yaḥ sarvato veśmani dahyamāne śayīta mohānna tato vyapeyāt /
children.translated_text: One who, when the house is burning on all sides, lies down and does not flee due to delusion —

children.text: kālāgninā vyādhijarāśikhena loke pradīpte sa bhavet pramattaḥ // Saund_5.41 //
children.translated_text: he would be heedless when the world is ablaze with the fire of time, whose flames are disease and old age. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.41]

children.text: praṇīyamānaśca yathā vadhāya matto hasecca pralapecca vadhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a condemned man being led to execution would be mad to laugh and babble,

children.text: mṛtyau tathā tiṣṭhati pāśahaste śocyaḥ pramādyan viparitacetāḥ // Saund_5.42 //
children.translated_text: so one who revels heedlessly while death stands with noose in hand is pitiable, his mind confused. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.42]

children.text: yadā narendrāśca kuṭumbinaśca vihāya bandhūṃśca parigrahāṃśca /
children.translated_text: When kings and householders have left behind kin and possessions

children.text: yayuśca yāsyanti ca yānti caiva priyeṣvanityeṣu kuto 'nurodhaḥ // Saund_5.43 //
children.translated_text: and have gone, will go, and are going — what attachment can there be to impermanent loved ones? [<s>Saundarananda</s> 5.43]

children.text: kiñcinna paśyāmi ratasya yatra tadanyabhāvena bhavenna duḥkham /
children.translated_text: "I see nowhere that, for one who is attached, there would not be suffering through the transformation of that [attachment] into something else;

children.text: tasmāt kvacinna kṣamate prasaktiryadi kṣamastadvigamānna śokaḥ // Saund_5.44 //
children.translated_text: Therefore attachment to anything is never bearable — if one is [truly] capable, why grieve over its departure?" // Saund 5.44 //

children.text: tatsaumya lolaṃ parigamya lokaṃ māyopamaṃ citramivendrajālam /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, gentle one, having recognized this fickle world — illusory, like a wondrous magic show —

children.text: priyābhidhānaṃ tyaja mohajālaṃ chettuṃ matiste yadi duḥkhajālam // Saund_5.45 //
children.translated_text: Abandon the net of delusion called 'the beloved,' if your mind is set on cutting the net of suffering." // Saund 5.45 //

children.text: varaṃ hitodarkamāniṣṭamannaṃ na svādu yat syādahitānubaddham /
children.translated_text: "Better is distasteful food that results in benefit, than what is pleasant but accompanied by harm;

children.text: yasmādahaṃ tvāṃ viniyojayāmi śive śucau vartmani vipriye 'pi // Saund_5.46 //
children.translated_text: This is why I am directing you onto the auspicious and pure path, even though it be unpleasant." // Saund 5.46 //

children.text: bālasya dhātrī vinigṛhya loṣṭhaṃ yathoddharatyāsyapuṭapraviṣṭam /
children.translated_text: "Just as a nurse, having seized a clod [of dirt] that has entered a child's mouth, removes it by force,

children.text: tathojjihīrṣuḥ khalu rāgaśalyaṃ tattvāmavocaṃ paruṣaṃ hitāya // Saund_5.47 //
children.translated_text: So, wishing to extract the thorn of passion, I have spoken harshly to you for your benefit." // Saund 5.47 //

children.text: aniṣṭamapyauṣadhamāturāya dadāti vaidyaśca yathā nigṛhya /
children.translated_text: "Just as a physician forcibly gives even disagreeable medicine to a patient,

children.text: tadvanmayoktaṃ pratikūlametattubhyaṃ hitodarkamanugrahāya // Saund_5.48 //
children.translated_text: So too what I have said, though contrary [to your wishes], is for your benefit and out of compassion." // Saund 5.48 //

children.text: tadyāvadeva kṣaṇasaṃnipāto na mṛtyurāgacchati yāvadeva /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, while this conjunction of moments [still endures], while death has not yet arrived,

children.text: yāvadvayo yogavidhau samarthaṃ buddhiṃ kuru śreyasi tāvadeva // Saund_5.49 //
children.translated_text: While the body is yet capable of the practice of <s>yoga</s>, set your mind on the highest good in that very time." // Saund 5.49 //

children.text: ityevamuktaḥ sa vināyakena hitaiṣiṇā kāruṇikena nandaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the Guide, who was benevolent and compassionate, <s>Nanda</s>

children.text: kartāsmi sarvaṃ bhagavan vacaste tathā yathājñāpayasītyuvāca // Saund_5.50 //
children.translated_text: Said: "I will do everything as you command, O Blessed One — as you direct." // Saund 5.50 //

children.text: ādāya vaidehamunistatastaṃ nināya saṃśliṣya viceṣṭamānam /
children.translated_text: Then the sage of the <s>Vaideha</s> [lineage] took him, and led away the struggling [<s>Nanda</s>], embracing him,

children.text: vyayojayaccāśrupariplutākṣaṃ keśaśriyaṃ chatranibhasya mūrdhnaḥ // Saund_5.51 //
children.translated_text: And separated the glory of hair from his umbrella-like head, while his eyes were flooded with tears. // Saund 5.51 //

children.text: atho nataṃ tasya mukhaṃ sabāṣpaṃ pravāsyamāneṣu śiroruheṣu /
children.translated_text: And his face, bent down and tearful as the hair was being cut away,

children.text: vakrāgranālaṃ nalinaṃ taḍāge varṣodakaklinnamivābabhāse // Saund_5.52 //
children.translated_text: Shone like a lotus in a pond — drenched by rain-water, with its stalk curved at the tip. // Saund 5.52 //

children.text: nandastatastarukaṣāyaviraktavāsāścintāvaśo navagṛhīta iva dvipendraḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, wearing bark-dyed, faded garments, absorbed in thought, like a newly captured king-elephant,

children.text: pūrṇaḥ śaśī bahulapakṣagataḥ kṣapānte bālātapena pariṣikta ivāvabhāse // Saund_5.53 //
children.translated_text: Appeared like the full moon gone into the dark fortnight, at the end of night, as if sprinkled with the rays of the morning sun. // Saund 5.53 //

children.text: saundarananda kāvye "nandadīkṣā" nāma pañcama sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda</s> poem, the fifth canto, named '<s>Nandadīkṣā</s>' (The Ordination of <s>Nanda</s>), is completed.

children.text:
ṣaṣṭhaḥ sargaḥ
bhāryāvilāpa
children.translated_text: Sixth Canto: <s>Bhāryāvilāpa</s> (The Wife's Lamentation)

children.text: tato hṛte bharttari gauraveṇa prītau hṛtāyāmaratau kṛtāyām /
children.translated_text: Then, when her husband had been taken away with reverence, when joy had been seized away and grief had been made,

children.text: tatraiva harmyopari vartamānā na sundarī saiva tadā babhāse // Saund_6.1 //
children.translated_text: Remaining right there atop the mansion, <s>Sundarī</s> herself no longer appeared the same. // Saund 6.1 //

children.text: sā bharturabhyāgamanapratīkṣā gavākṣamākramya payodharābhyām /
children.translated_text: She, awaiting her husband's return, leaning forward with her breasts against the window,

children.text: dvāronmukhī harmyatalāllalambe mukhena tiryaṅnatakuṇḍalena // Saund_6.2 //
children.translated_text: Hung down facing the door from the mansion's terrace, her face with its earrings tilted sideways. // Saund 6.2 //

children.text: vilambahārā calayoktrakā sā tasmād vimānād vinatā cakāśe /
children.translated_text: With her necklace hanging low and her sash swaying, she shone forth, leaning from that mansion,

children.text: tapaḥ kṣayādapsarasāṃ vareva cyutaṃ vimānāt priyamīkṣamāṇā // Saund_6.3 //
children.translated_text: Like the foremost of <s>Apsarases</s>, gazing at her beloved who had fallen from a celestial palace due to the exhaustion of merit. // Saund 6.3 //

children.text: sā khedasaṃsvinnalalāṭakena niśvāsaniṣpītaviśeṣakeṇa /
children.translated_text: She stood there with her face — its forehead moist with the sweat of weariness, its <s>viśeṣaka</s> (forehead ornament) consumed by her sighs,

children.text: cintācalākṣeṇa mukhena tasthau bharttāramanyatra viśaṅkamānā // Saund_6.4 //
children.translated_text: Its eyes restless with worry — suspecting her husband to be elsewhere. // Saund 6.4 //

children.text: tataścirasthānapariśrameṇa sthitaiva paryaṅkatale papāta /
children.translated_text: Then, from the fatigue of standing so long, she collapsed upon the surface of the couch while still standing,

children.text: tiryakca śiśye pravikīrṇahārā sapādukaikārdhavilambapādā // Saund_6.5 //
children.translated_text: And lay sideways with her necklace scattered, one foot half-dangling with its sandal. // Saund 6.5 //

children.text: athātra kācit pramadā sabāṣpāṃ tāṃ duḥkhitāṃ draṣṭumanīpsamānā /
children.translated_text: Then a certain woman, with tears, not wishing to see her [in] such distress,

children.text: prāsādasopānatalapraṇādaṃ cakāra padbhyāṃ sahasā rudantī // Saund_6.6 //
children.translated_text: Suddenly, weeping, made a loud sound on the staircase platform with her feet. // Saund 6.6 //

children.text: tasyāśca sopānatalapraṇādaṃ śrutvaiva tūrṇaṃ punarutpapāta /
children.translated_text: And hearing the sound on the staircase platform, she [<s>Sundarī</s>] at once sprang up again,

children.text: prītyāṃ prasaktaiva ca saṃjaharṣa priyopayānaṃ pariśaṅkamānā // Saund_6.7 //
children.translated_text: And thrilled with joy, as if gripped by delight — suspecting the approaching of her beloved. // Saund 6.7 //

children.text: sā trāsayantī valabhīpuṭasthān pārāvatān nūpūranisvanena /
children.translated_text: She, frightening the pigeons settled in the balcony alcoves with the jangling of her anklets,

children.text: sopānakukṣiṃ prasasāra harṣād bhraṣṭaṃ dukūlāntamacintayantī // Saund_6.8 //
children.translated_text: Rushed toward the stairway out of joy, not caring about the slipping hem of her silk garment. // Saund 6.8 //

children.text: tāmaṅganāṃ prekṣya ca vipralabdhā niśvasya bhūyaḥ śayanaṃ prapede /
children.translated_text: But seeing [only] that woman, and feeling deceived, she sighed deeply and returned to bed;

children.text: vivarṇavaktrā na rarāja cāśu vivarṇacandreva himāgame dyauḥ // Saund_6.9 //
children.translated_text: Pale-faced, she no longer shone — like the sky at the onset of winter, with a pale moon. // Saund 6.9 //

children.text: sā duḥkhitā bhartturadarśanena kāmena kopena ca dahyamānā /
children.translated_text: She, distressed by not seeing her husband, burning with desire and anger,

children.text: kṛtvā kare vaktramupopaviṣṭā cintānadīṃ śokajalāṃ tatāra // Saund_6.10 //
children.translated_text: Sat down resting her face in her hand, and crossed a river of grief with waters of sorrow. // Saund 6.10 //

children.text: tasyāḥ mukhaṃ padmasapatnabhūtaṃ pāṇau sthitaṃ pallavarāgatāmre /
children.translated_text: Her face, a rival to the lotus, resting upon her hand — copper-hued as a tender shoot —

children.text: chāyāmayasyāmbhasi paṅkajasya babhau nataṃ padmamivopariṣṭāt // Saund_6.11 //
children.translated_text: Appeared like a lotus above a shadowy lotus reflected in the water, drooping downward. // Saund 6.11 //

children.text: sā strīsvabhāvena vicintya tattad dṛṣṭānurāge 'bhimukhe 'pi patyau /
children.translated_text: She, by the nature of women imagining this and that, even though her husband, visibly affectionate, was well-disposed [toward her],

children.text: dharmāśrite tattvamavindamānā saṃkalpya tattadvilalāpa tattat // Saund_6.12 //
children.translated_text: Not finding the truth since he had taken refuge in the <s>Dharma</s>, imagined this and that and lamented variously. // Saund 6.12 //

children.text: eṣyāmyanāśyānaviśeṣakāyāṃ tvayīti kṛtvā mayi taṃ pratijñām /
children.translated_text: "'I shall come before your <s>viśeṣaka</s> (forehead ornament) dries' — having made that promise to me,

children.text: kasmānnu hetordayitapratijñaḥ so 'dya priyo me vitathapratijñaḥ // Saund_6.13 //
children.translated_text: For what reason, then, is he — my beloved who was faithful to his promises — today false to his promise?" // Saund 6.13 //

children.text: āryasya sādhoḥ karuṇātmakasya mannityabhīroratidakṣiṇasya /
children.translated_text: "Of one who is noble, good, compassionate by nature, always fearless regarding me, and exceedingly gentle —

children.text: kuto vikāro 'yamabhūtapūrvaḥ svenāparāgeṇa mamāpacārāt // Saund_6.14 //
children.translated_text: Whence comes this unprecedented change? Is it from his own loss of affection, or from my own offense?" // Saund 6.14 //

children.text: ratipriyasya priyavartino me priyasya nūnaṃ hṛdaya viraktam /
children.translated_text: "Of my beloved, who delights in love and acts lovingly — surely his heart has become disenchanted;

children.text: tathāpi rāgo yadi tasya hi syān maccittarakṣī na sa nāgataḥ syāt // Saund_6.15 //
children.translated_text: Even so, if he still had affection, being the guardian of my heart, he would not have failed to return." // Saund 6.15 //

children.text: rūpeṇa bhāvena ca madviśiṣṭā priyeṇa dṛṣṭā niyataṃ tato 'nyā /
children.translated_text: "Surely another woman, surpassing me in beauty and character, has been seen by my beloved;

children.text: tathā hi kṛtvā mayi moghasāntvaṃ lagnāṃ satiṃ māmāgamad vihāya // Saund_6.16 //
children.translated_text: For having spoken vain consolation to me, he departed, leaving me, though I clung to him faithfully." // Saund 6.16 //

children.text: bhaktiṃ sa buddhaṃ prati yāvavocattasya prayātuṃ mayi so 'padeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The devotion he spoke of toward the <s>Buddha</s> was [merely] his pretext for departing from me;

children.text: munau prasādo yadi tasya hi syānmṛtyorivogrādanṛtād bibhīyāt // Saund_6.17 //
children.translated_text: For if he truly had faith in the sage, he would shrink from falsehood as from dreadful death." // Saund 6.17 //

children.text: sevārthamādarśanamanyacitto vibhūṣayantyā mama dhārayitvā /
children.translated_text: "The garland that I, with devoted mind, adorned and placed for serving [him], prepared before a mirror —

children.text: bibharti so 'nyasya janasya taṃ cennamo 'stu tasmai calasauhṛdāya // Saund_6.18 //
children.translated_text: If he wears it for another person, then obeisance to him of fickle friendship!" // Saund 6.18 //

children.text: necchanti yāḥ śokamavāptumevaṃ śraddhātumarhanti na tā narāṇām /
children.translated_text: "Those women who do not wish to obtain grief in this way should not place faith in men;

children.text: kva cānuvṛttirmayi sāsya pūrvaṃ tyāgaḥ kva cāyaṃ janavat kṣaṇena // Saund_6.19 //
children.translated_text: Where was his former devotion to me, and where is this abandonment in a moment, like [one among] common people?" // Saund 6.19 //

children.text: ityevamādi priyaviprayuktā priye 'nyadāśaṅkya ca sā jagāda /
children.translated_text: Thus and more did she say, separated from her beloved, suspecting him with another;

children.text: saṃbhrāntamāruhya ca tadvimānaṃ tāṃ strī sabāṣpā giramityuvāca // Saund_6.20 //
children.translated_text: Then a woman who had hurriedly climbed up to that mansion, with tears, spoke these words: // Saund 6.20 //

children.text: yuvāpi tāvat priyadarśano 'pi saubhāgyabhāgyābhijanānvito 'pi /
children.translated_text: "He who is young, fair to look upon, endowed with fortune, blessings, and noble birth,

children.text: yastvāṃ priyo nābhyacarat kadācittamanyathā yāsyatikātarāsi // Saund_6.21 //
children.translated_text: He who has never wronged you, your beloved — you are alarmed that he will become otherwise!" // Saund 6.21 //

children.text: mā svāminaṃ svāmini doṣato gāḥ priyaṃ priyārhaṃ priyakāriṇaṃ tam /
children.translated_text: "Do not accuse your lord of faults, O mistress — that dear one, worthy of love, who acts with love;

children.text: na sa tvadanyāṃ pramadāmavaiti svacakravākyā iva cakravākaḥ // Saund_6.22 //
children.translated_text: He knows no other woman but you — like a <s>cakravāka</s> drake devoted to his own <s>cakravākī</s>." // Saund 6.22 //

children.text: sa tu tvadarthaṃ gṛhavāsamīpsan jijīviṣustvatparitoṣahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: "He indeed, desiring household life for your sake, wishing to live for the purpose of your contentment,

children.text: bhrātrā kilāryeṇa tathāgatena pravrājito netrajalārdravaktraḥ // Saund_6.23 //
children.translated_text: Was led forth to renunciation, they say, by his noble elder brother the <s>Tathāgata</s>, his face moist with tears." // Saund 6.23 //

children.text: śrutvā tato bhartari tāṃ pravṛttiṃ savepathuḥ sā sahasotpapāt /
children.translated_text: Then, hearing this report concerning her husband, she suddenly sprang up trembling,

children.text: pragṛhya bāhū virurāva coccairhṛdīva digdhābhihata kareṇuḥ // Saund_6.24 //
children.translated_text: And raising her arms, cried aloud — like a cow-elephant struck in the heart by a poisoned [arrow]. // Saund 6.24 //

children.text: sā rodanāroṣitaraktadṛṣṭiḥ saṃtāpasaṃkṣobhitagātrayaṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: She, her eyes reddened with raging tears, her body shaken by the trembling of anguish,

children.text: papāta śīrṇākulahārayaṣṭiḥ phalātibhārādiva cūtayaṣṭiḥ // Saund_6.25 //
children.translated_text: Fell like a mango branch under the excess weight of fruit — her necklace strands scattered and tangled. // Saund 6.25 //

children.text: sā padmarāgaṃ vasanaṃ vasānā padmānanā padmadalāyatākṣī /
children.translated_text: She, wearing garments [red as] rubies, lotus-faced, with eyes wide as lotus petals —

children.text: padmā vipadmā patiteva lakṣmīḥ śuśoṣa padmasragivātapena // Saund_6.26 //
children.translated_text: <s>Padmā</s> (Lakṣmī) without a lotus — like <s>Lakṣmī</s> fallen from grace — withered in the scorching wind, her lotus garland [drooping]. // Saund 6.26 //

children.text: saṃcintya sacintya guṇāṃśca bharturdīrghaṃ niśaśvāsa tatāma caiva /
children.translated_text: Recalling again and again the virtues of her husband, she sighed deeply and grew faint;

children.text: vibhūṣaṇaśrīnihite prakoṣṭhe tāmre karāgre ca vinirdudhāva // Saund_6.27 //
children.translated_text: And she thrust her hands, on whose forearms the beauty of ornaments had been placed, forward with coppery fingertips. // Saund 6.27 //

children.text: na bhūṣaṇārtho mama saṃpratīti sā dikṣu cikṣepa vibhūṣaṇāni /
children.translated_text: "There is no purpose of ornament for me now" — so saying, she flung her ornaments in all directions;

children.text: nirbhūṣaṇā sā patitā cakāśe viśīrṇapuṣpastabakā lateva // Saund_6.28 //
children.translated_text: And unadorned, fallen down, she appeared like a creeper with its clusters of flowers scattered. // Saund 6.28 //

children.text: dhṛtaḥ priyeṇāyamabhūnmameti rukmatsaruṃ darpaṇamāliliṅge /
children.translated_text: "This was held by my beloved" — thus she embraced a mirror with a golden handle;

children.text: yatnācca vinyastatamālapatrau ruṣṭeva dhṛṣṭaṃ pramamājaṃ gaṇḍau // Saund_6.29 //
children.translated_text: And angrily, boldly wiped her cheeks where <s>tamāla</s>-leaf [designs] had been carefully applied. // Saund 6.29 //

children.text: sā cakravākīva bhṛśaṃ cukūja śyenāgrapakṣakṣatacakravākā /
children.translated_text: She cooed pitifully, like a <s>cakravākī</s> female — a <s>cakravākī</s> whose mate has been seized by a hawk's talons —

children.text: vispardhamāneva vimānasaṃsthaiḥ pārāvataiḥ kūjanalolakaṇṭhaiḥ // Saund_6.30 //
children.translated_text: As if competing with the pigeons perched on the mansion, cooing with trembling throats. // Saund 6.30 //

children.text: vicitramṛdvāstaraṇe 'pi suptā vaiḍūryavajrapratimaṇḍite 'pi /
children.translated_text: Though lying on a splendid bed with variegated soft coverings, adorned with <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl) and diamond,

children.text: rukmāṅgapāde śayane mahārhe na śarma lebhe pariceṣṭamānā // Saund_6.31 //
children.translated_text: On a couch with golden feet, of great value — she found no comfort, tossing about. // Saund 6.31 //

children.text: sandṛśya bhartuśca vibhūṣaṇāni vāsāṃsi vīṇāprabhṛtīṃśca līlāḥ /
children.translated_text: Beholding her husband's ornaments, garments, his <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) and other playthings,

children.text: tamo viveśābhinanāda coccaiḥ paṅkāvatīrṇeva ca saṃsasāda // Saund_6.32 //
children.translated_text: She entered darkness [of grief], wailed loudly, and sank down as if mired in mud. // Saund 6.32 //

children.text: sā sundarī śvāsacalodarī hi vajrāgnisaṃbhinnadarīguheva /
children.translated_text: That beautiful <s>Sundarī</s>, her belly heaving with sighs — like a mountain cave whose cavern is split by thunderbolt and fire,

children.text: śokāgnināntarhṛdi dahyamānā vibhrāntacitteva tadā babhūva // Saund_6.33 //
children.translated_text: Burning within her heart with the fire of grief — became as one whose mind is bewildered. // Saund 6.33 //

children.text: ruroda mamlau virurāva jaglau babhrāma tasthau vilalāpa dadhyau /
children.translated_text: She wept, she wilted, she wailed, she swooned, she wandered about, she stood still, she lamented, she brooded;

children.text: cakāra roṣaṃ vicakāra mālyaṃ cakarta vaktraṃ vicakarṣa vastram // Saund_6.34 //
children.translated_text: She grew angry, she tore apart garlands, she scratched her face, she tugged at her garments. // Saund 6.34 //

children.text: tāṃ cārudantīṃ prasabhaṃ rudantīṃ saṃśrutya nāryaḥ paramābhitaptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing her — she of beautiful teeth — weeping violently, the women, deeply distressed,

children.text: antargṛhādāruruhurvimānaṃ trāsena kinnarya ivādripṛṣṭham // Saund_6.35 //
children.translated_text: Ascended the mansion from within the house — like <s>Kinnarī</s>-maidens [climbing] a mountain ridge out of alarm. // Saund 6.35 //

children.text: bāṣpeṇa tāḥ klinnaviṣaṇṇavaktrā varṣeṇa padminya ivārdrapadmāḥ /
children.translated_text: They, their faces dejected and moistened with tears — like lotuses in a pond, wet with rain —

children.text: sthānānurūpeṇa yathābhimānaṃ nililyire tāmanudahyamānāḥ // Saund_6.36 //
children.translated_text: Settled around her according to their stations, each as she deemed fit, being burned [with sympathy]. // Saund 6.36 //

children.text: tābhirvṛtā harmyatale 'ṅganābhiścintātanuḥ sā sutanurbabhāse /
children.translated_text: Surrounded by those women atop the mansion, she — her body emaciated by worry yet graceful —

children.text: śatahradābhiḥ pariveṣṭiteva śaśāṅkalekhā śaradabhramadhye // Saund_6.37 //
children.translated_text: Appeared like a crescent of the moon amidst autumn clouds, encircled by flashes of lightning. // Saund 6.37 //

children.text: yā tatra tāsāṃ vacasopapannā mānyā ca tasyā vayasādhikā ca /
children.translated_text: Among them, she who was endowed with eloquence, respected, and senior in age,

children.text: sā pṛṣṭhatastāṃ tu samāliliṅge pramṛjya cāśrūṇi vacāṃsyuvāca // Saund_6.38 //
children.translated_text: Embraced her from behind, and wiping away [her] tears, spoke these words: // Saund 6.38 //

children.text: rājarṣivadhvāstava nānurūpo dharmāśrite bhartari jātu śokaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Grief is never becoming for the wife of a royal sage when her husband has taken refuge in the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: ikṣvākuvaṃśe hyabhikāṅkṣitāni dāyādyabhūtāni tapovanāni // Saund_6.39 //
children.translated_text: For in the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, hermitage-groves are hereditary and desired." // Saund 6.39 //

children.text: prāyeṇa mokṣāya viniḥsṛtānāṃ śākyarṣabhāṇāṃ viditāḥ striyaste /
children.translated_text: "You know well the wives of the <s>Śākya</s> bulls who have generally departed for liberation —

children.text: tapovanānīva gṛhāṇi yāsāṃ sādhvīvrataṃ kāmavadāśritānām // Saund_6.40 //
children.translated_text: Whose households were like hermitage-groves, who had embraced the vow of a virtuous wife even while dwelling with [their husbands'] passions." // Saund 6.40 //

children.text: yadyanyayā rūpaguṇādhikatvād bharttā hṛtaste kuru bāṣpamokṣam /
children.translated_text: "If your husband has been stolen by another woman superior in beauty and virtue, then shed tears;

children.text: manasvinī rūpavatī guṇāḍhyā hṛdi kṣate kātra hi nāśru muñcet // Saund_6.41 //
children.translated_text: What woman of spirit, beautiful and endowed with qualities, would not release tears when wounded in the heart?" // Saund 6.41 //

children.text: athāpi kiṃcid vyasanaṃ prapanno mā caiva tad bhūt sadṛśo 'tra bāṣpaḥ /
children.translated_text: "But if he has met with some misfortune — may that never be! — then tears are fitting;

children.text: ato viśiṣṭaṃ na hi duḥkhamasti kulodgatāyāḥ patidevatāyāḥ // Saund_6.42 //
children.translated_text: For there is no greater suffering for a wife of noble birth, for whom her husband is her deity." // Saund 6.42 //

children.text: atha tvidānīṃ laḍitaḥ sukhena svasthaḥ phalastho vyasanānyadṛṣṭvā /
children.translated_text: "But if now, having lived in ease, content, established in [his] fruits, having seen no adversity,

children.text: vītaspṛho dharmamanuprapannaḥ kiṃ viklavā rodiṣi harṣakāle // Saund_6.43 //
children.translated_text: Free from craving, he has embraced the <s>Dharma</s> — why do you weep distraught at a time for joy?" // Saund 6.43 //

children.text: ityevamuktāpi bahuprakāraṃ snehāttayā naiva dhṛtiṃ cakāra /
children.translated_text: Though thus addressed in many ways, she did not find steadiness, out of love for her [husband];

children.text: athāparā tāṃ manaso 'nukūlaṃ kālopapannaṃ praṇayāduvāca // Saund_6.44 //
children.translated_text: Then another [woman] spoke to her what was agreeable to her mind, fitting for the occasion, out of affection: // Saund 6.44 //

children.text: bravīmi satyaṃ suviniścitaṃ me prāptaṃ priyaṃ drakṣyasi śīghrameva /
children.translated_text: "I speak the truth — I am firmly convinced — you will see your beloved returned very soon;

children.text: tvayā vinā sthāsyati tatra nāsau sattvāśrayaścetanayeva hīnaḥ // Saund_6.45 //
children.translated_text: Without you, he will not remain there — he, who is of noble spirit, would be as if bereft of consciousness." // Saund 6.45 //

children.text: aṅke 'pi lakṣmyā na sa nirvṛtaḥ syāt tvaṃ tasya pārśve yadi tatra na syāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even in the lap of <s>Lakṣmī</s> he would not be content, if you were not by his side;

children.text: āpatsu kṛcchrāsvapi cāgatāsu tvāṃ paśyatastasya bhavenna duḥkham // Saund_6.46 //
children.translated_text: Even in the most terrible calamities, so long as he sees you, there would be no suffering for him." // Saund 6.46 //

children.text: tvaṃ nirvṛtiṃ gaccha niyaccha bāṣpaṃ taptāśrumokṣāt parirakṣa cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: "Be at peace, restrain your tears, protect your eyes from the shedding of hot tears;

children.text: yastasya bhāvastvayi yaśca rāgo na raṃsyate tvadvirahāt sa dharme // Saund_6.47 //
children.translated_text: The affection and passion he has for you — he will not delight in the <s>Dharma</s> being separated from you." // Saund 6.47 //

children.text: syādatra nāsau kulasattvayogāt kāṣāyamādāya vihāsyatīti /
children.translated_text: "Perhaps, given his family and character, he will not discard the ochre robe and laugh [at us]" —

children.text: anātmanādāya gṛhonmukhasya punarvimoktuṃ ka ivāsti doṣaḥ // Saund_6.48 //
children.translated_text: for one who has taken it up without inner conviction, facing homeward, what fault is there in releasing it again? (6.48)

children.text: iti yuvatijanena sāntvyamānā hṛtahṛdayā ramaṇena sundarī sā /
children.translated_text: Thus consoled by the young women, <s>Sundarī</s>, her heart stolen [by her beloved],

children.text: dramiḍamabhimukhī pureva rambhā kṣitimagamat parivāritāpsarobhiḥ // Saund_6.49 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Rambhā</s> (the celestial nymph) going toward <s>Dramiḍa</s> (the South), went to the earth, surrounded by <s>Apsarases</s>. (6.49)

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "bhāryāvilāpa" nāma ṣaṣṭha sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth canto, entitled 'The Wife's Lament,' in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.

children.text:
saptamaḥ sargaḥ
nandavilāpa
children.translated_text:
Seventh Canto:
The Lament of <s>Nanda</s>

children.text: liṅgaṃ tataḥ śāstṛvidhipradiṣṭaṃ gātreṇa bibhranna tu cetasā tat /
children.translated_text: Then, bearing on his body the mendicant's garb prescribed by the Teacher, but not in his mind,

children.text: bhāryāgataireva manovitarkairjehrīyamāṇo na nananda nandaḥ // Saund_7.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> found no joy, being tormented by mental fantasies connected with his wife. (7.1)

children.text: sa puṣpamāsasya ca puṣpalakṣmyā sarvābhisāreṇa ca puṣpaketoḥ /
children.translated_text: He, by the beauty of flowers in the month of spring, by every advance of <s>Puṣpaketu</s> (Flower-Bannered, i.e., <s>Kāma</s>),

children.text: yānīyabhāvena ca yauvanasya vihārasaṃstho na śamaṃ jagāma // Saund_7.2 //
children.translated_text: and by the susceptibility of youth — while dwelling in the monastery, did not attain peace. (7.2)

children.text: sthitaḥ saḥ dīnaḥ sahakāravīthyāmālīnasaṃmūrcchitaṣaṭpadāyām /
children.translated_text: Standing there, dejected, in a row of mango trees where bees had gathered and swarmed,

children.text: bhṛśaṃ jajṛmbhe yugadīrghabāhurdhyātvā priyāṃ cāpamivācakarṣa // Saund_7.3 //
children.translated_text: he yawned greatly, his arms long as a yoke-pole, and thinking of his beloved, drew [himself] back as if drawing a bow. (7.3)

children.text: sa pītakakṣodamiva pratīcchan cūtadrumebhyastanupuṣpavarṣam /
children.translated_text: He, as if receiving a shower of delicate blossom-rain from the mango trees like golden-hued pollen,

children.text: dīrghaṃ niśaśvāsa vicintya bhāryāṃ navagraho nāga ivāvaruddhaḥ // Saund_7.4 //
children.translated_text: sighed long, thinking of his wife — confined like a newly captured elephant. (7.4)

children.text: śokasya hartā śaraṇāgatānāṃ śokasya karttā pratigarvitānām /
children.translated_text: He who removes grief from those who seek refuge, and causes grief to the arrogant —

children.text: aśokamālambya sa jātaśokaḥ priyāṃ priyāśokakavanāṃ śuśoca // Saund_7.5 //
children.translated_text: leaning upon the <s>Aśoka</s> (sorrowless) tree, he who was born to grief (<s>jātaśoka</s>) grieved for his beloved, who was dear to the <s>Aśoka</s> grove. (7.5)

children.text: priyāṃ priyāyāḥ pratanuṃ priyaṅguṃ niśāmya bhītāmiva niṣpatantīm /
children.translated_text: Beholding the slender <s>Priyangu</s> (beauty-berry) vine, dear to his beloved, as if trembling and rushing forth in fright,

children.text: sasmāra tāmaśrumukhīṃ sabāṣpaḥ priyāṃ priyaṅguprasavāvadātām // Saund_7.6 //
children.translated_text: he remembered her, tear-faced, weeping — his beloved, fair as the blossom of <s>Priyangu</s>. (7.6)

children.text: puṣpāvanaddhe tilakadrumasya dṛṣṭvānyapuṣṭāṃ śikhare niviṣṭām /
children.translated_text: Seeing a cuckoo (<s>anyapuṣṭā</s>) perched on the flower-laden crown of a <s>Tilaka</s> tree,

children.text: saṃkalpayāmāsa śikhāṃ priyāyāḥ śuklāṃśuke 'ṭṭālapāśritāyāḥ // Saund_7.7 //
children.translated_text: he imagined the tuft of hair of his beloved, leaning against a balcony in a white garment. (7.7)

children.text: latāṃ praphullāmatimuktakasya cūtasya pārśve parirabhya jātām /
children.translated_text: Beholding a creeper of the blooming <s>Atimukta</s> (jasmine), clinging to the side of a mango, having grown there,

children.text: niśāmya cintāmagamattadaivaṃ śliṣṭā bhavenmāmapi sundarīti // Saund_7.8 //
children.translated_text: he fell into thought: 'Would that <s>Sundarī</s> were thus embracing even me!' (7.8)

children.text: puṣpotkarālā api nāgavṛkṣā dāntaiḥ samudgairiva hemagarbhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Nāga</s> trees (ironwood), though resplendent with clusters of blossoms, like ivory caskets with golden interiors,

children.text: kāntāravṛkṣā iva duḥkhitasya na cakṣurācikṣipurasya tatra // Saund_7.9 //
children.translated_text: did not attract his eye — they were to him like trees in a wilderness, for he was wretched. (7.9)

children.text: gandhaṃ vamanto 'pi ca gandhaparṇā gandharvaveśyā iva gandhapūrṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Gandhaparṇa</s> (fragrant-leaved) trees, though exhaling fragrance, full of scent like the courtesans of the <s>Gandharvas</s>,

children.text: tasyānyacittasya śugātmakasya ghrāṇaṃ na janhurhṛdayaṃ pratepuḥ // Saund_7.10 //
children.translated_text: did not gratify his nose but burned his heart — for his mind was elsewhere and his being was made of sorrow. (7.10)

children.text: saṃraktakaṇṭhaiśca vinīlakaṇṭhaistuṣṭaiḥ prahṛṣṭairapi cānyapuṣṭaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By the red-throated [cuckoos] and the blue-throated [peacocks], by the joyful, exhilarated <s>Anyapuṣṭas</s> (cuckoos),

children.text: lelihyamānaiśca madhu dvirephaiḥ svanadvanaṃ tasya mano nunoda // Saund_7.11 //
children.translated_text: and by the bees licking honey — the resounding forest assailed his mind. (7.11)

children.text: sa tatra bhāryāraṇisaṃbhavena vitarkadhūmena tamaḥśikhena /
children.translated_text: There, by the fire of <s>Kāma</s> (Love), born from the fire-stick of his wife, its smoke being mental agitation, its flame-tip being darkness,

children.text: kāmāgnināntarhṛdi dahyamāno vihāya dhairyaṃ vilalāpa tattat // Saund_7.12 //
children.translated_text: being burned inwardly in his heart, he abandoned composure and lamented thus: (7.12)

children.text: adyāvagacchāmi suduṣkaraṃ te cakruḥ kariṣyanti ca kurvate ca /
children.translated_text: "Now I understand how exceedingly difficult was, is, and will be [the deed] of those who

children.text: tyaktvā priyāmaśrumukhīṃ tapo ye cerūścariṣyanti caranti caiva // Saund_7.13 //
children.translated_text: have practiced, practice, and will practice austerity, having abandoned a tear-faced beloved! (7.13)

children.text: tāvad dṛḍhaṃ bandhanamasti loke na dāravaṃ tāntavamāyasaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: "There is no bond in the world so strong — not one of wood, nor of cord, nor of iron —

children.text: yāvad dṛḍhaṃ bandhanametadeva mukhaṃ calākṣaṃ lalitaṃ ca vākyam // Saund_7.14 //
children.translated_text: as this very bond: a face with darting eyes and charming words. (7.14)

children.text: chittvā ca bhittvā ca hi yānti tāni svapauruṣāccaiva suhṛdbalācca /
children.translated_text: "For those [other bonds] can be cut and broken through one's own valor or the strength of friends;

children.text: jñānācca raukṣyācca vinā vimoktuṃ na śakyate snehamayastu pāśaḥ // Saund_7.15 //
children.translated_text: but the noose made of affection cannot be released without knowledge and detachment. (7.15)

children.text: jñānaṃ na me tacca śamāya yat syānna na cāsti raukṣyaṃ karuṇātmako 'smi /
children.translated_text: "And I do not have the knowledge that would lead to peace, nor do I have detachment — for I am compassionate by nature;

children.text: kāmātmakaścāsmi guruśca buddhaḥ sthito 'ntare cakragaterivāsmi // Saund_7.16 //
children.translated_text: I am given to desire, and the <s>Buddha</s> is my teacher — I stand caught between, like one on a wheel. (7.16)

children.text: ahaṃ gṛhītvāpi hi bhikṣuliṅgaṃ bhrātṝṣiṇā dviguruṇānuśiṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For even though I have taken up the mendicant's garb, instructed by my brother the sage, a twofold teacher,

children.text: sarvāsvavasthāsu labhe na śāntiṃ priyāviyogādiva cakravākaḥ // Saund_7.17 //
children.translated_text: in all conditions I find no peace — like a <s>cakravāka</s> bird separated from its mate. (7.17)

children.text: adyāpi tanme hṛdi vartate ca yaddarpaṇe vyākulite mayā sā /
children.translated_text: "Even now, this remains in my heart: when I disturbed the mirror, she

children.text: kṛtānutakrodhakamabravīnmāṃ kathaṃkṛto 'sīti śaṭhaṃ hasantī // Saund_7.18 //
children.translated_text: said to me with feigned anger, laughing mischievously, 'What have you done?' (7.18)

children.text: yathaiṣyanāśyānaviśeṣakāyāṃ mayīti yanmāmavadacca sāśru /
children.translated_text: "And that word she said to me with tears — 'How will I go on when you are gone?' — her face flushed as if about to weep,

children.text: pāriplavākṣeṇa mukhena bālā tanme vaco 'dyāpi mano ruṇaddhi // Saund_7.19 //
children.translated_text: that word, spoken by the young girl with trembling eyes, still blocks my mind even today. (7.19)

children.text: buddhvāsanaṃ parvatanirjharasthaḥ svastho yathā dhyāyati bhikṣureṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This monk, sitting by the mountain stream, composed, meditates as if comfortable;

children.text: saktaḥ kvacinnāhamivaiṣa nūnaṃ śāntastathā tṛpta ivopaviṣṭaḥ // Saund_7.20 //
children.translated_text: surely he is not attached anywhere as I am — so calm, seated as if content. (7.20)

children.text: puṃskokilānāmavicintya ghoṣaṃ vasantalakṣmyāmavicārya cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: "Without giving a thought to the call of the male cuckoo, without letting his eye wander upon the beauty of spring,

children.text: śāstraṃ yathābhyasyati caiṣa yuktaḥ śaṅke priyākarṣati nāsya cetaḥ // Saund_7.21 //
children.translated_text: see how he studies the scriptures with concentration — I suspect no beloved pulls at his heart. (7.21)

children.text: asmai namo 'stu sthiraniścayāya nivṛttakautūhalavismayāya /
children.translated_text: "Homage to this one of firm resolve, free from curiosity and wonder,

children.text: śāntātmane 'ntargatamānāsāya caṅkramyamāṇāya nirutsukāya // Saund_7.22 //
children.translated_text: of peaceful self, his aspirations turned inward, walking the cloister without yearning! (7.22)

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇasya jalaṃ sapadmaṃ vanaṃ ca phullaṃ parapuṣṭajuṣṭam /
children.translated_text: "When one gazes upon lotus-laden waters and blossoming groves alive with cuckoos,

children.text: kasyāsti dhairyaṃ navayauvanasya māse madhau dharmasapatnabhūte // Saund_7.23 //
children.translated_text: who has composure in fresh youth, in the month of spring — that rival of <s>dharma</s>? (7.23)

children.text: bhāvena garveṇa gatena lakṣmyā smitena kopena madena vāgbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "By their bearing, their pride, their departing grace, their smile, their anger, their intoxication, their words —

children.text: jahruḥ striyo devanṛparṣisaṃghān kasmāddhi nāsmadvidhamākṣipeyuḥ // Saund_7.24 //
children.translated_text: women have conquered assemblies of gods, kings, and sages — why would they not captivate one like me? (7.24)

children.text: kāmābhibhūto hi hiraṇyaretāḥ svāhāṃ siṣeve madhavānahalyām /
children.translated_text: "For the gold-seeded <s>Hiraṇyaretas</s> (Fire), overpowered by desire, resorted to <s>Svāhā</s>; and <s>Madhava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) to <s>Ahalyā</s>;

children.text: sattvena sargeṇa ca tena hīnaḥ strinirjitaḥ kiṃ bata mānuṣo 'ham // Saund_7.25 //
children.translated_text: I, a human, being inferior to them in strength and in creative power — what wonder if I am conquered by women? (7.25)

children.text: sūryaḥ saraṇyūṃ prati jātarāgastatprītaye taṣṭa iti śrutaṃ naḥ /
children.translated_text: "We have heard that <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), smitten with passion for <s>Saraṇyū</s>, transformed himself to please her;

children.text: ratamaśvabhūto 'śvavadhūṃ sametya yato 'śvinau tau janayāṃbabhūva // Saund_7.26 //
children.translated_text: becoming a stallion, he united with that mare-wife, from which union the twin <s>Aśvins</s> were born. (7.26)

children.text: strīkāraṇaṃ vairaviśaktabuddhyorvaivasvatāgnyoścalitātmadhṛtyoḥ /
children.translated_text: "Over a woman, the war between <s>Vaivasvata</s> (<s>Yama</s>) and <s>Agni</s> (Fire), both of whom lost their composure and whose minds were set upon enmity,

children.text: bahūni varṣāṇi babhūva yuddhaṃ kaḥ strīnimittaṃ na caledihānyaḥ // Saund_7.27 //
children.translated_text: lasted many years — who else in this world would not be shaken on account of a woman? (7.27)

children.text: bheje śvapākīṃ munirakṣamālāṃ kāmādvasiṣṭhaśca sa sadvariṣṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The sage <s>Akṣamālā</s> (better known as <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the best of the virtuous) resorted to a <s>Śvapākī</s> (outcaste woman) out of desire;

children.text: yasyāṃ vivaśvāniva bhūjalādaḥ sutaḥ prasūto 'sya kapiñjalādaḥ // Saund_7.28 //
children.translated_text: in her — like the sun [giving light] from the depths of the earth — his son <s>Kapiñjalāda</s> was born. (7.28)

children.text: parāśaraḥ śāpaśarastatharṣiḥ kālīṃ siṣeve jhaṣagarbhayonim /
children.translated_text: "<s>Parāśara</s>, that sage whose arrows were curses, resorted to <s>Kālī</s>, born from the womb of a fish;

children.text: suto 'sya yasyāṃ suṣuve mahātmā dvaipāyano vedavibhāgakarttā // Saund_7.29 //
children.translated_text: in her was born his son, the great-souled <s>Dvaipāyana</s> (Vyāsa), the divider of the <s>Vedas</s>. (7.29)

children.text: dvaipāyano dharmaparāyaṇaśca reme samaṃ kāśiṣu veśyavadhvā /
children.translated_text: "And <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, though devoted to <s>dharma</s>, disported himself with a courtesan-wife in <s>Kāśī</s>;

children.text: yayā hato 'bhūccalanūpureṇa pādena vidyullatayeva meghaḥ // Saund_7.30 //
children.translated_text: by her, he was struck with a foot bearing a jingling anklet — like a cloud by a streak of lightning. (7.30)

children.text: tathāṅgirā rāgaparītacetāḥ sarasvatīṃ brahmasutaḥ siṣeve /
children.translated_text: "Likewise, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Brahman</s>'s son, his mind enveloped by passion, resorted to <s>Sarasvatī</s>;

children.text: sārasvato yatra suto 'sya jajñe naṣṭasya vedasya punaḥpravaktā // Saund_7.31 //
children.translated_text: there his son <s>Sārasvata</s> was born — the re-proclaimer of the lost <s>Veda</s>. (7.31)

children.text: tathā nṛparṣerdilīpasya yajñe svargastriyāṃ kāśyapa āgatāsthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Likewise, at the sacrifice of the royal sage <s>Dilīpa</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, overcome by passion for a celestial woman,

children.text: sruvaṃ gṛhītvā sravadātmatejaścikṣepa vahrāvasito yato 'bhūt // Saund_7.32 //
children.translated_text: seized the sacrificial ladle, and with his own vital energy flowing, cast it into the fire — from which <s>Vahrā</s> (?) was born. (7.32)

children.text: tathāṅgado 'ntaṃ tapaso 'pi gatvā kāmābhibhūto yamunāmagacchat /
children.translated_text: "Likewise, <s>Aṅgada</s> (?), though having reached the summit of austerity, overpowered by desire, went to the <s>Yamunā</s>;

children.text: dhīmattaraṃ yatra rathītaraṃ sa sāraṅgajuṣṭaṃ janayāmbabhūva // Saund_7.33 //
children.translated_text: there he begot one wiser than himself, a greater chariot-warrior — [<s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>], frequented by deer. (7.33)

children.text: niśāmya śāntāṃ naradevakanyāṃ vane 'pi śānte 'pi ca vartamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even while dwelling in the peaceful forest, upon seeing the serene king's daughter,

children.text: cacāla dhairyānmuniṛṣyaśrṛṅgaḥ śailo mahīkampa ivoccaśrṛṅgaḥ // Saund_7.34 //
children.translated_text: the sage <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> was shaken from his composure, like a mountain with high peaks during an earthquake. (7.34)

children.text: brahmarṣibhāvārthamapāsya rājyaṃ bheje vanaṃ yo viṣayeṣvanāsthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He who had renounced his kingdom for the attainment of Brahmanical sagehood, indifferent to sense-objects, took to the forest —

children.text: sa gādhijaścāpahṛto ghṛtācyā samā daśaikaṃ divasaṃ viveda // Saund_7.35 //
children.translated_text: that son of <s>Gādhi</s> (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>), carried away by <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, experienced ten years as a single day. (7.35)

children.text: tathaiva kandarpaśarābhimṛṣṭo rambhāṃ prati sthūlaśirā mumūrccha /
children.translated_text: "Likewise, struck by the arrows of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love), <s>Sthūlaśiras</s> swooned over <s>Rambhā</s>;

children.text: yaḥ kāmaroṣātmatayānapekṣaḥ śaśāpa tāmapratigṛhyamāṇaḥ // Saund_7.36 //
children.translated_text: and when she spurned him, he, heedless due to the anger born of desire, cursed her. (7.36)

children.text: pramadvarāyāṃ ca ruruḥ priyāyāṃ bhujaṅgamenāpahṛtendriyāyām /
children.translated_text: "And <s>Ruru</s>, when his beloved <s>Pramadvarā</s> had her senses stolen by a serpent —

children.text: saṃdṛśya saṃdṛśya jaghāna sarpān priyaṃ na roṣeṇa tapo rarakṣa // Saund_7.37 //
children.translated_text: again and again seeing [serpents], he slaughtered them; he did not preserve his austerity through fondness, but through anger. (7.37)

children.text: naptā śaśāṅkasya yaśoguṇāṅko budhasya sūnurvibudhaprabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The grandson of the moon, marked with the virtue of fame, the son of <s>Budha</s>, of divine power —

children.text: tathorvaśīmapsarasaṃ vicintya rājarṣirunmādamagacchadaiḍaḥ // Saund_7.38 //
children.translated_text: that royal sage <s>Aiḍa</s> (<s>Purūravas</s>), brooding over the <s>Apsaras</s> <s>Urvaśī</s>, went to madness. (7.38)

children.text: rakto girermūrdhani menakāyāṃ kāmātmakatvācca sa tālajaṅghaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Passionate on the mountain-top for <s>Menakā</s>, that <s>Tālajaṅgha</s>, due to his lustful nature,

children.text: pādena viśvāvasunā saroṣaṃ vajreṇa hintāla ivābhijaghne // Saund_7.39 //
children.translated_text: was struck angrily by the foot of <s>Viśvāvasu</s> — like a <s>Hintāla</s> palm by a thunderbolt. (7.39)

children.text: nāśaṃ gatāyāṃ paramāṅganāyāṃ gaṃgājale 'naṅgaparītacetāḥ /
children.translated_text: "When the supreme woman (<s>Gaṅgā</s>) had disappeared, his mind seized by <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless Love),

children.text: janhuśca gaṅgāṃ nṛpatirbhujābhyāṃ rurodha maināka ivācalendraḥ // Saund_7.40 //
children.translated_text: the king <s>Janhū</s> (<s>Jahnu</s>) held back the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with his arms, like <s>Maināka</s>, the king of mountains. (7.40)

children.text: nṛpaśca gaṅgāvirahājjughūrṇa gaṅgāmbhasā sāla ivāttamūlaḥ /
children.translated_text: "And the king was shaken by separation from <s>Gaṅgā</s>, like a <s>Sāla</s> tree uprooted by the <s>Gaṅgā</s>'s waters —

children.text: kulapradīpaḥ pratipasya sūnuḥ śrīmattanuḥ śantanurasvatantraḥ // Saund_7.41 //
children.translated_text: the lamp of his dynasty, the son of <s>Pratipa</s>, the glorious <s>Śantanu</s>, who was not master of himself. (7.41)

children.text: hṛtāṃ ca saunandakinānu 'śocan prāptāmivorvīṃ striyamurvaśīṃ tām /
children.translated_text: "And grieving for her — the <s>Urvaśī</s>-like woman who had been taken from <s>Saunandakinī</s> (?) — as if grieving for a kingdom he had gained,

children.text: sadvṛttavarmā kila somavarmā babhrāma citodbhavabhinnavarmā // Saund_7.42 //
children.translated_text: <s>Somavarmā</s> of good conduct, it is said, wandered about, his armor broken by [the arrow of] Love. (7.42)

children.text: bhāryāṃ mṛtāṃ cānumamāra rājā bhīmaprabhāvo bhuvi bhīmakaḥ saḥ /
children.translated_text: "And the king <s>Bhīmaka</s>, of terrible might on earth, died following his dead wife;

children.text: balena senāka iti prakāśaḥ senāpatirdeva ivāttasenaḥ // Saund_7.43 //
children.translated_text: renowned as <s>Senāka</s> for his strength, a commander like a god with army raised. (7.43)

children.text: svargaṃ gate bhartari śantanau ca kālīṃ jihīrṣan janamejayaḥ saḥ /
children.translated_text: "And when her husband <s>Śantanu</s> had gone to heaven, <s>Janamejaya</s>, desiring to abduct <s>Kālī</s>,

children.text: avāpa bhīṣmāt samavetya mṛtyuṃ na tadgataṃ manmathamutsasarja // Saund_7.44 //
children.translated_text: met death in an encounter with <s>Bhīṣma</s> — and did not abandon the passion that had entered him. (7.44)

children.text: śaptaśca pāṇḍurmadanena nūnaṃ strīsaṃgame mṛtyumavāpsyasīti /
children.translated_text: "And <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, surely cursed by <s>Madana</s> (Love) — 'In the embrace of a woman you will meet death' —

children.text: jagāma mādrīṃ na maharṣiśāpādasevyasevī vimamarśa mṛtyum // Saund_7.45 //
children.translated_text: yet went to <s>Mādrī</s>, heedless of the great sage's curse, and encountered death like one who serves the unserviceable. (7.45)

children.text: evaṃvidhā devanṛparṣisaṅghāḥ strīṇāṃ vaśaṃ kāmavaśena jagmuḥ /
children.translated_text: "Thus hosts of gods, kings, and sages were brought under the sway of women through the power of desire;

children.text: dhiyā ca sāreṇa ca durbalaḥ san priyāmapaśyan kimu viklavo 'ham // Saund_7.46 //
children.translated_text: I, being weak in wisdom and in strength, not seeing my beloved — what wonder that I am so distressed? (7.46)

children.text: yāsyāmi tasmād gṛhameva bhūyaḥ kāmaṃ kariṣye vidhivat sakāmam /
children.translated_text: "Therefore I shall go home again, and I shall fulfill my desire according to propriety;

children.text: na hyanyacittasya calendriyasya liṅgaṃ kṣamaṃ dharmapathāccyutasya // Saund_7.47 //
children.translated_text: for the mendicant's garb is not fitting for one whose mind is elsewhere, whose senses are unsteady, who has fallen from the path of <s>dharma</s>. (7.47)

children.text: pāṇau kapālamavadhārya vidhāya mauṇḍyaṃ mānaṃ nidhāya vikṛtaṃ paridhāya vāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Holding the begging bowl in hand, having adopted the tonsure, having set aside pride, having put on disfiguring garments —

children.text: yasyoddhavo na dhṛtirasti na śāntirasti citrapradīpa iva so 'sti ca nāsti caiva // Saund_7.48 //
children.translated_text: one who has neither elevation nor steadfastness nor peace — like a lamp in a painting, he both exists and does not exist. (7.48)

children.text: yo niḥsṛtaśca na ca niḥsṛtakāmarāgaḥ kāṣāyamudvahati yo na ca niṣkaṣāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "One who has gone forth but has not gone forth from desire and passion, who wears the ochre robe but is not free from the stain [of passion],

children.text: pātraṃ bibharti ca guṇairna ca pātrabhūto liṅgaṃ vahannapi sa naiva gṛhī na bhikṣuḥ // Saund_7.49 //
children.translated_text: who carries the begging bowl but is not a worthy vessel through virtues — bearing the mark [of a monk], he is neither a householder nor a mendicant. (7.49)

children.text: na nyāyyamanvayavataḥ parigṛhya liṅgaṃ bhūyo vimoktumiti yo 'pi hi me vicāraḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even the thought that occurs to me — 'It is not proper for one of good lineage to discard the garb once assumed' —

children.text: so 'pi praṇaśyati vicintya nṛpapravīrāstānye tapovanamapāsya gṛhāṇyatīyuḥ // Saund_7.50 //
children.translated_text: even that vanishes when I consider those foremost warrior-kings who, abandoning the ascetic grove, returned to their homes. (7.50)

children.text: śālbādhipo hi sasuto 'pi tathāmbarīṣo rāmo 'ndha eva sa ca sāṃskṛtirantidevaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For the lord of <s>Śālva</s> together with his son, and also <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, and <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Andha</s> himself, and that descendant of <s>Saṃskṛti</s>, <s>Antideva</s> —

children.text: cīrāṇyapāsya dadhire punaraṃśukāni chittvā jaṭāśca kuṭilā mukuṭāni babhruḥ // Saund_7.51 //
children.translated_text: they cast off their bark garments and donned fine clothes again; they cut their matted locks and wore diadems. (7.51)

children.text: tasmād bhikṣārthaṃ mama gururito yāvadeva prayātas
children.translated_text: Therefore, as soon as my teacher has departed here [on his begging rounds],

children.text: tyaktvā kāṣāyaṃ ṛhamahamitastāvadeva prayāsye /
children.translated_text: I shall cast off the ochre robe and hasten homeward from here;

children.text: pūjyaṃ liṅgaṃ hi skhalitamanaso bibhrataḥ kliṣṭabuddher
children.translated_text: for one whose mind has stumbled, whose understanding is tormented, bearing the venerable garb —

children.text: nāmutrārthaḥ syādupahatamaternāpyayaṃ jīvalokaḥ // Saund_7.52 //
children.translated_text: neither is there profit in the next world, nor, with his thinking impaired, in this world of the living. (7.52)

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "nandavilāpa" nāma saptama sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh canto, entitled 'The Lament of <s>Nanda</s>,' in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.

children.text:
aṣṭamaḥ sargaḥ
strīvighna
children.translated_text:
Eighth Canto:
The Obstacle of Women

children.text: atha nandamadhīralocanaṃ gṛhayānotsukamutsukotsukam /
children.translated_text: Then [seeing] <s>Nanda</s>, with unsteady gaze, eager to go home, restlessly restless —

children.text: abhigamya śivena cakṣuṣā śramaṇaḥ kaściduvāca maitrayā // Saund_8.1 //
children.translated_text: a certain <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), approaching with benevolent eye and with friendliness, spoke: (8.1)

children.text: kimidaṃ mukhamaśrudurdinaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ vivṛṇoti te tamaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What is this? Your face, overcast with tears, reveals the darkness dwelling in your heart;

children.text: dhṛtimehi niyaccha vikriyāṃ na hi bāṣpaśca śamaśca śobhate // Saund_8.2 //
children.translated_text: take courage, restrain this disturbance — for tears and tranquility do not go well together. (8.2)

children.text: dvividhā samudeti vedanā niyataṃ cetasi deha eva ca /
children.translated_text: Sensation arises in two forms — invariably in the mind and in the body;

children.text: śrutavidhyupacārakovidā dvividhā eva tayościkitsakāḥ // Saund_8.3 //
children.translated_text: and the physicians for both of these are of two kinds: those skilled in learning and treatment. (8.3)

children.text: tadiyaṃ yadi kāyikī rujā bhiṣaje tūrṇamanūnamucyatām /
children.translated_text: If this is a bodily affliction, let it be told at once and fully to a physician;

children.text: viniguhya hi rogamāturo nacirāttīvramanarthamṛcchati // Saund_8.4 //
children.translated_text: for a sick person who conceals his disease quickly falls into severe calamity. (8.4)

children.text: atha duḥkhamidaṃ manomayaṃ vada vakṣyāmi yadatra bheṣajam /
children.translated_text: But if this suffering is born of the mind, tell me — I shall prescribe the remedy for it;

children.text: manaso hi rajastamasvino bhiṣajo 'dhyātmavidaḥ parīkṣakāḥ // Saund_8.5 //
children.translated_text: for the physicians of a mind afflicted by <s>rajas</s> (passion) and <s>tamas</s> (darkness) are those who know the inner self and are examiners. (8.5)

children.text: nikhilena ca satyamucyatāṃ yadi vācyaṃ mayi saumya manyase /
children.translated_text: And let the truth be told in full, if you think it proper to confide in me, dear friend;

children.text: gatayo vividhā hi cetasāṃ bahuguhyāni mahākulāni ca // Saund_8.6 //
children.translated_text: for the ways of minds are varied, deeply hidden, and greatly tangled.' (8.6)

children.text: iti tena sa coditastadā vyavasāyaṃ pravivakṣurātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus urged by him, [<s>Nanda</s>], wishing to disclose his own resolve,

children.text: avalambya kare kareṇa taṃ praviveśānyatarad vanāntaram // Saund_8.7 //
children.translated_text: taking him by the hand, entered another part of the forest. (8.7)

children.text: atha tatra śucau latāgṛhe kusumodgāriṇi tau niṣedatuḥ /
children.translated_text: Then in that place, in a clean bower of creepers bursting with blossoms, they sat down,

children.text: mṛdubhirmṛdumāruteritairupagūḍhāviva bālapallavaiḥ // Saund_8.8 //
children.translated_text: as if embraced by soft young shoots stirred by gentle breezes. (8.8)

children.text: sa jagāda tataścikīrṣitaṃ ghananiśvāsagṛhītamantarā /
children.translated_text: He then declared his intention, interrupted by deep sighs,

children.text: śrutavāgviśadāya bhikṣave viduṣā pravrajitena durvacam // Saund_8.9 //
children.translated_text: speaking what was difficult to say — by a wise renunciant to a monk whose speech was clear from learning. (8.9)

children.text: sadṛśaṃ yadi dharmacāriṇaḥ satataṃ prāṇiṣu maitracetasaḥ /
