children.translated_text: 'If it is fitting for a practitioner of <s>Dharma</s>, one who always has a friendly mind toward living beings,

children.text: adhṛtau yadiyaṃ hitaiṣitā mayi te syāt karuṇātmanaḥ sataḥ // Saund_8.10 //
children.translated_text: if this goodwill of yours, who are compassionate by nature, should extend to me in my distress — (8.10)

children.text: ata eva ca me viśeṣataḥ pravivakṣā kṣamavādini tvayi /
children.translated_text: for that very reason I especially wish to speak to you, who are patient in speech;

children.text: na hi bhāvamimaṃ calātmane kathayeyaṃ bruvate 'pyasādhave // Saund_8.11 //
children.translated_text: for I would not reveal this state of mind to a fickle person, even if he spoke, nor to a wicked one. (8.11)

children.text: tadidaṃ śrṛṇu me samāsato na rame dharmavidhāvṛte priyām /
children.translated_text: Then hear this from me in brief: I take no delight in the practice of <s>Dharma</s>, bereft of my beloved,

children.text: girisānuṣu kāminīmṛte kṛtaretā iva kinnaraścaran // Saund_8.12 //
children.translated_text: like a <s>Kinnara</s> wandering on mountain slopes, bereft of his mate, though still passionate. (8.12)

children.text: vanavāsasukhāt parāṅmukhaḥ prayiyāsā gṛhameva yena me /
children.translated_text: Averse to the happiness of forest dwelling, my desire is only to go home;

children.text: na hi śarma labhe tayā binā nṛpatirhīna ivottamaśriyā // Saund_8.13 //
children.translated_text: for I find no peace without her, like a king deprived of his supreme glory.' (8.13)

children.text: atha tasya niśamya tadvacaḥ priyabhāryābhimukhasya śocataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, hearing those words of his — grieving, turned toward his beloved wife —

children.text: śramaṇaḥ sa śiraḥ prakampayannijagādātmagataṃ śanairidam // Saund_8.14 //
children.translated_text: that <s>śramaṇa</s>, shaking his head, spoke slowly these words as if to himself: (8.14)

children.text: kṛpaṇaṃ bata yūthalālaso mahato vyādhabhayād viniḥsṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, how pitiable! A deer, having escaped from the great danger of the hunter, sluggish from attachment to the herd,

children.text: pravivikṣati vāgurāṃ mṛgaścapalo gītaraveṇa vañcitaḥ // Saund_8.15 //
children.translated_text: now the restless one wishes to enter the snare, deceived by the sound of a song! (8.15)

children.text: vihagaḥ khalu jālasaṃvṛto hitakāmena janena mokṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Truly, a bird, freed from a net by a person who wished it well,

children.text: vicaran phalapuṣpavadvanaṃ pravivikṣuḥ svayameva pañcaram // Saund_8.16 //
children.translated_text: wandering in a forest full of fruits and flowers, wishes of its own accord to enter the cage! (8.16)

children.text: kalabhaḥ kariṇā khalūddhṛtoḥ bahupaṅkād viṣamānnadītalāt /
children.translated_text: Truly, a young elephant, pulled out by a [mother] elephant from deep mud on a treacherous riverbank,

children.text: jalatarṣavaśena tāṃ punaḥ saritaṃ grāhavatīṃ titīrṣati // Saund_8.17 //
children.translated_text: driven by thirst for water, wishes to cross again that river full of crocodiles! (8.17)

children.text: śaraṇe sabhujaṅgame svapan pratibuddhena pareṇa bodhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: A young man, sleeping in a shelter infested with serpents, awakened by another who was alert,

children.text: taruṇaḥ khalu jātavibhramaḥ svayamugraṃ bhujagaṃ jighṛkṣati // Saund_8.18 //
children.translated_text: truly, bewildered, of his own accord wishes to seize the fierce serpent! (8.18)

children.text: mahatā khalu jātavedasā jvalitādutpatito vanadrumāt /
children.translated_text: Truly, a bird, having risen from a forest tree set ablaze by a great fire,

children.text: punaricchati nīḍatṛṣṇayā patituṃ tatra gatavyatho dvijaḥ // Saund_8.19 //
children.translated_text: out of longing for its nest, though past its distress, wishes to fall back there again! (8.19)

children.text: avaśaḥ khalu kāmamūrcchayā priyayā śyenabhayād vinākṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Truly, overpowered by the swooning of desire, the <s>jīvajīvaka</s> bird, separated from his mate by fear of a hawk,

children.text: na dhṛtiṃ samupaiti na hriyaṃ karuṇaṃ jīvati jīvajīvakaḥ // Saund_8.20 //
children.translated_text: finds neither courage nor shame, and lives pitifully. (8.20)

children.text: akṛtātmatayā tṛṣānvito ghṛṇayā caiva dhiyā ca varjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Driven by craving due to lack of self-mastery, devoid of both conscience and judgment,

children.text: aśanaṃ khalu vāntamātmanā kṛpaṇaḥ śvā punarattumicchati // Saund_8.21 //
children.translated_text: truly, a wretched dog wishes to eat again the food vomited by himself! (8.21)

children.text: iti manmathaśokakarṣitaṃ tamanudhyāya muhurnirīkṣya ca /
children.translated_text: Thus, reflecting and observing again and again that one consumed by the grief of desire,

children.text: śramaṇaḥ sa hitābhikāṅkṣayā guṇavad vākyamuvāca vipriyam // Saund_8.22 //
children.translated_text: that <s>śramaṇa</s>, out of a wish for his welfare, spoke words that were virtuous yet disagreeable. (8.22)

children.text: avicārayataḥ śubhāśubhaṃ viṣayeṣveva niviṣṭacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If, not discriminating between the wholesome and unwholesome, with mind fixed only on sense objects,

children.text: upapannamalabdhacakṣuṣo na ratiḥ śreyasi ced bhavettava // Saund_8.23 //
children.translated_text: if there were no delight in the good for you — one who has gained it [already], yet lacks vision — that would be fitting. (8.23)

children.text: śravaṇe grahaṇe 'tha dhāraṇe paramārthāvagame manaḥśame /
children.translated_text: In hearing, grasping, retaining, understanding the ultimate meaning, and calming the mind,

children.text: aviṣaktamateścalātmano na hi dharme 'bhiratirvidhīyate // Saund_8.24 //
children.translated_text: for one whose intellect is unattached and whose mind is fickle — delight in <s>Dharma</s> is indeed not to be found. (8.24)

children.text: viṣayeṣu tu doṣadarśinaḥ parituṣṭasya śuceramāninaḥ /
children.translated_text: But for one who sees faults in sense objects, who is content, pure, and free from pride,

children.text: śamakarmasu yuktacetasaḥ kṛtabuddhena ratirna vidyate // Saund_8.25 //
children.translated_text: whose mind is engaged in the work of tranquility — no delight is found by one of cultivated wisdom [in sensual pleasures]. (8.25)

children.text: ramate tṛṣito dhanaśriyā ramate kāmasukhena bāliśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The thirsty one delights in the splendor of wealth; the fool delights in the pleasure of desires;

children.text: ramate praśamena sajjanaḥ paribhogān paribhūya vidyayā // Saund_8.26 //
children.translated_text: but the good person delights in tranquility, having disdained enjoyments through wisdom. (8.26)

children.text: api ca prathitasya dhīmataḥ kulajasyārcitaliṅgadhāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, for one who is renowned, wise, of noble birth, and bears the honored insignia,

children.text: sadṛśī na gṛhāya cetanā praṇatirvāyuvaśad gireriva // Saund_8.27 //
children.translated_text: the intention toward the household is not fitting — like the bending of a mountain before the wind. (8.27)

children.text: spṛhayet parasaṃśritāya yaḥ paribhūyātmavaśāṃ svatantratām /
children.translated_text: One who, standing on the auspicious path of tranquility, would desire the household — dependent on others —

children.text: upaśāntipathe śive sthitaḥ spṛhayeddoṣavate gṛhāya saḥ // Saund_8.28 //
children.translated_text: scorning self-mastery and independence, he would desire the fault-ridden household. (8.28)

children.text: vyasanābhihato yathā viśet parimuktaḥ punareva bandhanam /
children.translated_text: Just as one struck by misfortune, though freed, would enter bondage again,

children.text: samupetya vanaṃ tathā punargṛhasaṃjñaṃ mṛgayeta bandhanam // Saund_8.29 //
children.translated_text: so having reached the forest, one would again seek the bondage called 'household.' (8.29)

children.text: puruṣaśca vihāya yaḥ kaliṃ punaricchet kalimeva sevitum /
children.translated_text: And a man who, having abandoned strife, would again wish to pursue strife —

children.text: sa vihāya bhajeta bāliśaḥ kalibhūtāmajitendriyaḥ priyām // Saund_8.30 //
children.translated_text: that fool, with senses unconquered, having abandoned [peace], would embrace his beloved who is [herself] strife. (8.30)

children.text: saviṣā iva saṃśritā latāḥ parimṛṣṭā iva soragā guhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Like creepers entwined with poison, like caves infested with serpents,

children.text: vivṛtā iva cāsayo dhṛtā vyasanāntā hi bhavanti yoṣitaḥ // Saund_8.31 //
children.translated_text: like swords concealed yet drawn — women end in calamity. (8.31)

children.text: pramadāḥ samadā madapradāḥ pramadā vitamadā bhayapradāḥ /
children.translated_text: Women (<s>pramadā</s>) are intoxicating and give intoxication; women, when bereft of passion, give fear;

children.text: iti doṣabhayāvahāśca tāḥ kathamarhanti niṣevaṇaṃ nu tāḥ // Saund_8.32 //
children.translated_text: thus, since they bring both fault and danger, how can they deserve to be served? (8.32)

children.text: svajanaḥ svajanena bhidyate suhadaścāpi suhṛjjanena yat /
children.translated_text: Kinsmen are divided from kinsmen, and friends are [divided] from friends,

children.text: paradoṣavicakṣaṇāḥ śaṭhāstadanāryāḥ pracaranti yoṣitaḥ // Saund_8.33 //
children.translated_text: because those ignoble women go about — sharp-eyed for others' faults, deceitful. (8.33)

children.text: kulajāḥ kṛpaṇībhavanti yadyadayuktaṃ pracaranti sāhasam /
children.translated_text: That men of noble birth become wretched, that they commit reckless deeds,

children.text: praviśanti ca yaccamūmukhaṃ rabhasāstatra nimittamaṅganāḥ // Saund_8.34 //
children.translated_text: that they rush headlong into the front of the army — the cause in all these cases is women. (8.34)

children.text: vacanena haranti valgunā niśitena praharanti cetasā /
children.translated_text: They captivate with sweet words and strike with a sharp mind;

children.text: madhu tiṣṭhati vāci yoṣitāṃ hṛdaye hālahalaṃ mahadviṣaśam // Saund_8.35 //
children.translated_text: honey rests on the lips of women, but deadly poison (<s>hālāhala</s>) in their hearts. (8.35)

children.text: pradahan dahano 'pi gṛhyate viśarīraḥ pavano 'pi gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: Burning fire can be grasped, bodiless wind can be grasped,

children.text: kupito bhujago 'pi gṛhyate pramadānāṃ tu mano na gṛhyate // Saund_8.36 //
children.translated_text: an angry serpent can be grasped — but the mind of women cannot be grasped. (8.36)

children.text: na vapurvimṛśanti na śriyaṃ na matiṃ nāpi kulaṃ na vikramam /
children.translated_text: They regard neither beauty, nor fortune, nor intellect, nor lineage, nor valor;

children.text: praharantyaviśeṣataḥ striyaḥ sarito grāhakulākulā iva // Saund_8.37 //
children.translated_text: women strike without distinction — like rivers crowded with crocodiles. (8.37)

children.text: na vaco madhuraṃ na lālanaṃ smarati strī na ca sauhṛdaṃ kvacit /
children.translated_text: A woman remembers neither sweet words, nor caresses, nor friendship at any time;

children.text: kalitā vanitaiva cañcalā tadihāriṣviva nāvalambyate // Saund_8.38 //
children.translated_text: adorned, a woman is fickle — therefore one should not rely upon them, as upon enemies. (8.38)

children.text: adadatsu bhavanti narmadāḥ pradadatsu praviśanti vibhramam /
children.translated_text: With those who do not give, they are playful; with those who give, they become capricious;

children.text: praṇateṣu bhavanti garvitāḥ pramadāstṛptatarāśca māniṣu // Saund_8.39 //
children.translated_text: before the humble, they are proud; and among the proud, women are even more haughty. (8.39)

children.text: guṇavatsu caranti bhartṛvad guṇahīneṣu caranti putravat /
children.translated_text: Among the virtuous, they behave as wives; among the virtue-less, they behave as toward sons;

children.text: dhanavatsu caranti tṛṣṇayā dhanahīneṣu carantyavajñayā // Saund_8.40 //
children.translated_text: among the wealthy, they act with greed; among the poor, they act with contempt. (8.40)

children.text: viṣayād viṣayāntaraṃ gatā pracaratyeva yathā hṛtāpi gau /
children.translated_text: Just as a stolen cow, going from one pasture to another, wanders on,

children.text: anavekṣitapūrvasauhṛdā ramate 'nyatra gatā tathāṅganā // Saund_8.41 //
children.translated_text: so a woman, gone elsewhere, without regard for former affection, delights in another. (8.41)

children.text: praviśantyapi hi striyaścitāmanubadhnantyapi muktajīvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: For women even enter the funeral pyre, and cling [to their husbands] having abandoned their very lives,

children.text: api bibhrati caiva yantraṇā na tu bhāvena vahanti sauhṛdam // Saund_8.42 //
children.translated_text: and even endure torments — yet they do not carry friendship in their hearts. (8.42)

children.text: ramayanti patīn kathañcana pramadā yāḥ patidevatāḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: Those women who somehow please their husbands, who treat their husbands as gods,

children.text: calacittatayā sahastraśo ramayante hṛdayaṃ svameva tāḥ // Saund_8.43 //
children.translated_text: by the fickleness of their minds, please their own hearts a thousandfold. (8.43)

children.text: śvapacaṃ kila senajitsutā cakame mīnaripuṃ kumudvatī /
children.translated_text: The daughter of <s>Senajit</s>, they say, desired a <s>śvapaca</s> (outcaste); <s>Kumudvatī</s> desired an enemy of fish;

children.text: mṛgarājamatho bṛhadrathā pramadānāmagatirna vidyate // Saund_8.44 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Bṛhadrath</s>'s [wife desired] a lion — truly there is no limit to the ways of women. (8.44)

children.text: kuruhaihayavṛṣṇivaṃśajā bahumāyākavaco 'tha śambaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Those born of the <s>Kuru</s>, <s>Haihaya</s>, and <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> lineages, and <s>Śambara</s> of many wiles and armor,

children.text: munirugratapāśca gautamaḥ samavāpurvanitoddhataṃ rajaḥ // Saund_8.45 //
children.translated_text: and the sage <s>Gautama</s> of fierce austerity — all were stained by the dust raised by women. (8.45)

children.text: akṛtajñamanāryamasthiraṃ vanitānāmidamīdṛśaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Ungrateful, ignoble, unsteady — such is the mind of women;

children.text: kathamarhati tāsu paṇḍito hṛdayaṃ sañjayituṃ calātmasu // Saund_8.46 //
children.translated_text: how then can a wise man deserve to fix his heart upon those of fickle nature? (8.46)

children.text: atha sūkṣmamatidvayāśivaṃ laghu tāsāṃ hṛdayaṃ na paśyasi /
children.translated_text: If you do not see the inauspicious, fickle, and subtle heart of women,

children.text: kimu kāyamasadgṛhaṃ sravad vanitānāmaśuciṃ na paśyasi // Saund_8.47 //
children.translated_text: then do you not see the impure body of women — that unwholesome dwelling, oozing? (8.47)

children.text: yadahanyahani pradhāvanairvasanaiścābharaṇaiśca saṃskṛtam /
children.translated_text: That which day after day, through washings, garments, and ornaments, is embellished —

children.text: aśubhaṃ tamasāvṛtekṣaṇaḥ śubhato gacchasi nāvagacchasi // Saund_8.48 //
children.translated_text: that impure [body], with eyes covered by darkness, you regard as pure — do you not understand? (8.48)

children.text: athavā samavaiṣi tattanūmaśubhāṃ tvaṃ na tu saṃvidasti te /
children.translated_text: Or perhaps you do know that body to be impure, but you have no awareness of it;

children.text: surabhiṃ vidadhāsi hi kriyāmaśucestatprabhavasya śāntaye // Saund_8.49 //
children.translated_text: for you perform sweet-smelling rites to pacify that which is born of impurity. (8.49)

children.text: anulepanamañjanaṃ srajo maṇimuktātapanīyamaṃśukam /
children.translated_text: Ointment, collyrium, garlands, gems, pearls, gold, fine cloth —

children.text: yadi sādhu kimatra yoṣitāṃ sahajaṃ tāsu vicīyatāṃ śuci // Saund_8.50 //
children.translated_text: if these are beautiful, what in this belongs to women? Let their innate purity be examined. (8.50)

children.text: malapaṅkadharā digambarā prakṛtisthairnakhadantaromabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Bearing the mud and mire, naked, with nails, teeth, and body-hair in their natural state —

children.text: yadi sā tava sundarī bhavenniyataṃ te 'dya na sundarī bhavet // Saund_8.51 //
children.translated_text: if she were your 'beautiful one,' assuredly she would not be beautiful to you today. (8.51)

children.text: stravatīmaśuciṃ spṛśecca kaḥ saghṛṇo jarjarabhāṇḍavat striyam /
children.translated_text: Who with any feeling of revulsion would touch a woman — oozing impurity, like a leaking vessel —

children.text: yadi kevalayā tvacāvṛtā na bhavenmakṣikapatramātrayā // Saund_8.52 //
children.translated_text: if she were not covered by skin, a mere fly-wing's thickness? (8.52)

children.text: tvacaveṣṭitamasthipañjaraṃ yadi kāyaṃ samavaiṣi yoṣitām /
children.translated_text: If you know the body of women to be a cage of bones wrapped in skin,

children.text: madanena ca kṛṣyase balādaghṛṇaḥ khalvadhṛtiśca manmathaḥ // Saund_8.53 //
children.translated_text: and yet are forcibly dragged by passion — truly desire is shameless and love is without restraint! (8.53)

children.text: śubhatāmaśubheṣu kalpayan nakhadantatvacakeśaromasu /
children.translated_text: Attributing beauty to the unbeautiful — nails, teeth, skin, hair, and body-hair —

children.text: avicakṣaṇa kiṃ na paśyasi prakṛtiṃ ca prabhavaṃ ca yoṣitām // Saund_8.54 //
children.translated_text: O undiscerning one, why do you not see the true nature and origin of women? (8.54)

children.text: tadavetya manaḥśarirayorvanitā doṣavatīrviśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing that women are especially full of faults in mind and body,

children.text: capalaṃ bhavanotsukaṃ manaḥ pratisaṃkhyānabalena vāryatām // Saund_8.55 //
children.translated_text: let the restless mind, eager for worldly life, be restrained by the power of reflection. (8.55)

children.text: śrutavān matimān kulodgataḥ paramasya praśamasya bhājanam /
children.translated_text: You are learned, wise, nobly born, a vessel for the supreme tranquility;

children.text: upagamya yathā tathā punarna hi bhettuṃ niyamaṃ tvamarhasi // Saund_8.56 //
children.translated_text: having approached [the <s>Dharma</s>] as you have, you should not deserve to break your vow. (8.56)

children.text: abhijanamahato manasvinaḥ priyayaśaso bahumānamicchataḥ /
children.translated_text: For a man of great nobility, of spirit, fond of good repute, and desiring honor —

children.text: nidhanamapi varaṃ sthirātmanaścyutavinayasya na caiva jīvitam // Saund_8.57 //
children.translated_text: even death is preferable for one of steadfast self, rather than a life in which discipline has fallen. (8.57)

children.text: baddhvā yathā hi kavacaṃ pragṛhītacāpo, nindyo bhavatyapasṛtaḥ samarād rathasthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as one who has put on armor and taken up a bow becomes contemptible if he retreats from battle while mounted on a chariot,

children.text: bhaikṣākamabhyupagataḥ parigṛhya liṅgaṃ, nindyastathā bhavati kāmahṛtendriyāśvaḥ // Saund_8.58 //
children.translated_text: so one who has taken up the mendicant's life and assumed the insignia becomes contemptible if the horses of his senses are seized by desire. (8.58)

children.text: hāsyo yathā ca paramābharaṇāmbarastrag bhaikṣaṃ caran dhṛtadhanuścalacitramauliḥ /
children.translated_text: And just as one wandering about begging, wearing the finest ornaments, garments, and garlands, with a bow in hand and a waving, colorful crest, would be laughable,

children.text: vairūpyamabhyupagataḥ parapiṇḍabhojī hāsyastathā gṛhasukhābhimukhaḥ satṛṣṇaḥ // Saund_8.59 //
children.translated_text: so too one who has assumed deformity [of a renunciant] and eats others' food becomes laughable if he is inclined toward household pleasures and full of craving. (8.59)

children.text: yathā svannaṃ bhuktvā paramaśayanīye 'pi śayito
children.translated_text: Just as a pig, having eaten good food and having lain on the finest couch,

children.text: varāho nirmuktaḥ punaraśuci dhāvet paricitam /
children.translated_text: once released, would again run toward the familiar filth,

children.text: tathā śreyaḥ śrṛṇvan praśamasukhamāsvādya guṇavad,
children.translated_text: so one who hears the good, who has tasted the virtuous happiness of tranquility,

children.text: vanaṃ śāntaṃ hitvā gṛhamabhilaṣet kāmatṛṣitaḥ // Saund_8.60 //
children.translated_text: and yet, thirsting for desires, would long for the household, abandoning the peaceful forest. (8.60)

children.text: yatholkā hastasthā dahati pavanapreritaśikhā
children.translated_text: Just as a torch held in the hand, its flame driven by the wind, burns [the bearer],

children.text: yathā pādākrānto daśati bhujagaḥ krodharabhasaḥ /
children.translated_text: just as a snake trodden underfoot bites with the fury of anger,

children.text: yathā hanti vyāghraḥ śiśurapi gṛhīto gṛhagataḥ
children.translated_text: just as a tiger, even a cub, when captured and brought home, kills —

children.text: tathā strīsaṃsargo bahuvidhamanarthāya bhavati // Saund_8.61 //
children.translated_text: So too, the company of women leads to manifold calamity. // Saund 8.61 //

children.text: tadvijñāya manaḥśarīraniyatānnārīṣu doṣānimān,
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing these faults toward women, fixed in mind and body,

children.text: matvā kāmasukhaṃ nadījalacalaṃ kleśāya śokāya ca /
children.translated_text: Considering sensual pleasure to be as unstable as river water, [leading] to affliction and grief,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā durbalamāmapātrasadṛśaṃ mṛtyūpasṛṣṭaṃ jagan -
children.translated_text: Seeing the world as weak, resembling an unsteady vessel, consigned to death —

children.text: nirmokṣāya kuruṣva buddhimatulāmutkaṇṭhituṃ nārhasi // Saund_8.62 //
children.translated_text: Apply your incomparable intelligence toward liberation; you should not yearn [for sensual things]. // Saund 8.62 //

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "strīvighna" nāma aṣṭama sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth canto, entitled 'The Obstacle of Women,' in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.

children.text:
navamaḥ sargaḥ
abhimānanindā
children.translated_text: Ninth Canto: The Censure of Pride

children.text: athaivamukto 'pi sa tena bhikṣuṇā jagāma naivopaśamaṃ priyāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: Then, though thus addressed by that monk, he did not attain peace regarding his beloved;

children.text: tathā hi tāmeva tadā sa cintayan na tasya śuśrāva visaṃjñavad vacaḥ // Saund_9.1 //
children.translated_text: For, thinking of her at that time, he did not hear his words, as if unconscious. // Saund 9.1 //

children.text: yathā hi vaidyasya cikīrṣataḥ śivaṃ vaco na gṛṇhāti mumūrṣurāturaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a sick man who wishes to die does not heed the words of a physician who desires his welfare,

children.text: tathaiva matto balarūpayauvanairhitaṃ na jagrāha sa tasya tadvacaḥ // Saund_9.2 //
children.translated_text: So he, intoxicated by strength, beauty, and youth, did not accept those beneficial words of his. // Saund 9.2 //

children.text: na cātra citraṃ yadi rāgapāpmanā mano 'bhibhūyeta tamovṛtātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: And it is no wonder that the mind of one whose self is enveloped in darkness should be overpowered by the evil of passion;

children.text: narasya pāpmā hi tadā nivartate yadā bhavatyantagataṃ tamastanu // Saund_9.3 //
children.translated_text: For a person's evil departs only when the darkness within him has reached its end and become thin. // Saund 9.3 //

children.text: tatastathākṣiptamavekṣya taṃ tadā balena rūpeṇa ca yauvanena ca /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing him so carried away by strength, beauty, and youth,

children.text: gṛhaprayāṇaṃ prati ca vyavasthitaṃ śaśāsa nandaṃ śramaṇaḥ sa śāntaye // Saund_9.4 //
children.translated_text: And determined to go home, that ascetic admonished <s>Nanda</s> for his peace. // Saund 9.4 //

children.text: balaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca navaṃ ca yauvanaṃ tathāvagacchāmi yathāvagacchasi /
children.translated_text: "Strength, beauty, and fresh youth — I understand them as you understand them;

children.text: ahaṃ tvidaṃ te trayamavyavasthitaṃ yathāvabuddhye na tathāvabudhyase // Saund_9.5 //
children.translated_text: But I understand what you do not — that this triad of yours is unstable. // Saund 9.5 //

children.text: idaṃ hi rogāyatanaṃ jarāvaśaṃ nadītaṭānokahavaccalācalam /
children.translated_text: For this body, the abode of disease, subject to old age, as unsteady as a tree on a river bank,

children.text: na vetsi dehaṃ jalaphenadurbalaṃ balasthatāmātmani yena manyase // Saund_9.6 //
children.translated_text: Weak as water-foam — you do not know it, hence you think yourself to be in [a state of] strength. // Saund 9.6 //

children.text: yadānnapānāsanayānakarmaṇāmasevanādapyatisevanādapi /
children.translated_text: When the body is seen to be on the verge of ruin from both the neglect and the excess

children.text: śarīramāsannavipatti dṛśyate bale 'bhimānastava kena hetunā // Saund_9.7 //
children.translated_text: Of food, drink, sitting, traveling, and activity — by what reason is your pride in strength? // Saund 9.7 //

children.text: himātapavyādhijarākṣudādibhiryadāpyanarthairupamīyate jagat /
children.translated_text: When the world is consumed by such calamities as cold, heat, disease, old age, hunger, and the rest,

children.text: jalaṃ śucau māsa ivārkaraśmibhiḥ kṣayaṃ vrajan kiṃ baladṛpta manyase // Saund_9.8 //
children.translated_text: Like water in the hot season [evaporated] by the sun's rays — going to destruction, what, O one proud of strength, do you think? // Saund 9.8 //

children.text: tvagasthimāṃsakṣatajātmakaṃ yadā śarīramāhāravaśena tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: When this body, consisting of skin, bone, flesh, and blood, subsists by the power of food,

children.text: ajasramārtaṃ satatapratikriyaṃ balānvito 'smīti kathaṃ vihanyase // Saund_9.9 //
children.translated_text: Perpetually ailing, requiring constant treatment — how are you deluded [into thinking] 'I am endowed with strength'? // Saund 9.9 //

children.text: yathā ghaṭaṃ mṛnmayamāmamāśrito narastitīrṣet kṣubhitaṃ mahārṇavam /
children.translated_text: Just as a man, relying on an unfired clay pot, would attempt to cross a turbulent ocean,

children.text: samucchrayaṃ tadvadasāramudvarahan balaṃ vyavasyed viṣayārthamudyataḥ // Saund_9.10 //
children.translated_text: So one who, bearing this lofty but essence-less [frame], would count on strength while intent on sense objects. // Saund 9.10 //

children.text: śarīramāmādapi mṛnmayād ghaṭādidaṃ tu niḥsāratamaṃ mataṃ mama /
children.translated_text: In my view, this body is even more substanceless than an unfired clay pot;

children.text: ciraṃ hi tiṣṭhed vidhivad dhṛto ghaṭaḥ samucchrayo 'yaṃ sudhṛto 'pi bhidyate // Saund_9.11 //
children.translated_text: For a pot, properly maintained, lasts a long time, but this lofty [body], even if well-tended, breaks apart. // Saund 9.11 //

children.text: yadāmbubhūvāyvanalāśca dhātavaḥ sadā viruddhā viṣamā ivoragāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the elements — water, earth, wind, and fire — always at enmity like hostile serpents,

children.text: bhavantyanarthāya śarīramāśritāḥ kathaṃ balaṃ rogavidho vyavasyasi // Saund_9.12 //
children.translated_text: Dwelling within the body, bring about calamity — how do you count on strength, O dispenser of disease? // Saund 9.12 //

children.text: prayānti mantraiḥ praśamaṃ bhujaṅgamā na mantrasādhyastu bhavanti dhātavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Serpents can be pacified by mantras, but the elements are not controllable by mantras;

children.text: kvacicca kaṃcicca daśanti pannagāḥ sadā ca sarvaṃ ca tudanti dhātavaḥ // Saund_9.13 //
children.translated_text: And serpents bite only some persons at some times, but the elements afflict everyone always. // Saund 9.13 //

children.text: idaṃ hi śayyāsanapānabhojanairguṇaiḥ śarīraṃ ciramapyavekṣitam /
children.translated_text: For this body, though long tended with the virtues of sleep, seating, drink, and food,

children.text: na marṣayatyekamapi vyatikramaṃ yato mahāśīviṣavat prakupyati // Saund_9.14 //
children.translated_text: Does not tolerate even a single transgression, for it becomes enraged like a great venomous snake. // Saund 9.14 //

children.text: yadā himārto jvalanaṃ niṣevate himaṃ nidādhābhihato 'bhikāṅkṣati /
children.translated_text: When one afflicted by cold resorts to fire, and one oppressed by heat craves coolness,

children.text: kṣudhānvito 'nnaṃ salilaṃ tṛṣānvito balaṃ kutaḥ kiṃ ca kathaṃ ca kasya ca // Saund_9.15 //
children.translated_text: When the hungry [crave] food and the thirsty [crave] water — where is strength, and what is it, and how, and whose? // Saund 9.15 //

children.text: tadevamājñāya śarīramāturaṃ balānvito 'smīti na mantumarhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing the body to be ailing, you should not think 'I am endowed with strength';

children.text: asāramasvantamaniścitaṃ jagajjagatyanitye balamavyavasthitam // Saund_9.16 //
children.translated_text: The world is essenceless, not one's own, uncertain — in an impermanent world, strength is unstable. // Saund 9.16 //

children.text: kva kārtavīryasya balābhimāninaḥ sahasrabāhobalamarjunasya tat /
children.translated_text: Where is that strength of <s>Kārtavīrya</s>, proud of his might, of <s>Arjuna</s> of the thousand arms?

children.text: cakarta bāhūn yudhi yasya bhārgavaḥ mahānti śrṛṅgāṇyaśanirgiretiva // Saund_9.17 //
children.translated_text: Whose arms <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) cut off in battle, like lightning [striking] great peaks of a mountain. // Saund 9.17 //

children.text: kva tad valaṃ kaṃsavikarṣiṇo haresturaṅgarājasya puṭāvabhedinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where is that strength of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the subduer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the splitter of the jaws of the king of horses?

children.text: yamekabāṇena nijaghnivān jarāḥ kramāgatā rūpamivottamaṃ jarā // Saund_9.18 //
children.translated_text: Whom old age, gradually arriving, slew with a single arrow, as old age [destroys] the most excellent form. // Saund 9.18 //

children.text: diteḥ sutasyāmararoṣakāriṇaścamūrucervā namuceḥ kva tad balam /
children.translated_text: Where is that strength of <s>Diti</s>'s son, who provoked the wrath of the immortals, or of <s>Namuci</s> with his mighty thighs?

children.text: yamāhave kruddhamivāntakaṃ sthitaṃ jaghāna phenāvayavena vāsavaḥ // Saund_9.19 //
children.translated_text: Whom <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>), standing [in battle] like wrathful Death itself, slew with a weapon made of foam. // Saund 9.19 //

children.text: balaṃ kurūṇāṃ kva ca tattadābhavad yudhi jvalitvā tarasaujasā ca ye /
children.translated_text: And where was that strength of the <s>Kurus</s>, who blazed in battle with speed and vigor,

children.text: samitsamiddhā jvalanā ivādhvare hatāsavo bhasmani paryavasthitāḥ // Saund_9.20 //
children.translated_text: Who, like fires kindled at a sacrifice, their lives extinguished, came to rest in ashes? // Saund 9.20 //

children.text: ato viditvā balavīryamānināṃ balānvitānāmavamarditaṃ balam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing that the strength of those who prided themselves on strength and valor was crushed,

children.text: jagajjarāmṛtyuvaśaṃ vicārayan bale 'bhimānaṃ na vidhātumarhasi // Saund_9.21 //
children.translated_text: Reflecting that the world is subject to old age and death — you should not entertain pride in strength. // Saund 9.21 //

children.text: balaṃ mahad yadi vā na manyase kuruṣva yuddhaṃ saha tāvadindriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: If you consider your strength to be great, then fight first with your own senses;

children.text: jayaśca te 'trāsti mahacca te balaṃ parājayaśced vitathaṃ ca te balam // Saund_9.22 //
children.translated_text: If you are victorious therein, your strength is great; but if defeated, your strength is false. // Saund 9.22 //

children.text: tathā hi vīrāḥ puruṣā na te matā jayanti ye sāśvarathadvipānarīn
yathā matā vīratarā manīṣiṇo jayanti lolāni ṣaḍindriyāṇi ye // Saund_9.23 //
children.translated_text: As much as the wise are considered more heroic who conquer the six restless senses. // Saund 9.23 //
For those men are not considered heroes who conquer [foes with] horses, chariots, elephants, and armies,

children.text: ahaṃ vapuṣmāniti yacca manyase vicakṣaṇaṃ naitadidaṃ ca gṛhyatām /
children.translated_text: 'I am handsome' — if you think this, it is not discerning; and consider this:

children.text: kva tadvapuḥ sā ca vapuṣmatī tanurgadasya śāmbasya ca sāraṇasya ca // Saund_9.24 //
children.translated_text: Where is that beauty and those handsome forms of <s>Gada</s>, <s>Sāmba</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>? // Saund 9.24 //

children.text: yathā mayūraścalacitracandrako bibharti rūpaṃ guṇavat svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a peacock with its trembling, colorful crest bears beauty by its very nature,

children.text: śarīrasaṃskāraguṇādṛte tathā bibharti rūpaṃ yadi rūpavānasi // Saund_9.25 //
children.translated_text: If you are handsome, do you bear beauty in that manner, apart from the merit of bodily adornment? // Saund 9.25 //

children.text: yadi pratīpaṃ vṛṇuyānna vāsasā na śaucakāle yadi saṃspṛśedapaḥ /
children.translated_text: If one were to wear garments the wrong way, if one did not touch water at the time of purification,

children.text: mṛjāviśeṣaṃ yadi nādadīta vā vapurvapuṣman vada kīdṛśaṃ bhavet // Saund_9.26 //
children.translated_text: If one did not adopt special grooming — tell me, what would the form of the handsome one be? // Saund 9.26 //

children.text: navaṃ vayaścātmagataṃ niśāmya yadgṛ honmukhaṃ te viṣayāptaye manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Perceiving the fresh youth within yourself, if your mind, eager for sense objects, turns homeward,

children.text: niyaccha tacchailanadīrayopamaṃ drutaṃ hi gacchatyanivarti yauvanam // Saund_9.27 //
children.translated_text: Restrain it — for like a mountain torrent, youth swiftly passes, never to return. // Saund 9.27 //

children.text: ṛturvyatītaḥ parivartate punaḥ kṣayaṃ prayātaḥ punareti candramāḥ /
children.translated_text: A season that has passed revolves again; the moon that has waned returns once more;

children.text: gataṃ gataṃ naiva tu saṃnivartate jalaṃ nadīnāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ ca yauvanam // Saund_9.28 //
children.translated_text: But the youth of rivers' waters and of men, once gone, never returns. // Saund 9.28 //

children.text: vivarṇitaśmaśru valīvikuñcitaṃ viśīrṇadantaṃ śithilabhru niṣprabham /
children.translated_text: When you shall see your face discolored in beard, wrinkled with folds, with teeth fallen out, eyebrows drooping, lusterless,

children.text: yadā mukhaṃ drakṣyasi jarjaraṃ tadā jarābhibhūto vimado bhaviṣyasi // Saund_9.29 //
children.translated_text: Decrepit — then, overcome by old age, you will become free of pride. // Saund 9.29 //

children.text: niṣevya pānaṃ madanīyamuttamaṃ niśāvivāseṣu cirād vimādyati /
children.translated_text: Having partaken of the finest intoxicating drink, at night's entertainment, one eventually becomes sober;

children.text: narastu matto balarūpayouvanairna kaścidaprāpya jarāṃ vimādyati // Saund_9.30 //
children.translated_text: But a man intoxicated by strength, beauty, and youth — no one becomes sober without reaching old age. // Saund 9.30 //

children.text: yathekṣuratyantarasaprapīḍito bhuvi praviddho dahanāya śuṣyate /
children.translated_text: Just as sugarcane, excessively pressed for its juice, discarded on the ground, dries up for burning,

children.text: tathā jarāyantranipīḍitā tanurnipītasārā maraṇāya tiṣṭhati // Saund_9.31 //
children.translated_text: So the body, squeezed by the press of old age, its essence drained, remains [only] for death. // Saund 9.31 //

children.text: yathā hi nṛbhyāṃ karapatramīritaṃ samucchritaṃ dāru bhinattyanekadhā /
children.translated_text: Just as a saw driven by two men splits a tall tree into many pieces,

children.text: tathocchritāṃ pātayati prajāmimāmaharniśābhyāmupasaṃhitā jarā // Saund_9.32 //
children.translated_text: So old age, driven by day and night, fells these lofty beings. // Saund 9.32 //

children.text: smṛteḥ pramoṣo vapuṣaḥ parābhavo rateḥ kṣayo vācchruticakṣuṣāṃ grahaḥ /
children.translated_text: The theft of memory, the defeat of the body, the loss of pleasure, the impairment of speech, hearing, and sight,

children.text: śramasya yonirbalavīryayorvadho jarāsamo nāsti śarīriṇāṃ ripuḥ // Saund_9.33 //
children.translated_text: The source of weariness, the slaying of strength and vigor — there is no enemy of embodied beings equal to old age. // Saund 9.33 //

children.text: idaṃ viditvā nidhanasya daiśikaṃ jarābhidhānaṃ jagato mahadbhayam /
children.translated_text: Knowing this, the great terror of the world called old age, the guide to destruction,

children.text: ahaṃ vapuṣmān balavān yuveti vā na mānamāroḍhumanāryamarhasi // Saund_9.34 //
children.translated_text: You should not be so ignoble as to mount the pride of 'I am handsome, strong, or young.' // Saund 9.34 //

children.text: ahaṃ mametyeva ca raktacetasāṃ śarīrasaṃjñā tava yaḥ kalau grahaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I, mine' — your clinging to the notion of the body, born of a mind stained with passion,

children.text: tamutsṛjaivaṃ yadi śāmyatā bhaved bhayaṃ hyahaṃ ceti mameti cārchati // Saund_9.35 //
children.translated_text: Abandon it; if there could be peace [thereby] — for fear arises from [the notions] 'I' and 'mine.' // Saund 9.35 //

children.text: yadā śarīre na vaśo 'sti kasyacinnirasyamāne vividhairupaplavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: When no one has control over the body, which is assailed by various calamities,

children.text: kathaṃ kṣamaṃ vettumahaṃ mameti vā śarīrasaṃjñaṃ gṛhamāpadāmidam // Saund_9.36 //
children.translated_text: How is it fitting to know [it as] 'I' or 'mine' — this body-notion, this abode of misfortunes? // Saund 9.36 //

children.text: sapannage yaḥ kugṛhe sadāśucau rameta nityaṃ pratisaṃskṛte 'bale /
children.translated_text: One who would delight in a wretched house — infested with serpents, ever impure, constantly requiring repair, and weak —

children.text: sa duṣṭadhātāvaśucau calācale rameta kāye viparītadarśanaḥ // Saund_9.37 //
children.translated_text: He, of perverted vision, would delight in this body of corrupt elements, impure, unstable, and ever-changing. // Saund 9.37 //

children.text: yathā prajābhyaḥ kunṛpo balād balīn haratyaśeṣaṃ ca na cābhirakṣati /
children.translated_text: Just as a wicked king forcibly takes tribute from his subjects, all of it, yet does not protect them,

children.text: tathaiva kāyo vasanādisādhanaṃ haratyaśeṣaṃ ca na cānuvartate // Saund_9.38 //
children.translated_text: So too the body takes all that is furnished — clothing and the rest — yet does not comply [with our wishes]. // Saund 9.38 //

children.text: yathā prarohanti tṛṇānyayatnataḥ kṣitau prayatnāt tu bhavanti śālayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as weeds grow effortlessly on the ground, while rice grows only with effort,

children.text: tathaiva duḥkhāni bhavantyayatnataḥ sukhāni yatnena bhavanti vā na vā // Saund_9.39 //
children.translated_text: So too sufferings arise effortlessly, while pleasures come with effort — or not at all. // Saund 9.39 //

children.text: śarīramārtaṃ parikarṣataścalaṃ na cāsti kiñcit paramārthataḥ sukham /
children.translated_text: Dragging along this ailing, unstable body — there is no true happiness in the ultimate sense;

children.text: sukhaṃ hi duḥkhapratikārasevayā sthite ca duḥkhe tanuni vyavasyati // Saund_9.40 //
children.translated_text: For what is called happiness is [merely] the application of a remedy to pain, and [even that] happiness is recognized only when the pain subsides to a small degree. // Saund 9.40 //

children.text: yathānapekṣyāgryamapīpsitaṃ sukhaṃ pravādhate duḥkhamupetamaṇvapi /
children.translated_text: Just as, disregarding even the foremost desired happiness, even a tiny pain that has arrived overpowers [it],

children.text: tathānapekṣyātmani duḥkhamāgataṃ na vidyate kiñcana kasyacit sukhaṃ // Saund_9.41 //
children.translated_text: So, not disregarding the suffering that has come upon oneself, there is no happiness whatsoever for anyone. // Saund 9.41 //

children.text: śarīramīdṛg bahuduḥkhādhruvaṃ phalānurodhādatha nāvagacchasi /
children.translated_text: If you do not understand this body, which is such — full of suffering and impermanent — because of attachment to its fruits,

children.text: dravatphalebhyo dhṛtiraśmibhirmano nigṛhyatāṃ gauriva śasyalālasā // Saund_9.42 //
children.translated_text: Then let the mind be restrained with reins from fleeting pleasures, like a cow greedy for grain. // Saund 9.42 //

children.text: na kāmabhogā hi bhavanti tṛptaye havīṃṣi dīptasya vibhāvasoriva /
children.translated_text: For sensual pleasures do not lead to satisfaction, just as oblations [do not satisfy] a blazing fire;

children.text: yathā yathā kāmasukheṣu vartate tathā tathecchā viṣayeṣu varddhate // Saund_9.43 //
children.translated_text: The more one indulges in sensual pleasures, the more desire grows for sense objects. // Saund 9.43 //

children.text: yathā ca kuṣṭhavyasanena duḥkhitaḥ pratāpanānnaiva śamaṃ nigacchati /
children.translated_text: And just as one afflicted with leprosy, through heating [the sores], does not attain relief,

children.text: tathendriyārtheṣvajitendriyaścaranna kāmabhogairupaśāntimṛcchati // Saund_9.44 //
children.translated_text: So one who has not conquered the senses, roaming among sense objects, does not reach peace through sensual enjoyments. // Saund 9.44 //

children.text: yathā hi bhaiṣajyasukhābhikāṅkṣayā bhajeta rogānna bhajeta tatkṣamam /
children.translated_text: Just as one who, craving the pleasure of medicine, would invite diseases rather than what is appropriate for them,

children.text: tathā śarīre bahuduḥkhabhājane rameta mohād viṣayābhikāṅkṣayā // Saund_9.45 //
children.translated_text: So through delusion one would delight in this body, a vessel of much suffering, out of craving for sense objects. // Saund 9.45 //

children.text: anarthakāmaḥ puruṣasya yo janaḥ sa tasya śatruḥ kila tena karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: A person who desires harm for another is surely his enemy by that very action;

children.text: anarthamūlā viṣayāśca kevalā nanu praheyā viṣamā yathārayaḥ // Saund_9.46 //
children.translated_text: And sense objects are nothing but the root of harm — surely they should be abandoned, like dangerous enemies. // Saund 9.46 //

children.text: ihaiva bhūtvā ripavo vadhātmakāḥ prayānti kāle puruṣasya mitratāṃ /
children.translated_text: Even enemies whose nature is to kill become friends of a person in the course of time here in this world;

children.text: paratra caiveha ca duḥkhahetavo bhavanti kāmā na tu kasyacicchivāḥ // Saund_9.47 //
children.translated_text: But sensual desires (<s>kāmas</s>), causing suffering both here and hereafter, are never auspicious for anyone. // Saund 9.47 //

children.text: yathopayuktaṃ rasavarṇagandhavad vadhāya kimpākaphalaṃ na puṣṭaye /
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>kimpāka</s> (Strychnos) fruit, though consumed [for its] taste, color, and fragrance, leads to death, not nourishment,

children.text: niṣevyamāṇā viṣayāścalātmano bhavantyanarthāya tathā na bhūtaye // Saund_9.48 //
children.translated_text: So sense objects, when indulged in by one of unsteady mind, lead to harm, not to well-being. // Saund 9.48 //

children.text: tadetadājñāya vipāpmanātmanā vimokṣadharmādyupasahitaṃ hitam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing this, with a sinless self, accept my view, which is conjoined with the <s>Dharma</s> of liberation and so forth, which is beneficial,

children.text: juṣasva me sajjanasaṃmataṃ mataṃ pracakṣva vā niścayamud giran giram // Saund_9.49 //
children.translated_text: Approved by the good — or else declare your firm resolve, uttering your [own] word. // Saund 9.49 //

children.text: iti hitamapi bahvapīdamuktaḥ śrutamahatā śramaṇena tena nandaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed with much that was beneficial by that monk of great learning, <s>Nanda</s>

children.text: na dhṛtimupayayau na śarma lebhe dvirada ivātimado madāndhacetāḥ // Saund_9.50 //
children.translated_text: Neither found steadiness nor obtained peace — like a rogue elephant, excessively maddened, blind with rut. // Saund 9.50 //

children.text: nandasya bhāvamavagamya tataḥ sa bhikṣuḥ pāriplavaṃ gṛhasukhābhimukhaṃ na dharme /
children.translated_text: Then that monk, perceiving <s>Nanda</s>'s disposition — wavering, inclined toward household pleasures, not toward the <s>Dharma</s> —

children.text: sattvāśayānuśayabhāvaparīkṣakāya buddhāya tattvaviduṣe kathayāṃcakāra // Saund_9.51 //
children.translated_text: Reported it to the <s>Buddha</s>, the knower of truth, who examines the dispositions, latent tendencies, and natures of beings. // Saund 9.51 //

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "abhimānanindā" nāma navama sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth canto, entitled 'The Censure of Pride,' in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.

children.text:
daśamaḥ sargaḥ
svargadarśana
children.translated_text: Tenth Canto: The Vision of Heaven

children.text: śrutvā tataḥ sadvratamutsisṛkṣuṃ bhāryāṃ didṛkṣuṃ bhavanaṃ vivikṣum /
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that he wished to abandon the excellent vow, wished to see his wife, and wished to enter the household,

children.text: nandaṃ nirānandamapetadhairyamabhyujjihīrṣurmunirājuhāva // Saund_10.1 //
children.translated_text: the sage, desiring to rescue the joyless <s>Nanda</s> who had lost his composure, summoned him. (10.1)

children.text: taṃ prāptamaprāptavimokṣamārgaṃ papraccha cittaskhalitaṃ sucittaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, who had arrived but had not attained the path of liberation, whose mind had stumbled, was questioned by the clear-minded one;

children.text: sa hrīmate hrīvinato jagāda svaṃ niścayaṃ niścayakovidāya // Saund_10.2 //
children.translated_text: and he, modest and bowing before the modest one, declared his resolution to the one skilled in resolution. (10.2)

children.text: nandaṃ viditvā sugatastatastaṃ bhāryābhidhāne tamasi bhramantam /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), having understood that <s>Nanda</s> was wandering in the darkness called "wife,"

children.text: pāṇau gṛhītvā viyadutpapāta malaṃ jale sādhurivojjihīrṣuḥ // Saund_10.3 //
children.translated_text: took him by the hand and flew up into the sky, like a good man wishing to extract impurity from water. (10.3)

children.text: kāṣāyavastrau kanakāvadātau virejatustau nabhasi prasanne /
children.translated_text: The two of them, wearing ochre robes and golden in complexion, shone resplendent in the clear sky,

children.text: anyonyasaṃśliṣṭavikīrṇapakṣau saraḥprakīrṇāviva cakravākau // Saund_10.4 //
children.translated_text: like a pair of <s>cakravāka</s> birds with wings interlocked and spread, scattered from a lake. (10.4)

children.text: tau devadārūttamagandhavantaṃ nadīsaraḥprasravaṇaughavantam /
children.translated_text: They swiftly reached <s>Himavat</s> (the Himalayas), fragrant with the finest <s>devadāru</s> (divine cedar) trees,

children.text: ājagmatuḥ kāñcanadhātumantaṃ devarṣimantaṃ himavantamāśu // Saund_10.5 //
children.translated_text: abounding in rivers, lakes, and waterfalls, rich in veins of gold, and frequented by divine sages. (10.5)

children.text: tasmin girau cāraṇāsiddhajuṣṭe śive havirdhūmakṛtottarīye /
children.translated_text: On that mountain, frequented by <s>Cāraṇas</s> and <s>Siddhas</s>, auspicious, wearing the smoke of sacrificial offerings as an upper garment,

children.text: agamyapārasya nirāśrayasya tau tasthaturdvīpa ivāmbarasya // Saund_10.6 //
children.translated_text: they stood like an island in the fathomless, shelterless sky. (10.6)

children.text: śāntendriye tatra munau sthite tu savismayaṃ dikṣu dadarśa nandaḥ /
children.translated_text: While the sage of tranquil senses stood there, <s>Nanda</s> looked about in all directions with wonder,

children.text: darīśca kuñjāṃśca vanaukasaśca vibhūṣaṇaṃ rakṣaṇameva cādreḥ // Saund_10.7 //
children.translated_text: at the caves, groves, and forest-dwellers — the very ornament and guardians of the mountain. (10.7)

children.text: bahvāyate tatra site hi śṛṅge saṃkṣiptabarhaḥ śayito mayūraḥ /
children.translated_text: For on a tall white peak there, a peacock with its plumage folded, lying at rest,

children.text: bhuje balasyāyatapīnabāhorvaiḍūryakeyūra ivābabhāse // Saund_10.8 //
children.translated_text: appeared like a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) armlet on the long, full arm of <s>Bala</s> (a mighty being). (10.8)

children.text: manaḥśīlādhātuśilāśrayeṇa pītākṛtāṃso virarāja siṃhaḥ /
children.translated_text: A lion, its shoulders made yellow by resting on slabs of realgar-hued mineral rock,

children.text: saṃtaptacāmīkarabhakticitraṃ rūpyāṅgadaṃ śīrṇamivāmbikasya // Saund_10.9 //
children.translated_text: shone like the fallen silver armlet of <s>Ambika</s>'s lord (<s>Śiva</s>), variegated with streaks of molten gold. (10.9)

children.text: vyāghraḥ klamavyāyatakhelagāmī lāṅgūlacakreṇa kṛtāpasavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: A tiger, moving with a slow, extended, and languid gait, circumambulating with its curling tail,

children.text: babhau gireḥ prasravaṇa pipāsurditsan pitṛbhyo 'mbha ivāvatīrṇaḥ // Saund_10.10 //
children.translated_text: shone as it descended toward a mountain stream to drink, as if going down to offer water to the ancestors. (10.10)

children.text: calatkadambe himavannitambe tarau pralambe camaro lalambe /
children.translated_text: On the slope of <s>Himavat</s>, upon a low-hanging branch of a swaying <s>kadamba</s> tree, a yak hung suspended;

children.text: chettuṃ vilagnaṃ na śaśāka bālaṃ kulodgatāṃ prītimivāryavṛttaḥ // Saund_10.11 //
children.translated_text: it could not bring itself to sever its tangled young [tail-hair], like one of noble conduct [who cannot cut off] the affection arising from his family. (10.11)

children.text: suvarṇagaurāśca kirātasaṃghā mayūrapitrojjvalagātralekhāḥ /
children.translated_text: And bands of <s>Kirātas</s> (mountain tribesmen), golden-hued, with body-lines brilliant as peacock feathers,

children.text: śārdūlapātapratimā guhābhyo niṣpeturudgāra ivācalasya // Saund_10.12 //
children.translated_text: sprang from the caves with the swiftness of leopards, like eruptions from the mountain. (10.12)

children.text: darīcarīṇāmatisundarīṇāṃ manoharaśroṇikucodarīṇām /
children.translated_text: In every direction, groups of exceedingly beautiful <s>Kinnarī</s> women — cave-dwellers with captivating hips, breasts, and waists —

children.text: vṛndāni rejurdiśi kinnarīṇāṃ puṣpotkacānāmiva vallarīṇām // Saund_10.13 //
children.translated_text: shone like clusters of flowering creepers with blossoming tips. (10.13)

children.text: nagānnagasyopari devadārūnāyāsayantaḥ kapayo viceruḥ /
children.translated_text: Monkeys roamed about, straining the <s>devadāru</s> trees atop trees upon the mountain;

children.text: tebhyaḥ phalaṃ nāpurato 'pajagmurmoghaprasādebhya iveśvarebhyaḥ // Saund_10.14 //
children.translated_text: they obtained no fruit from those [trees], as if from lords whose favors are fruitless. (10.14)

children.text: tasmāttu yūthādapasāryamāṇāṃ niṣpīḍitālaktakaraktavaktrām /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing a she-monkey being driven away from a troop, her face reddened as if smeared with pressed lac,

children.text: śākhāmṛgīmekavipannadṛṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭvā munirnandamidaṃ babhāṣe // Saund_10.15 //
children.translated_text: with one eye ruined, the sage spoke thus to <s>Nanda</s>: (10.15)

children.text: kā nanda rūpeṇa ca ceṣṭayā ca saṃpaśyataścārutarā matā te /
children.translated_text: "Who, <s>Nanda</s>, do you consider more beautiful in form and bearing as you behold [them] —

children.text: eṣā mṛgī vaikavipannadṛṣṭiḥ sa vā jano yatra gatā taveṣṭiḥ // Saund_10.16 //
children.translated_text: this she-monkey with one eye ruined, or that person toward whom your desire has gone?" (10.16)

children.text: ityevamuktaḥ sugatena nandaḥ kṛtvā smitaṃ kiṃcididaṃ jagāda /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the <s>Sugata</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, with a slight smile, said:

children.text: kva cottamastrī bhagavan vadhūste mṛgī nagakleśakarī kva caiṣā // Saund_10.17 //
children.translated_text: "Where, O Lord, is the supreme woman, your daughter-in-law, and where is this she-monkey, a source of mountain-misery?" (10.17)

children.text: tato munistasya niśamya vākyaṃ hetvantaraṃ kiṃcidavekṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the sage, having heard his words and considering some further purpose,

children.text: ālambya nandaṃ prayayau tathaiva krīḍāvanaṃ vajradharasya rājñaḥ // Saund_10.18 //
children.translated_text: took hold of <s>Nanda</s> and proceeded in the same manner to the pleasure-garden of king <s>Vajradhara</s> (<s>Indra</s>). (10.18)

children.text: ṛtāvṛtāvākṛtimeka eke kṣaṇe kṣaṇe bibhrati yatra vṛkṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where certain trees bear a single form in each season,

children.text: citrāṃ samastāmapi kecidanye ṣaṇṇāmṛtūnāṃ śriyamudvahanti // Saund_10.19 //
children.translated_text: while certain others bear simultaneously the varied splendor of all six seasons. (10.19)

children.text: puṣyanti kecit surabhīrudārā mālāḥ srajaśca granthitā vicitrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some put forth fragrant, magnificent garlands and intricately woven wreaths,

children.text: karṇānukūlānavataṃsakāṃśca pratyarthibhūtāniva kuṇḍalānām // Saund_10.20 //
children.translated_text: and ear-ornaments pleasing to the ear, as if rivaling earrings. (10.20)

children.text: raktāni phullāḥ kamalāni yatra pradīpavṛkṣā iva bhānti vṛkṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where certain trees, blooming with red lotuses, shine like lamp-trees,

children.text: praphullanīlotpalarohiṇo 'nye sonmīlitākṣā eva bhānti vṛkṣāḥ // Saund_10.21 //
children.translated_text: while other trees, bearing blooming blue lotuses, shine as if with half-opened eyes. (10.21)

children.text: nānāvirāgāṇyatha pāṇḍarāṇi suvarṇabhaktivyavabhāsitāni /
children.translated_text: Where trees bear garments — of various faded colors, and white ones,

children.text: atāntavānyekaghanāni yatra sūkṣmāṇi vāsāṃsi phalanti vṛkṣāḥ // Saund_10.22 //
children.translated_text: illuminated with golden patterns, unwoven, of a single weave, and fine. (10.22)

children.text: hārān maṇinuttamakuṇḍalāni keyūravaryāṇyatha nūpurāṇi /
children.translated_text: Where trees bear ornaments befitting heaven — necklaces, jewels, excellent earrings,

children.text: evaṃvidhānyābharaṇāni yatra svargānurūpāṇi phalanti vṛkṣāḥ // Saund_10.23 //
children.translated_text: the finest armlets, and anklets of such kind. (10.23)

children.text: vaiḍūryanālāni ca kāñcanāni padmāni vajrāṅkurakesarāṇi /
children.translated_text: And lotuses with stems of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) and petals of gold,

children.text: sparśakṣamāṇyuttamagandhavanti rohanti niṣkampatalā nalinyaḥ // Saund_10.24 //
children.translated_text: with diamond-tipped filaments, touchable and supremely fragrant, grow in ponds with still waters. (10.24)

children.text: yatrāyatāṃścaiva tatāṃśca tāṃstān vādyasya hetūn suṣirān ghanāṃśca /
children.translated_text: Where trees, variegated with jewels and gold, companions of play for the denizens of heaven,

children.text: phalanti vṛkṣā maṇihemacitrāḥ krīḍāsahāyāstridaśālayānām // Saund_10.25 //
children.translated_text: bear as fruits the various instruments of music — elongated and broad, hollow and solid. (10.25)

children.text: mandāravṛkṣāṃśca kuśeśayāṃśca puṣpānatān kokanadāṃśca vṛkṣān /
children.translated_text: Where that <s>Pārijāta</s> tree reigns supreme, outshining with its majestic qualities

children.text: ākramya māhātmyaguṇairvirājan rājāyate yatra sa pārijātaḥ // Saund_10.26 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Mandāra</s> trees, the lotuses, the <s>kuśeśaya</s> flowers, and the <s>kokanada</s> trees bowed down with blossoms. (10.26)

children.text: kṛṣṭe tapaḥśīlahalairakhinnaistriviṣṭapakṣetratale prasūtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where such trees, produced on the ground of the heavenly field ploughed by the tireless ploughs of austerity and virtue,

children.text: evaṃvidhā yatra sadānuvṛttā divaukasāṃ bhogavidhānavṛkṣāḥ // Saund_10.27 //
children.translated_text: always attend upon the celestials, providing for their enjoyment. (10.27)

children.text: manaḥśilābhairvadanairvihaṃgā yatrākṣibhiḥ sphāṭikasaṃnibhaiśca /
children.translated_text: Where birds have faces [red] as realgar, eyes resembling crystal,

children.text: śāvaiśca pakṣairabhilohitāntairmāñjiṣṭhakairardhasitaiśca pādaiḥ // Saund_10.28 //
children.translated_text: young wings with crimson tips, and feet half-red, half-white like <s>mañjiṣṭha</s> (madder dye). (10.28)

children.text: citraiḥ suvarṇacchadanaistathānye vaiḍuryanīlairnayanaiḥ prasannaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And other birds called <s>śiñjirikā</s>, with variegated golden plumage,

children.text: vihaṃgamāḥ śiñjirikābhidhānā rutairmanaḥśrotraharairbhramanti // Saund_10.29 //
children.translated_text: clear eyes blue as <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, wander about with songs that captivate the mind and ear. (10.29)

children.text: raktābhiragreṣu ca vallarībhirmadhyeṣu cāmīkarapiñjarābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Where birds wander adorned with creepers — red at the tips,

children.text: vaiḍūryavarṇābhirupāntamadhyeṣvalaṃkṛtā yatra khagāścaranti // Saund_10.30 //
children.translated_text: gold-tawny in the middle, and <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-colored at the edges of the middle portions. (10.30)

children.text: rociṣṇavo nāma patatriṇo 'nye diptāgnivarṇā jvalitairivāsyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Other birds called <s>rociṣṇu</s> ("radiant ones"), of blazing fire-like color, with mouths as if aflame,

children.text: bhramanti dṛṣṭīrvapuṣākṣipantaḥ svanaiḥ śubhairapsaraso harantaḥ // Saund_10.31 //
children.translated_text: wander about, dazzling the eyes with their beauty, captivating the <s>Apsarases</s> with their auspicious songs. (10.31)

children.text: yatreṣṭaceṣṭāḥ satataprahṛṣṭā nirartayo nirjaraso viśokāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where the meritorious ones, with forms as they desire, perpetually delighted, free from distress, free from aging, free from grief,

children.text: svaiḥ karmabhirhīnaviśiṣṭamadhyāḥ svayaṃprabhāḥ puṇyakṛto ramante // Saund_10.32 //
children.translated_text: of inferior, superior, and middling [rank] according to their own deeds, self-luminous, take their pleasure. (10.32)

children.text: pūrvaṃ tapomūlyaparigraheṇa svargakrayārthaṃ kṛtaniścayānām /
children.translated_text: Where the playful <s>Apsarases</s> steal the weary minds of those rich in austerities

children.text: manāṃsi khinnāni tapodhanānāṃ haranti yatrāpsaraso laḍantyaḥ // Saund_10.33 //
children.translated_text: who had formerly resolved to purchase heaven with the price of their penance. (10.33)

children.text: nityotsavaṃ taṃ ca niśāmya lokaṃ nistandrinidrāratiśokarogam /
children.translated_text: And beholding that world of perpetual festivity, free from torpor, sleep, displeasure, grief, and disease,

children.text: nando jarāmṛtyuvaśaṃ sadārtaṃ mene śmaśānapratimaṃ nṛlokam // Saund_10.34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> deemed the human world — subject to old age and death, always afflicted — to be like a cremation ground. (10.34)

children.text: aindraṃ vanaṃ tacca dadarśa nandaḥ samantato vismayaphulladṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> beheld that garden of <s>Indra</s>, his gaze blossoming wide with wonder on all sides;

children.text: harṣānvitāścāpsarasaḥ parīyuḥ sagarvamanyonyamavekṣamāṇāḥ // Saund_10.35 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Apsarases</s>, filled with joy, surrounded [him], glancing at one another with pride. (10.35)

children.text: sadā yuvatyo madanaikakāryāḥ sādhāraṇāḥ puṇyakṛtāṃ vihārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Ever youthful, occupied solely with love, shared among the meritorious, the delight of the gods —

children.text: divyāśca nirdoṣaparigrahāśca tapaḥphalasyāśrayaṇaṃ surāṇām // Saund_10.36 //
children.translated_text: divine and with faultless attendants — [they are] the resort of the fruit of austerity. (10.36)

children.text: tāsāṃ jagurdhīramudāttamanyāḥ padmāni kāścillalitaṃ babhañjuḥ /
children.translated_text: Some of them sang in deep, exalted tones; some gracefully plucked lotuses;

children.text: anyonyaharṣān nanṛtustathānyāścitrāṅgahārāḥ stanabhinnahārāḥ // Saund_10.37 //
children.translated_text: and others danced with joy at one another, with varied bodily gestures, their necklaces broken against their breasts. (10.37)

children.text: kāsāṃcidāsāṃ vadanāni rejurvanāntarebhyaścalakuṇḍalāni /
children.translated_text: The faces of some of them, with trembling earrings, shone forth from the interiors of the groves,

children.text: vyāviddhaparṇebhya ivākarebhyaḥ padmāni kāraṇḍavaghaṭṭitāni // Saund_10.38 //
children.translated_text: like lotuses disturbed by <s>kāraṇḍava</s> birds, [emerging] from thickets with parted leaves. (10.38)

children.text: tāḥ niḥsṛtāḥ prekṣya vanāntarebhyastaḍitpatākā iva toyadebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing them emerge from the interiors of the groves like lightning-banners from clouds,

children.text: nandasya rāgeṇa tanurvivepe jale cale candramasaḥ prabheva // Saund_10.39 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>'s body trembled with passion, like the reflection of the moon in rippling water. (10.39)

children.text: vapuśca divyaṃ lalitāśca ceṣṭāstataḥ sa tāsāṃ manasā jahāra /
children.translated_text: Their divine forms and graceful movements he then absorbed with his mind,

children.text: kautūhalāvarjitayā ca dṛṣṭyā saṃśleṣatarṣādiva jātarāgaḥ // Saund_10.40 //
children.translated_text: and with a gaze drawn by curiosity, as if passion had arisen from the thirst for their embrace. (10.40)

children.text: sa jātatarṣo 'psarasaḥ pipāsustatprāptaye 'dhiṣṭhitaviklavārtaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, having become thirsty for the <s>Apsarases</s>, desirous of attaining them, established in anxiety and distress,

children.text: lolendriyāśvena manorathena jehrīyamāṇo na dhṛtiṃ cakāra // Saund_10.41 //
children.translated_text: being dragged about by the chariot of desire with its horses of unsteady senses, could find no composure. (10.41)

children.text: yathā manuṣyo malinaṃ hi vāsaḥ kṣāreṇa bhūyo malinīkaroti /
children.translated_text: For just as a person applies alkali to a soiled garment, making it even more stained [at first],

children.text: malakṣayārthaṃ na malodbhavārthaṃ rajastathāsmai munirācakarṣa // Saund_10.42 //
children.translated_text: in order to remove the stain, not to produce it — so the sage applied passion to him. (10.42)

children.text: doṣāṃśca kāyād bhiṣagujjihīrṣurbhūyo yathā kleśayituṃ yateta /
children.translated_text: Just as a physician, wishing to extract the afflictions from the body, would endeavor to cause further discomfort [temporarily],

children.text: rāgaṃ tathā tasya munirjighāṃsurbhūyastaraṃ rāgamupānināya // Saund_10.43 //
children.translated_text: so the sage, wishing to destroy his passion, introduced an even greater passion. (10.43)

children.text: dīpaprabhāṃ hanti yathāndhakāre sahasraraśmeruditasya dīptiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the radiance of the risen sun of a thousand rays extinguishes the light of a lamp in the darkness,

children.text: manuṣyaloke dyutimaṅganānāmantardadhātyapsarasāṃ tathā śrīḥ // Saund_10.44 //
children.translated_text: so the splendor of the <s>Apsarases</s> eclipses the beauty of mortal women in the human world. (10.44)

children.text: mahacca rūpaṃ svaṇu hanti rūpaṃ śabdo mahān hanti ca śabdamalpam /
children.translated_text: A great form destroys a small form; a great sound overwhelms a faint sound;

children.text: gurvī rujā hanti rujāṃ ca mṛdvīṃ sarvo mahān heturaṇorvadhāya // Saund_10.45 //
children.translated_text: a severe pain suppresses a mild one — every great cause brings about the destruction of a small one. (10.45)

children.text: muneḥ prabhāvācca śaśāka nandastaddarśanaṃ soḍhumasahyamanyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And by the power of the sage, <s>Nanda</s> was able to endure that vision, unbearable for others;

children.text: avītarāgasya hi durbalasya mano dahedapsarasāṃ vapuḥśrīḥ // Saund_10.46 //
children.translated_text: for the bodily splendor of the <s>Apsarases</s> would burn the mind of one who has not abandoned passion and is weak. (10.46)

children.text: matvā tato nandamudīrṇarāgaṃ bhāryānurodhādapavṛttarāgam /
children.translated_text: Then, perceiving <s>Nanda</s> to be inflamed with passion — his former attachment to his wife now displaced by [this greater] passion —

children.text: rāgeṇa rāgaṃ pratihantukāmo munirvirāgo giramityuvāca // Saund_10.47 //
children.translated_text: the passionless sage, wishing to destroy passion by means of passion, spoke these words: (10.47)

children.text: etāḥ striyaḥ paśya divaukasastvaṃ nirīkṣya ca brūhi yathārthatattvam /
children.translated_text: "Behold these women of the celestials, and having observed them, speak the truth of the matter:

children.text: etāḥ kathaṃ rūpaguṇairmatāste sa vā jano yatra gataṃ manaste // Saund_10.48 //
children.translated_text: how do these compare in beauty and qualities, in your estimation, to that person toward whom your mind has gone?" (10.48)

children.text: athāpsaraḥsveva niviṣṭadṛṣṭī rāgāgnināntarhṛdaye pradīptaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, with his gaze fixed upon the <s>Apsarases</s> alone, his heart ablaze within with the fire of passion,

children.text: sagadgadaṃ kāmaviṣaktacetāḥ kṛtāñjalirvākyamuvāca nandaḥ // Saund_10.49 //
children.translated_text: spoke with faltering voice, his mind attached to desire, with palms joined: (10.49)

children.text: haryaṅganāsau muṣitaikadṛṣṭiryadantare syāttava nātha vadhvāḥ /
children.translated_text: "That one-eyed she-monkey — were she placed beside your daughter-in-law, my Lord,

children.text: tadantare 'sau kṛpaṇā vadhūste vapuṣmatīrapsarasaḥ pratītya // Saund_10.50 //
children.translated_text: then in comparison [to these <s>Apsarases</s>], your poor daughter-in-law [would be like the monkey] beside these magnificent <s>Apsarases</s>. (10.50)

children.text: āsthā yathā pūrvamabhūnna kācidanyāsu me strīṣu niśāmya bhāryām /
children.translated_text: Just as formerly I had no regard for any other women upon seeing my wife,

children.text: tasyāṃ tataḥsamprati kācidāsthā na me niśāmyaiva hi rūpamāsām // Saund_10.51 //
children.translated_text: so now I have no regard for her upon beholding the beauty of these [celestial women]. (10.51)

children.text: yathā pratapto mṛdunātapena dahyeta kaścin mahatānalena /
children.translated_text: Just as one who was warmed by a gentle heat would be burned by a great fire,

children.text: rāgeṇa pūrvaṃ mṛdunābhitapto rāgāgninānena tathābhidahye // Saund_10.52 //
children.translated_text: so I, formerly scorched by a mild passion, am now being consumed by this fire of passion. (10.52)

children.text: vāgvāriṇāṃ māṃ pariṣiñca tasmādyāvanna dahye sa ivābjaśatruḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore sprinkle me with the water of your words before I am burned up like that enemy of the lotus [the sun burns water];

children.text: rāgāgniradyaiva hiṃ māṃ didhakṣuḥ kakṣaṃ savṛkṣāgramivotthito 'gniḥ // Saund_10.53 //
children.translated_text: for the fire of passion now seeks to consume me, like a fire that has risen [to burn] the dry brush and treetops. (10.53)

children.text: prasīda sīdāmi vimuñca mā mune vasundharādhairya na dhairyamasti me /
children.translated_text: Have mercy — I am sinking! Release me, O sage! The earth's steadfastness is not mine;

children.text: asūn vimokṣyāmi vimuktamānasa prayaccha vā vāgamṛtaṃ mumūrṣave // Saund_10.54 //
children.translated_text: I will give up my life-breath, O liberated one — or else grant the nectar of your words to one who is about to die. (10.54)

children.text: anarthabhogena vighātadṛṣṭinā pramādadaṃṣṭreṇa tamoviṣāgninā /
children.translated_text: For I have been bitten in the heart by the serpent of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) — whose enjoyment brings harm, whose gaze brings destruction,

children.text: ahaṃ hi daṣṭo hṛdi manmathāhinā vidhatsva tasmādagadaṃ mahābhiṣak // Saund_10.55 //
children.translated_text: whose fangs are heedlessness, whose venom and fire are darkness — therefore administer the antidote, O great physician! (10.55)

children.text: anena daṣṭo madanāhināhinā na kaścidātmanyanavasthitaḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: No one bitten by this serpent of desire — the serpent among serpents — has remained composed within himself;

children.text: mumoha bodhyorhyacalātmano mano babhūva dhīmāṃśca sa śantanustanuḥ // Saund_10.56 //
children.translated_text: the mind of <s>Bodhi</s> (the awakened one), firm as a mountain, was bewildered, and <s>Śantanu</s>, the wise one, became emaciated. (10.56)

children.text: sthite viśiṣṭe tvayi saṃśraye śraye yathā na yāmīha vasan diśaṃ diśam /
children.translated_text: Since you, the supreme refuge, stand distinguished, grant that I, dwelling here, not wander from direction to direction;

children.text: yathā ca labdhvā vyasanakṣayaṃ kṣayaṃ vrajāmi tanme kuru śaṃsataḥ sataḥ // Saund_10.57 //
children.translated_text: and that I, having obtained the destruction of calamity, may reach an abode [of peace] — this do for me, who speaks truthfully, the truth." (10.57)

children.text: tato jighāṃsurhṛdi tasya tattamastamonudo naktamivotthitaṃ tamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, wishing to destroy that darkness which had arisen in his heart — like the dispeller of darkness [destroying] the darkness risen in the night —

children.text: maharṣicandro jagatastamonudastamaḥprahīṇo nijagāda gautamaḥ // Saund_10.58 //
children.translated_text: The moon among great sages, the dispeller of the world's darkness — <s>Gautama</s>, whose darkness was dispelled, thus spoke: // Saund 10.58 //

children.text: dhṛtiṃ pariṣvajya vidhūya vikriyāṃ nigṛhya tāvacchrutacetasī śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: "Embracing fortitude, shaking off agitation, restraining your hearing and mind for a moment, listen:

children.text: imā yadi prārthayase tvamaṅganā vidhatsva śuklārthamihottamaṃ tapaḥ // Saund_10.59 //
children.translated_text: If you desire these women, then undertake the supreme <s>tapas</s> (austerity) here for a pure purpose." // Saund 10.59 //

children.text: imā hi śakyā na balānna sevayā na saṃpradānena na rūpavattayā /
children.translated_text: "For these cannot be won by force, nor by service, nor by gifts, nor by beauty of form;

children.text: imā hriyante khalu dharmacaryayā sacet praharṣaścara dharmamādṛtaḥ // Saund_10.60 //
children.translated_text: these are won only by the practice of <s>dharma</s> — so if there is delight, practice <s>dharma</s> with devotion!" // Saund 10.60 //

children.text: ihādhivāso divi daivataiḥ samaṃ vanāni ramyāṇyajarāśca yoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Dwelling here among the gods in heaven, in lovely groves, with women who know no aging —

children.text: idaṃ phalaṃ svasya śubhasya karmaṇo na dattamanyena na cāpyahetutaḥ // Saund_10.61 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of one's own meritorious <s>karma</s> — it is neither given by another, nor [arisen] without cause." // Saund 10.61 //

children.text: kṣitau manuṣyo dhanurādibhiḥ śramaiḥ striyaḥ kadāciddhi labheta vā na vā /
children.translated_text: "On earth, a man through the toils of archery and the like may sometimes win women — or may not;

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ yattviha dharmacaryayā bhaveyuretā divi puṇyakarmaṇaḥ // Saund_10.62 //
children.translated_text: but without doubt, through the practice of <s>dharma</s>, these [celestial women] would be [won] in heaven by one of meritorious deeds." // Saund 10.62 //

children.text: tadapramatto niyame samudyato ramasva yadyapsaraso 'bhilipsase /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, vigilant and striving in your discipline, enjoy — if you desire the <s>Apsarases</s>;

children.text: ahaṃ ca te 'tra pratibhūḥ sthire vrate yathā tvamābhiniyataṃ sameṣyasi // Saund_10.63 //
children.translated_text: and I shall be your guarantor in your steadfast vow, that you will certainly attain them." // Saund 10.63 //

children.text: ataḥparaṃ paramamiti vyavasthitaḥ parāṃ dhṛtiṃ paramamunau cakāra saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having resolved that there is nothing higher than this supreme [attainment], he placed supreme trust in the supreme sage.

children.text: tato muniḥ pavana ivāmbarāt patan pragṛhya taṃ punaragamanmahītalam // Saund_10.64 //
children.translated_text: Then the sage, descending like the wind from the sky, took him and returned again to the earth. // Saund 10.64 //

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "svargadarśana" nāma daśama sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: In the great poem <s>Saundarananda</s>, the tenth canto named 'The Vision of Heaven' (<s>Svargadarśana</s>) is concluded.

children.text:
ekādaśaḥ sargaḥ
svarga kī hīnatā
children.translated_text: Eleventh Canto: The Inferiority of Heaven

children.text: tatastā yoṣito dṛṣṭvā nando nandanacāriṇīḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having seen those women wandering in <s>Nandana</s> (the divine garden), <s>Nanda</s>

children.text: babandha niyamastambhe durdamaṃ capalaṃ manaḥ // Saund_11.1 //
children.translated_text: bound his restless, unruly mind to the pillar of discipline. // Saund 11.1 //

children.text: so 'niṣṭanaiṣkramyaraso mlānatāmarasopamaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, whose relish for going forth was gone, who was like a withered lotus,

children.text: cacāra viraso dharmaṃ niveśyāpsaraso hṛdi // Saund_11.2 //
children.translated_text: practiced <s>dharma</s> without any relish, having placed the <s>Apsarases</s> in his heart. // Saund 11.2 //

children.text: tathā lolendriyo bhūtvā dayitendriyagocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, having been one whose senses were restless, a delight to his beloved's senses,

children.text: indriyārthavaśādeva babhūva niyatendriyaḥ // Saund_11.3 //
children.translated_text: he became one of restrained senses, precisely by the force of [desire for] sense-objects. // Saund 11.3 //

children.text: kāmacaryāsu kuśalo bhikṣucaryāsu viklavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Skilled in the conduct of desires, bewildered in the conduct of a <s>bhikṣu</s>,

children.text: paramācāryaviṣṭabdho brahmacaryeṃ cacāra saḥ // Saund_11.4 //
children.translated_text: upheld by the supreme teacher, he practiced the celibate life (<s>brahmacarya</s>). // Saund 11.4 //

children.text: saṃvṛtena ca śāntena tīvreṇa madanena ca /
children.translated_text: With love that was suppressed yet fierce, both quelled and burning,

children.text: jalāgneriva saṃsargācchaśāma ca śuśoṣa ca // Saund_11.5 //
children.translated_text: like the union of water and fire, he was both extinguished and dried up. // Saund 11.5 //

children.text: svabhāvadarśanīyo 'pi vairūpyamagamat param /
children.translated_text: Though handsome by nature, he attained extreme disfigurement,

children.text: cintayāpsarasāṃ caiva niyamenāyatena ca // Saund_11.6 //
children.translated_text: from brooding over the <s>Apsarases</s> and from the prolonged discipline. // Saund 11.6 //

children.text: prastāveṣvapi bhāryāyāṃ priyabhāryastathāpi saḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when occasions arose [to speak of] his wife, though he loved his wife,

children.text: vītarāga ivātasthau na jaharṣa na cukṣubhe // Saund_11.7 //
children.translated_text: he stood as if free from passion — neither rejoicing nor agitated. // Saund 11.7 //

children.text: taṃ vyavasthitamājñāya bhāryārāgāt parāṅmukham /
children.translated_text: Perceiving him thus resolved, turned away from passion for his wife,

children.text: abhigamyābravīnnandamānandaḥ praṇayādidam // Saund_11.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> approached and affectionately said this to <s>Nanda</s>: // Saund 11.8 //

children.text: aho sadṛśamārabdhaṃ śrutamasyābhijanasya ca /
children.translated_text: "Ah! What has been undertaken is fitting for your learning and your lineage —

children.text: nigṛhītendriyaḥ svastho niyame yadi saṃsthitaḥ // Saund_11.9 //
children.translated_text: if, with senses restrained and self-composed, you are established in discipline! // Saund 11.9 //

children.text: abhiṣvaktasya kāmeṣu rāgiṇo viṣayātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who was addicted to pleasures, passionate, given over to sense-objects,

children.text: yadiyaṃ saṃvidutpannā neyamalpena hetunā // Saund_11.10 //
children.translated_text: if this transformation of understanding has arisen, it was not from a small cause. // Saund 11.10 //

children.text: vyādhiralpena yatnena mṛduḥ pratinivāryate /
children.translated_text: A mild disease is averted with little effort;

children.text: prabalaḥ prabalaireva yatnairnaśyati vā na vā // Saund_11.11 //
children.translated_text: a severe one is destroyed only with great efforts — or perhaps not at all. // Saund 11.11 //

children.text: durharo mānaso vyādhirbalavāṃśca tavābhavat /
children.translated_text: The mental disease was difficult to overcome and was strong in your case;

children.text: vinivṛtto yadi [ca] te sarvathā dhṛtimānasi // Saund_11.12 //
children.translated_text: if it has truly been averted, you are indeed resolute. // Saund 11.12 //

children.text: duṣkaraṃ sādhvanāryeṇa māninā caiva mārdavam /
children.translated_text: Humility is difficult for one who is ignoble; gentleness for the proud;

children.text: atisargaśca lubdhena brahmacaryaṃ ca rāgiṇā // Saund_11.13 //
children.translated_text: generosity for the greedy; and celibacy for one full of passion. // Saund 11.13 //

children.text: ekastu mama saṃdehastavāsyāṃ niyame dhṛtau /
children.translated_text: But I have one doubt regarding this resolve of yours;

children.text: atrānunayamicchāmi vaktavyaṃ yadi manyase // Saund_11.14 //
children.translated_text: I wish for clarification — speak if you think it should be said. // Saund 11.14 //

children.text: ārjavābhihitaṃ vākyaṃ na ca mantavyamanyathā /
children.translated_text: These words are spoken out of sincerity and should not be taken otherwise;

children.text: rūkṣamapyāśaye śuddhe rukṣato naiti sajjanaḥ // Saund_11.15 //
children.translated_text: even what is harsh, when the intention is pure, is not taken as harsh by a good person. // Saund 11.15 //

children.text: apriyaṃ hi hitaṃ snigdhamasnigdhamahitaṃ priyam /
children.translated_text: For what is beneficial though unpleasant is affectionate; what is pleasant but unhelpful is not affectionate;

children.text: durlabhaṃ tu priyahitaṃ svādu pathyamivauṣadham // Saund_11.16 //
children.translated_text: rare indeed is what is both pleasant and beneficial — like medicine that is both sweet and wholesome. // Saund 11.16 //

children.text: viśvāsaścārthacaryā ca sāmānyaṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Trust, beneficial conduct, sharing in happiness and sorrow,

children.text: marṣaṇaṃ praṇayaścaiva mitravṛttiriyaṃ satām // Saund_11.17 //
children.translated_text: patience, and love — this is the behavior of true friends. // Saund 11.17 //

children.text: tadidaṃ tvāṃ vivakṣāmi praṇayānna jighāṃsayā /
