children.translated_text: Therefore, I wish to tell you this out of love, not to harm;

children.text: tvacchreyo hi vivakṣā me yato nārhāmyupekṣitum // Saund_11.18 //
children.translated_text: for my wish is to tell you what is for your good, since I cannot be indifferent. // Saund 11.18 //

children.text: apsarobhṛtako dharmaṃ carasītyabhidhīyase /
children.translated_text: It is said that you practice <s>dharma</s> as one hired by the <s>Apsarases</s> —

children.text: kimidaṃ bhūtamāhosvit parihāso 'yamīdṛśaḥ // Saund_11.19 //
children.translated_text: is this true, or is it some such jest? // Saund 11.19 //

children.text: yadi tāvadidaṃ satyaṃ vakṣyāmyatra yadauṣadham /
children.translated_text: If this is indeed true, I shall prescribe the remedy for it;

children.text: auddhatyamatha vaktṛṇāmabhidhāsyāmi tadrajaḥ // Saund_11.20 //
children.translated_text: but if it is mere gossip of idle talkers, I shall address that impurity." // Saund 11.20 //

children.text: ślakṣṇapūrvamatho tena hṛdi so 'bhihatastadā /
children.translated_text: Struck in the heart by these words, prefaced with gentleness,

children.text: dhyātvā dīrghaṃ niśaśvāsa kiñciccāvāṅmukho 'bhavat // Saund_11.21 //
children.translated_text: he brooded long, sighed deeply, and became somewhat downcast. // Saund 11.21 //

children.text: tatastasyeṅgitaṃ jñātvā manaḥsaṃkalpasūcakam /
children.translated_text: Then, knowing his gesture, which indicated his mind's intention,

children.text: babhāṣe vākyamānando madhurodarkamapriyam // Saund_11.22 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> spoke words that were unpleasant but sweet in their outcome: // Saund 11.22 //

children.text: ākāreṇāvagacchāmi tava dharmaprayojanam /
children.translated_text: "From your expression I understand the motive for your religious practice —

children.text: yajjñātvā tvayi jātaṃ me hāsyaṃ kāruṇyameva ca // Saund_11.23 //
children.translated_text: and having understood it, both laughter and compassion have arisen in me regarding you. // Saund 11.23 //

children.text: yathāsanārthaṃ skandhena kaścid gurvīṃ śilāṃ vahet /
children.translated_text: Just as someone might carry a heavy rock on his shoulder for the sake of a seat,

children.text: tadvattvamapi kāmārthaṃ niyamaṃ voḍhumudyataḥ // Saund_11.24 //
children.translated_text: so too, you are endeavoring to bear discipline for the sake of desire. // Saund 11.24 //

children.text: titāḍayiṣayā dṛpto yathā meṣo 'parsati /
children.translated_text: Just as a proud ram retreats in order to butt,

children.text: tadvadabrahmacaryāya brahmacaryamidaṃ tava // Saund_11.25 //
children.translated_text: so too, this celibacy of yours is for the sake of non-celibacy. // Saund 11.25 //

children.text: cikrīṣanti yathā paṇyaṃ vaṇijo lābhalipsayā /
children.translated_text: Just as merchants wish to sell their wares out of desire for profit,

children.text: dharmacaryā tava tathā paṇyabhūtā na śāntaye // Saund_11.26 //
children.translated_text: so too, your religious practice has become a commodity — not for peace. // Saund 11.26 //

children.text: yathā phalaviśeṣārtha bījaṃ vapati kārṣakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a farmer sows a seed for the sake of a particular fruit,

children.text: tadvad viṣayakārpaṇyād viṣayāṃstyaktavānasi // Saund_11.27 //
children.translated_text: so too, out of wretchedness for sense-objects, you have renounced sense-objects. // Saund 11.27 //

children.text: ākāṅkṣecca yathā rogaṃ pratīkārasukhepsayā /
children.translated_text: Just as one would welcome a disease for the sake of the pleasure of its cure,

children.text: duḥkhamanvicchati bhavāṃstathā viṣayatṛṣṇayā // Saund_11.28 //
children.translated_text: so you seek suffering out of thirst for sense-objects. // Saund 11.28 //

children.text: yathā paśyati madhveva na prapātamavekṣate /
children.translated_text: Just as one sees only the honey and does not look at the precipice,

children.text: paśyasyapsarasastadvad bhraṃśamante na paśyasi // Saund_11.29 //
children.translated_text: you see the <s>Apsarases</s> but do not see the fall at the end. // Saund 11.29 //

children.text: hṛdi kāmāgninā dīpte kāyena vahato vratam /
children.translated_text: When the fire of desire blazes in the heart while the body observes a vow —

children.text: kimidaṃ brahmacaryaṃ te manasābrahmacāriṇaḥ // Saund_11.30 //
children.translated_text: what is this celibacy of yours, who are not celibate in mind? // Saund 11.30 //

children.text: saṃsāre vartamānena yadā cāpsarasastvayā /
children.translated_text: While wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>, you have obtained and lost

children.text: prāptāstyaktāśca śataśastābhyaḥ kimiti te spṛhā // Saund_11.31 //
children.translated_text: <s>Apsarases</s> by the hundreds — why then do you crave them? // Saund 11.31 //

children.text: tṛptirnāstīndhanairagnernāmbhasā lavaṇāmbhasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fire is never sated with fuel; the salt ocean is never sated with water;

children.text: nāpi kāmaiḥ satṛṣṇasya tasmāt kāmā na tṛṣtaye // Saund_11.32 //
children.translated_text: nor is the thirsty one ever sated with desires — therefore, desires do not [lead to] satisfaction. // Saund 11.32 //

children.text: atṛptau sa kutaḥ śāntiraśāntau ca kutaḥ sukham /
children.translated_text: Without satisfaction, where is peace? Without peace, where is happiness?

children.text: asukhe ca kutaḥ prītiraprītau ca kuto ratiḥ // Saund_11.33 //
children.translated_text: Without happiness, where is delight? And without delight, where is pleasure? // Saund 11.33 //

children.text: riraṃsā yadi te tasmādadhyātme dhīyatāṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: If you desire enjoyment, therefore fix your mind on the inner self (<s>adhyātma</s>);

children.text: praśāntā cānavadyā ca nāstyadhyātmasamā ratiḥ // Saund_11.34 //
children.translated_text: for there is no pleasure equal to that of the inner self — tranquil and faultless. // Saund 11.34 //

children.text: na tatra kāryaṃ tūryaiste na strībhirna vibhūṣaṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: There you need no musical instruments, no women, no ornaments;

children.text: ekastvaṃ [yatra]tatrasthastayā ratyābhiraṃsyase // Saund_11.35 //
children.translated_text: alone, abiding there, you will delight in that pleasure. // Saund 11.35 //

children.text: mānasaṃ balavad duḥkhaṃ tarṣe tiṣṭhati tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: Powerful mental suffering persists as long as thirst persists;

children.text: taṃ tarṣaṃ chindhi duḥkhaṃ hi tṛṣṇā cāsti ca nāsti ca // Saund_11.36 //
children.translated_text: cut off that thirst — for craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) both exists and does not exist. // Saund 11.36 //

children.text: saṃpattau vā vipattau vā divā vā naktameva vā /
children.translated_text: Whether in prosperity or adversity, by day or by night,

children.text: kāmeṣu hi satṛṣṇasya na śāntirupapadyate // Saund_11.37 //
children.translated_text: for one who has thirst for pleasures, peace is not possible. // Saund 11.37 //

children.text: kāmānāṃ prārthanā duḥkhā prāptau tṛptirna vidyate /
children.translated_text: The craving for pleasures is painful; in their attainment, no satisfaction is found;

children.text: viyogānniyataḥ śoko viyogaśca dhruvo divi // Saund_11.38 //
children.translated_text: from separation comes inevitable grief — and separation in heaven is certain. // Saund 11.38 //

children.text: kṛtvāpi duṣkaraṃ karma svarge labdhvāpi durlabham /
children.translated_text: Even having performed the most difficult deeds, even having obtained the rare [reward] in heaven,

children.text: nṛlokaṃ punarevaiti pravāsāt svagṛhaṃ yathā // Saund_11.39 //
children.translated_text: one returns again to the world of mortals — like [returning] home from a foreign sojourn. // Saund 11.39 //

children.text: yadā bhraṣṭasya kuśalaṃ śiṣṭaṃ kiṃcinna vidyate /
children.translated_text: When the merit of one who has fallen [from heaven] is exhausted, with nothing left,

children.text: tiryakṣu pitṛloke vā narake copapadyate // Saund_11.40 //
children.translated_text: one is reborn among animals, in the world of the ancestors, or in hell. // Saund 11.40 //

children.text: tasya bhuktavataḥ svarge viṣayānuttamānapi /
children.translated_text: For one who has enjoyed even the supreme sense-pleasures in heaven

children.text: bhraṣṭasyārtasya duḥkhena kimāsvādaḥ karoti saḥ // Saund_11.41 //
children.translated_text: and then fallen, afflicted with suffering — what does that [previous] enjoyment do for him? // Saund 11.41 //

children.text: śyenāya prāṇivātsalyāt svamāṃsānyapi dattavān /
children.translated_text: <s>Śibi</s>, out of tenderness for living beings, gave even his own flesh to the hawk,

children.text: śiviḥ svargāt paribhraṣṭastādṛk kṛtvāpi duṣkaram // Saund_11.42 //
children.translated_text: yet even after performing such a difficult deed, he fell from heaven. // Saund 11.42 //

children.text: śakrasyārdhāsanaṃ gatvā pūrvapārthiva eṃva yaḥ /
children.translated_text: The former king who went to the half-seat of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) —

children.text: sa devatvaṃ gataḥ kāle māndhātādhaḥ punaryayau // Saund_11.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, having attained divine status, in time fell down again. // Saund 11.43 //

children.text: rājyaṃ kṛtvāpi devānāṃ papāta nahuṣo bhuvi /
children.translated_text: <s>Nahuṣa</s>, even after ruling over the gods, fell to the earth;

children.text: prāptaḥ kila bhujaṃgatvaṃ nādyāpi parimucyate // Saund_11.44 //
children.translated_text: having become a serpent, he is said to not be freed even now. // Saund 11.44 //

children.text: tathaivelivilo rājā rājavṛttena saṃskṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, King <s>Elivila</s>, refined with royal merit,

children.text: svargaṃ gatvā punarbhraṣṭaḥ kūrmībhūtaḥ kilārṇave // Saund_11.45 //
children.translated_text: having gone to heaven and fallen again, is said to have become a tortoise in the ocean. // Saund 11.45 //

children.text: bhūridyumno yayātiśca te cānye ca nṛparṣabhāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūridyumna</s>, <s>Yayāti</s>, and those other bulls among kings —

children.text: karmabhirdyāmabhikrīya tatkṣayāt punaratyajan // Saund_11.46 //
children.translated_text: having purchased heaven with their deeds, upon the exhaustion of those [merits], they lost it again. // Saund 11.46 //

children.text: asurāḥ pūrvadevāstu surairapahṛtaśriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Asuras</s>, who were formerly gods, their glory seized by the <s>Suras</s>,

children.text: śriyaṃ samanuśocantaḥ pātālaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ // Saund_11.47 //
children.translated_text: lamenting their lost glory, went to <s>Pātāla</s> (the netherworld) for refuge. // Saund 11.47 //

children.text: kiṃ ca rājarṣibhistāvadasurairvā surādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: But what of the royal sages or the <s>Asuras</s> or the gods and the rest?

children.text: mahendrāḥ śataśaḥ peturmāhātmyamapi na sthiram // Saund_11.48 //
children.translated_text: Hundreds of great <s>Indras</s> have fallen — even greatness is not lasting. // Saund 11.48 //

children.text: saṃsadaṃ śobhāyitvaindrīmupendraścendravikramaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Upendra</s>, of <s>Indra</s>-like valor, having graced <s>Indra</s>'s assembly,

children.text: kṣīṇakarmā papātorvīṃ madhyādapsarasāṃ rasan // Saund_11.49 //
children.translated_text: when his merit was spent, fell to the earth from amidst the <s>Apsarases</s>. // Saund 11.49 //

children.text: hā caitraratha hā vāpi hā mandākini hā priye /
children.translated_text: "Alas, <s>Caitraratha</s>! Alas! Alas, <s>Mandākinī</s>! Alas, beloved!"

children.text: ityārtā vilapanto 'pi gāṃ patanti divaukasaḥ // Saund_11.50 //
children.translated_text: — thus lamenting in anguish, the denizens of heaven fall to the earth. // Saund 11.50 //

children.text: tīvraṃ hyutpadyate duḥkhamiha tāvanmumūrṣatām /
children.translated_text: For intense suffering arises here for those who are about to die;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ patatāṃ svargādevānte sukhasevinām // Saund_11.51 //
children.translated_text: how much more so for those falling from heaven, those who had enjoyed happiness until the end of their time! // Saund 11.51 //

children.text: rajo gṛṇhanti vāsāṃsi mlāyanti paramāḥ srajaḥ /
children.translated_text: Their garments gather dust, their supreme garlands wither,

children.text: gātrebhyo jāyate svedo ratirbhavati nāsane // Saund_11.52 //
children.translated_text: sweat arises from their limbs, and there is no pleasure in sitting. // Saund 11.52 //

children.text: etānyādau nimittāni cyutau svargād divaukasām /
children.translated_text: These are the first signs of the fall of the heavenly beings from heaven —

children.text: aniṣṭānīva martyānāmariṣṭāni mumūrṣatām // Saund_11.53 //
children.translated_text: portents of doom, as unwelcome as the signs of death for mortals. // Saund 11.53 //

children.text: sukhamutpadyate yacca divi kāmānupāśnatām /
children.translated_text: Whatever happiness arises in heaven for those enjoying pleasures,

children.text: yacca duḥkhaṃ nipatatāṃ duḥkhameva viśiṣyate // Saund_11.54 //
children.translated_text: and whatever suffering for those who fall — the suffering is greater. // Saund 11.54 //

children.text: tasmādasvantamatrāṇamaviśvāsyamatarpakam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing heaven to be perishable, without [ultimate] end, without refuge,

children.text: vijñāya kṣayiṇaṃ svargamapavarge matiṃ kuru // Saund_11.55 //
children.translated_text: untrustworthy, and unsatisfying — set your mind on <s>apavarga</s> (final liberation). // Saund 11.55 //

children.text: aśarīraṃ bhavāgraṃ hi gatvāpi munirudrakaḥ /
children.translated_text: For even the sage <s>Udraka</s>, having reached the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) — the formless [realm],

children.text: karmaṇo 'nte cyutastasmāt tiryagyoniṃ prapatsyate // Saund_11.56 //
children.translated_text: at the end of his <s>karma</s>, fell from there and will enter an animal birth. // Saund 11.56 //

children.text: maitrayā saptavārṣikyā brahmalokamito gataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sunetra</s>, having gone from here to the <s>Brahmaloka</s> through seven years of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>),

children.text: sunetraḥ punarāvṛtto garbhavāsamupeyivān // Saund_11.57 //
children.translated_text: returned again and entered the dwelling of the womb. // Saund 11.57 //

children.text: yadā caiśvaryavanto 'pi kṣayiṇaḥ svargavāsinaḥ /
children.translated_text: When even the powerful dwellers in heaven are subject to decay,

children.text: ko nāma svargavāsaya kṣeṣṇave spṛhayed budhaḥ // Saund_11.58 //
children.translated_text: what wise person would desire heaven, which is perishable? // Saund 11.58 //

children.text: sūtreṇa baddho hi yathā vihaṃgo vyāvartate dūragato 'pi bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a bird tied by a string, even though it has flown far, returns again,

children.text: ajñānasūtreṇa tathāvabaddho gato 'pi dūraṃ punareti lokaḥ // Saund_11.59 //
children.translated_text: so too, bound by the string of ignorance, the world, even having gone far, returns again. // Saund 11.59 //

children.text: kṛtvā kālavilakṣaṇaṃ pratibhuvā mukto yathā bandhanād
children.translated_text: Just as one released from prison on bail, having distinguished the time [for release],

children.text: bhuktvā veśmasukhānyatītya samayaṃ bhūyo viśed vandhanaṃ /
children.translated_text: having enjoyed the comforts of home, when the appointed time has passed, must enter prison again —

children.text: tadvad dyāṃ pratibhūvadātmaniyamairdhyānādibhiḥ prāptavān
children.translated_text: so one who has attained heaven through self-restraint and meditations, as if through a guarantor,

children.text: kāle karmasu teṣu bhuktaviṣayeṣvākṛṣate gāṃ punaḥ // Saund_11.60 //
children.translated_text: when in time those deeds have yielded their pleasures, is dragged back to earth again. // Saund 11.60 //

children.text: antarjālagatāḥ pramattamanaso mīnāstaḍāge yathā
children.translated_text: Just as fish within a net in a pond, their minds heedless,

children.text: jānanti vyasanaṃ na rodhajanitaṃ svasthāścarantyambhasi /
children.translated_text: not knowing the danger born of the enclosure, move about at ease in the water —

children.text: antarlokagatāḥ kṛtārthamatayastadvaddivi dhyāyino
children.translated_text: so too, meditators in the world between [births], thinking themselves fulfilled, dwelling in heaven,

children.text: manyante śivamacyutaṃ dhruvamiti svaṃ sthānamāvartakam // Saund_11.61 //
children.translated_text: consider their revolving abode to be auspicious, permanent, and unfailing. // Saund 11.61 //

children.text: tajjanmavyādhimṛtyuvyasanaparigataṃ matvā jagadidaṃ
children.translated_text: Knowing this world to be beset with birth, disease, death, and misfortune —

children.text: saṃsāre bhrāmyamāṇaṃ divi nṛṣu narake tiryakpitṛṣu ca /
children.translated_text: wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> — among gods, humans, in hell, among animals, and among the departed ancestors;

children.text: yattrāṇaṃ nirbhayaṃ yacchivamamarajaraṃ niḥśokamamṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: that which is protection, fearlessness, auspiciousness, freedom from aging and death, sorrowlessness, and immortality —

children.text: taddhetorbrahmacaryaṃ cara jahi hi calaṃ svargaṃ prati rucim // Saund_11.62 //
children.translated_text: for that purpose, practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (the holy life), and abandon your inclination toward the unstable heaven. // Saund_11.62 //

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "svarga kī hīnatā" nāma ekādaśa sarga samāpta //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>Mahākāvya</s>, the eleventh canto, called 'The Inferiority of Heaven,' is complete.

children.text:
dvādaśaḥ sargaḥ
viveka
children.translated_text: Twelfth Canto: Discernment

children.text: apsarobhṛtako dharmaṃ carasītyatha coditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having been told by <s>Ānanda</s>, 'You are practicing <s>dharma</s> as a hired servant of the <s>apsarases</s>,'

children.text: ānandena tadā nandaḥ paraṃ vrīḍamupāgamat // Saund_12.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> was overcome by extreme shame. // Saund_12.1 //

children.text: tasya vrīḍena mahatā pramodo hṛdi nābhavat /
children.translated_text: Due to that great shame, joy did not arise in his heart;

children.text: aprāmodyena vimukhaṃ nāvatasthe vrate manaḥ // Saund_12.2 //
children.translated_text: and due to the absence of joy, his mind turned away and did not remain steadfast in the vow. // Saund_12.2 //

children.text: kāmarāgapradhāno 'pi parihāsasamo 'pi san /
children.translated_text: Though predominantly [subject to] passion for sensual pleasures, and though equal [in bearing] to ridicule,

children.text: paripākagate hetau na sa tanmamṛṣe vacaḥ // Saund_12.3 //
children.translated_text: when the cause had reached maturity, he could not endure those words. // Saund_12.3 //

children.text: aparīkṣakabhāvācca pūrvaṃ matvā divaṃ dhruvam /
children.translated_text: And because he had not investigated before and had considered heaven to be permanent,

children.text: tasmāt kṣeṣṇuṃ pariśrutya bhṛśaṃ saṃvegameyivān // Saund_12.4 //
children.translated_text: having learned that it was perishable, he was overcome by intense spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>). // Saund_12.4 //

children.text: tasya svargānnivavṛte saṃkalpāśvo manorathaḥ /
children.translated_text: His desire, whose steed was imagination, turned back from heaven,

children.text: mahāratha ivonmārgādapramattasya sāratheḥ // Saund_12.5 //
children.translated_text: like a great chariot [turned back] from a wrong path by an attentive charioteer. // Saund_12.5 //

children.text: svargatarṣānnivṛttaśca sadyaḥ svastha ivābhavat /
children.translated_text: Having turned back from the craving for heaven, he immediately became, as it were, healthy,

children.text: mṛṣṭādapathyād virato jijīviṣurivāturaḥ // Saund_12.6 //
children.translated_text: like a sick man who wishes to live and has given up rich but unwholesome food. // Saund_12.6 //

children.text: visasmāra priyāṃ bhāryāmapsarodarśanād yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as he had forgotten his dear wife upon seeing the <s>apsarases</s>,

children.text: tathānityatayodvignastatyājāpsaraso 'pi saḥ // Saund_12.7 //
children.translated_text: so too, being agitated by impermanence, he abandoned even the <s>apsarases</s>. // Saund_12.7 //

children.text: mahatāmapi bhūtānāmāvṛttiriti cintayan /
children.translated_text: Reflecting that even great beings are subject to return [to <s>saṃsāra</s>],

children.text: saṃvegācca sarāgo 'pi vītarāga ivābhavat // Saund_12.8 //
children.translated_text: even though still attached, he became, as it were, free from attachment, due to spiritual urgency. // Saund_12.8 //

children.text: babhūva sa hi saṃvegaḥ śreyasastasya vṛddhaye /
children.translated_text: For that spiritual urgency served the growth of his spiritual welfare,

children.text: dhāturedhirivākhyāte paṭhito 'kṣaracintakaiḥ // Saund_12.9 //
children.translated_text: like the root <s>edh</s> ('to grow'), recited by grammarians, stated in the [grammatical] element [list]. // Saund_12.9 //

children.text: na tu kāmānmanastasya kenacijjagṛhe dhṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: But no firmness held his mind back from sensual desires

children.text: triṣu kāleṣu sarveṣu nipāto 'stiriva smṛtaḥ // Saund_12.10 //
children.translated_text: at any of the three times whatsoever, just as the particle <s>asti</s> ('is') is remembered [as applying] in all [tenses]. // Saund_12.10 //

children.text: khelagāmī mahābāhurgajendra iva nirmadaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moving with a slow gait, mighty-armed, like a great elephant without rut,

children.text: so 'bhyagacchad guruṃ kāle vivakṣurbhāvamātmanaḥ // Saund_12.11 //
children.translated_text: he approached his teacher at the right time, wishing to express his inner state. // Saund_12.11 //

children.text: praṇamya ca gurau murdhnā bāṣpavyākulalocanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Bowing his head before the teacher, his eyes filled with tears,

children.text: kṛtvāñjalimuvācedaṃ hriyā kiṃcidavāṅmukhaḥ // Saund_12.12 //
children.translated_text: with palms joined, he spoke thus, his face slightly downcast with shame: // Saund_12.12 //

children.text: apsaraḥ prāptaye yanme bhagavan pratibhūrasi /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, you who are my surety for attaining the <s>apsarases</s> —

children.text: nāpsarobhirmamārtho 'sti pratibhūtvaṃ tyajāmyaham // Saund_12.13 //
children.translated_text: I have no desire for the <s>apsarases</s>; I release you from your suretyship. // Saund_12.13 //

children.text: śrutvā hyāvartakaṃ svargaṃ saṃsārastha ca citratām /
children.translated_text: For having heard that heaven is subject to return, and [having heard] of the diversity of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: na martyeṣu na deveṣu pravṛttirmama rocate // Saund_12.14 //
children.translated_text: engagement neither among mortals nor among gods appeals to me. // Saund_12.14 //

children.text: yadi prāpya divaṃ yatnānniyamena damena ca /
children.translated_text: If, having reached heaven through effort, restraint, and self-control,

children.text: avitṛptāḥ patantyante svargāya tyāgine namaḥ // Saund_12.15 //
children.translated_text: they fall at the end, unsatiated — homage to the one who renounces for the sake of heaven! // Saund_12.15 //

children.text: ataśca nikhilaṃ lokaṃ viditvā sacarācaram /
children.translated_text: And therefore, knowing the entire world, with all its moving and unmoving [beings],

children.text: sarvaduḥkhakṣayakare tvaddharme parame rame // Saund_12.16 //
children.translated_text: I delight in your supreme <s>Dharma</s>, which removes all suffering. // Saund_12.16 //

children.text: tasmād vyāsasamāsābhyāṃ tanme vyākhyātumarhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, please explain to me, in summary and in detail,

children.text: yacchrutvā śṛṇvatāṃ śreṣṭha paramaṃ prāpnuyāṃ padam // Saund_12.17 //
children.translated_text: that by hearing which, O best of hearers, I may attain the supreme state.' // Saund_12.17 //

children.text: tatastasyāśayaṃ jñātvā vipakṣāṇindriyāṇi ca /
children.translated_text: Then, knowing his disposition and [that] his faculties were opposed [to defilements],

children.text: śreyaścaivāmukhībhūtaṃ nijagāda tathāgataḥ // Saund_12.18 //
children.translated_text: and that [his] spiritual welfare had become manifest, the <s>Tathāgata</s> spoke: // Saund_12.18 //

children.text: aho pratyavamarśo 'yaṃ śreyasaste purojavaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, this reflection of yours runs ahead of your spiritual welfare,

children.text: araṇyāṃ mathyamānāyāmagnerdhūma ivotthitaḥ // Saund_12.19 //
children.translated_text: like smoke rising when the fire-drill is being churned. // Saund_12.19 //

children.text: ciramunmārgavihṛto lolairindriyavājibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Long carried along the wrong path by the fickle horses of the senses,

children.text: avatīrṇo 'si panthānaṃ diṣṭyā dṛṣṭyavimūḍhayā // Saund_12.20 //
children.translated_text: you have fortunately descended onto the [right] road, with your vision undeluded. // Saund_12.20 //

children.text: adya te saphalaṃ janma lābho 'dya sumahāṃstava /
children.translated_text: Today your birth is fruitful; today your gain is supremely great,

children.text: yasya kāmarasajñasya naiṣkramyāyotsukaṃ manaḥ // Saund_12.21 //
children.translated_text: you whose mind, though you know sensual pleasures, is eager for renunciation. // Saund_12.21 //

children.text: loke 'sminnālayārāme nivṛttau durlabhā ratiḥ /
children.translated_text: In this world that delights in attachment, delight in cessation is hard to find;

children.text: vyathante hyapunarbhāvāt prapātādiva bāliśāḥ // Saund_12.22 //
children.translated_text: for the childish are distressed by non-return [to existence], as from a precipice. // Saund_12.22 //

children.text: duḥkhaṃ na syāt sukhaṃ me syāditi prayatate janaḥ /
children.translated_text: People strive [thinking] "May I have no suffering, may I have happiness,"

children.text: atyantaduḥkhoparamaṃ sukhaṃ tacca na budhyate // Saund_12.23 //
children.translated_text: yet they do not understand that happiness which is the complete cessation of suffering. // Saund_12.23 //

children.text: aribhūteṣvanityeṣu satataṃ duḥkhahetuṣu /
children.translated_text: Attached to sensual pleasures and the like, which have become hostile, are impermanent, and are constantly causes of suffering,

children.text: kāmādiṣu jagat saktaṃ na vetti sukhamavyayam // Saund_12.24 //
children.translated_text: the world does not know imperishable happiness. // Saund_12.24 //

children.text: sarvaduḥkhāpahaṃ tattu hastasthamamṛtaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: But that [happiness] which removes all suffering — that nectar is within your reach,

children.text: viṣaṃ pītvā yadagadaṃ samaye pātumicchasi // Saund_12.25 //
children.translated_text: since, having drunk poison, you now wish to drink the remedy at the right time. // Saund_12.25 //

children.text: anarhasaṃsārabhayaṃ mānārhaṃ te cikīrṣitam /
children.translated_text: Worthy of honor is your intention, which fears the unworthy <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: rāgāgnistādṛśo yasya dharmonmukha parāṅmukhaḥ // Saund_12.26 //
children.translated_text: [for you are one] whose fire of passion, so formidable, has turned away, [now] turned toward <s>dharma</s>. // Saund_12.26 //

children.text: rāgoddāmena manasā sarvathā duṣkarā dhṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: With a mind unrestrained by passion, firmness is by all means difficult to attain,

children.text: sadoṣaṃ salilaṃ dṛṣṭvā pathineva pipāsunā // Saund_12.27 //
children.translated_text: like [self-restraint for] a thirsty person on a road who sees water, even if polluted. // Saund_12.27 //

children.text: īdṛśī nāma buddhiste viruddhā rajasābhavat /
children.translated_text: Such was your intellect, which had been obstructed by <s>rajas</s> (passion);

children.text: rajasā caṇḍavātena vivasvata iva prabhā // Saund_12.28 //
children.translated_text: like the radiance of the sun [obscured] by the fierce wind of <s>rajas</s> (dust). // Saund_12.28 //

children.text: sā jighāṃsustamo hārdaṃ yā saṃprati vijṛmbhate /
children.translated_text: That [intellect] which now expands, intent on destroying the darkness of the heart,

children.text: tamo naiśaṃ prabhā saurī vinirgīrṇeva meruṇā // Saund_12.29 //
children.translated_text: [is] like the solar radiance, as if poured forth by <s>Meru</s>, [destroying] the darkness of night. // Saund_12.29 //

children.text: yuktarūpamidaṃ caiva śuddhasattvasya cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this is fitting for a mind whose <s>sattva</s> is pure —

children.text: yatte syānnaiṣṭhike sūkṣme śreyasi śraddadhānatā // Saund_12.30 //
children.translated_text: that you should have faith in the ultimate, subtle spiritual good. // Saund_12.30 //

children.text: dharmacchandamimaṃ tasmādvivardhayitumarhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should cultivate this desire for <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sarvadharmā hi dharmajña niyamācchandahetavaḥ // Saund_12.31 //
children.translated_text: for all <s>dharmas</s>, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, invariably have desire as their cause. // Saund_12.31 //

children.text: satyāṃ gamanabuddhau hi gamanāya pravartate /
children.translated_text: For when there is the intention to go, one proceeds to go;

children.text: śayyābuddhau ca śayanaṃ sthānabuddhau tathā sthitiḥ // Saund_12.32 //
children.translated_text: when there is the intention to lie down, one lies down; and likewise, when there is the intention to stand, one stands. // Saund_12.32 //

children.text: antarbhūmigataṃ hyambhaḥ śraddadhāti naro yadā /
children.translated_text: For when a person has faith that water lies beneath the ground,

children.text: arthiṃtve sati yatnena tadā khanati gāmimām // Saund_12.33 //
children.translated_text: then, when the need exists, he digs this earth with effort. // Saund_12.33 //

children.text: nārthī yadyagninā vā syācchraddadhyāttaṃ na vāraṇau /
children.translated_text: If one were not in need of fire, or had no faith in it within the wood,

children.text: mathnīyānnāraṇiṃ kaścittabhaāve sati mathyate // Saund_12.34 //
children.translated_text: no one would churn the fire-drill; but when that [faith and need] exist, it is churned. // Saund_12.34 //

children.text: sasyotpattiṃ yadi na vā śraddadhyāt kārṣakaḥ kṣitau /
children.translated_text: If a farmer had no faith in the production of crops from the earth,

children.text: arthī sasyena vā na syād bījāni na vaped bhuvi // Saund_12.35 //
children.translated_text: or were not in need of crops, he would not sow seeds in the ground. // Saund_12.35 //

children.text: ataśca hasta ityuktā mayā śraddhā viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: And therefore, faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) has been called by me especially a 'hand,'

children.text: yasmād gṛṇhāti saddharmaṃ dāyaṃ hasta yato yathāḥ // Saund_12.36 //
children.translated_text: because, like an unimpaired hand, it grasps the true <s>dharma</s> as a gift. // Saund_12.36 //

children.text: prādhānyādindriyamiti sthiratvād balamityataḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of its primacy, it is called a 'faculty' (<s>indriya</s>); because of its steadfastness, it is called 'strength' (<s>bala</s>);

children.text: guṇadāridrayaśamanād dhanamityabhivarṇitā // Saund_12.37 //
children.translated_text: and because it removes the poverty of virtues, it has been described as 'wealth' (<s>dhana</s>). // Saund_12.37 //

children.text: rakṣaṇārthena dharmasya tatheṣīketyudāhṛtā /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of protecting <s>dharma</s>, it is likewise called a 'shaft' (<s>iṣīkā</s>);

children.text: loke 'smin durlabhatvācca ratnamityabhibhāṣitā // Saund_12.38 //
children.translated_text: and because of its rarity in this world, it is called a 'jewel' (<s>ratna</s>). // Saund_12.38 //

children.text: punaśca bījamityuktā nimittaṃ śreyaso yadā /
children.translated_text: And again, it is called a 'seed' (<s>bīja</s>), since it is the cause of spiritual welfare;

children.text: pāvanārthena pāpasya nadītyabhihitā punaḥ // Saund_12.39 //
children.translated_text: and again, for the purpose of purifying sin, it is called a 'river' (<s>nadī</s>). // Saund_12.39 //

children.text: yasmāddharmasya cotpattau śraddhā kāraṇamuttamam /
children.translated_text: Since faith is the supreme cause for the arising of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: mayoktā kāryatastasmāttatra tatra tathā tathā // Saund_12.40 //
children.translated_text: it has been spoken of by me accordingly, in various ways, in terms of its effects. // Saund_12.40 //

children.text: śraddhāṅkuramimaṃ tasmāt saṃvardhayitumarhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should nurture this sprout of faith;

children.text: tadvṛddhau vardhate dharmo mūlavṛddhau yathā drumaḥ // Saund_12.41 //
children.translated_text: when it grows, <s>dharma</s> grows, as a tree [grows] when its root grows. // Saund_12.41 //

children.text: vyākulaṃ darśanaṃ yasya durbalo yasya niścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: One whose view is confused and whose resolve is weak —

children.text: tasya pāriplavā śraddhā na hiṃ kṛtyāya vartate // Saund_12.42 //
children.translated_text: his faith is wavering, for it does not operate for what has been accomplished. // Saund_12.42 //

children.text: yāvattattvaṃ na bhavati hi dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vā tāvacchraddhā na bhavati balasthā sthirā vā /
children.translated_text: For as long as the truth has not been seen or heard,

children.text: dṛṣṭe tattve niyamaparibhūtendriyasya śraddhāvṛkṣo bhavati saphalaścāśrayaśca // Saund_12.43 //
children.translated_text: so long faith does not become strong or firm; but when the truth is seen, for one whose senses are conquered by discipline, the tree of faith becomes fruitful and a [firm] support. // Saund_12.43 //

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvya meṃ "viveka" nāmaka dvādaśa sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>Mahākāvya</s>, the twelfth canto, called 'Discernment,' is complete.

children.text:
trayodaśaḥ sargaḥ
śīla evaṃ indriyasaṃyama
children.translated_text: Thirteenth Canto: Moral Conduct and Sense-Restraint

children.text: atha saṃrādhito nandaḥ śraddhāṃ prati maharṣiṇā /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, having been gladdened by the great sage regarding faith,

children.text: pariṣikto 'mṛteneva yuyuje parayā mudā // Saund_13.1 //
children.translated_text: as though sprinkled with nectar, was united with supreme joy. // Saund_13.1 //

children.text: kṛtārthamiva taṃ mene saṃbuddhaḥ śraddhayā tayā /
children.translated_text: The fully awakened one (<s>Saṃbuddha</s>) considered him accomplished through that faith;

children.text: mene prāptamiva śreyaḥ sa ca buddhena saṃskṛtaḥ // Saund_13.2 //
children.translated_text: and he, refined by the <s>Buddha</s>, considered [his] spiritual welfare as attained. // Saund_13.2 //

children.text: ślakṣṇena vacasā kāṃścit kāṃścit paruṣayā girā /
children.translated_text: Some through gentle speech, some through harsh words,

children.text: kāṃścidābhyāmupāyābhyāṃ sa vininye vināyakaḥ // Saund_13.3 //
children.translated_text: and some through both methods — thus did the Guide (<s>Vināyaka</s>) discipline [beings]. // Saund_13.3 //

children.text: pāṃsubhyaḥ kāñcanaṃ jātaṃ viśuddhaṃ nirmalaṃ śuci /
children.translated_text: Just as gold, born from dust, purified, stainless, and clean,

children.text: sthitaṃ pāṃsuṣvapi yathā pāṃsudoṣairna lipyate // Saund_13.4 //
children.translated_text: even while resting in the dust, is not stained by the faults of the dust; // Saund_13.4 //

children.text: padmaparṇaṃ yathā caiva jale jātaṃ jale sthitam /
children.translated_text: and just as a lotus leaf, born in water and resting in water,

children.text: upariṣṭādadhastādvā na jalenopalipyate // Saund_13.5 //
children.translated_text: is not soiled by water, whether from above or below; // Saund_13.5 //

children.text: tadvalloke munirjāto lokasyānugrahaṃ caran /
children.translated_text: so too the sage, born in the world and acting for the benefit of the world,

children.text: kṛtitvānnirmalatvācca lokadharmairna lipyate // Saund_13.6 //
children.translated_text: because of his accomplishment and purity, is not stained by the ways of the world. // Saund_13.6 //

children.text: śleṣaṃ tyāgaṃ priyaṃ rūkṣaṃ kathāṃ ca dhyānameva ca /
children.translated_text: Attachment and renunciation, the pleasant and the harsh, discourse and meditation —

children.text: mantukāle cikitsārthaṃ cakre nātmānuvṛttaye // Saund_13.7 //
children.translated_text: he employed [these] at the time of treatment for the purpose of healing, not for self-indulgence. // Saund_13.7 //

children.text: ataśca sandadhe kāyaṃ mahākaruṇayā tayā /
children.translated_text: And thus, with that great compassion, he prepared [his] body [for teaching],

children.text: mocayeyaṃ kathaṃ duḥkhāt sattvānītyanukampakaḥ // Saund_13.8 //
children.translated_text: compassionate, [thinking] 'How may I liberate beings from suffering?' // Saund_13.8 //

children.text: atha saṃharṣaṇānnandaṃ viditvā bhājanīkṛtam /
children.translated_text: Then, knowing that <s>Nanda</s> had been made a worthy vessel through encouragement,

children.text: abravīd bruvatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ kramajñaḥ śreyasāṃ kramam // Saund_13.9 //
children.translated_text: the best of speakers, who knew the [proper] sequence, spoke the sequence of spiritual goods: // Saund_13.9 //

children.text: ataḥ prabhṛti bhūyastvaṃ średdhendriyapuraḥsaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'From now on, you, O gentle one, with the faculty of faith as your forerunner,

children.text: amṛtasyāptaye saumya vṛttaṃ rakṣitumarhasi // Saund_13.10 //
children.translated_text: should protect your conduct for the attainment of the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>). // Saund_13.10 //

children.text: prayogaḥ kāyavacasoḥ śuddho bhavati te yathā /
children.translated_text: So that the practice of your body and speech becomes pure,

children.text: uttāno vivṛto gupto 'navacchidrastathā kuru // Saund_13.11 //
children.translated_text: make it open, transparent, guarded, and without gaps. // Saund_13.11 //

children.text: uttāno bhāvakaraṇād vivṛtaścāpyagūhanāt /
children.translated_text: Open through sincerity of disposition, transparent through non-concealment,

children.text: gupto rakṣaṇatātparyādacchidraścānavadyataḥ // Saund_13.12 //
children.translated_text: guarded through devotion to protection, and without gaps through blamelessness. // Saund_13.12 //

children.text: śarīravacasoḥ śuddhau saptāṃge cāpi karmaṇi /
children.translated_text: In the purity of body and speech, and in the sevenfold action,

children.text: ājīvasamudācāraṃ śaucāt saṃskartumarhasi // Saund_13.13 //
children.translated_text: you should purify your livelihood and conduct through [ethical] purity. // Saund_13.13 //

children.text: doṣāṇāṃ kuhanādīnāṃ pañcānāmaniṣevaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Through not engaging in the five faults such as deception and the like,

children.text: tyāgācca jyotiṣādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ vṛttighātinām // Saund_13.14 //
children.translated_text: and through the abandonment of the four destroyers of livelihood such as fortune-telling and the like, // Saund_13.14 //

children.text: prāṇidhānyadhanādīnāṃ varjyānāmapratigrahāt /
children.translated_text: through not accepting what is to be avoided — living beings, grain, wealth, and the like —

children.text: bhaikṣāṅgānāṃ nisṛṣṭānāṃ niyatānāṃ pratigrahāt // Saund_13.15 //
children.translated_text: and through accepting what is permitted, fixed, and [pertaining to] the requisites of the alms-life, // Saund_13.15 //

children.text: parituṣṭaḥ śucirmañjuścaukṣayā jīvasaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: being content, pure, and agreeable, with a fine and proper livelihood,

children.text: kuryā duḥkhapratīkāraṃ yāvadeva vimuktaye // Saund_13.16 //
children.translated_text: one should practice the remedy for suffering, even unto liberation. // Saund_13.16 //

children.text: karmaṇo hi yathādṛṣṭāt kāyavākprabhavādapi /
children.translated_text: For although livelihood springs from the visible actions of body and speech,

children.text: ājīvaḥ pṛthagevokto duḥśodhatvādayaṃ mayā // Saund_13.17 //
children.translated_text: it has been stated separately by me because it is difficult to purify. // Saund_13.17 //

children.text: gṛhasthena hi duḥśodhā dṛṣṭirvividhadṛṣṭinā /
children.translated_text: For right view is difficult to purify for a householder who holds various views,

children.text: ājīvo bhikṣuṇā caiva pareṣvāyattavṛttinā // Saund_13.18 //
children.translated_text: and livelihood is [difficult to purify] for a mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>) whose sustenance depends on others. // Saund_13.18 //

children.text: etāvacchīlamityuktamācāro 'yaṃ samāsataḥ /
children.translated_text: This much has been called moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>); this is the code of behavior, in brief;

children.text: asya nāśena naiva syāt pravrajyā na gṛhasthatā // Saund_13.19 //
children.translated_text: without it, there could be neither the renunciant life nor the householder life. // Saund_13.19 //

children.text: tasmāccāritrasampanno brahmacaryamidaṃ cara /
children.translated_text: Therefore, endowed with good conduct, practice this holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>),

children.text: aṇumātreṣvadyeṣu bhayadarśī dṛḍhavrataḥ // Saund_13.20 //
children.translated_text: seeing danger even in the slightest faults, firm in your vows. // Saund_13.20 //

children.text: śīlamāsthāya vartante sarvā hi śreyasi kriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Based on moral conduct, all actions for spiritual welfare proceed,

children.text: sthānādyānīva kāryāṇi pratiṣṭhāya vasundharām // Saund_13.21 //
children.translated_text: just as all activities — standing, going, and the like — rest upon the earth. // Saund_13.21 //

children.text: mokṣasyopaniṣat saumya vairāgyamiti gṛhyatām /
children.translated_text: Understand, O gentle one, that the prerequisite of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>);

children.text: vairāgyasyāpi saṃvedaḥ saṃvido jñānadarśanam // Saund_13.22 //
children.translated_text: and the prerequisite of dispassion is discernment (<s>saṃveda</s>), and of discernment, the vision of knowledge. // Saund_13.22 //

children.text: jñānasyopaniṣaccaiva samādhirupadhāryatām /
children.translated_text: And understand that the prerequisite of knowledge is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration);

children.text: samādherapyupaniṣat sukhaṃ śārīramānasam // Saund_13.23 //
children.translated_text: and the prerequisite of <s>samādhi</s> is bodily and mental happiness. // Saund_13.23 //

children.text: praśrabdhiḥ kāyamanasaḥ sukhasyopaniṣat parā /
children.translated_text: Tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>) of body and mind is the supreme prerequisite of happiness;

children.text: praśrabdherapyupaniṣat prītirapyavagamyatām // Saund_13.24 //
children.translated_text: and understand that the prerequisite of tranquility is joy (<s>prīti</s>). // Saund_13.24 //

children.text: tathā prīterupaniṣat prāmodyaṃ paramaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the prerequisite of joy is considered to be supreme gladness (<s>prāmodya</s>);

children.text: prāmodyasyāpyahṛllekhaḥ kukṛteṣvakṛteṣu vā // Saund_13.25 //
children.translated_text: and the prerequisite of gladness is the absence of remorse regarding misdeeds or undone deeds. // Saund_13.25 //

children.text: ahṛllekhasya manasaḥ śīlaṃ tūpaniṣacchuci /
children.translated_text: And the prerequisite of a mind free from remorse is pure moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>);

children.text: ataḥ śīlaṃ nayatyagryamiti śīlaṃ viśodhaya // Saund_13.26 //
children.translated_text: therefore, since moral conduct leads to the highest, purify your moral conduct. // Saund_13.26 //

children.text: śīlanācchīlamityuktaṃ śīlanaṃ sevanādapi /
children.translated_text: <s>Śīla</s> (moral conduct) is so called from <s>śīlana</s> (habitual practice), and <s>śīlana</s> from <s>sevana</s> (cultivation);

children.text: sevanaṃ tannideśācca nideśaśca tadāśrayāt // Saund_13.27 //
children.translated_text: <s>sevana</s> from <s>nideśa</s> (instruction), and <s>nideśa</s> from reliance on that [instruction]. // Saund_13.27 //

children.text: śīlaṃ hi śaraṇaṃ saubhya kāntāra iva daiśikaḥ /
children.translated_text: For <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) is a refuge, O gentle one, like a guide in a wilderness,

children.text: pitraṃ bandhuśca rakṣā ca dhanaṃ ca balameva ca // Saund_13.28 //
children.translated_text: A father, a kinsman, a guardian, wealth, and strength indeed. // 13.28 //

children.text: yataḥ śīlamataḥ saumya śīlaṃ saṃskartumarhasi /
children.translated_text: Since <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) [is the foundation], O gentle one, you should cultivate <s>śīla</s>;

children.text: etatsthānamathānye [nanyaṃ] ca mokṣārambheṣu yoginām // Saund_13.29 //
children.translated_text: This is the ground, and the other, for practitioners (<s>yogins</s>) in their endeavors toward liberation. // 13.29 //

children.text: tataḥ smṛtimadhiṣṭhāya capalāni svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, establishing <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), the senses which are fickle by nature —

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyo nivārayitumarhasi // Saund_13.30 //
children.translated_text: You should restrain from their objects. // 13.30 //

children.text: bhetavyaṃ na tathā śatrornāgnernāherna cāśaneḥ /
children.translated_text: One should not fear an enemy, nor fire, nor a serpent, nor lightning,

children.text: indriyebhyo yathā svebhyastairajasraṃ hi hanyate // Saund_13.31 //
children.translated_text: As much as one's own senses — for by them one is constantly destroyed. // 13.31 //

children.text: dviṣadbhiḥ śatrubhiḥ kaścit kadācit pīḍyate na vā /
children.translated_text: Someone may sometimes be harassed by hostile enemies, or may not be;

children.text: indriyairbādhyate sarvaḥ sarvatra ca sadaiva ca // Saund_13.32 //
children.translated_text: But everyone is afflicted by the senses, everywhere and at all times. // 13.32 //

children.text: na ca prayāti narakaṃ śatruprabhṛtibhirhataḥ /
children.translated_text: One slain by enemies and the like does not go to hell;

children.text: kṛṣyate tatra nighnastu capalairindriyairhataḥ // Saund_13.33 //
children.translated_text: But one slain by the fickle senses is inevitably dragged there. // 13.33 //

children.text: hanyamānasya tairduḥkhaṃ hārdaṃ bhavati vā na vā /
children.translated_text: When one is slain by them [enemies], the suffering may or may not be heartfelt;

children.text: indriyairbādhyamānasya hārdaṃ śārīrameva ca // Saund_13.34 //
children.translated_text: But when one is afflicted by the senses, there is both heartfelt and bodily [suffering]. // 13.34 //

children.text: saṃkalpaviṣadigdhā hi pañcendriyamayāḥ śarāḥ /
children.translated_text: For the arrows consisting of the five senses, smeared with the poison of mental fabrication,

children.text: cintāpuṅkhā ratiphalā viṣayākāśagocarāḥ // Saund_13.35 //
children.translated_text: Fletched with anxious thought, bearing the fruit of pleasure, flying through the expanse of sense-objects —

children.text: manuṣyahariṇān ghnanti kāmavyādheritā hṛdi /
children.translated_text: They slay the human-deer in the heart, shot by the hunter of desire;

children.text: vihanyante yadi na te tataḥ patanti taiḥ kṣatāḥ // Saund_13.36 //
children.translated_text: If they are not warded off, those struck by them fall. // 13.36 //

children.text: niyamājirasaṃsthena dhairyakārmukadhāriṇā /
children.translated_text: Standing in the courtyard of restraint, bearing the bow of firmness,

children.text: nipatanto nivāryāste mahatā smṛtivarmaṇā // Saund_13.37 //
children.translated_text: Those [arrows] as they fall should be warded off with the great armor of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness). // 13.37 //

children.text: indriyāṇāmupaśamādarīṇāṃ nigrahādiva /
children.translated_text: Through the pacification of the senses, as through the restraint of snakes,

children.text: sukhaṃ svapiti vāste vā yatra tatra gatoddhavaḥ // Saund_13.38 //
children.translated_text: One sleeps or dwells in happiness, wherever one goes, free from anxiety. // 13.38 //

children.text: teṣāṃ hi satataṃ loke viṣayānabhikāṅkṣatām /
children.translated_text: For those in the world who constantly crave sense-objects,

children.text: saṃvinnaivāsti kārpaṇyācchunāmāśāvatāmiva // Saund_13.39 //
children.translated_text: There is no contentment out of their wretchedness — like dogs that are ever expectant. // 13.39 //

children.text: viṣayairindriyagrāmo na tṛptimadhigacchati /
children.translated_text: The aggregate of the senses does not attain satisfaction from sense-objects,

children.text: ajasraṃ pūryamāṇo 'pi samudraḥ salilairiva // Saund_13.40 //
children.translated_text: Though being filled constantly — like the ocean by streams of water. // 13.40 //

children.text: avaśyaṃ gocare sve sve vartitavyamihendriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The senses must inevitably operate in their respective domains here;

children.text: nimittaṃ tatra na grāhyamanuvyañjanameva ca // Saund_13.41 //
children.translated_text: But neither the general sign nor the subsidiary characteristics should be grasped therein. // 13.41 //

children.text: ālokya cakṣuṣā rūpaṃ dhātumātre vyavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen a form with the eye, remaining established merely in the element,

children.text: strī veti puruṣo veti na kalpayitumarhasi // Saund_13.42 //
children.translated_text: You should not conceptualize 'this is a woman' or 'this is a man.' // 13.42 //

children.text: sacet strīpuruṣagrāhaḥ kvacid vidyeta kaścan /
children.translated_text: If some apprehension of 'woman' or 'man' should arise anywhere,

children.text: śubhataḥ keśadantādīnnānuprasthātumarhasi // Saund_13.43 //
children.translated_text: You should not dwell upon hair, teeth, and the like as beautiful. // 13.43 //

children.text: nāpaneyaṃ tataḥ kiṃcit prakṣepyaṃ nāpi kiñcana /
children.translated_text: Nothing is to be taken away from it, nor is anything to be added;

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ bhūtato bhūtaṃ yādṛśaṃ ca yathā ca yat // Saund_13.44 //
children.translated_text: What is real should be seen as it truly is — whatever it is and however it is. // 13.44 //

children.text: evaṃ te paśyatastattvaṃ śaśvadindriyagocaram /
children.translated_text: For one who thus constantly sees the reality of what falls within the range of the senses,

children.text: bhaviṣyati padasthānaṃ nābhidhyādaurmanasyayoḥ // Saund_13.45 //
children.translated_text: There will be no foothold for covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) or dejection (<s>daurmanasya</s>). // 13.45 //

children.text: abhidhyā priyarūpeṇa hanti kāmātmakaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: <s>Abhidhyā</s> (covetousness) destroys the world that is given to desire, under the guise of what is pleasing,

children.text: arirmitramukheneva priyavākkaluṣāśayaḥ // Saund_13.46 //
children.translated_text: Like an enemy wearing the face of a friend — with sweet words but a treacherous heart. // 13.46 //

children.text: daurmanasyābhidhānastu pratigho viṣayāśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: And aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), called dejection, is dependent on sense-objects;

children.text: mohādyenānuvṛtena paratreha ca hanyate // Saund_13.47 //
children.translated_text: Through delusion, following after it, one is destroyed both here and hereafter. // 13.47 //

children.text: anurodhavirodhābhyāṃ śitoṣṇābhyāmivārditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Tormented by attraction and aversion, as by cold and heat,

children.text: śarma nāpnoti na śreyaścalendriyamato jagat // Saund_13.48 //
children.translated_text: The world with its fickle senses attains neither comfort nor the highest good. // 13.48 //

children.text: nendriyaṃ viṣaye tāvat pravṛttamapi sajjate /
children.translated_text: A sense organ, even when it has turned toward a sense-object, does not become attached to it,

children.text: yāvanna manasastatra parikalpaḥ pravartate // Saund_13.49 //
children.translated_text: So long as the mind's conceptual fabrication does not arise there. // 13.49 //

children.text: indhane sati vāyau ca yathā jvalati pāvakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as fire blazes when there is fuel and wind,

children.text: viṣayāt parikalpācca kleśāgnirjāyate tathā // Saund_13.50 //
children.translated_text: So from the sense-object and conceptual fabrication, the fire of <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) is born. // 13.50 //

children.text: abhūtaparikalpena viṣayasya hi vadhyate /
children.translated_text: For through false conceptualization of the sense-object, one is bound;

children.text: tameva viṣayaṃ paśyan bhūtataḥ parimucyate // Saund_13.51 //
children.translated_text: Seeing that very sense-object as it truly is, one is liberated. // 13.51 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvaikaṃ rūpamanyo hi rajyate 'nyaḥ praduṣyati /
children.translated_text: Having seen one and the same form, one person is attracted, another is repelled,

children.text: kaścid bhavati madhyasthastatraivānyo ghṛṇāyate // Saund_13.52 //
children.translated_text: Someone remains indifferent, and yet another is disgusted — in that very [instance]. // 13.52 //

children.text: ato na viṣayo heturbandhāya na vimuktaye /
children.translated_text: Therefore the sense-object is not the cause — neither for bondage nor for liberation;

children.text: parikalpaviśeṣeṇa saṃgo bhavati vā na vā // Saund_13.53 //
children.translated_text: It is through the particular conceptualization that attachment arises or does not. // 13.53 //

children.text: kāryaḥ paramayatnena tasmādindriyasaṃvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore the utmost effort should be made in the restraint of the senses;

children.text: indriyāṇi hyagutpāni duḥkhāya ca bhavāya ca // Saund_13.54 //
children.translated_text: For the senses, when unguarded, lead to suffering and to [continued] existence. // 13.54 //

children.text: kāmabhogabhogavadbhirātmadṛṣṭidṛṣṭibhiḥ pramādanaikamūrddhabhiḥ praharṣalolajivhakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With fangs of enjoyment of desire, with the sight of self-view, with heads raised in heedlessness, with tongues flickering with excitement,

children.text: indriyoragairmanobilaśrayaiḥ spṛhāviṣaiḥ śamāgadādṛte na dṛṣṭamasti yaccikitset // Saund_13.55 //
children.translated_text: The serpents of the senses, dwelling in the cave of the mind, with the venom of craving — no cure has been found other than the antidote of tranquility (<s>śama</s>). // 13.55 //

children.text: tasmādeṣāmakuśalakarāṇāmarīṇāṃ cakṣurghrāṇaśravaṇarasanasparśanānām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, of these producers of evil — the enemies that are eye, nose, ear, tongue, and touch —

children.text: sarvāvasthaṃ bhava viniyamādapramatto māsminnarthe kṣaṇamapi kṛthāstvaṃ pramādam // Saund_13.56 //
children.translated_text: Be vigilant in restraining them in all states; do not be heedless in this matter even for a moment. // 13.56 //

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "śīla evaṃ indriyasaṃyama" nāma trayodaśa sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda Mahākāvya</s>, the Thirteenth Canto, named '<s>Śīla</s> (Moral Conduct) and Sense-Restraint,' is completed.

children.text:
caturdaśaḥ sargaḥ
ādiprasthāna
children.translated_text:
Fourteenth Canto:
The Initial Setting Forth.

children.text: atha smṛtikavāṭena pidhāyendriyasaṃvaram /
children.translated_text: Now, having covered sense-restraint with the door-bolt of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness),

children.text: bhojane bhava mātrājño dhyānāyānāmayāya ca // Saund_14.1 //
children.translated_text: Be moderate in food, for the sake of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and for good health. // 14.1 //

children.text: prāṇāpānau nigṛṇhāti glāninidre prayacchati /
children.translated_text: Excessive food suppresses the <s>prāṇa</s> (inhalation) and <s>apāna</s> (exhalation) and produces sluggishness and drowsiness;

children.text: kṛto hyatyarthamāhāro vihanti ca parākramam // Saund_14.2 //
children.translated_text: For food taken in excess also destroys one's capacity for exertion. // 14.2 //

children.text: yathā cātyarthamāhāraḥ kṛto 'narthāya kalpate /
children.translated_text: And just as excessive food leads to harm,

children.text: upayuktastathātyalpo na sāmarthyāya kalpate // Saund_14.3 //
children.translated_text: So too, food consumed in too small a quantity does not conduce to strength. // 14.3 //

children.text: ācayaṃ dyutimutsāhaṃ prayogaṃ balameva ca /
children.translated_text: Nourishment, radiance, enthusiasm, capacity, and strength itself —

children.text: bhojanaṃ kṛtamatyalpaṃ śarīrasyāpakarṣati // Saund_14.4 //
children.translated_text: Food eaten in too small a quantity diminishes from the body. // 14.4 //

children.text: yathā bhāreṇa namate laghunonnamate tulā /
children.translated_text: Just as a balance tips down under a heavy weight and rises with a light one,

children.text: samā tiṣṭhati yuktena bhojyeneyaṃ tathā tanuḥ // Saund_14.5 //
children.translated_text: So this body remains balanced with properly measured food. // 14.5 //

children.text: tasmādabhyavaharttavyaṃ svaśaktimanupaśyatā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should eat, observing one's own capacity,

children.text: nātimātraṃ na cātyalpaṃ meyaṃ mānavaśādapi // Saund_14.6 //
children.translated_text: Neither too much nor too little — measuring even by the measure [of one's own need]. // 14.6 //

children.text: atyākrānto hi kāyāgnirguruṇānnena śāmyati /
children.translated_text: For the digestive fire of the body, overwhelmed by heavy food, is extinguished,

children.text: avacchanna ivālpo 'gniḥ sahasā mahatendhasā // Saund_14.7 //
children.translated_text: Like a small fire suddenly smothered by a great quantity of fuel. // 14.7 //

children.text: atyantamapi saṃhāro nāhārasya praśasyate /
children.translated_text: Complete abstinence from food is also not praised;

children.text: anāhāro hi nirvāti nirindhana ivānalaḥ // Saund_14.8 //
children.translated_text: For without food one is extinguished, like a fire without fuel. // 14.8 //

children.text: yasmānnāsti vināhārāt sarvaprāṇābhṛtāṃ sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Since there is no survival of any living being without food,

children.text: tasmād duṣyati nāhāro vikalpo 'tra tu vāryate // Saund_14.9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore food itself is not faulty — but the wrong attitude toward it is to be avoided. // 14.9 //

children.text: na hyekaviṣaye 'nyatra sajyante prāṇinastathā /
children.translated_text: For beings do not become attached to any other single object

children.text: avijñāte yathāhāre boddhavyaṃ tatra kāraṇam // Saund_14.10 //
children.translated_text: As much as to food when it is not understood — the cause [of attachment] should be recognized therein. // 14.10 //

children.text: cikitsārthaṃ yathā dhatte vraṇasyālepanaṃ vraṇī /
children.translated_text: Just as one with a wound applies a poultice for the purpose of healing,

children.text: kṣudvighātārthamāhārastadvat sevyo mumukṣuṇā // Saund_14.11 //
children.translated_text: So food should be consumed by one who seeks liberation, solely for the purpose of dispelling hunger. // 14.11 //

children.text: bhārasyodvahanārthaṃ ca rathākṣo 'bhyajyate yathā /
children.translated_text: And just as an axle of a chariot is greased for the purpose of carrying a load,

children.text: bhojanaṃ prāṇayātrārthaṃ tadvad vidvānniṣevate // Saund_14.12 //
children.translated_text: So the wise one partakes of food for the purpose of sustaining life. // 14.12 //

children.text: samatikramaṇārthaṃ ca kāntārasya yathādhvagau /
children.translated_text: And just as two travelers, in order to cross a wilderness,

children.text: putramāṃsāni khādetāṃ dampatī bhṛśaduḥkhitau // Saund_14.13 //
children.translated_text: Would eat the flesh of their own child — a husband and wife in extreme distress — // 14.13 //

children.text: evamabhyavaharttavyaṃ bhojanaṃ pratisaṃkhyayā /
children.translated_text: So food should be consumed with reflection,

children.text: na bhūṣārthaṃ na vapuṣo na madāya na dṛptaye // Saund_14.14 //
children.translated_text: Not for adornment, not for the beauty of the body, not for intoxication, not for pride. // 14.14 //

children.text: dhāraṇārthaṃ śarīrasya bhojanaṃ hi vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: For food is prescribed for the maintenance of the body,

children.text: upastambhaḥ pipatiṣordubalasyeva veśmanaḥ // Saund_14.15 //
children.translated_text: Like a prop for a weak house that is about to collapse. // 14.15 //

children.text: plavaṃ yatnād yathā kaścid badhnīyād dhārayedapi /
children.translated_text: Just as someone would carefully build and maintain a raft,

children.text: na tatsnehena yāvattu mahaughasyottitīrṣayā // Saund_14.16 //
children.translated_text: Not out of love for it, but for the purpose of crossing a great flood — // 14.16 //

children.text: tathopakaraṇaiḥ kāyaṃ dhārayanti parīkṣakāḥ /
children.translated_text: So the discerning maintain the body with its requisites,

children.text: na tatsnehena yāvattu duḥkhaughasya titīrṣayā // Saund_14.17 //
children.translated_text: Not out of love for it, but for the purpose of crossing the flood of suffering. // 14.17 //

children.text: śocatā pīḍyamānena dīyate śatrave yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as one who is grieving and afflicted gives [tribute] to an enemy,

children.text: na bhaktyā nāpi tarṣeṇa kevalaṃ prāṇaguptaye // Saund_14.18 //
children.translated_text: Not out of devotion or desire, but solely for the protection of life — // 14.18 //

children.text: yogācārastathāhāraṃ śarīrāya prayacchati /
children.translated_text: So the practitioner of <s>yoga</s> gives food to the body,

children.text: kevalaṃ kṣudvighātārthaṃ na rāgeṇa na bhaktaye // Saund_14.19 //
children.translated_text: Solely for the purpose of dispelling hunger — not from passion, not from devotion. // 14.19 //

children.text: manodhāraṇayā caiva pariṇāmyātmavānahaḥ /
children.translated_text: And through the concentration of the mind, the self-controlled one should pass the day with mental focus;

children.text: vidhūya nidrāṃ yogena niśāmapyatināmayet // Saund_14.20 //
children.translated_text: Shaking off drowsiness through <s>yoga</s>, he should also pass the night. // 14.20 //

children.text: hṛdi yatsaṃjñinaścaiva nidrā prādurbhavettava /
children.translated_text: And if, O conscious one, sleep should arise in your heart,

children.text: guṇavatsaṃjñitāṃ saṃjñāṃ tadā manasi mā kṛthāḥ // Saund_14.21 //
children.translated_text: Then you should not hold in your mind a perception qualified by wholesome content. // 14.21 //

children.text: dhāturārambhadhṛtyośca sthāmavikramayorapi /
children.translated_text: Of the constitution [of the body], of initial resolve and firmness,

children.text: nityaṃ manasi kāryaste bādhyamānena nidrayā // Saund_14.22 //
children.translated_text: Of power and vigor — you should always keep these in mind when oppressed by sleep. // 14.22 //

children.text: āmnātavyāśca viśadaṃ te dharmā ye pariśrutāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those teachings that have been heard should be clearly recited,

children.text: parebhyaścopadeṣṭavyāḥ saṃcintyāḥ svayameva ca // Saund_14.23 //
children.translated_text: They should be taught to others, and contemplated by oneself as well. // 14.23 //

children.text: prakledyamadbhirvadanaṃ vilokyāḥ sarvato diśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sprinkling the face with water, looking in all directions,

children.text: cāryā dṛṣṭiśca tārāsu jijāgariṣuṇā sadā // Saund_14.24 //
children.translated_text: And directing the gaze toward the stars — [this should be done] by one who constantly wishes to stay awake. // 14.24 //

children.text: antargatairacapalairvaśasthāyibhirindriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With the senses withdrawn, calm, and under control,

children.text: avikṣiptena manasā caṃkramyasvāsva vā niśi // Saund_14.25 //
children.translated_text: With undistracted mind, walk about or sit at night. // 14.25 //

children.text: bhaye prītau ca śoke ca nidrayā nābhibhūyate /
children.translated_text: Through fear, through joy, and through sorrow, one is not overcome by sleep;

children.text: tasmānnidrābhiyogeṣu sevitavyamidaṃ trayam // Saund_14.26 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in [periods of] inclination toward sleep, these three should be cultivated. // 14.26 //

children.text: bhayamāgamanānmṛtyoḥ prītiṃ dharmaparigrahāt /
children.translated_text: Fear from the approach of death, joy from the acquisition of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: janmaduḥkhādaparyantācchokamāgantumarhasi // Saund_14.27 //
children.translated_text: And sorrow from the endless suffering of birth — you should let these come [to mind]. // 14.27 //

children.text: evamādiḥ kramaḥ saumya kāryo jāgaraṇaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: This and such is the procedure, O gentle one, to be followed regarding wakefulness;

children.text: vandhyaṃ hi śayanādāyuḥ ka prājñaḥ kartumarhasi // Saund_14.28 //
children.translated_text: For what wise person would make life barren through excessive sleep? // 14.28 //

children.text: doṣavyālānatikramya vyālān gṛhagatāniva /
children.translated_text: Without having crossed beyond the serpents of faults, like serpents dwelling within a house,

children.text: kṣamaṃ prājñasya na svaptuṃ nistitīrṣormahad bhayam // Saund_14.29 //
children.translated_text: It is not fitting for a wise person to sleep — one who wishes to cross beyond the great danger. // 14.29 //

children.text: pradīpte jīvaloke hi mṛtyuvyādhijarāgnibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: For when the living world is ablaze with the fires of death, disease, and old age,

children.text: kaḥ śayīta nirudvegaḥ pradīpta iva veśmani // Saund_14.30 //
children.translated_text: Who would lie down without alarm, as if in a burning house? // 14.30 //

children.text: tasmāttama iti jñātvā nidrāṃ nāveṣṭumarhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing sleep to be darkness (<s>tamas</s>), you should not indulge in it,

children.text: apraśānteṣu doṣeṣu saśastreṣviva śatruṣu // Saund_14.31 //
children.translated_text: While the faults remain unextinguished — like enemies with weapons in hand. // 14.31 //

children.text: pūrvaṃ yāmaṃ triyāmāyāḥ prayogeṇātināmya tu /
children.translated_text: Having passed the first watch of the three-watch night in practice,

children.text: sevyā śayyā śarīrasya viśrāmārthaṃ svatantriṇā // Saund_14.32 //
children.translated_text: The bed should be resorted to by a self-disciplined person for the purpose of resting the body. // 14.32 //

children.text: dakṣiṇena tu pārśvena sthitayālokasaṃjñayā /
children.translated_text: Lying on the right side, with the perception of light established,

children.text: prabodhaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā śayīthāḥ śāntamānasaḥ // Saund_14.33 //
children.translated_text: Having placed the intention of awakening in the heart, you should sleep with tranquil mind. // 14.33 //

children.text: yāme tṛtīye cotthāya carannāsīna eva vā /
children.translated_text: And in the third watch, having risen, whether walking or seated,

children.text: bhūyo yogaṃ manaḥśuddhau kurvīthā niyatendriyaḥ // Saund_14.34 //
children.translated_text: You should again practice <s>yoga</s> for the purification of the mind, with senses controlled. // 14.34 //

children.text: athāsanagatasthānaprekṣitavyāhṛtādiṣu /
children.translated_text: In sitting, standing, looking, speaking, and other [activities],

children.text: saṃprajānan kriyāḥ sarvāḥ smṛtimādhātumarhasi // Saund_14.35 //
children.translated_text: You should maintain <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), being fully aware in all actions. // 14.35 //

children.text: dvārādhyakṣa iva dvāri yasya praṇihitā smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: He whose <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is stationed like a gatekeeper at the gate —

children.text: dharṣayanti na taṃ doṣāḥ puraṃ guptamivārayaḥ // Saund_14.36 //
children.translated_text: The faults do not assail him, like enemies [cannot assail] a well-guarded city. // 14.36 //

children.text: na tasyotpadyate kleśo yasya kāyagatā smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: No <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) arises in one whose <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is directed toward the body;

children.text: cittaṃ sarvāsvavasthāsu bālaṃ dhātrīva rakṣati // Saund_14.37 //
children.translated_text: It protects the mind in all conditions, like a nurse [protects] a child. // 14.37 //

children.text: śaravyaḥ sa tu doṣāṇāṃ yo hīnaḥ smṛtivarmaṇā /
children.translated_text: But he who is devoid of the armor of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is a target for the faults,

children.text: raṇasthaḥ pratiśatrūṇāṃ vihīna iva varmaṇā // Saund_14.38 //
children.translated_text: Like one standing in battle before enemies, deprived of armor. // 14.38 //

children.text: anāthaṃ tanmano jñeyaṃ yatsmṛtirnābhirakṣati /
children.translated_text: That mind should be known as unprotected which <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) does not guard —

children.text: nirṇetā dṛṣṭirahito viṣameṣu caranniva // Saund_14.39 //
children.translated_text: Like a guide without sight, walking on uneven ground. // 14.39 //

children.text: anartheṣu prasaktāśca svārthebhyaśca parāṅmukhā /
children.translated_text: Those who are attached to harmful things and turn away from what is beneficial,

children.text: yadbhaye sati nodvignāḥ smṛtināśo 'tra kāraṇam // Saund_14.40 //
children.translated_text: Who are not alarmed when there is cause for alarm — the loss of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is the cause of this. // 14.40 //

children.text: svabhūmiṣu guṇāḥ sarve ye ca śīlādayaḥ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All virtues, beginning with <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) and the rest, that are established in their respective domains —

children.text: vikīrṇā iva gā gopaḥ smṛtistānanugacchati // Saund_14.41 //
children.translated_text: <s>Smṛti</s> (mindfulness) follows after them, like a cowherd [follows] scattered cattle. // 14.41 //

children.text: pranaṣṭamamṛtaṃ tasya yasya viprasṛtā smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: The immortal nectar is lost for one whose <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) has strayed far;

children.text: hastasthamamṛtaṃ tasya yasya kāyagatā smṛtiḥ // Saund_14.42 //
children.translated_text: The immortal nectar is in the hand of one whose <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is directed toward the body. // 14.42 //

children.text: āryo nyāyaḥ kutastasya smṛtiryasya na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Whence comes the noble path for one in whom <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is absent?

children.text: yasyāryo nāsti ca nyāyaḥ pranaṣṭastasya satpathaḥ // Saund_14.43 //
children.translated_text: And for one who lacks the noble path, the true way is lost. // 14.43 //

children.text: pranaṣṭo yasya sanmārgo naṣṭaṃ tasyāmṛtaṃ padam /
children.translated_text: For one whose true way is lost, the immortal state is lost;

children.text: pranaṣṭamamṛtaṃ yasya sa duḥkhānna vimucyate // Saund_14.44 //
children.translated_text: one whose nectar [of mindfulness] has been lost does not become free from suffering.

children.text: tasmāccarana caro 'smīti sthito 'smīti cādhiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in [actions such as] 'I am walking,' 'I am standing,'

children.text: evamādiṣu kāryeṣu smṛtimādhātumarhasi // Saund_14.45 //
children.translated_text: and such activities, you should establish mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>).

children.text: yogānulomaṃ vijanaṃ viśabdaṃ śayyāsanaṃ saumya tathā bhajasva /
children.translated_text: "Gentle one, resort to a bed and seat that is secluded, free from people and noise, conducive to <s>yoga</s>;

children.text: kāyasya kṛtvā hi vivekamādau sukho 'dhigantuṃ manaso vivekaḥ // Saund_14.46 //
children.translated_text: for having first achieved the seclusion of the body, it is easy to attain the seclusion of the mind."

children.text: alabdhacetaḥpraśamaḥ sarāgo yo na pracāraṃ bhajate viviktam /
children.translated_text: "One who, being passionate and having not attained peace of mind, does not resort to a secluded place,

children.text: sa kṣaṇyate hyapratilabdhamārgaścarannivorvyāṃ bahukaṇṭakāyām // Saund_14.47 //
children.translated_text: is injured like one walking on ground full of thorns without having found the path."

children.text: adṛṣṭatattvena parīkṣakeṇa sthitena citre viṣayapracāre /
children.translated_text: "For one who has not seen the truth, who remains in the varied domain of sense-objects,

children.text: cittaṃ niṣeddhuṃ na sukhena śakyaṃ kṛṣṭādako gauriva sasyamadhyāt // Saund_14.48 //
children.translated_text: the mind cannot easily be restrained — like a cow drawn to water from amidst the crops."

children.text: anīryamāṇastu yathānilena praśāntimāgacchati citrabhānuḥ /
children.translated_text: "But just as a multicolored flame, not fanned by wind, reaches stillness,

children.text: alpena yatnena tathā vivikteṣvaghaṭṭitaṃ śāntimupaiti cetaḥ // Saund_14.49 //
children.translated_text: so too, in secluded places, the mind undisturbed attains peace with little effort."

children.text: kvacidbhuktvā yattad vasanamapi yattatparihito
children.translated_text: "Having eaten whatever food somewhere, and wearing whatever garment,

children.text: vasannātmārāmaḥ kvacana vijane yo 'bhiramate /
children.translated_text: one who delights in the self and rejoices somewhere in solitude,

children.text: kṛtārthaḥ sa jñeyaḥ śamasukharasajñaḥ kṛtamatiḥ
children.translated_text: that one should be known as fulfilled — one who knows the taste of the bliss of peace, with a satisfied mind,

children.text: pareṣāṃ saṃsargaṃ pariharati yaḥ kaṇṭakamiva // Saund_14.50 //
children.translated_text: who avoids the company of others as one would thorns."

children.text: yadi dvandvārāme jagati viṣayavyagrahṛdaye
children.translated_text: "If, in this world that is a garden of opposites (<s>dvandva</s>), with a heart distracted by sense-objects,

children.text: vivikte nirdvando viharati kṛtī śāntahṛdayaḥ /
children.translated_text: one who is accomplished dwells free from opposites in seclusion, with a peaceful heart,

children.text: tataḥ pītvā prajñārasamamṛtavattṛptahṛdayo
children.translated_text: then, having drunk the nectar-like taste of wisdom, with a contented heart,

children.text: viviktaḥ saṃsaktaṃ viṣayakṛpaṇaṃ śocati jagat // Saund_14.51 //
children.translated_text: the secluded one grieves for the world that is attached and wretched in its pursuit of sense-objects."

children.text: vasañśūnyāgāre yadi satatameko 'bhiramate
children.translated_text: "If, dwelling constantly alone in an empty house, one rejoices,

children.text: yadi kleśotpādaiḥ saha na ramate śatrubhiriva /
children.translated_text: if one does not delight in the arising of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), as one would not delight in enemies,

children.text: carannātmārāmo yadi ca pibati prītisalilaṃ
children.translated_text: if, moving about delighting in the self, one drinks the water of joy,

children.text: tato bhuṅkte śreṣṭhaṃ tridaśapatirājyādapi sukham // Saund_14.52 //
children.translated_text: then one enjoys happiness greater than even the sovereignty of the lord of the thirty [gods]."

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "ādiprasthāna" nāma caturdaśa sarga samāpta //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>, the fourteenth canto named 'The Initial Departure' is completed.

children.text:
pañcadaśaḥsargaḥ
vitarkaprahāṇa
children.translated_text:
Fifteenth Canto:
The Abandonment of Discursive Thought (<s>vitarkaprahāṇa</s>).

children.text: yatra tatra vivikte tu baddhvā paryaṅkamuttamam /
children.translated_text: "In whatever secluded place, having crossed the legs in the excellent posture (<s>paryaṅka</s>),

children.text: ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ samādhāya smṛtyābhimukhayānvitaḥ // Saund_15.1 //
children.translated_text: holding the body upright, endowed with mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) directed forward,"

children.text: nāsāgre vā lalāṭe vā bhruvorantara eva vā /
children.translated_text: "at the tip of the nose, or at the forehead, or between the eyebrows,

children.text: kurvīthāścapalaṃ cittamālambanaparāyaṇam // Saund_15.2 //
children.translated_text: you should make the restless mind focused on its support (<s>ālambana</s>)."

children.text: sacet kāmavitarkastvāṃ dharṣayenmānaso jvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: "If discursive thought (<s>vitarka</s>) of desire should assail you — a fever of the mind —

children.text: kṣeptavyo nādhivāsyaḥ sa vastre reṇurivāgataḥ // Saund_15.3 //
children.translated_text: it should be cast away, not entertained, like dust that has fallen on a garment."

children.text: yadyapi pratisaṃkhyānāt kāmānutsṛṣṭavānasi /
children.translated_text: "Even if through discernment you have not [fully] relinquished desires,

children.text: tamāṃsīva prakāśena pratipakṣeṇa tāñjahi // Saund_15.4 //
children.translated_text: destroy them with the antidote, as darkness is [destroyed] by light."

children.text: tiṣṭhatyanuśayasteṣāṃ channo 'gniriva bhasmanā /
children.translated_text: "Their latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) remains, hidden like fire beneath ashes;

children.text: sa te bhāvanayā saumya praśāmyo 'gnirivāmbunā // Saund_15.5 //
children.translated_text: that, gentle one, should be pacified through meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), as fire is [pacified] by water."

children.text: te hi tasmāt pravartante bhūyo vījādivāṅkurāḥ /
children.translated_text: "For they sprout forth again from that [latent tendency], as shoots from a seed;

children.text: tasya nāśena te na syurbījanāśādivāṅkurāḥ // Saund_15.6 //
children.translated_text: by its destruction, they would not arise, as shoots would not [arise] from a destroyed seed."

children.text: arjanādīni kāmebhyo dṛṣṭvā duḥkhāni kāminām /
children.translated_text: "Having seen the sufferings that come from desires — the earning [of wealth] and the like — for those who desire,

children.text: tasmāttānmūlataśchindhi mitrasaṃjñānarīniva // Saund_15.7 //
children.translated_text: therefore cut them at the root, like enemies bearing the name of friends."

children.text: anityā moṣadharmāṇo riktā vyasanahetavaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Impermanent, subject to being stolen, empty, causes of calamity,

children.text: bahusādhāraṇāḥ kāmā varhyā hyāśīviṣā iva // Saund_15.8 //
children.translated_text: shared by many — pleasures should be discarded, like venomous serpents."

children.text: ye mṛgyamāṇā duḥkhāya rakṣyamāṇā na śāntaye /
children.translated_text: "Those which, when sought, bring suffering; when guarded, do not bring peace;

children.text: bhraṣṭāḥ śokāya mahate prāptāśca na vitṛptaye // Saund_15.9 //
children.translated_text: when lost, lead to great grief; and when obtained, do not bring satisfaction."

children.text: tṛptiṃ vittaprakarṣeṇa svargāvāptyā kṛtārthatām /
children.translated_text: "One who sees fulfillment in the abundance of wealth, the attainment of purpose in reaching heaven,

children.text: kāmebhyaśca sukhotpattiṃ yaḥ paśyati sa naśyati // Saund_15.10 //
children.translated_text: and the arising of happiness from pleasures — that one perishes."

children.text: calānapariniṣpannānasārānanavasthitān /
children.translated_text: "Unstable, imperfect, without essence, without permanence,

children.text: parikalpasukhān kāmānna tānsmartumihārhasi // Saund_15.11 //
children.translated_text: with imagined happiness — you should not even recall such pleasures here."

children.text: vyāpādo vā vihiṃsā vā kṣobhayed yadi te manaḥ /
children.translated_text: "If ill-will or the desire to harm should agitate your mind,

children.text: prasādyaṃ tadvipakṣeṇa maṇinevākulaṃ jalam // Saund_15.12 //
children.translated_text: it should be pacified by its opposite, as turbid water [is cleared] by a jewel."

children.text: pratipakṣastayorjñeyo maitrī kāruṇyameva ca /
