children.translated_text: "The antidote to those two should be known as loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>);

children.text: virodho hi tayornityaṃ prakāśatamasoriva // Saund_15.13 //
children.translated_text: for their opposition is perpetual, like that of light and darkness."

children.text: nivṛttaṃ yasya dauḥśīlyaṃ vyāpādaśca pravartate /
children.translated_text: "One whose immoral conduct has ceased but in whom ill-will still operates

children.text: hanti pāṃsubhirātmānaṃ sa snāta iva vāraṇaḥ // Saund_15.14 //
children.translated_text: destroys himself, like an elephant that has bathed and then [rolls] in the dust."

children.text: duḥkhitebhyo hi martyebhyo vyādhimṛtyujarādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "For mortals who suffer from disease, death, old age, and the like,

children.text: āryaḥ ko duḥkhamaparaṃ saghṛṇo dhātumarhati // Saund_15.15 //
children.translated_text: what noble person, having compassion, would inflict yet more suffering?"

children.text: duṣṭena ceha manasā bādhyate vā paro na vā /
children.translated_text: "With a corrupt mind here, another may or may not be harmed,

children.text: sadyastu dahyate tāvat svaṃ mano duṣṭacetasaḥ // Saund_15.16 //
children.translated_text: but the mind of the one with a corrupt mind is itself immediately burned."

children.text: tasmāt sarveṣu bhūteṣu maitrīṃ kāruṇyameva ca /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, toward all beings, you should cultivate

children.text: na vyāpādaṃ vihiṃsāṃ vā vikalpayitumarhasi // Saund_15.17 //
children.translated_text: loving-kindness and compassion, not ill-will or the desire to harm."

children.text: yadyadeva prasaktaṃ hi vitarkayati mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For whatever a person habitually thinks about,

children.text: abhyāsāttena tenāsya natirbhavati cetasaḥ // Saund_15.18 //
children.translated_text: through that habitual practice, the mind inclines in that direction."

children.text: tasmādakuśalaṃ tyaktvā kuśalaṃ dhyātumarhasi /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, abandoning the unwholesome, you should meditate on the wholesome,

children.text: yatte syādiha cārthāya paramārthasya cāptaye // Saund_15.19 //
children.translated_text: which will serve your purpose here and lead to the attainment of the highest truth."

children.text: saṃvardhante hyakuśalā vitarkāḥ saṃbhṛtā hṛdi /
children.translated_text: "For unwholesome thoughts, when nourished in the heart, grow,

children.text: anarthajanakāstulyamātmanaśca parasya ca // Saund_15.20 //
children.translated_text: producing harm equally to oneself and to others."

children.text: śreyaso vighnakaraṇād bhavantyātmavipattaye /
children.translated_text: "By obstructing the good, they lead to the ruin of oneself,

children.text: pātrībhāvopaghātāttu parabhaktivipattaye // Saund_15.21 //
children.translated_text: and by destroying one's fitness as a vessel [for teaching], they lead to the ruin of others' devotion."

children.text: manaḥkarmasvavikṣepamapi cābhyastumarhasi /
children.translated_text: "And you should practice non-distraction in mental activities;

children.text: na tvevākuśalaṃ saumya vitarkayitumarhasi // Saund_15.22 //
children.translated_text: but you should certainly not, gentle one, engage in unwholesome thought."

children.text: yā vikāmopabhogāya cintā manasi vartate /
children.translated_text: "The thought that dwells in the mind for the enjoyment of sense-pleasures

children.text: na ca taṃ guṇamāpnoti bandhanāya ca kalpate // Saund_15.23 //
children.translated_text: does not attain that virtue and leads only to bondage."

children.text: sattvānāmupaghātāya parikleśāya cātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Leading to the harm of beings and to the affliction of oneself,

children.text: mohaṃ vrajati kāluṣyaṃ narakāya ca vartate // Saund_15.24 //
children.translated_text: it falls into delusion and corruption and leads to hell."

children.text: tad vitarkairakuśalairnātmānaṃ hantumarhasi /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, you should not destroy yourself with unwholesome thoughts,

children.text: suśastraṃ ratnavikṛtaṃ mṛddhato gāṃ khananniva // Saund_15.25 //
children.translated_text: like one who digs up fine land adorned with jewels with a sharp instrument."

children.text: anabhijño yathā jātyaṃ dahedaguru kāṣṭhavat /
children.translated_text: "Just as one ignorant [of its value] would burn noble <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) like ordinary firewood,

children.text: anyāyena manuṣyatvamupahanyādidaṃ tathā // Saund_15.26 //
children.translated_text: so would one wrongfully waste this human birth."

children.text: tyaktvā ratnaṃ yathā loṣṭaṃ ratnadvīpācca saṃharet /
children.translated_text: "Just as one would discard a jewel and collect a clod from a jewel-island,

children.text: tyaktvā naiḥśreyasaṃ dharmaṃ cintayedaśubhaṃ tathā // Saund_15.27 //
children.translated_text: so, having abandoned the <s>dharma</s> of the highest good, one would contemplate what is inauspicious."

children.text: himavantaṃ yathā gatvā viṣaṃ bhuñjīta nauṣadham /
children.translated_text: "Just as one who has gone to the <s>Himālayas</s> would consume poison and not medicine,

children.text: manuṣyatvaṃ tathā prāpya pāpaṃ seveta no śubham // Saund_15.28 //
children.translated_text: so, having obtained human birth, one would pursue evil and not the good."

children.text: tad buddhavā pratipakṣeṇa vitarkaṃ kṣeptumarhasi /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, having understood [this], you should cast out [unwholesome] thought with the antidote,

children.text: sūkṣmeṇa pratikīlena kīlaṃ dārvantarādiva // Saund_15.29 //
children.translated_text: like [driving out] a wedge from within wood with a fine counter-wedge."

children.text: vṛddhyavṛddhyoratha bhaveccintā jñātijanaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: "If anxiety should arise regarding kinfolk, about their prosperity or decline,

children.text: svabhāvo jīvalokasya parīkṣyastannivṛttaye // Saund_15.30 //
children.translated_text: the nature of the world of the living should be examined, for its cessation."

children.text: saṃsāre kṛṣyamāṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ svena karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: "For beings dragged through <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) by their own <s>karma</s> (actions),

children.text: ko janaḥ svajanaḥ ko vā mohāt sakto jane janaḥ // Saund_15.31 //
children.translated_text: who is one's own and who is a stranger? A person, through delusion, is attached to people."

children.text: atīte 'dhvani saṃvṛttaḥ svajano hi janastava /
children.translated_text: "In the past, strangers have become your kin,

children.text: aprāpte cādhvani janaḥ svajanaste bhaviṣyati // Saund_15.32 //
children.translated_text: and in the future, strangers will become your kin."

children.text: vihagānāṃ yathā sāyaṃ tatra tatra samāgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Just as birds come together here and there in the evening,

children.text: jātau jātau tathāśleṣo janasya svajanasya ca // Saund_15.33 //
children.translated_text: so in birth after birth, there is the coming together of people and kinfolk."

children.text: pratiśrayaṃ bahuvidhaṃ saṃśrayanti yathādhvagāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Just as travelers resort to various shelters

children.text: pratiyānti punastyaktvā tadvajjñātisamāgamaḥ // Saund_15.34 //
children.translated_text: and then depart, leaving them behind — so is the meeting of relatives."

children.text: loke prakṛtibhinne 'sminna kaścit kasyacit priyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "In this world, which is by nature divided, no one is truly dear to anyone;

children.text: kāryakāraṇasambaddhaṃ vālukāmuṣṭivajjagat // Saund_15.35 //
children.translated_text: the world is connected by cause and effect, like a handful of sand."

children.text: bibharti hi sutaṃ mātā dhārayiṣyati māmiti /
children.translated_text: "A mother bears a son thinking, 'He will support me';

children.text: mātaraṃ bhajate putro garbheṇādhatta māmiti // Saund_15.36 //
children.translated_text: a son serves his mother thinking, 'She bore me in her womb.'"

children.text: anukūlaṃ pravartante jñātiṣu jñātayo yadā /
children.translated_text: "When kinfolk act favorably toward kinfolk,

children.text: tadā snehaṃ prakurvanti riputvaṃ tu viparyayāt // Saund_15.37 //
children.translated_text: they develop affection; but when the reverse occurs, enmity."

children.text: ahito dṛśyate jñātirajñātirdṛśyate hitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "A kinsman is seen to be harmful; a stranger is seen to be helpful.

children.text: snehaṃ kāryāntarāllokāśchinatti ca karoti ca // Saund_15.38 //
children.translated_text: People cut and create affection based on different interests."

children.text: svayameva yathālikhya rajyeccitrakaraḥ striyam /
children.translated_text: "Just as a painter, having himself painted a woman, becomes enamored [of her],

children.text: tathā kṛtvā svayaṃ snehaṃ saṃgameti jane janaḥ // Saund_15.39 //
children.translated_text: so, having created attachment himself, a person becomes involved with people."

children.text: yo 'bhavad bāndhavajanaḥ paraloke priyastava /
children.translated_text: "The person who was your kinsman and dear one in a previous life —

children.text: sa te karmathaṃ kurute tvaṃ vā tasmai karoṣi kam // Saund_15.40 //
children.translated_text: what does he do for you now, or what do you do for him?"

children.text: tasmājjñātivitarkeṇa mano nāveṣṭumarhasi /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, you should not entangle your mind with thoughts about relatives;

children.text: vyavasthā nāsti saṃsāre svajanasya janasya ca // Saund_15.41 //
children.translated_text: there is no fixed arrangement in <s>saṃsāra</s> between one's own people and strangers."

children.text: asau kṣemo janapadaḥ subhikṣo 'sāvasau śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: "'That region is safe, prosperous, auspicious' —

children.text: ityevamatha jāyeta vitarkastava kaścana // Saund_15.42 //
children.translated_text: if some such thought should arise in you,"

children.text: praheyaḥ sa tvayā saumya nādhivāsyaḥ kathaṃcana /
children.translated_text: "it should be abandoned by you, gentle one, and not entertained in any way,

children.text: viditvā sarvamādīptaṃ taistairdoṣāgnibhirjagat // Saund_15.43 //
children.translated_text: knowing the entire world to be ablaze with the various fires of faults."

children.text: ṛtucakranivartācca kṣutpipāsāklamādapi /
children.translated_text: "Due to the cycle of seasons, and due to hunger, thirst, and fatigue,

children.text: sarvatra niyataṃ duḥkhaṃ na kvacid vidyate śivam // Saund_15.44 //
children.translated_text: suffering is inevitable everywhere; nowhere is there safety."

children.text: kvacicchītaṃ kvacid dharmaḥ kvacid rogo bhayaṃ kvacit /
children.translated_text: "Somewhere cold, somewhere [harsh] law, somewhere disease, somewhere fear —

children.text: bādhate 'bhyadhikaṃ lokaṃ tasmādaśaraṇaṃ jagat // Saund_15.45 //
children.translated_text: these afflict the world exceedingly; therefore, the world is without refuge."

children.text: jarā vyādhiśca mṛtyuśca lokasyāsya mahad bhayam /
children.translated_text: "Old age, disease, and death are the great terror of this world;

children.text: nāsti deśaḥ sa yatrāsya tad bhayaṃ nopapadyate // Saund_15.46 //
children.translated_text: there is no place where that terror does not arise."

children.text: yatra gacchati kāyo 'yaṃ duḥkhaṃ tatrānugacchati /
children.translated_text: "Wherever this body goes, suffering follows;

children.text: nāsti kācid gatirloke gato yatra na bādhyate // Saund_15.47 //
children.translated_text: there is no path in the world where one who has gone is not afflicted."

children.text: ramaṇīyo 'pi deśaḥ san subhikṣaḥ kṣema eva ca /
children.translated_text: "A place, even though delightful, prosperous, and safe,

children.text: kudeśa iti vijñeyo yatra kleśairvidahyate // Saund_15.48 //
children.translated_text: should be known as a bad place where one is burned by afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>)."

children.text: lokasyābhyāhatasyāsya duḥkhaiḥ śārīramānasaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "For this world, assailed by sufferings both bodily and mental,

children.text: kṣemaḥ kaścinna deśo 'sti svastho yatra gato bhavet // Saund_15.49 //
children.translated_text: there is no safe place where one who has gone would be well."

children.text: duḥkhaṃ sarvatra sarvasya vartate sarvadā yadā /
children.translated_text: "When suffering exists everywhere, for everyone, at all times,

children.text: chandarāgamataḥ saumya lokacitreṣu mā kṛthāḥ // Saund_15.50 //
children.translated_text: do not, gentle one, let desire and passion take hold regarding the spectacles of the world."

children.text: yadā tasmānnivṛttaste chandarāgo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: "When desire and passion have been turned away from that,

children.text: jīvalokaṃ tadā sarvamādīptamiva maṃsyase // Saund_15.51 //
children.translated_text: then you will regard the entire world of the living as if ablaze."

children.text: atha kaścid vitarkaste bhavedamaraṇāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "If some thought should arise in you based on the [desire for] non-death [i.e., immortality],

children.text: yatnena sa vihantavyo vyādhirātmagato yathā // Saund_15.52 //
children.translated_text: it should be dispelled with effort, like a disease that has entered the body."

children.text: muhūrtamapi viśrambhaḥ kāryoṃ na khalu jīvite /
children.translated_text: "Not even for a moment should one place trust in life,

children.text: nilīna iva hi vyāghraḥ kālo viśvastaghātakaḥ // Saund_15.53 //
children.translated_text: for time, like a lurking tiger, kills the unsuspecting."

children.text: balastho 'haṃ yuvā veti na te bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: "'I am strong, I am young' — such a thought should not arise in you;

children.text: mṛtyuḥ sarvāsvasthāsu hanti nāvekṣate vayaḥ // Saund_15.54 //
children.translated_text: death strikes in all states and does not consider age."

children.text: kṣetrabhūtamanarthānāṃ śarīraṃ parikarṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: "For one who drags along the body, which is a field of misfortunes,

children.text: svāsthyāśā jīvitāśā vā na dṛṣṭārthasya jāyate // Saund_15.55 //
children.translated_text: neither hope for health nor hope for life arises, once the truth has been seen."

children.text: nirvṛttaḥ ko bhavet kāyaṃ mahābhūtāśrayaṃ vahan /
children.translated_text: "Who could be content, carrying a body dependent on the great elements,

children.text: parasparaviruddhānāmahīnāmiva bhājanam // Saund_15.56 //
children.translated_text: which is like a vessel of mutually hostile serpents?"

children.text: praśvasityayamanvakṣaṃ yaducchvasiti mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: "That this person exhales right after inhaling —

children.text: avagaccha tadāścaryamaviśvāsyaṃ hi jīvitam // Saund_15.57 //
children.translated_text: understand this as a wonder, for life is truly untrustworthy."

children.text: idamāścaryamaparaṃ yatsuptaḥ pratibudhyate /
children.translated_text: "This is yet another wonder — that one who has fallen asleep wakes again,

children.text: svapityutthāya vā bhūyo bahvamitrā hi dehinaḥ // Saund_15.58 //
children.translated_text: or, having risen, sleeps again — for embodied beings have many enemies."

children.text: garbhāt prabhṛti yo lokaṃ jighāṃsuranugacchati /
children.translated_text: "Death, who follows the world wishing to kill from the very moment of conception —

children.text: kastasmin viśvasenmṛtyāvudyatāsāvarāviva // Saund_15.59 //
children.translated_text: who would trust in him, like [trusting] a raised sword of the enemy?"

children.text: prasūtaḥ puruṣo loke śrutavān balavānapi /
children.translated_text: "No person born in this world, however learned or powerful,

children.text: na jayatyantakaṃ kaścinnājayannāpi jeṣyati // Saund_15.60 //
children.translated_text: ever conquers death — none has conquered, nor will any conquer."

children.text: sāmnā dānena bhedena daṇḍena niyamena vā /
children.translated_text: "By conciliation, by gifts, by stratagem, by punishment, or by restraint —

children.text: prāpto hi rabhaso mṛtyuḥ pratihantuṃ na śakyate // Saund_15.61 //
children.translated_text: death, once it has arrived in fury, cannot be repelled."

children.text: tasmānnāyuṣi viśvāsaṃ cañcale kartumarhasi /
children.translated_text: "Therefore you should not place trust in this fickle life;

children.text: nityaṃ harati kālo hi sthāviryaṃ na pratīkṣate // Saund_15.62 //
children.translated_text: for time constantly carries [beings] away and does not wait for old age. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 15.62]

children.text: niḥsāraṃ paśyato lokaṃ toyabudbuddurbalam /
children.translated_text: For one who sees the world as without substance, weak as a water-bubble,

children.text: kasyāmaravitarko hi syādanunmattacetasaḥ // Saund_15.63 //
children.translated_text: what thought of immortality could arise in a mind that is not insane? [<s>Saundarananda</s> 15.63]

children.text: tasmādeṣāṃ vitarkāṇāṃ prahāṇārthaṃ samāsataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O gentle one, for the purpose of abandoning these [harmful] thoughts, in brief,

children.text: ānāpānasmṛtiṃ saumya viṣayīkartumarhasi // Saund_15.64 //
children.translated_text: you should make <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing) your object of focus. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 15.64]

children.text: ityanena prayogeṇa kāle sevitumarhasi /
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method, you should duly apply at the right time

children.text: pratipakṣān vitarkāṇāṃ gadānāmagadāniva // Saund_15.65 //
children.translated_text: the antidotes to [harmful] thoughts, as medicines [are applied] to diseases." [<s>Saundarananda</s> 15.65]

children.text: suvarṇahetorapi pāṃsudhāvakau vihāya pāṃsūn bṛhato yathāditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a gold-washer, for the sake of gold, first discards large particles of dirt,

children.text: jahāti sūkṣmānapi tadviśuddhaye viśodhya hemāvayavān niyacchati // Saund_15.66 //
children.translated_text: then discards even the fine ones, and for its purification, refining the gold-particles, restrains [them]; [<s>Saundarananda</s> 15.66]

children.text: vimokṣahetorapi yuktamānaso vihāya doṣān bṛhatastathāditaḥ /
children.translated_text: so too one whose mind is yoked, for the sake of liberation, first discards the great faults,

children.text: jahāti sūkṣmānapi tadviśuddhaye viśodhya dharmāvayavān niyacchati // Saund_15.67 //
children.translated_text: then discards even the subtle ones, and for its purification, refining the factors of <s>dharma</s>, restrains [the mind]. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 15.67]

children.text: krameṇādbhiḥ śuddhaṃ kanakamiha pāṃsuvyavahitaṃ
children.translated_text: Just as gold, obscured by dirt, is gradually [purified] by water, and then

children.text: yathāgnau karmāraḥ pacati bhṛśamāvartayati ca /
children.translated_text: the goldsmith heats it intensely in fire and turns it over and over;

children.text: tathā yogācāro nipuṇamiha doṣavyavahitaṃ
children.translated_text: so too the practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, carefully [purifying] the mind obscured by faults,

children.text: viśodhya kleśebhyaḥ śamayati manaḥ saṃkṣipati ca // Saund_15.68 //
children.translated_text: cleansing it of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), calms it and concentrates it. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 15.68]

children.text: yathā ca svacchandādupanayati karmāśrayasukhaṃ
children.translated_text: And just as a goldsmith shapes gold at will, [rendered] pliable by [his] craftsmanship,

children.text: suvarṇaṃ karmāro bahuvidhamalaṅkāravidhiṣu /
children.translated_text: into the various forms of ornaments;

children.text: manaḥśuddho bhikṣurvaśagatamabhijñāsvapi tathā
children.translated_text: so too a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) whose mind is pure, having it under control, even with the <s>abhijñās</s> (supernormal knowledges),

children.text: yathecchaṃ yatrecchaṃ śamayati manaḥ prerayati ca // Saund_15.69 //
children.translated_text: calms and directs the mind wherever he wishes, as he wishes. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 15.69]

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "vitarkaprahāṇa" nāma pañcadaśa sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>, the fifteenth <s>sarga</s> named 'The Abandonment of Harmful Thoughts' is complete.

children.text:
ṣoḍaśaḥ sargaḥ
āryasatya
children.translated_text: Sixteenth Canto: The Noble Truths

children.text: evaṃ manodhāraṇayā krameṇa vyapohya kiñcit samupohya kiñcit /
children.translated_text: "Thus, through concentration of mind, gradually setting aside some [faults] and gathering some [qualities],

children.text: dhyānāni catvāryadhigamya yogī prāpnotyabhijñā niyamena pañca // Saund_16.1 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s>, having attained the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), necessarily obtains the five <s>abhijñās</s> (supernormal knowledges). [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.1]

children.text: ṛddhipravekaṃ ca bahuprakāraṃ parasya cetaścaritāvabodham /
children.translated_text: The foremost of supernatural powers, of many kinds; understanding the conduct of another's mind;

children.text: atītajanmasmaraṇaṃ ca dīrghaṃ divye viśuddhe śruticakṣuṣī ca // Saund_16.2 //
children.translated_text: long recollection of past births; and the divine, purified [faculties of] hearing and sight. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.2]

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ tattvaparikṣaṇena mano dadhātyāsravasaṃkṣayāya /
children.translated_text: Thereafter, through investigation of reality, the mind is directed toward the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements);

children.text: tato hi duḥkhaprabhṛtīni samyak catvāri satyāni padānyavaiti // Saund_16.3 //
children.translated_text: for then one rightly comprehends the four truths, the stages beginning with suffering. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.3]

children.text: bādhātmakaṃ duḥkhamidaṃ prasaktaṃ duḥkhasya hetuḥ prabhavātmako 'yam /
children.translated_text: 'This suffering is of the nature of affliction, pervasive; this is the cause of suffering, of the nature of origination;

children.text: duḥkhakṣayo niḥsaraṇātmako 'yaṃ trāṇātmako 'yaṃ praśamāya mārgaḥ // Saund_16.4 //
children.translated_text: this is the cessation of suffering, of the nature of release; this is the path leading to peace, of the nature of protection.' [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.4]

children.text: ityāryasatyānyavabudhya buddhyā catvāri samyak pratividhya caiva /
children.translated_text: Having understood these four <s>āryasatyas</s> (noble truths) with wisdom, and having rightly penetrated them,

children.text: sarvāsravān bhāvanayābhibhūya na jāyate śāntimavāpya bhūyaḥ // Saund_16.5 //
children.translated_text: having overcome all <s>āsravas</s> through cultivation, one attains peace and is not born again. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.5]

children.text: abodhato hyaprativedhataśca tattvātmakasyāsya catuṣṭasya /
children.translated_text: For from not understanding and not penetrating this fourfold [truth] whose nature is reality,

children.text: bhavād bhavaṃ yāti na śantimeti saṃsāradolāmadhiruhya lokaḥ // Saund_16.6 //
children.translated_text: the world, having mounted the swing of <s>saṃsāra</s>, goes from existence to existence and does not reach peace. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.6]

children.text: tasmājjarādervyasanasya mūlaṃ samāsato duḥkhamavaihi janma /
children.translated_text: Therefore know, in brief, that birth is the root of suffering, which is the misfortune of old age and the rest;

children.text: sarvauṣadhīnāmiva bhūrbhavāya sarvāpadāṃ kṣetramidaṃ hi janma // Saund_16.7 //
children.translated_text: for just as the earth [is the source] of all plants for growth, so birth is the field of all calamities. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.7]

children.text: yajjanmarūpasya hi sendriyasya duḥkhasya tannaikavidhasya janma /
children.translated_text: For the birth of that which has the form of name-and-form, endowed with senses — birth is [the cause] of that manifold suffering;

children.text: yaḥ saṃbhavaścāsya samucchrayasya mṛtyośca rogasya ca saṃbhavaḥ saḥ // Saund_16.8 //
children.translated_text: and that which is the arising and growth of this [being] — that too is the arising of death and disease. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.8]

children.text: sadvāpyasadvā viṣamiśramannaṃ yathā vināśāya na dhāraṇāya /
children.translated_text: Just as food mixed with poison, whether good or bad, leads to destruction, not nourishment,

children.text: loke tathā tiryaguparyadho vā duḥkhāya sarvaṃ na sukhāya janma // Saund_16.9 //
children.translated_text: so in the world — in animal realms, above, or below — all birth leads to suffering, not to happiness. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.9]

children.text: jarādayo naikavidhāḥ prajānāṃ satyāṃ pravṛttau prabhavantyanarthāḥ /
children.translated_text: Old age and the other manifold misfortunes arise for beings when there is continued existence;

children.text: pravātsu ghoreṣvapi māruteṣu na hyaprasūtāstaravaścalanti // Saund_16.10 //
children.translated_text: for trees that have not sprouted do not tremble even in fierce storms. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.10]

children.text: ākāśayoniḥ pavano yathā hi yathā śamīgarbhaśayo hutāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as wind is born of space, just as fire rests in the womb of the <s>śamī</s> tree,

children.text: āpo yathāntarvasudhāśayāśca duḥkhaṃ tathā cittaśarīrayoniḥ // Saund_16.11 //
children.translated_text: and just as waters lie within the earth — so suffering is born of mind and body. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.11]

children.text: apāṃ dravatvaṃ kaṭhinatvamurvyā vāyoścalatvaṃ dhruvamauṣṇyamagneḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as liquidity is the nature of water, hardness of earth, movement of wind, and heat invariably of fire,

children.text: yathā svabhāvo hi tathā svabhāvo duḥkhaṃ śarīrasya ca cetasaśca // Saund_16.12 //
children.translated_text: so suffering is the nature of the body and the mind. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.12]

children.text: kāye sati vyādhijarādi duḥkhaṃ kṣuttarṣavarṣoṣṇahimādi caiva /
children.translated_text: When the body exists, there is the suffering of disease, old age, and the like, and also of hunger, thirst, rain, heat, cold, and the like;

children.text: rūpāśrite cetasi sānubandhe śokāratikrodhabhayādi duḥkham // Saund_16.13 //
children.translated_text: and for the mind, dependent on form and having attachments, there is the suffering of grief, discontent, anger, fear, and the like. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.13]

children.text: pratyakṣamālokya ca janmaduḥkhaṃ duḥkhaṃ tathātītamapīti viddhi /
children.translated_text: Having perceived the suffering of birth directly, know that past [suffering] was also thus;

children.text: yathā ca tadduḥkhamidaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaṃ tathānāgatamapyavehi // Saund_16.14 //
children.translated_text: and just as that was suffering and this is suffering, understand that future [suffering] too will be the same. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.14]

children.text: bījasvabhāvo hi yatheha dṛṣṭo bhūto 'pi bhavyo 'pi tathānumeyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as the nature of a seed is seen here [in the present], so too the past and future [seeds] should be inferred;

children.text: pratyakṣataśca jvalano yathoṣṇo bhūto 'pi bhavyo 'pi tathoṣṇa eva // Saund_16.15 //
children.translated_text: and just as fire is perceptibly hot, so too it was hot in the past and will be in the future. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.15]

children.text: tannāmarūpasya guṇānurūpaṃ yatraiva nirvṛttirudāravṛtta /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O noble one, wherever there is the arising of name-and-form according to its qualities,

children.text: tatraiva duḥkhaṃ na hi tadvimuktaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyatyabhavad bhaved vā // Saund_16.16 //
children.translated_text: right there is suffering; for that which is not free from suffering will not be, was not, and could not be [free from it]. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.16]

children.text: pravṛttiduḥkhasya ca tasya loke tṛṣṇādayo doṣagaṇā nimittam /
children.translated_text: And the cause of this suffering arising in the world is the host of faults beginning with <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving);

children.text: naiveśvaro na prakṛtirnaṃ kālo nāpo svabhāvo na vidhiryadṛcchā // Saund_16.17 //
children.translated_text: it is neither a lord (<s>īśvara</s>), nor primordial matter (<s>prakṛti</s>), nor time, nor the waters, nor inherent nature, nor fate, nor chance. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.17]

children.text: jñātavyametena ca kāraṇena lokasya doṣebhya iti pravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: And by this reasoning it should be known that the continued existence of the world is due to [its own] faults:

children.text: yasmānmriyante sarajastamaskā na jāyate vītarajastamaskaḥ // Saund_16.18 //
children.translated_text: for those possessed of <s>rajas</s> (passion) and <s>tamas</s> (darkness) die, while one free from passion and darkness is not born [again]. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.18]

children.text: icchāviśeṣe sati tatra tatra yānāsanāderbhavati prayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: When there is a particular desire, the employment of vehicles, seats, and the like takes place here and there;

children.text: yasmādatastarṣavaśāttathaiva janma prajānāmiti veditavyam // Saund_16.19 //
children.translated_text: therefore it should be known that the birth of beings is likewise due to the power of craving. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.19]

children.text: sattvānyabhiṣvaṅgavaśāni dṛṣṭvā svajātiṣu prītiparāṇyatīva /
children.translated_text: Seeing that beings are under the sway of attachment, exceedingly fond of their own species,

children.text: abhyāsayogādupapāditāni taireva doṣairiti tāni viddhi // Saund_16.20 //
children.translated_text: know that they have been brought about through the force of habit, by those very faults. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.20]

children.text: krodhapraharṣādibhirāśrayāṇāmutpadyate ceha yathā viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a particular [complexion] arises in bodies here due to anger, joy, and the like,

children.text: tathaiva janmasvapi naikarūpo nirvartate kleśakṛto viśeṣaḥ // Saund_16.21 //
children.translated_text: so too in births, a particular variation, which is not of one kind, is brought about by the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.21]

children.text: doṣādhike janmani tīvradoṣa utpadyate rāgiṇi tīvrarāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: In a birth predominated by faults, intense faults arise; in a passionate [birth], intense passion;

children.text: mohādhike mohabalādhikaśca tadalpadoṣe ca tadalpadoṣaḥ // Saund_16.22 //
children.translated_text: in one predominated by delusion, the power of delusion is greater; and in one with few faults, there are few faults. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.22]

children.text: phalaṃ hi yādṛk samavaiti sākṣāt tadāgamād bījamavaityatītam /
children.translated_text: For by the fruit that one directly perceives, one infers the seed of the past from [the evidence of] that [fruit];

children.text: avetya bījaprakṛtiṃ ca sākṣādanāgataṃ tatphalamabhyupaiti // Saund_16.23 //
children.translated_text: and by perceiving the nature of the seed directly, one anticipates the future fruit. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.23]

children.text: doṣakṣayo jātiṣu yāsu yasya vairāgyatastāsu na jāyate saḥ /
children.translated_text: In whichever births one's faults are diminished, one is not born there through dispassion;

children.text: doṣāśayastiṣṭhati yasya yatra tasyopapattirvivaśasya tatra // Saund_16.24 //
children.translated_text: but wherever one's residue of faults remains, there the helpless one takes rebirth. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.24]

children.text: tajjanmano naikavidhasya saumya tṛṣṇādayo hetava ityavetya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O gentle one, knowing that craving and the rest are the causes of manifold birth,

children.text: tāṃśchindhi duḥkhād yadi nirmumukṣā kāryakṣayaḥ kāraṇasaṃkṣayāddhi // Saund_16.25 //
children.translated_text: cut them off if you wish to be free from suffering; for the cessation of the effect comes from the cessation of the cause. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.25]

children.text: duḥkhakṣayo hetuparikṣayācca śāntaṃ śivaṃ sākṣikuruṣva dharmaṃ /
children.translated_text: And through the complete exhaustion of causes, [there is] cessation of suffering — realize directly the <s>dharma</s> that is peaceful and auspicious:

children.text: tṛṣṇāvirāgaṃ layanaṃ nirodhaṃ sanātanaṃ trāṇamahāryamāryam // Saund_16.26 //
children.translated_text: dispassion toward craving, dissolution, cessation — the eternal refuge, inviolable, noble. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.26]

children.text: yasminna jātirna jarā na mṛtyurna vyādhayo nāpriyasaṃprayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: In which there is no birth, no old age, no death, no disease, no unpleasant conjunction,

children.text: necchāvipanna priyaviprayogaḥ kṣemaṃ padaṃ naiṣṭhikamacyutaṃ tat // Saund_16.27 //
children.translated_text: no loss of what is wished for, no separation from the beloved — that is the secure, final, unfailing state. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.27]

children.text: dīpo yathā nirvṛtimabhyupeto naivāvaniṃ gacchati nāntarikṣam /
children.translated_text: Just as a lamp that has reached extinction does not go to the earth, nor to the sky,

children.text: diśaṃ na kāṃcid vidiśaṃ na kāṃcit snehakṣayāt kevalameti śāntim // Saund_16.28 //
children.translated_text: nor to any direction or intermediate direction — merely through the exhaustion of fuel, it attains peace; [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.28]

children.text: evaṃ kṛtī nirvṛtimabhyupeto naivāvaniṃ gacchati nāntarikṣam /
children.translated_text: so too one who has accomplished [the path] and reached <s>nirvṛti</s> (extinction) does not go to the earth, nor to the sky,

children.text: diśaṃ na kāṃcid vidiśaṃ na kāṃcit kleśakṣayāt kevalameti śāntim // Saund_16.29 //
children.translated_text: nor to any direction or intermediate direction — merely through the exhaustion of the <s>kleśas</s>, one attains peace. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.29]

children.text: asyābhyupāyo 'dhigamāya mārgaḥ prajñātrikalpaḥ praśamadvikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: The means of approach for attaining this is the path, threefold in its wisdom aspect and twofold in its tranquility aspect;

children.text: sa bhāvanīyo vidhivad budhena śīle śucau tripramukhe sthitena // Saund_16.30 //
children.translated_text: it should be cultivated according to method by the wise one, who stands established in the three-headed, pure <s>śīla</s> (conduct). [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.30]

children.text: vākkarma samyak sahākāyakarma yathāvadājīvanayaśca śuddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Right speech, together with right action, and likewise a pure livelihood —

children.text: idaṃ trayaṃ vṛttavidhau pravṛttaṃ śīlāśrayaṃ karmaparigrahāya // Saund_16.31 //
children.translated_text: this triad, operating in the domain of conduct, is based on <s>śīla</s> (virtue), for the mastery of action. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.31]

children.text: satyeṣu duḥkhādiṣu dṛṣṭirāryā samyagvitarkaśca parākramaśca /
children.translated_text: The noble view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) regarding the truths such as suffering, right thought, and right effort —

children.text: idaṃ trayaṃ jñānavidhau pravṛttaṃ prajñāśrayaṃ kleśaparikṣayāya // Saund_16.32 //
children.translated_text: this triad, operating in the domain of knowledge, is based on <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), for the complete destruction of the <s>kleśas</s>. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.32]

children.text: nyāyena satyādhigamāya yuktā samyak smṛtiḥ samyagatho samādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Right mindfulness and also right <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), properly applied for the attainment of truth —

children.text: idaṃ dvayaṃ yogavidhau pravṛttaṃ śamāśrayaṃ cittaparigrahāya // Saund_16.33 //
children.translated_text: this pair, operating in the domain of <s>yoga</s> (meditation), is based on <s>śama</s> (tranquility), for the mastery of the mind. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.33]

children.text: kleśāṃkurānna pratanoti śīlaṃ bījāṅkurān kāla ivātivṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śīla</s> (virtue) does not allow the sprouts of the <s>kleśas</s> to grow, like a season that has passed [does not sprout] seed-sprouts;

children.text: śucau hi śīle puruṣasya doṣā manaḥ salajjā iva dharṣayanti // Saund_16.34 //
children.translated_text: for when <s>śīla</s> is pure, faults assail a person as if with shame. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.34]

children.text: kleśāṃstu viṣkambhayate samādhirvegānivādrirmahato nadīnām /
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhi</s> (concentration) suppresses the <s>kleśas</s> like a mountain [damming] the currents of great rivers;

children.text: sthite samādhau hi na dharṣayanti doṣā bhujaṃgā iva mantrabaddhāḥ // Saund_16.35 //
children.translated_text: for when <s>samādhi</s> is established, faults do not assail, like serpents bound by <s>mantras</s>. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.35]

children.text: prajñā tvaśeṣeṇa nihanti doṣāṃstīradrumān prāvṛṣi nimnageva /
children.translated_text: But <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) destroys the faults completely, like a swollen river [uprooting] trees on the bank in the rainy season;

children.text: dagdhā yayā na prabhavanti doṣā vajrāgninevānusṛtena vṛkṣāḥ // Saund_16.36 //
children.translated_text: burned by it, faults do not grow again, like trees [burned] by a fire following a lightning strike. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.36]

children.text: triskandhametaṃ pravigāhya mārgaṃ praspaṣṭamaṣṭāṅgamahāryamāryam /
children.translated_text: Entering upon this threefold path — the manifest, noble, inviolable Eightfold [Path] —

children.text: duḥkhasya hetūn prajahāti doṣān prāpnoti cātyantaśivaṃ padaṃ tat // Saund_16.37 //
children.translated_text: one abandons the faults that are the causes of suffering and attains that supremely auspicious state. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.37]

children.text: asyopacāre dhṛtirārjavaṃ ca hrīrapramādaḥ praviviktatā ca /
children.translated_text: In its practice, [the requisites are:] steadfastness, sincerity, modesty, diligence, seclusion,

children.text: alpecchatā tuṣṭirasaṃgatā ca lokapravṛttāvaratiḥ kṣamā ca // Saund_16.38 //
children.translated_text: few desires, contentment, non-association [with the worldly], disenchantment with worldly pursuits, and patience. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.38]

children.text: yāthātmyato vindati yo hi duḥkhaṃ tasyodbhavaṃ tasya ca yo nirodham /
children.translated_text: For one who truly comprehends suffering, its arising, and its cessation —

children.text: āryeṇa mārgeṇa sa śāntimeti kalyāṇamitraiḥ saha vartamānaḥ // Saund_16.39 //
children.translated_text: that one attains peace through the Noble Path, dwelling with spiritual friends. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.39]

children.text: yo vyādhito vyādhimavaiti samyag vyādhernidānaṃ ca tadauṣadhaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Just as one who is diseased and rightly understands the disease, the cause of the disease, and the medicine —

children.text: ārogyamāpnoti hi so 'cireṇa mitrairabhijñairupacaryamāṇaḥ // Saund_16.40 //
children.translated_text: that person attains health before long, being attended by knowledgeable friends. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.40]

children.text: tadvyādhisaṃjñāṃ kuru duḥkhasatye doṣeṣvapi vyādhinidānasaṃjñām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, apply the notion of 'disease' to the truth of suffering; the notion of 'cause of disease' to the faults;

children.text: ārogyaṃjñāṃ ca nirodhasatye bhaiṣajyasaṃjñāmapi mārgasatye // Saund_16.41 //
children.translated_text: the notion of 'health' to the truth of cessation; and the notion of 'medicine' to the truth of the path. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.41]

children.text: tasmāt pravṛttiṃparigaccha duḥkhaṃ pravartakānapyavagaccha doṣān /
children.translated_text: Therefore, comprehend continued existence as suffering; understand the faults as the instigators;

children.text: nivṛttimāgaccha ca tannirodhaṃ nivartakaṃ cāpyavagaccha mārgam // Saund_16.42 //
children.translated_text: arrive at cessation as the stopping [of suffering]; and understand the path as the means of stopping. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.42]

children.text: śirasyatho vāsasi saṃpradīpte satyāvabodhāya mativicāryā /
children.translated_text: Even if your head or garment were on fire, the resolve for the realization of the truths should be made;

children.text: dagdhaṃ jagat satyanayaṃ hyadṛṣṭvā pradahyate saṃprati dhakṣyate ca // Saund_16.43 //
children.translated_text: for the world, not having seen the way of truth, has been burnt, is being burnt now, and will be burnt. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.43]

children.text: yadaiva yaḥ paśyati nāmarūpaṃ kṣayīti taddarśanamasya samyak /
children.translated_text: The very moment one sees that name-and-form is perishable — that seeing is one's right view;

children.text: samyak ca nirvedamupaiti paśyan nandīkṣayācca kṣayameti rāgaḥ // Saund_16.44 //
children.translated_text: and seeing rightly, one attains true disenchantment; and from the destruction of delight, passion reaches destruction. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.44]

children.text: tayośca nandīrajasoḥ kṣayeṇa samyagvimuktaṃ pravadāmi cetaḥ /
children.translated_text: And through the destruction of both delight and passion, I declare the mind to be rightly liberated;

children.text: samyagvimuktirmanasaśca tābhyāṃ na cāsya bhūyaḥ karaṇīyamasti // Saund_16.45 //
children.translated_text: and with the right liberation of the mind from these two, there is nothing further to be done. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.45]

children.text: yathāsvabhāvena hi nāmarūpaṃ taddhetumevāstagamaṃ ca tasya /
children.translated_text: For one who knows name-and-form according to its true nature, its cause, and its cessation,

children.text: vijānataḥ pasyata eva cāhaṃ bravīmi samyak kṣayamāsravāṇām // Saund_16.46 //
children.translated_text: and who sees [this directly] — to such a one I declare the right destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements). [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.46]

children.text: tasmāt paraṃ saumya vidhāya vīryaṃ śīghraṃ ghaṭasvāstravasaṃkṣayāya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O gentle one, summoning supreme effort, strive quickly for the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s>,

children.text: duḥkhānanityāṃśca nirātmakāṃśca dhātūn viśeṣeṇa parīkṣamāṇaḥ // Saund_16.47 //
children.translated_text: examining especially the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) as suffering, impermanent, and without self. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.47]

children.text: dhātūn hi ṣaḍ bhūsalilānalādīn sāmānyataḥ svena ca lakṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: For one who comprehends the six <s>dhātus</s> — earth, water, fire, and the rest — both in their general and particular characteristics,

children.text: avaiti yo nānyamavaiti tebhyaḥ so 'tyantikaṃ mokṣamavaiti tebhyaḥ // Saund_16.48 //
children.translated_text: and knows nothing other than them — that one knows the ultimate liberation from them. [<s>Saundarananda</s> 16.48]

children.text: kleśaprahāṇāya ca niścitena kālo 'bhyupāyasśca parīkṣitavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And for one determined upon the abandonment of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), both the right time and the right method must be examined.

children.text: yogo 'pyakāle hyanupāyataśca bhavatyanarthāya na tadguṇāya // Saund_16.49 //
children.translated_text: "For even <s>yoga</s> (practice), when [performed] at the wrong time and without the proper method, leads to harm, not to benefit." // Saund 16.49 //

children.text: ajātavatsāṃ yadi gāṃ duhīta naivāpnuyāt kṣīramakāladohī /
children.translated_text: "If one were to milk a cow that has not yet calved, one would obtain no milk — [that is] milking at the wrong time;

children.text: kāle 'pi vā syānna payo labheta mohena śṛṅgād yadi gāṃ duhīta // Saund_16.50 //
children.translated_text: Even at the right time, one would get no milk if, through delusion, one milked the cow from its horn." // Saund 16.50 //

children.text: ārdrācca kāṣṭhājjvalanābhikāmo naiva prayatnādapi vahnimṛcchet /
children.translated_text: "And one who desires fire from wet wood would never obtain flame even with effort;

children.text: kāṣṭhācca śuṣkādapi pātanena naivāgnimāpnotyanupāyapūrvam // Saund_16.51 //
children.translated_text: Even from dry wood, one who simply strikes it would not obtain fire without the proper method." // Saund 16.51 //

children.text: taddeśakālau vidhivat parīkṣya yogasya mātrāmapi cābhyupāyam /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, having duly examined the place and time, and also the measure and method of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: balābale cātmani saṃpradhārya kāryaḥ prayatno na tu tadviruddhaḥ // Saund_16.52 //
children.translated_text: And having assessed one's own strengths and weaknesses, effort should be applied — but not in a manner contrary to these." // Saund 16.52 //

children.text: pragrāhakaṃ yattu nimittamuktamuddhanyamāne hṛdi tanna sevyam /
children.translated_text: "The restraining meditation-object that has been described — that should not be employed when the mind is agitated;

children.text: evaṃ hi cittaṃ praśama na yāti pravāyunā vahniriveryamāṇaḥ // Saund_16.53 //
children.translated_text: For thus the mind does not attain tranquility, just as a fire fanned by wind does not [go out]." // Saund 16.53 //

children.text: śamāya yat syānniyataṃ nimittaṃ jātoddhave cetasi tasya kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The meditation-object that is certainly conducive to calm — its time is when the mind has become agitated;

children.text: evaṃ hi cittaṃ praśamaṃ niyacchet pradīpyamāno 'gnirivodakena // Saund_16.54 //
children.translated_text: For thus the mind is brought to tranquility, just as a blazing fire [is quenched] by water." // Saund 16.54 //

children.text: śamāvahaṃ yanniyataṃ nimittaṃ sevyaṃ na taccetasi līyamāne /
children.translated_text: "The meditation-object that is certainly conducive to calm should not be employed when the mind is sinking;

children.text: evaṃ hi bhūyo layameti cittamanīryamāṇo 'gnirivālpasāraḥ // Saund_16.55 //
children.translated_text: For thus the mind sinks further into torpor, like a fire of little substance that is not stirred." // Saund 16.55 //

children.text: pragrāhakaṃ yanniyataṃ nimittaṃ layaṃ gate cetasi tasya kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The restraining meditation-object — its time is when the mind has become torpid;

children.text: kriyāsamarthaṃ hi manastathā syānmandāyamāno 'gnirivendhanena // Saund_16.56 //
children.translated_text: For thus the mind becomes capable of action, just as a dwindling fire [is revived] by fuel." // Saund 16.56 //

children.text: aupekṣikaṃ nāpi nimittamiṣṭaṃ layaṃ gate cetasi soddhave vā /
children.translated_text: "Nor is the equanimous meditation-object desirable when the mind has sunk into torpor or when it is agitated;

children.text: evaṃ hi tīvraṃ janayedanarthamupekṣito vyādhirivāturasya // Saund_16.57 //
children.translated_text: For thus it would produce severe harm, like a disease of a sick person that is neglected." // Saund 16.57 //

children.text: yatsyādupekṣāniyataṃ nimittaṃ sāmyaṃ gate cetasi tasya kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The meditation-object belonging to equanimity — its time is when the mind has attained equilibrium;

children.text: evaṃ hi kṛtyāya bhavetprayogo ratho vidheyāśva iva prayātaḥ // Saund_16.58 //
children.translated_text: For thus the effort would serve its purpose, like a chariot set in motion with obedient horses." // Saund 16.58 //

children.text: rāgoddhavavyākulite 'pi citte maitropasaṃhāravidhirna kāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even when the mind is disturbed and agitated by passion, the practice of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) should not be applied;

children.text: rāgātmako muhyati maitrayā hi snehaṃ kaphakṣobha ivopayujya // Saund_16.59 //
children.translated_text: For one of passionate nature is further deluded by loving-kindness, like applying [what increases] <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) to one of phlegmatic constitution, [thereby increasing] attachment." // Saund 16.59 //

children.text: rāgoddhate cetasi dhairyametya niṣevitavyaṃ tvaśubhaṃ nimittam /
children.translated_text: "When the mind is agitated by passion, one should resort to courage and apply the <s>aśubha</s> (impurity) meditation-object;

children.text: rāgātmako hyevamupaiti śarma kaphātmako rūkṣamivopayujya // Saund_16.60 //
children.translated_text: For thus one of passionate nature attains peace, like one of phlegmatic constitution [who is cured] by applying dry [remedies]." // Saund 16.60 //

children.text: vyāpādadoṣeṇa manasyudīrṇe na sevitavyaṃ tvaśubhaṃ nimittam /
children.translated_text: "When the mind is stirred by the fault of ill-will, the <s>aśubha</s> (impurity) meditation-object should not be employed;

children.text: dveṣātmakasya hyaśubhā vadhāya pittātmanastīkṣṇa ivopacāraḥ // Saund_16.61 //
children.translated_text: For the impure [meditation] for one of hateful nature leads to destruction, like a sharp remedy for one of bilious (<s>pitta</s>) constitution." // Saund 16.61 //

children.text: vyāpādadoṣakṣubhite tu citte sevyā svapakṣopanayena maitrī /
children.translated_text: "But when the mind is agitated by the fault of ill-will, <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) should be practiced, bringing [the opponent] to one's own side;

children.text: dveṣātmano hi praśamāya maitrī pittātmanaḥ śīta ivopacāraḥ // Saund_16.62 //
children.translated_text: For loving-kindness calms one of hateful nature, like a cooling remedy for one of bilious constitution." // Saund 16.62 //

children.text: mohānubaddhe manasaḥ pracāre maitrāśubhā vaiva bhavatyayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: "When the activity of the mind is bound by delusion, both <s>maitrī</s> and <s>aśubhā</s> become an improper practice;

children.text: tābhyāṃ hi saṃmohamupaiti bhūyo vāyvātmako rūkṣamivopanīya // Saund_16.63 //
children.translated_text: For by both, one is further deluded, like applying dry [remedies] to one of <s>vāta</s> (wind) constitution." // Saund 16.63 //

children.text: mohātmikāyāṃ manasaḥ pravṛttau sevyastvidampratyayatāvihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: "When the mind's activity is characterized by delusion, the practice of contemplating dependent origination (<s>idaṃpratyayatā</s>) should be employed;

children.text: mūḍhe manasyeṣa hi śāntimārgo vāyvātmake snigdha ivopacāraḥ // Saund_16.64 //
children.translated_text: For when the mind is stupefied, this is the path to peace — like an unctuous remedy for one of <s>vāta</s> constitution." // Saund 16.64 //

children.text: ulkāmukhasthaṃ hi yathā suvarṇaṃ suvarṇakāro dhamatīha kāle /
children.translated_text: "For just as a goldsmith blows upon gold placed at the mouth of a furnace at the right time,

children.text: kāle pariprokṣayate jalena krameṇa kāle samupekṣate ca // Saund_16.65 //
children.translated_text: At the right time sprinkles it with water, and at the right time simply observes it with equanimity — // Saund 16.65 //

children.text: dahet suvarṇaṃ hi dhamannakāle jale kṣipan saṃśameyedakāle /
children.translated_text: "He would burn the gold if he blew at the wrong time; by casting it in water at the wrong time, he would cool it prematurely;

children.text: na cāpi samyak paripākamenaṃ nayedakāle samupekṣamāṇaḥ // Saund_16.66 //
children.translated_text: And by neglecting it at the wrong time, he would not properly bring it to full refinement — // Saund 16.66 //

children.text: saṃpragrahasya praśamasya caiva tathaiva kāle samupekṣaṇasya /
children.translated_text: "So too, at the [right] time for restraint, for calming, and likewise for equanimous observation,

children.text: samyaṅ nimittaṃ manasā tvavekṣyaṃ nāśo hi yatno 'pyanupāyapūrvaḥ // Saund_16.67 //
children.translated_text: The proper meditation-object should be discerned by the mind; for effort without the right method is destruction." // Saund 16.67 //

children.text: ityevamanyāyanivartanaṃ ca nyāyaṃ ca tasmai sugato babhāṣe /
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One) spoke to him about the turning away from other paths and about the right method;

children.text: bhūyaśca tattaccaritaṃ viditvā vitarkahānāya viodhīnuvāca // Saund_16.68 //
children.translated_text: And further, knowing his particular disposition, he spoke of the stages [of practice] for the abandonment of discursive thoughts. // Saund 16.68 //

children.text: yathā bhiṣak pittakaphānilānāṃ ya eva kopaṃ samupaiti doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Just as a physician, for whichever <s>doṣa</s> (humor) — <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, or <s>vāta</s> — becomes aggravated,

children.text: śamāya tasyaiva vidhiṃ vidhatte vyadhatta doṣeṣu tathaiva buddhaḥ // Saund_16.69 //
children.translated_text: Prescribes a remedy for the pacification of that very one, so too did the <s>Buddha</s> [prescribe] for the mental afflictions." // Saund 16.69 //

children.text: ekena kalpena sacenna hanyāt svabhyastabhāvādasubhān vitarkān /
children.translated_text: "If with one method one does not destroy the unwholesome thoughts that have been habitually nurtured,

children.text: tato dvitīyaṃ kramāmarabheta na tveva heyo guṇavān prayogaḥ // Saund_16.70 //
children.translated_text: Then one should progressively begin a second — but a beneficial practice should never be abandoned." // Saund 16.70 //

children.text: anādikālopacitātmakatvād balīyasaḥ kleśagaṇasya caiva /
children.translated_text: "Since the host of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), accumulated since beginningless time, is mighty,

children.text: samyak prayogasya ca duṣkaratvācchettuṃ na śakyāḥ sahasā hi doṣāḥ // Saund_16.71 //
children.translated_text: And since proper practice is difficult to perform — faults cannot be cut all at once." // Saund 16.71 //

children.text: aṇvyā yathāṇyā vipulāṇiranyā nirvāhyate tadviduṣā nareṇa /
children.translated_text: "Just as a small thorn is removed by another by one skilled in that [art],

children.text: tadvattadevākuśalaṃ nimittaṃ kṣipennimittāntarasevanena // Saund_16.72 //
children.translated_text: So too should one expel that very unwholesome meditation-object by the employment of another meditation-object." // Saund 16.72 //

children.text: tathāpyathādhyātmanavagrahatvānnaivopaśāmyedaśubho vitarkaḥ /
children.translated_text: "If, even so, due to the strength of inner attachment, the unwholesome thought does not subside,

children.text: heyaḥ sa taddoṣaparīkṣaṇena saśvāpado mārga ivādhvagena // Saund_16.73 //
children.translated_text: It should be abandoned by examining its faults — like a dangerous road [avoided] by a traveler." // Saund 16.73 //

children.text: yathā kṣudhārto 'pi viśeṣa pṛktaṃ jijīviṣurnecchati bhoktumannam /
children.translated_text: "Just as one who is hungry but wishes to live does not wish to eat food mixed with poison,

children.text: tathaiva doṣāvahamityavetya jahāti vidvānaśubhaṃ nimittam // Saund_16.74 //
children.translated_text: So too, knowing it to be fault-bringing, the wise one abandons the unwholesome meditation-object." // Saund 16.74 //

children.text: na doṣataḥ paśyati yo hi doṣaṃ kastaṃ tato vārayituṃ samarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For one who does not see a fault as a fault — who is able to restrain him from it?

children.text: guṇaṃ guṇe paśyati yaśca yatra sa vāryamāṇo 'pi tataḥ prayāti // Saund_16.75 //
children.translated_text: But one who sees virtue in virtue wherever it is — even when restrained, he proceeds toward it." // Saund 16.75 //

children.text: vyapatrapante hi kulaprasūtā manaḥpracārairaśubhaiḥ pravṛtaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "For those born of good family are ashamed of unwholesome mental activities that have arisen —

children.text: kaṇṭhe manasvīva yuvā vapuṣmānacākṣuṣairaprayatairviṣaktaiḥ // Saund_16.76 //
children.translated_text: Like a handsome, spirited youth [who is ashamed] of impure, unsightly things clinging to his neck." // Saund 16.76 //

children.text: nirdhūyamānāstvatha leśato 'pi tiṣṭheyurevākuśalā vitarkāḥ /
children.translated_text: "If, even when being shaken off, unwholesome thoughts should persist even slightly,

children.text: kāryāntarairadhyayanakriyādyaiḥ sevyo vidhirvismaraṇāya teṣām // Saund_16.77 //
children.translated_text: The method of forgetting them through other activities such as study and work should be employed." // Saund 16.77 //

children.text: svaptavyamapyeva vicakṣaṇena kāyaklamo vāpi niṣevitavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even sleep should be resorted to by the discerning one, or even bodily fatigue should be employed;

children.text: na tveva saṃcintyamasannimittaṃ yatrāvasaktasya bhavedanarthaḥ // Saund_16.78 //
children.translated_text: But one should never deliberately dwell on an improper meditation-object, attachment to which would bring harm." // Saund 16.78 //

children.text: yathā hi bhīto niśi taskarebhyo dvāraṃ priyebhyo 'pi na dātumicchet /
children.translated_text: "Just as one who is afraid of thieves at night would not wish to open the door even to loved ones,

children.text: prājñastathā saṃharati prayogaṃ samaṃ śubhasyāpyaśubhasya doṣaiḥ // Saund_16.79 //
children.translated_text: So the wise one shuts down practice equally to wholesome [thoughts] as well, when [they come] together with the faults of the unwholesome." // Saund 16.79 //

children.text: evaṃ prakārairapi yadyupāyairnivāryamāṇā na parāṅmukhāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: "If, even by these kinds of methods, [the unwholesome thoughts] being warded off do not turn away,

children.text: tato yathāśthūlanivarhaṇena suvarṇadoṣā iva te praheyāḥ // Saund_16.80 //
children.translated_text: Then they should be eliminated by progressive coarsening — like impurities in gold." // Saund 16.80 //

children.text: drutaprayāṇaprabhṛtīṃśca tīkṣṇāt kāmaprayogāt parikhidyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Just as a person afflicted by the sharp onset of passion takes refuge in swift walking and such [activities],

children.text: yathā naraḥ saṃśrayate tathaiva prājñena doṣeṣvapi vartitavyam // Saund_16.81 //
children.translated_text: So too should the wise person act with regard to the mental faults." // Saund 16.81 //

children.text: te cedalabdhapratipakṣabhāvā naivopaśāmyeyurasadvitarkāḥ /
children.translated_text: "If they, having found no antidote, these wrong thoughts do not subside,

children.text: muhūrtamapyaprativadhyamānā gṛhe bhujaṃgā iva nādhivāsyāḥ // Saund_16.82 //
children.translated_text: They should not be harbored even for a moment without being opposed — like snakes in a house." // Saund 16.82 //

children.text: dante 'pi dantaṃ praṇidhāya kāmaṃ tālvagramutpīḍya ca jivhayāpi /
children.translated_text: "Pressing tooth against tooth if need be, pressing the palate with the tongue,

children.text: cittena cittaṃ parigṛhya cāpi kāryaḥ prayatno na tu te 'nuvṛttāḥ // Saund_16.83 //
children.translated_text: And gripping mind with mind — effort must be made, but they must not be indulged." // Saund 16.83 //

children.text: kimatra citraṃ yadi vītamoho vanaṃ gataḥ svasthamanā na muhyet /
children.translated_text: "What wonder is it if one free from delusion, gone to the forest, with a composed mind, is not confused?

children.text: ākṣipyamāṇo hṛdi tannimittairna kṣobhyate yaḥ sa kṛtī sa dhīraḥ // Saund_16.84 //
children.translated_text: He who is not shaken when assailed in the heart by those objects — he is the accomplished one, he is the steadfast one." // Saund 16.84 //

children.text: tadāryasatyādhigamāya pūrvaṃ viṃśodhayānena nayena mārgam /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, for the attainment of the Noble Truths, first purify the path by this method,

children.text: yātrāgataḥ śatruvinigrahārthaṃ rājeva lakṣmīmajitāṃ jigīṣan // Saund_16.85 //
children.translated_text: Like a king who has set out to conquer unconquered prosperity for the purpose of subduing enemies." // Saund 16.85 //

children.text: etānyaraṇyānyabhitaḥ śivāni yogānukūlānyajaneritāni /
children.translated_text: "These peaceful forests around [you], favorable to <s>yoga</s>, undisturbed by people —

children.text: kāyasya kṛtvā pravivekamātraṃ kleśaprahāṇāya bhajasva mārgam // Saund_16.86 //
children.translated_text: Having achieved mere solitude of body, pursue the path for the abandonment of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)." // Saund 16.86 //

children.text: kauṇḍinyanandakṛmilāniruddhāstiṣyopasenau vimalo 'tha rādhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, <s>Nandaka</s>, <s>Kṛmila</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, <s>Upasena</s>, <s>Vimala</s>, and <s>Rādha</s>;

children.text: bāṣpottarau dhautakimoharājau kātyāyanadravyapilindavatsāḥ // Saund_16.87 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bāṣpottara</s>, <s>Dhautaki</s>, <s>Moharāja</s>; <s>Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Dravya</s>, <s>Pilindavatsa</s>; // Saund 16.87 //

children.text: bhaddālibhadrāyaṇasarpadāsasubhūtigodattasujātavatsāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaddāli</s>, <s>Bhadrāyaṇa</s>, <s>Sarpadāsa</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Godatta</s>, <s>Sujāta</s>, <s>Vatsa</s>;

children.text: saṃgrāmajid bhadrajidaśvajicca śroṇaśca śoṇaśca ca koṭikarṇaḥ // Saund_16.88 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃgrāmajit</s>, <s>Bhadrajit</s>, and <s>Aśvajit</s>; and <s>Śroṇa</s>, and <s>Śoṇa</s>, and <s>Koṭikarṇa</s>; // Saund 16.88 //

children.text: kṣemājito nandakanandamātāvupālivāgīśayaśoyaśodāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣemājita</s>, <s>Nandaka</s>, <s>Nandamātā</s>, <s>Upāli</s>, <s>Vāgīśa</s>, <s>Yaśas</s>, <s>Yaśodā</s>;

children.text: mahāvhayo valkalirāṣṭrapālau sudarśanasvāgatamedhikāśca // Saund_16.89 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāvha</s>, <s>Valkali</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Svāgata</s>, and <s>Medhika</s>; // Saund 16.89 //

children.text: sa kapphinaḥ kāśyapa auruvilvo mahāmahākāśyapatiṣyanandāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kapphinaḥ</s>, <s>Kāśyapa Auruvilva</s>, <s>Mahā-Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, <s>Nanda</s>;

children.text: pūrṇaśca pūrṇaśca sa pūrṇakaśca śonāparāntaśca sa pūrṇa eva // Saund_16.90 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇa</s>, and <s>Pūrṇa</s>, and that <s>Pūrṇaka</s>; and <s>Śonāparānta</s>, and that <s>Pūrṇa</s> himself; // Saund 16.90 //

children.text: śāradvatīputrasubāhucundāḥ kondeyakāpyabhṛgukuṇṭhadhānāḥ /
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Śāradvatī</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, <s>Cunda</s>; <s>Kondeya</s>, <s>Kāpya</s>, <s>Abhṛgu</s>, <s>Kuṇṭhadhāna</s>;

children.text: saśaivalau revatakauṣṭhilau ca maudgalyagotraśca gavāṃpatiśca // Saund_16.91 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śaivala</s> and <s>Revataka</s> and <s>Kauṣṭhila</s>; and one of <s>Maudgalya</s> clan, and <s>Gavāṃpati</s>. // Saund 16.91 //

children.text: yaṃ vikramaṃ yogavidhāvakurvaṃstameva śīghraṃ vidhivat kuruṣva /
children.translated_text: "The effort that they made in the practice of <s>yoga</s> — make that same [effort] swiftly and according to method;

children.text: tataḥ padaṃ prāpsyasi tairavāptaṃ sukhāvṛtaistvaṃ niyataṃ yaśaśca // Saund_16.92 //
children.translated_text: Then you will certainly attain the state attained by them — those enveloped in bliss — and glory too." // Saund 16.92 //

children.text: dravyaṃ yathā syat kaṭukaṃ rasena taccopayuktaṃ madhuraṃ vipāke /
children.translated_text: "Just as a substance may be bitter in taste, yet that same substance, when consumed, is sweet in its result,

children.text: tathaiva vīryaṃ kaṭukaṃ śrameṇa tasyārtha siddhyai madhuro vipākaḥ // Saund_16.93 //
children.translated_text: So too is vigor bitter with exertion, but for the accomplishment of its purpose, sweet is its result." // Saund 16.93 //

children.text: vīryaṃ paraṃ kāryakṛtau hi mūlaṃ vīryādṛte kācana nāsti siddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Supreme vigor indeed is the root of accomplishment; without vigor, there is no attainment whatsoever;

children.text: udeti vīryādiha sarvasaṃpannirvīryatā cet sakalaśca pāpmā // Saund_16.94 //
children.translated_text: From vigor arises all prosperity in this world; and from lack of vigor, all misfortune." // Saund 16.94 //

children.text: alabdhasyālābho niyatamupalabdhasya vigamas
children.translated_text: "Non-acquisition of what has not been acquired, and the loss of what has been acquired,

children.text: tathaivātmāvajñā kṛpaṇamadhikebhyaḥ paribhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: And likewise self-contempt, wretched humiliation by superiors,

children.text: tamo nistejastvaṃ śrutiniyamatuṣṭivyuparamo
children.translated_text: Darkness, spiritlessness, the cessation of satisfaction in learning and discipline —

children.text: nṛṇāṃ nirvīryāṇāṃ bhavati vinipātaśca bhavati // Saund_16.95 //
children.translated_text: For men who lack vigor, downfall indeed occurs." // Saund 16.95 //

children.text: nayaṃ śrutvā śakto yadayamabhivṛddhiṃ na labhate
children.translated_text: "If, having heard the right method, one does not gain progress;

children.text: paraṃ dharmaṃ jñātvā yadupari nivāsaṃ na labhate /
children.translated_text: If, having known the supreme <s>Dharma</s>, one does not gain a higher abode;

children.text: gṛhaṃ tyaktvā muktau yadayamupaśāntiṃ na labhate /
children.translated_text: If, having renounced the household, one does not gain peace in liberation —

children.text: nimittaṃ kausīdyaṃ bhavati puruṣasyātra na ripuḥ // Saund_16.96 //
children.translated_text: The cause is laziness, not an enemy." // Saund 16.96 //

children.text: anikṣiptotsāho yadi khanati gāṃ vāri labhate /
children.translated_text: "If one digs the earth with unrelenting effort, one obtains water;

children.text: prasaktaṃ vyāmathnan jvalanamaraṇibhyāṃ janayati /
children.translated_text: By persistent churning, one generates fire from the fire-sticks;

children.text: prayuktā yoge tu dhruvamupalabhante śramaphalaṃ
children.translated_text: Those devoted to <s>yoga</s> surely obtain the fruit of their exertion —

children.text: drutaṃ nityaṃ yāntyo girimapi hi bhindanti saritaḥ // Saund_16.97 //
children.translated_text: Rivers, flowing swiftly and ceaselessly, even split mountains." // Saund 16.97 //

children.text: kṛṣṭvā gāṃ paripālya ca śramaśatairaśnoti sasyaśriyaṃ
children.translated_text: "Having plowed the earth and tended it with a hundred labors, one enjoys the wealth of crops;

children.text: yatnena pravigāhya sāgarajalaṃ ratnaśriyā krīḍati /
children.translated_text: Having plunged with effort into the ocean waters, one plays with the wealth of gems;

children.text: śatrūṇāmavadhūya vīryamiṣubhirbhuṅkte narendraśriyaṃ
children.translated_text: Having vanquished the might of enemies with arrows, one enjoys royal splendor —

children.text: tadvīryaṃ kuru śāntaye viniyataṃ vīrye hi sarvarddhayaḥ // Saund_16.98 //
children.translated_text: Therefore apply vigor, disciplined for the sake of peace; for in vigor lie all prosperities." // Saund 16.98 //

children.text: saundarananda mahākāvye "āryasatya" nāma ṣoḍaśa sarga samāpta /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>, the sixteenth canto, named '<s>Āryasatya</s>' (The Noble Truths), is completed.

children.text:
saptadaśaḥ sargaḥ
amṛtaprāpti
children.translated_text: Seventeenth Canto: <s>Amṛtaprāpti</s> (The Attainment of the Deathless)

children.text: athaivamādeśitatattvamārgo nandastadā prāptavimokṣamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, thus instructed in the path of truth, having obtained the path to liberation,

children.text: sarveṇa bhāvena gurau praṇamya kleśaprahāṇāya vanaṃ jagāma // Saund_17.1 //
children.translated_text: Bowed to his teacher with his entire being, and went to the forest for the abandonment of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). // Saund 17.1 //

children.text: tatrāvakāśaṃ mṛdunīlaśaṣpaṃ dadarśa śāntaṃ taruṣaṇḍavantam /
children.translated_text: There he saw a peaceful clearing with soft green grass, possessing clusters of trees,

children.text: niḥśabdayā nimnagayopagūḍhaṃ vaiḍūryanīlodakayā vahantyā // Saund_17.2 //
children.translated_text: Embraced by a silent stream flowing with waters blue as <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl). // Saund 17.2 //

children.text: sa pādayostatra vidhāya śaucaṃ śucau śive śrīmati vṛkṣamūle /
children.translated_text: Having washed his feet there, at a pure, auspicious, beautiful tree-root,

children.text: mokṣāya baddhvā vyavasāyakakṣāṃ paryaṅkamaṅkāvahitaṃ babandha // Saund_17.3 //
children.translated_text: Having girded on the belt of resolution for the sake of liberation, he bound his legs in the <s>paryaṅka</s> (cross-legged) posture, attentive. // Saund 17.3 //

children.text: ṛjuṃ samagraṃ praṇidhāya kāyaṃ kāye smṛtiṃ cābhimukhīṃ vidhāya /
children.translated_text: Holding his body straight and whole, and directing mindfulness toward the body,

children.text: sarvendriyāṇyātmani saṃnidhāya sa tatra yogaṃ prayataḥ prapede // Saund_17.4 //
children.translated_text: Withdrawing all the senses into the self, he there zealously entered upon <s>yoga</s>. // Saund 17.4 //

children.text: tataḥ sa tattvaṃ nikhilaṃ cikīrṣurmokṣānukūlāṃśca vidhīṃścikīrṣan /
children.translated_text: Then he, wishing to accomplish the complete truth, and desiring to perform the practices conducive to liberation,

children.text: jñānena śīlena śamena caiva cacāra cetaḥ parikarmabhūmau // Saund_17.5 //
children.translated_text: Through knowledge, through moral conduct, and through tranquility, he exercised his mind on the ground of preliminary purification. // Saund 17.5 //

children.text: saṃdhāya dhairyaṃ praṇidhāya vīryaṃ vyapohya saktiṃ parigṛhya śaktim /
children.translated_text: Having gathered firmness, having directed effort, having cast away attachment and grasped capability,

children.text: praśāntacetā niyamasthacetāḥ svasthastatobhūd viṣayeṣvanāsthaḥ // Saund_17.6 //
children.translated_text: With a pacified mind, with a mind established in discipline, he became composed, without attachment to sense objects. // Saund 17.6 //

children.text: ātaptabuddheḥ prahitātmano 'pi svabhyastabhāvādatha kāmasaṃjñā /
children.translated_text: Yet for him, though his intelligence was kindled and his self was applied, the perception of sensuality,

children.text: paryākulaṃ tasya manaścakāra prāvṛṭsu vidyujjalamāgateva // Saund_17.7 //
children.translated_text: Due to its habitual force, threw his mind into confusion — like lightning and rain arriving in the monsoon. // Saund 17.7 //

children.text: sa paryavasthānamavetya sadyaścikṣepa tāṃ dharmavighātakartrīm /
children.translated_text: But he, recognizing that mental affliction at once, cast it aside — that destroyer of the <s>Dharma</s> —

children.text: priyāmapi krodhaparītacetā nārīmivodvṛttaguṇāṃ manasvī // Saund_17.8 //
children.translated_text: Like a self-possessed man, even though his heart is overcome by anger, [casts aside] a beloved woman whose virtues have deteriorated. // Saund 17.8 //

children.text: ārabdhavīryasya manaḥśamāya bhūyastu tasyākuśalo vitarkaḥ /
children.translated_text: Yet again, for him who had begun his effort toward mental calm, an unwholesome thought

children.text: vyādhipraṇāśāya niviṣṭavuddherupadravo ghora ivājagāma // Saund_17.9 //
children.translated_text: Arrived like a terrible complication for one whose mind was set on the destruction of disease. // Saund 17.9 //

children.text: sa tadvighātāya nimittamanyad yogānukūlaṃ kuśalaṃ prapede /
children.translated_text: For the destruction of that [thought], he resorted to another wholesome object, favorable to <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: ārtāyanaṃ kṣīṇabalo balasthaṃ nirasyamāno balināriṇeva // Saund_17.10 //
children.translated_text: Like one seeking refuge — weakened in strength — in a strong [protector], being repelled by a powerful enemy. // Saund 17.10 //

children.text: puraṃ vidhāyānuvidhāya daṇḍaṃ mitrāṇi saṃgṛhya ripūn vigṛhya /
children.translated_text: Just as a king, having fortified his city, organized his army, gathered allies, and subdued enemies,

children.text: rājā yathāpnoti hi gāmapūrvāṃ nītirmumukṣorapi saiva yoge // Saund_17.11 //
children.translated_text: Attains territory not previously held — such is the very statecraft for one who seeks liberation in <s>yoga</s>. // Saund 17.11 //

children.text: vimokṣakāmasya hi yogino 'pi manaḥ puraṃ jñānavidhiśca daṇḍaḥ /
children.translated_text: For even for the <s>yogin</s> who desires liberation, the mind is the city, the method of knowledge is the army,

children.text: guṇāśca mitrāṇyarayaśca doṣā bhūmirvimuktiryatate yadartham // Saund_17.12 //
children.translated_text: Virtues are the allies and faults are the enemies, and liberation is the territory for which he strives. // Saund 17.12 //

children.text: sa duḥkhajālānmahato mumukṣurvimokṣamārgādhigame vivikṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: Wishing to be freed from the great net of suffering, desiring to enter upon the path of liberation,

children.text: panthānmāryaṃ paramaṃ didṛkṣuḥ śamaṃ yayau kiṃcidupāttacakṣuḥ // Saund_17.13 //
children.translated_text: Wishing to see the supreme Noble Path, he attained a measure of calm, his eye partially opened. // Saund 17.13 //

children.text: yaḥ syānniketastamaso 'niketaḥ śrutvāpi tattvaṃ sa bhavet pramattaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who, though a houseless abode of darkness, would remain heedless even after hearing the truth;

children.text: yasmāttu mokṣāya sa pātrabhūtastasmānmanaḥ svātmani saṃjahāra // Saund_17.14 //
children.translated_text: But since he was a worthy vessel for liberation, he gathered his mind into his own self. // Saund 17.14 //

children.text: sambhārataḥ pratyayataḥ svabhāvādāsvādato doṣaviśeṣataśca /
children.translated_text: Then that self-possessed one duly examined the <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) with regard to their constituents, their conditions, their own nature,

children.text: athātmavānniḥsaraṇātmataśca dharmeṣu cakre vidhivat parīkṣām // Saund_17.15 //
children.translated_text: Their relish, their particular faults, and also their means of escape. // Saund 17.15 //

children.text: sa rūpiṇaṃ kṛtsnamarūpiṇaṃ ca sāraṃ didṛkṣurvicikāya kāyam /
children.translated_text: Wishing to see what is essential, he analyzed the body — both its form and its formless [aspects];

children.text: athāśuciṃ duḥkhamanityamasvaṃ nirātmakaṃ caiva cikāya kāyam // Saund_17.16 //
children.translated_text: Then he analyzed the body as impure, suffering, impermanent, not one's own, and devoid of self. // Saund 17.16 //

children.text: anityatastatra hi śūnyataśca nirātmato duḥkhata eva cāpi /
children.translated_text: For therein, through impermanence, emptiness, selflessness, and suffering,

children.text: mārgapravekeṇa sa laukikena kleśadrumaṃ saṃcalayāṃcakāra // Saund_17.17 //
children.translated_text: Through the initial penetration of the mundane path, he shook the tree of defilements. // Saund 17.17 //

children.text: yasmādabhūtvā bhavatīha sarvaṃ bhutvā ca bhūyo na bhavatyavaśyam /
children.translated_text: Since everything here, having not existed, comes into being, and having existed, inevitably ceases to be,

children.text: sahetukaṃ ca kṣayi hetumacca tasmādanityaṃ jagadityavindat // Saund_17.18 //
children.translated_text: And since [all] is with cause and what has a cause is perishable — therefore he found the world to be impermanent. // Saund 17.18 //

children.text: yataḥ prasūtasya ca karmayogaḥ prasajyate bandhavighātahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Since for one who is born, the connection with <s>karma</s> ensues, which is the cause of bondage and its destruction,

children.text: duḥkhapratīkāravidhau sukhākhye tato bhavaṃ duḥkhamiti vyapaśyat // Saund_17.19 //
children.translated_text: And since what is called happiness is [merely] a remedy for suffering — therefore he saw existence as suffering. // Saund 17.19 //

children.text: yataśca saṃskāragataṃ viviktaṃ na kārakaḥ kaścana vedako vā /
children.translated_text: Since in what pertains to conditioned things, when discerned, there is no doer whatsoever, nor any experiencer,

children.text: samagryataḥ saṃbhavati pravṛttiḥ śūnyaṃ tato lokamimaṃ dadarśa // Saund_17.20 //
children.translated_text: And activity arises from the aggregate [of conditions] — therefore he saw this world as empty. // Saund 17.20 //

children.text: yasmānnirīhaṃ jagadasvatantraṃ naiśvaryamekaḥ kurute kriyāsu /
children.translated_text: Since the world is without [inherent] effort and not self-governing, and no single [entity] exercises sovereignty in actions,

children.text: tattatpratītya prabhavanti bhāvā nirātmakaṃ tena viveda lokam // Saund_17.21 //
children.translated_text: And things come into being dependent on this and that — therefore he understood the world as devoid of self. // Saund 17.21 //

children.text: tataḥ sa vātaṃ vyajanādivoṣṇe kāṣṭhāśritaṃ nirmathanādivāgnim /
children.translated_text: Then, like [obtaining] wind from a fan and the like when hot, like [obtaining] fire from wood through friction and the like,

children.text: antaḥkṣitisthaṃ khananādivāmbho lokottaraṃ vartma durāpamāpa // Saund_17.22 //
children.translated_text: Like [obtaining] water from underground through digging and the like — he attained the supramundane path, difficult to obtain. // Saund 17.22 //

children.text: sajjñānacāpaḥ smṛtivarma baddhvā viśuddhaśīlavratavāhanasthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having strung the bow of knowledge, having fastened the armor of mindfulness, mounted on the vehicle of pure conduct and moral vows,

children.text: kleśāribhiścittaraṇājirasthaiḥ sārdhaṃ yuyutsurvijayāya tasthau // Saund_17.23 //
children.translated_text: He stood ready to fight for victory against the enemies of defilements stationed on the battlefield of the mind. // Saund 17.23 //

children.text: tataḥ sa bodhyaṅgaśitāttaśastraḥ samyakpradhānottamavāhanasthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, with weapons sharpened by the factors of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), mounted on the supreme vehicle of right effort,

children.text: mārgāṅgamātaṅgavatā balena śanaiḥ śanaiḥ kleśacamūṃ jagāhe // Saund_17.24 //
children.translated_text: With a force as [mighty as] an elephant possessing the limbs of the path, he slowly entered the army of defilements. // Saund 17.24 //

children.text: sa smṛtyupasthānamayaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ śatrūn viparyāsamayān kṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: With the arrows made of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), in an instant,

children.text: duḥkhasya hetūṃścaturaścaturbhiḥ svaiḥ svaiḥ pracārāyatanairdadāra // Saund_17.25 //
children.translated_text: He pierced the four enemies consisting of wrong views — the four causes of suffering — each with their respective domains. // Saund 17.25 //

children.text: āryairbalaiḥ pañcabhireva pañca cetaḥkhilānyapratimairbabhañja /
children.translated_text: With the five matchless Noble Powers (<s>balas</s>) he shattered the five rigidities of the mind;

children.text: mithyāṅganāgāṃśca tathāṅganāgairvinirdudhāvāṣṭabhireva so 'ṣṭau // Saund_17.26 //
children.translated_text: And with the eight Noble Limbs of the Path, he drove away the eight wrong paths, like [driving away] rogue elephants with [tame] elephants. // Saund 17.26 //

children.text: athātmadṛṣṭiṃ sakalāṃ vidhūya caturṣu satyeṣvakathaṃkathaḥ san /
children.translated_text: Then, having completely dispelled the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>), being free from doubt regarding the Four Truths,

children.text: viśuddhaśīlavratadṛṣṭadharmā dharmasya pūrvāṃ phalabhūmimāpa // Saund_17.27 //
children.translated_text: With purified conduct, moral vows, and direct vision of the <s>Dharma</s>, he attained the first stage of the fruit of the <s>Dharma</s>. // Saund 17.27 //

children.text: sa darśanādāryacatuṣṭayasya kleśaikadeśasya ca viprayogāt /
children.translated_text: Through the vision of the four Noble [Truths], through partial separation from defilements,

children.text: pratyātmikāccāpi viśeṣalābhāt pratyakṣato jñānisukhasya caiva // Saund_17.28 //
children.translated_text: Through the personal attainment of distinction, and through the direct experience of the happiness of a knower, // Saund 17.28 //

children.text: dārḍhyāt prasādasya dhṛteḥ sthiratvāt satyeṣvasaṃmūḍhatayā caturṣu /
