children.translated_text: Through the firmness of faith, the stability of resolve, through being unconfused regarding the Four Truths,

children.text: śīlasya cācchidratayottamasya niḥsaṃśayo dharmavidhau babhūva // Saund_17.29 //
children.translated_text: And through the flawlessness of his supreme moral conduct — he became free from doubt regarding the method of the <s>Dharma</s>. // Saund 17.29 //

children.text: kudṛṣṭijālena sa viprayukto lokaṃ tathābhūtamavekṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Freed from the net of wrong views, observing the world as it truly is,

children.text: jñānāśrayāṃ prītimupājagāma bhūyaḥ prasādaṃ ca gurāviyāya // Saund_17.30 //
children.translated_text: He arrived at a joy grounded in knowledge, and his faith in the teacher grew even further. // Saund 17.30 //

children.text: yo hi pravṛttiṃ niyatāmavaiti nivānyahetoriha nāpyahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who understands that determined origination arises from a cause and not without a cause here,

children.text: pratītya tattatsamavaiti tattatsa naiṣṭhikaṃ paśyati dharmamāryam // Saund_17.31 //
children.translated_text: And understands this and that as dependent on this and that — he sees the ultimate Noble <s>Dharma</s>. // Saund 17.31 //

children.text: śāntaṃ śivaṃ nirjarasaṃ virāgaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ paśyati yaśca dharmam /
children.translated_text: And one who sees the <s>Dharma</s> as peaceful, auspicious, ageless, free from passion, and the highest good,

children.text: tasyopadeṣṭāramathāryavaryaṃ sa prekṣate buddhamavāptacakṣuḥ // Saund_17.32 //
children.translated_text: He, having gained the [Dharma-]eye, sees the <s>Buddha</s>, the best of the Noble Ones, as its teacher. // Saund 17.32 //

children.text: yathopadeśena śivena mukto rogādarogo bhiṣajaṃ kṛtajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as one freed from disease by auspicious treatment, [as] a grateful [patient] sees the physician —

children.text: anusmaran paśyati cittadṛṣṭyā maitryā ca śāstrajñatayā ca tuṣṭaḥ // Saund_17.33 //
children.translated_text: Remembering [him] with the eye of the mind, satisfied by his kindness and his mastery of the science. // Saund 17.33 //

children.text: āryeṇa mārgeṇa tathaiva muktastathāgataṃ tattvavidāryatattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just so, freed by the Noble Path, one who knows the truth of noble truth sees the <s>Tathāgata</s>,

children.text: anusmaran paśyati kāyasākṣī maitryā ca sarvajñatayā ta tuṣṭaḥ // Saund_17.34 //
children.translated_text: Remembering [him] as a bodily witness, satisfied by his kindness and his omniscience. // Saund 17.34 //

children.text: sa nāśakairdṛṣṭigatairvimuktaḥ paryantamālokya punarbhavasya /
children.translated_text: Freed from the destructive wrong views, having seen the limit of renewed existence,

children.text: bhaktvā ghṛṇāṃ kleśavijṛmbhiteṣu mṛtyorna tatrāsa na durgatibhyaḥ // Saund_17.35 //
children.translated_text: Having developed revulsion toward the manifestations of defilements — he feared neither death nor evil destinies. // Saund 17.35 //

children.text: tvaksnāyumedorudhirāsthimāṃsakeśādināmedhyagaṇena pūrṇam /
children.translated_text: Contemplating the body — filled with a heap of impure things such as skin, sinews, fat, blood, bones, flesh, hair, and the rest —

children.text: tataḥ sa kāyaṃ samavekṣamāṇaḥ sāraṃ vicintyāṇvapi nopalebhe // Saund_17.36 //
children.translated_text: He, searching, did not find even an atom of essence in it. // Saund 17.36 //

children.text: sa kāmarāgapratighau sthirātmā tenaiva yogena tanū cakāra /
children.translated_text: With firm resolve, through that very <s>yoga</s>, he made sensual desire and ill-will thin;

children.text: kṛtvā mahoraskatanustanū tau prāpa dvitīyaṃ phalamāryadharme // Saund_17.37 //
children.translated_text: Having made those two — [formerly] as great as mighty serpents — thin, he attained the second fruit of the Noble <s>Dharma</s>. // Saund 17.37 //

children.text: sa lobhacāpaṃ parikalpabāṇaṃ rāgaṃ mahāvairiṇamalpaśeṣam /
children.translated_text: The great enemy, passion — with the bow of greed and the arrows of false conception — remaining but slightly,

children.text: kāyasvabhāvādhigataurbibheda yogāyudhāstrairaśubhāpṛṣatkaiḥ // Saund_17.38 //
children.translated_text: He shattered with the weapons of <s>yoga</s> — the arrows of the <s>aśubha</s> (impure) [meditation] — and with insights gained from the body's true nature. // Saund 17.38 //

children.text: dveṣāyudhaṃ krodhavikīrṇabāṇaṃ vyāpādamantaḥprasavaṃ sapatnam /
children.translated_text: Ill-will — wielding the weapon of hatred, scattering arrows of anger, a foe breeding [evil] within —

children.text: maitrīpṛṣatkairdhṛtitūṇasaṃsthaiḥ kṣamādhanurjyāvisṛtairjaghāna // Saund_17.39 //
children.translated_text: He slew with the arrows of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), set in the quiver of fortitude, released from the bowstring of patience. // Saund 17.39 //

children.text: mūlānyatha trīṇyaśubhasya vīrastribhirvimokṣāyatanaiścakarta /
children.translated_text: Then the hero cut the three roots of unwholesomeness with the three gateways to liberation,

children.text: camūmukhasthān dhṛtakārmukāṃstrīnarīnivāristribhirāyasāgraiḥ // Saund_17.40 //
children.translated_text: Like cutting three enemy [leaders] standing at the front of an army, bearing bows, with three iron-tipped [arrows]. // Saund 17.40 //

children.text: sa kāmadhātoḥ samatikramāya pārṣṇigrahāṃstānabhibhūya śatrūn /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of transcending the realm of desire, having overcome those enemies — the rear-guard —

children.text: yogādanāgāmiphalaṃ prapadya dvārīva nirvāṇapurasya tasthau // Saund_17.41 //
children.translated_text: Through <s>yoga</s>, having attained the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), he stood as if at the gate of the city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Saund 17.41 //

children.text: kāmairviviktaṃ malinaiśca dharmairvitarkavaccāpi vicāravacca /
children.translated_text: Secluded from sensual desires and from unwholesome states, accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought,

children.text: vivekajaṃ prītisukhopapannaṃ dhyānaṃ tataḥ sa prathamaṃ prapede // Saund_17.42 //
children.translated_text: Born of seclusion, endowed with joy and happiness — he then attained the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). // Saund 17.42 //

children.text: kāmāgnidāhena sa vipramukto lhādaṃ paraṃ dhyānasukhādavāpa /
children.translated_text: Freed from the burning of the fire of desire, he experienced supreme delight from the happiness of <s>dhyāna</s>,

children.text: sukhaṃ vigāhyāpsviva dharmakhinnaḥ prāpyeva cārtha vipulaṃ daridraḥ // Saund_17.43 //
children.translated_text: Like one wearied by the <s>Dharma</s> plunging into pleasant water, or like a poor man obtaining great wealth. // Saund 17.43 //

children.text: tatrāpi taddharmagatān vitarkān guṇāguṇe ca prasṛtān vicārān /
children.translated_text: Yet even there, the thoughts directed toward the <s>Dharma</s> — and the examinations extending to virtues and non-virtues —

children.text: buddhvā manaḥkṣobhakarānaśāntāṃstadviprayogāya matiṃ cakāra // Saund_17.44 //
children.translated_text: Recognizing them as unpeaceful, causing agitation of the mind, he resolved to separate from them. // Saund 17.44 //

children.text: kṣobhaṃ prakurvanti yathormayo hi dhīraprasannāmbuvahasya sindhoḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as waves disturb the waters of a deep, calm, clear-flowing river,

children.text: ekāgrabhūtasya tathormibhūtāścittāmbhasaḥ kṣobhakarā vitarkāḥ // Saund_17.45 //
children.translated_text: So the wave-like thoughts disturb the waters of the mind that has become one-pointed. // Saund 17.45 //

children.text: khinnasya suptasya ca nirvṛtasya bādhaṃ yathā saṃjanayanti śabdāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as sounds create disturbance for one who is weary, asleep, or at ease,

children.text: adyātmamaikāgryamupāgatasya bhavanti bādhāya tathā vitarkāḥ // Saund_17.46 //
children.translated_text: So do discursive thoughts become a disturbance for one whose inner mind has attained one-pointedness. // Saund 17.46 //

children.text: athāvitarkaṃ kramaśo 'vicāramekāgrabhāvānmanasaḥ prasannam /
children.translated_text: Then, gradually [attaining a state] without applied thought and without sustained thought, serene through the one-pointedness of the mind,

children.text: samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānaṃ tadādhyātmaśivaṃ sa dadhyau // Saund_17.47 //
children.translated_text: He meditated upon the second <s>dhyāna</s>, born of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), endowed with joy and happiness, inwardly auspicious. // Saund 17.47 //

children.text: taddhyānamāgamya ca cittamaunaṃ lebhe parāṃ prītimalabdhapūrvām /
children.translated_text: And having attained that <s>dhyāna</s> and mental silence, he obtained supreme joy never before experienced;

children.text: prītau tu tatrāpi sa doṣadarśī yathā vitarkeṣvabhavattathaiva // Saund_17.48 //
children.translated_text: But even there, perceiving faults in joy, just as he had [perceived faults] in discursive thought. // Saund 17.48 //

children.text: prītiḥ parā vastuni yatra yasya viparyayāttasya hi tatra duḥkham /
children.translated_text: For whoever has great joy in anything — for him, when the reverse [occurs], there is suffering;

children.text: prītāvataḥ prekṣya sa tatra doṣān prītikṣaye yogamupāruroha // Saund_17.49 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, perceiving faults in joy there, he ascended to the <s>yoga</s> of the cessation of joy. // Saund 17.49 //

children.text: prītervirāgāt sukhamāryajuṣṭaṃ kāyena vindannatha saṃprajānan /
children.translated_text: Through dispassion toward joy, experiencing the noble happiness with the body, and knowing clearly,

children.text: upekṣakaḥ sa smṛtimān vyahārṣid dhyānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pratilabhya dhīraḥ // Saund_17.50 //
children.translated_text: Equanimous and mindful, the steadfast one rejoiced, having attained the third <s>dhyāna</s>. // Saund 17.50 //

children.text: yasmāt paraṃ tatra sukhaṃ sukhebhyastataḥ paraṃ nāsti sukhapravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the happiness therein is supreme among all happinesses, and beyond that there is no further pursuit of happiness,

children.text: tasmād babhāṣe śubhakṛtsnabhūmiḥ parāparajñaḥ parameti maitryā // Saund_17.51 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, having attained the stage of <s>śubhakṛtsna</s> (universal beauty), the knower of higher and lower spoke 'supreme' with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). // Saund 17.51 //

children.text: dhyāne 'pi tatrātha dadarśa doṣaṃ mene paraṃ śāntamaniñjameva /
children.translated_text: Even in that <s>dhyāna</s>, he then perceived a fault; he considered the supreme [state] to be the unperturbed, the motionless alone;

children.text: ābhogato 'pīñjayati sma tasya cittaṃ pravṛttaṃ sukhamityasram // Saund_17.52 //
children.translated_text: For even intentionally, the happiness [in the third dhyāna] caused a stirring of his mind, since [happiness] involves the flow [of subtle movement]. // Saund 17.52 //

children.text: yatreñjitaṃ spanditamasti tatra yatrāsti ca spanditamasti duḥkham /
children.translated_text: For where there is stirring, there is movement; and where there is movement, there is suffering;

children.text: yasmādatastatsukhamiñjakatvāt praśāntikāmā yatayastyajanti // Saund_17.53 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because that happiness is [still] a stirring, those who desire peace abandon it. // Saund 17.53 //

children.text: atha prahāṇāt sukhaduḥkhayośca manovikārasya ca pūrvameva /
children.translated_text: Then, through the abandonment of both happiness and suffering, and already before that of mental elation,

children.text: dadhyāvupekṣāsmṛtimad viśuddhaṃ dhyānaṃ tathāduḥkhasukhaṃ caturtham // Saund_17.54 //
children.translated_text: He meditated upon the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, purified by equanimity and mindfulness, free from both suffering and happiness. // Saund 17.54 //

children.text: yasmāttu tasminna sukhaṃ na duḥkhaṃ jñānaṃ ca tatrāsti tadarthacāri /
children.translated_text: Since in that [fourth dhyāna] there is neither happiness nor suffering, and knowledge is there, moving toward its purpose,

children.text: tasmādupekṣāsmṛtipāriśuddhirnirucyate dhyānavidhau caturthe // Saund_17.55 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, purity of equanimity and mindfulness is taught in the method of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. // Saund 17.55 //

children.text: dhyānaṃ sa niśritya tataścaturthamarhattvalābhāya matiṃ cakāra /
children.translated_text: Then, relying on the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, he resolved upon the attainment of <s>Arhatship</s>,

children.text: saṃdhāya mitraṃ balavantamāryaṃ rājeva deśānajitān jigīṣuḥ // Saund_17.56 //
children.translated_text: Like a king, having secured a powerful and noble ally, desiring to conquer unconquered territories. // Saund 17.56 //

children.text: ciccheda kārtsnyena tataḥ sa pañca prajñāsinā bhāvanayeritena /
children.translated_text: Then he completely cut the five higher fetters (<s>saṃyojanas</s>) with the sword of wisdom wielded through meditation —

children.text: ūrdhvaṅgamānyuttamabandhanāni saṃyojanānyuttamabandhanāni // Saund_17.57 //
children.translated_text: The supreme bonds [tending] upward — the supreme bonds [of existence]. // Saund 17.57 //

children.text: bodhyaṅganāgairapi saptabhiḥ sa saptaiva cittānuśayān mamarda /
children.translated_text: And with the seven elephants of the factors of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), he crushed the seven latent tendencies (<s>anuśayas</s>) of the mind,

children.text: dvipānivopasthitavipraṇāśān kālo grahaiḥ saptabhireva sapta // Saund_17.58 //
children.translated_text: Like [the planet] Time [crushing] seven [unfortunate] elephants facing impending doom with its seven planets. // Saund 17.58 //

children.text: agnidrumājyāmbuṣu yā hi vṛttiḥ kabandhavāyvagnidivākarāṇām /
children.translated_text: Just as the operation of a rain-cloud, wind, fire, and sun upon a tree, butter, water, and fuel respectively is [to extinguish, uproot, burn, and dry up],

children.text: doṣeṣu tāṃ vṛttimiyāya nando nirvāpaṇotpāṭanadāhaśoṣaiḥ // Saund_17.59 //
children.translated_text: So <s>Nanda</s> approached the defilements with [the operations of] extinguishing, uprooting, burning, and drying up. // Saund 17.59 //

children.text: iti trivegaṃ trijhaṣaṃ trivicamekāmbhasaṃ pañcarayaṃ dvikūlam /
children.translated_text: Thus, with the eightfold raft of the [Noble Path], he crossed the ocean of suffering — hard to cross —

children.text: dvigrāhamaṣṭāṅgavatā plavena duḥkhārṇavaṃ dustaramuttatāra // Saund_17.60 //
children.translated_text: With its three currents, three sea-monsters, three waves, its single water, five rapids, and two shores, its two [crocodile-]graspers. // Saund 17.60 //

children.text: arhattvamāsādya sa satkriyārho nirutsuko niṣpraṇayo nirāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having attained <s>Arhatship</s>, worthy of honor, he was without longing, without attachment, without hope;

children.text: vibhīrviśugvītamado virāgaḥ sa eva dhṛtyānya ivābabhāse // Saund_17.61 //
children.translated_text: Fearless, faultless, free from pride, free from passion — he, though the same, appeared as if another through [his new] steadfastness. // Saund 17.61 //

children.text: bhrātuśca śāstuśca tayānuśiṣṭyā nandastataḥ svena ca vikrameṇa /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, by the instruction of his brother and teacher, and by his own valor —

children.text: praśāntacetāḥ paripūrṇakāryo vāṇīmimāmātmagatāṃ jagāda // Saund_17.62 //
namo 'stu tasmai sugatāya yena hitaiṣiṇā me karuṇātmakena /
bahūni duḥkhānyapavartitāni sukhāni bhūyāṃsyupasaṃhṛtāni // Saund_17.63 //
ahaṃ hyanāryeṇa śarīrajena duḥkhātmake vartmani kṛṣyamāṇaḥ /
nivartitastadvacanāṅkuśena darpānvito nāga ivāṅkuśena // Saund_17.64 //
tasyājñayā kāruṇikasya śāsturhṛdisthamutpāṭya hi rāgaśalyam /
adyaiva tāvat sumahat sukhaṃ me sarvakṣaye kiṃbata nirvṛtasya // Saund_17.65 //
nirvāpya kāmāgnimahaṃ hi dīptaṃ dhṛtyambunā pāvakamambuneva /
hlādaṃ paraṃ sāṃpratamāgato 'smi śītaṃ hradaṃ gharma ivāvatīrṇaḥ // Saund_17.66 //
na me priyaṃ kiṃcana nāpriyaṃ me na me 'nurodho 'sti kuto virodhaḥ /
tayorabhāvāt sukhito 'smi sadyo himātapābhyāmiva vipramuktaḥ // Saund_17.67 //
mahābhayāt kṣemamivopalabhya mahāvarodhādiva vipramokṣam /
mahārṇavāt pāramivāplavaḥ san bhīmāndhakārādiva ca prakāśam // Saund_17.68 //
rogādivārogyamasahyarūpādṛṇādivānṛṇyamanantasaṃkhyāt /
dviṣatsakāśādiva cāpayānaṃ durbhikṣayogācca yathā subhikṣam // Saund_17.69 //
tadvatparāṃ śāntimupāgato 'haṃ yasyānubhāvena vināyakasya /
karomi bhūyaḥ punaruktamasmai namo namo 'rhāya tathāgatāya // Saund_17.70 //
yenāhaṃ girimupanīya rūkmaśṛṅgaṃ svargaṃ ca plavagavadhūnidarśanena /
kāmātmā tridivacarībhiraṅganābhirniṣkṛṣṭo yuvatimaye kalau nimagnaḥ // Saund_17.71 //
tasmācca vyasanaparādanarthapaṅkādutkṛṣya kramaśithilaḥ karīva paṅkāt /
śānte 'smin virajasi vijvare viśoke saddharme vitamasi naiṣṭhike vimuktaḥ // Saund_17.72 //
taṃ vande paramanukampakaṃ maharṣi mūrdhnāhaṃ prakṛtiguṇajñamāśayajñam /
saṃbuddhaṃ daśabalinaṃ bhiṣakpradhānaṃ trātāraṃ punarapi cāsmi saṃnatastam // Saund_17.73 //
saundarananda mahākāvya meṃ "amṛtaprāpti" nāmaka saptadaśa sarga samāpta /

aṣṭādaśaḥ sargaḥ
ājñāvyākaraṇa
atha dvijo bāla ivāptavedaḥ kṣipraṃ vaṇik prāpta ivāptalābhaḥ /
jitvā ca rājanya ivārisainyaṃ nandaḥ kṛtārtho gurumabhyagacchat // Saund_18.1 //
draṣṭuṃ sukhaṃ jñānasamāptikāle gururhi śiṣyasya gurośca śiṣyaḥ /
pariśramaste saphalo mayīti yato didṛkṣāsya munau babhūva // Saund_18.2 //
yato hi yenādhigato viśeṣastasyottamāṃso 'rhati kartumīḍyām /
āryaḥ sarāgo 'pi kṛtajñabhāvāt prakṣīṇamānaḥ kimu vītarāgaḥ // Saund_18.3 //
yasyārthakāmaprabhavā hi bhaktistato 'sya sā tiṣṭhati rūḍhamūlā /
dharmānvayo yasya tu bhaktirāgastasya prasādo hṛdayāvagāḍhaḥ // Saund_18.4 //
kāṣāyavāsāḥ kanakāvadātastataḥ sa mūrdhnā gurave praṇeme /
vāteritaḥ pallavatāmrarāgaḥ puṣpojjvalaśrīriva karṇikāraḥ // Saund_18.5 //
athātmanaḥ śiṣyaguṇasya caiva mahāmuneḥ śāstṛguṇasya caiva /
saṃdarśanārthaṃ sa na mānahetoḥ svāṃ kāryasiddhiṃ kathayāmbabhūva // Saund_18.6 //
yo dṛṣṭiśalyo hṛdayāvagāḍhaḥ prabho bhṛśaṃ māmatudat sutīkṣṇaḥ /
tvadvākyasaṃdaṃśamukhena me sa samuddhṛtaḥ śalyahṛteva śalyaḥ // Saund_18.7 //
kathaṃkathābhāvagatosmi yena chinnaḥ sa niḥsaṃśaya saṃśayo me /
tvacchāsanāt satpathamāgato 'smi sudeśikasyeva pathi pranaṣṭaḥ // Saund_18.8 //
yatpītamāsvādavaśendriyeṇa darpeṇa kandarpaviṣaṃ mayāsīt /
tanme hataṃ tvadvacanāgadena viṣaṃ vināśīva mahāgadena // Saund_18.9 //
kṣayaṃ gataṃ janma nirastajanman saddharmacaryāmuṣito 'smi samyak /
kṛtsnaṃ kṛtaṃ me kṛtakārya kāryaṃ lokeṣu bhūto 'smi na lokadharmā // Saund_18.10 //
maitrīstanīṃ vyañjanacārusāsnāṃ saddharmadugdhāṃ pratibhānaśṛṅgām /
tavāsmi gāṃ sādhu nipīya tṛptastṛṣeva gāmuttama vatsavarṇaḥ // Saund_18.11 //
yatpaśyataścādhigamo mamāyaṃ tanme samāsena mune nibodha /
sarvajña kāmaṃ viditaṃ tavaitat svaṃ tūpacāraṃ pravivakṣurasmi // Saund_18.12 //
anye 'pi santo vimumukṣavo hi śrutvā vimokṣāya nayaṃ parasya /
muktasya rogādiva rogavantastenaiva mārgeṇa sukhaṃ ghaṭante // Saund_18.13 //
urvyādikān janmani vedima dhātun nātmānamurvyādiṣu teṣu kiñcit /
yasmādatasteṣu na me 'sti saktirbahiśca kāyena samā matirme // Saund_18.14 //
skandhāṃśca rūpaprabhṛtīn daśārdhān paśyāmi yasmāccapalānasārān /
anātmakāṃścaiva vadhātmakāṃśca tasmād vimukto 'smyaśivebhya ebhyaḥ // Saund_18.15 //
yasmācca paśyāmyudayaṃ vyayaṃ ca sarvāsvavasthāsvahamindriyāṇām /
tasmādanityeṣu nirātmakeṣu duḥkheṣu me teṣvapi nāsti saṃgaḥ // Saund_18.16 //
yataśca lokaṃ samajanmaniṣṭhaṃ paśyāmi niḥsāramasacca sarvam /
ato dhiyā me manasā vibaddhamasmīti me neñjitamasti yena // Saund_18.17 //
caturvidhe naikavidhaprasaṅge yato 'hamāhāravidhāvasaktaḥ /
amūrcchitaścāgrathitaśca tatra tribhyo vimukto 'smi tato bhavebhyaḥ // Saund_18.18 //
aniścitaścāpratibaddhacitto dṛṣṭaśrutādau vyavahāradharme /
yasmāt samātmānugataśca tatra tasmād visaṃyogagato 'smi muktaḥ // Saund_18.19 //
ityevamuktvā gurubāhumānyāt sarveṇa kāyena sa gāṃ nipannaḥ /
praverito lohitacandanākto haimo mahāstambha ivābabhāse // Saund_18.20 //
tataḥ pramādat prasṛtasya pūrvaṃ śruvā dhṛtiṃ vyākaraṇaṃ ca tasya /
dharmānvayaṃ cānugataṃ prasādaṃ meghasvarastaṃ munirābabhāṣe // Saund_18.21 //
uttiṣṭha dharme sthita śiṣyajuṣṭe kiṃ pādayorme patito 'si murdhnā /
abhyarcanaṃ me na tathā praṇāmo dharme yathaiṣā pratipattireva // Saund_18.22 //
adyāsi supravrajito jitātmannaiśvaryamapyātmani yena labdham /
jitātmanaḥ pravrajanaṃ hi sādhu calātmano na tvajitendriyasya // Saund_18.23 //
adyāsi śaucena pareṇa yukto vākkāyacetāṃsi śucīni yatte /
ataḥ punaścāprayatāpasaumyāṃ yatsaumya no vekṣyasi garbhaśayyām // Saund_18.24 //
adyārthavatte śrutavacchrutaṃ tacchrutānurūpaṃ pratipadya dharmam /
kṛtaśruto vipratipadyamāno nindyo hi nirvīrya ivāttaśastraḥ // Saund_18.25 //
aho dhṛtiste 'viṣayātmakasya yattvaṃ matiṃ mokṣavidhāvakārṣīḥ /
yāsyāmi niṣṭhāmiti bāliśo hi janmakṣayāt trāsamihābhyupaiti // Saund_18.26 //
diṣṭyā durāpaḥ kṣaṇasaṃnipāto nāyaṃ kṛto mohavaśena moghaḥ /
udeti duḥkhena gato hyadhastāt kūrmo yugacchidra ivārṇavasthaḥ // Saund_18.27 //
nirjitya māraṃ yudhi durnivāramadyāsi loke raṇaśīrṣaśūraḥ /
śūro 'pyaśūraḥ sa hi veditavyo doṣairamitrairiva hanyate yaḥ // Saund_18.28 //
nirvāpya rāgāgnimudīrṇamadya diṣṭyā sukhaṃ svapsyasi vītadāhaḥ /
duḥkhaṃ hi śete śayane 'pyudāre kleśāgninā cetasi dahyamānaḥ // Saund_18.29 //
abhyucchrito dravyamadena pūrvamadyāsi tṛṣṇoparamāt samṛddhaḥ /
yāvat satarṣaḥ puruṣo hi loke tāvat samṛddho 'pi sadā daridraḥ // Saund_18.30 //
adyāpadeṣṭuṃ tava yuktarūpaṃ śuddhodano me nṛpatiḥ piteti /
bhraṣṭasya dharmāt pitṛbhirnipātādaślāghanīyo hi kulāpadeśaḥ // Saund_18.31 //
diṣṭyāsi śāntiṃ paramāmupeto nistīrṇakāntāra ivāptasāraḥ /
sarvo hi saṃsāragato bhayārto yathaiva kāntāragatastathaiva // Saund_18.32 //
āraṇyakaṃ bhaikṣacaraṃ vinītaṃ drakṣyāmi nandaṃ nibhṛtaṃ kadeti /
āsīt purastāttvayi me didṛkṣā tathāsi diṣṭyā mama darśanīyaḥ // Saund_18.33 //
bhavatyarūpo 'pi hi darśanīyaḥ svalaṃkṛtaḥ śreṣṭhatamaigurṇaiḥ svaiḥ /
doṣaiḥ parīto malinīkaraistu sudarśanīyo 'pi virūpa eva // Saund_18.34 //
adya prakṛṣṭā tava buddhimattā kṛtsnaṃ yayā te kṛtamātmakāryam /
śrutonnatasyāpi hi nāsti buddhirnotpadyate śreyasi yasya buddhiḥ // Saund_18.35 //
unmīlitasyāpi janasya madhye nimīlitasyāpi tathaiva cakṣuḥ /
prajñāmayaṃ yasya hi nāsti cakṣuścakṣurna tasyāsti sacakṣuṣo 'pi // Saund_18.36 //
duḥkhapratīkāranimittamārtaḥ kṛṣyādibhiḥ khedamupaiti lokaḥ /
ajasramāgacchati tacca bhūyo jñānena yasyādya kṛtastvayāntaḥ // Saund_18.37 //
duḥkhaṃ na me syāt sukhameva me syāditi pravṛttaḥ satataṃ hi lokaḥ /
na vetti taccaiva tathā yathā syāt prāptaṃ tvayādyāsulabhaṃ yathāvat // Saund_18.38 //
ityevamādi sthirabuddhicittastathāgatenābhihito hitāya /
staveṣu nindāsu ca nirvyapekṣaḥ kṛtāñjalirvākyamuvāca nandaḥ // Saund_18.39 //
aho viśeṣeṇa viśeṣadarśin stvayānukampā mayi darśiteyaṃ /
yatkāmapaṅke bhagavannimagnastrāto 'smi saṃsārabhayādakāmaḥ // Saund_18.40 //
bhrātrā tvayā śreyasi daiśikena pitrā phalasthena tathaiva mātrā /
hato 'bhaviṣyaṃ yadi na vyamokṣyaṃ sārthāt paribhraṣṭa ivākṛtārthaḥ // Saund_18.41 //
śāntasya tuṣṭasya sukho viveko vijñātatattvasva parīkṣakasya /
prahīṇamānasya ca nirmadasya sukhaṃ virāgatvamasaktabuddheḥ // Saund_18.42 //
atho hi tattvaṃ parigamya samyaṅnirdhūya doṣānadhigamya śāntim /
svaṃ nāśramaṃ samprati cintayāmi na taṃ janaṃ nāpsaraso na devān // Saund_18.43 //
idaṃ hi bhuktvā śuci śāmikaṃ sukhaṃ na me manaḥ kāṃkṣati kāmajaṃ sukham /
mahārhamapyannamadaivatāhṛtaṃ divaukaso bhuktavataḥ sudhāmiva // Saund_18.44 //
aho 'ndhavijñānanimīlitaṃ jagat paṭāntare paśyati nottamaṃ sukham /
sudhīramadhyatmasukhaṃ vyapāsya hi śramaṃ tathā kāmasukhārthamṛcchati // Saund_18.45 //
yathā hi ratnākarametya durmatirvihāya ratnānyasato maṇīn haret /
apāsya saṃbodhisukhaṃ tathottamaṃ śramaṃ vrajet kāmasukhopalabdhaye // Saund_18.46 //
aho hi sattveṣvatimaitracetasastathāgatasyānujighṛkṣutā parā /
apāsya yaddhyānasukhaṃ mune paraṃ parasya duḥkhoparamāya khidyase // Saund_18.47 //
mayā nu śakyaṃ pratikartumadya kiṃ gurau hitaiṣiṇyanukampake tvayi /
samuddhṛto yena bhavārṇavādahaṃ mahārṇavāccūrṇitanaurivormibhiḥ // Saund_18.48 //
tato ministasya niśamya hetumat prahīṇasarvāsravasūcakaṃ vacaḥ /
idaṃ babhāṣe vadatāmanuttamo yadarhati śrīghana eva bhāṣituṃ // Saund_18.49 //
idaṃ kṛtārthaḥ paramārthavit kṛtī tvameva dhīmannabhidhātumarhasi /
atītya kāntāramavāptasādhanaḥ sudaiśikasyeva kṛtaṃ mahāvaṇik // Saund_18.50 //
avaiti buddhaṃ naradamyasārathiṃ kṛtī yathārhannupaśāntamānasaḥ /
na dṛṣṭasatyo 'pi tathāvabudhyate pṛthagjanaḥ kiṃbata buddhimānapi // Saund_18.51 //
rajastamobhyāṃ parimuktacetasastavaiva ceyaṃ sadṛśī kṛtajñatā /
rajaḥprakarṣeṇa jagatyavasthite kṛtajñabhāvo hi kṛtajña durlabhaḥ // Saund_18.52 //
sadharma dharmānvayato yataśca te mayi prasādo 'dhigame ca kauśalam /
ato 'sti bhūyastvayi me vivakṣitaṃ nato hi bhaktaśca niyogamarhasi // Saund_18.53 //
avāptakāryo 'si parāṃ gatiṃ gato na te 'sti kiñcit karaṇīyamaṇvapi /
ataḥparaṃ saumya carānukampayā vimokṣayan kṛcchragatān parānapi // Saund_18.54 //
ihārthamevārabhate naro 'dhamo vimadhyamastūbhayalaukikīṃ kriyām /
kriyāmamutraiva phalāya madhyamo viśiṣṭadharmā punarapravṛttaye // Saund_18.55 //
ihottamebhyo 'pi mataḥ sa tūttamo ya uttamaṃ dharmamavāpya naiṣṭhikam /
acintayitvātmagataṃ pariśramaṃ śamaṃ parebhyo 'pyupadeṣṭumicchati // Saund_18.56 //
vihāya tasmādiha kāryamātmanaḥ kuru sthirātman parakāryamapyatho /
bhramatsu sattveṣu tamāvṛtātmasu śrutapradīpo niśi dhāryatāmayam // Saund_18.57 //
bravītu tāvat puri vismito janastvayi sthite kurvati dharmadeśanāḥ /
aho batāścaryamidaṃ vimuktaye karoti rāgī yadayaṃ kathāmiti // Saund_18.58 //
dhruvaṃ hi saṃśrutya tava sthiraṃ mano nivṛttanānāviṣayairmanorathaiḥ /
vadhūrgṛhe sāpi tavānukurvatī kariṣyate strīṣu virāgiṇīḥ kathāḥ // Saund_18.59 //
tvayi paramadhṛtau niviṣṭatattve bhavanagatā na hi raṃsyate dhruvaṃ sā /
manasi śamadamātmake vivikte matiriva kāmasukhaiḥ parīkṣakasya // Saund_18.60 //
ityarhataḥ paramakāruṇikasya śāsturmūrdhnā vacaśca caraṇau ca samaṃ gṛhītvā /
svasthaḥ praśāntahṛdayo vinivṛttakāryaḥ pārśvānmuneḥ pratiyayau vimadaḥ karīva // Saund_18.61 //
bhikṣārthaṃ samaye viveśa sa puraṃ dṛṣṭīrjanasyākṣipan
lābhālābhasukhāsukhādiṣu samaḥ svasthendriyo nispṛhaḥ /
nirmokṣāya cakāra tatra ca kathāṃ kāle janāyārthine
naivonmārgagatān parān paribhavannātmānamutkarṣayan // Saund_18.62 //
ityeṣā vyupaśāntaye na rataye mokṣārthagarbhā kṛtiḥ
śrotṛṇāṃ grahaṇārthamanyamanasāṃ kāvyopacārāt kṛtā /
yanmokṣāt kṛtamanyadatra hi mayā tatkāvyadharmāt
kṛtaṃ pātuṃ titkamivauṣadhaṃ madhuyutaṃ hṛdyaṃ kathaṃ syāditi // Saund_18.63 //
prāyeṇālokya lokaṃ viṣayaratiparaṃ mokṣāt pratihataṃ
kāvyavyājena tattvaṃ kathitamiha mayā mokṣaḥ paramiti /
tadbuddhvā śamikaṃ yattadavahitamito grāhyaṃ na lalitaṃ
pāṃsubhyo dhātujebhyo niyatamupakaraṃ cāmīkaramiti // Saund_18.64 //
saundarananda mahākāvya meṃ "ājñāvyākaraṇa" nāmaka aṣṭādaśa sarga samāpta /
